name: After School Matters (paid apprenticeships and assistantships)
pay_detail: Paid stipend based on program level and frequency. Dollar amounts vary by program and are not stated on the apply page.
duration: Spring: late Feb to mid May. Summer: late June to early Aug. Fall 2026: Sept 28 to Dec 12.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications opened Aug 26. Fall programs started Sept 28, 2026, and the fall interviews (Sept 21 to 23) have passed, so the fall round is over. Spring 2027 applications open in January, and summer 2027 applications open in April (per the session timeline on the apply page).

The apply page still shows fall 2026 wording, but fall programs began Sept 28, so the fall round is over for new applicants until the spring window opens. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.

name: Discovery Station volunteer, Udvar-Hazy Center

name: California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of California
city: California (session location not stated on the site)
grades: 11th grade (the site says each delegate is an 11th grade student during the 2026-27 school year)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22 to 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: 2027 (84th) session: dates and location not posted yet. The online form for Unit-selected 2027 delegates and alternates opens February 2027. The form for Department (statewide) alternate applicants opens April 2027. Last session: June 22 to 27, 2026.
who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade. A local American Legion Auxiliary Unit must pick and sponsor you. Each high school can send only one delegate. If no Unit sponsors your school, you can apply as a statewide alternate. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor. Or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. The site has a list to find one. Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Many use a form, an essay or an interview. Picked students then fill out an online form. It opens in February 2027. Is there no Unit at your school? You can apply as a statewide alternate. That form opens in April 2027.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages. The 2027 session will be the 84th. Adult staff must be at least 20 or out of high school for at least three years, so staff roles are not for teens.

name: Aquatic Internship Program
org: City of Alameda Recreation and Parks, Aquatics
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

notes: The program page does not give start and end dates or pay. Ask the aquatics team. Email arpdaquatics@alamedaca.gov or call the city at 510-747-7400. It is held at Encinal Swim Center, 230 Central Ave. Residency is not stated on the program page.

notes: The program page does not say if the job is paid, how long it lasts, or if a work permit is needed. Ask Human Resources at 510-747-4900.

name: HEAL Program High School Internships (HealthPATH, Highland Hospital)
city: Oakland, CA (Wilma Chan Highland Hospital Campus)
grades: Fall and spring: 10th to 12th grade (one fall cohort is 12th grade only). Summer: 11th grade only.
pay_detail: Fall 2026 cohorts: $400 stipend. Summer 2027: $2,000 stipend. Spring 2027 pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Spring 2027: about 5 weeks, Mon to Thu 4 to 6 pm (Cohort A Jan 11 to Feb 11, B Feb 22 to Mar 25, C Apr 5 to May 13). Summer 2027: June 14 to July 23, weekdays 9 am to 4:30 pm.
deadline_text: Spring 2027 cohorts: application opens Oct 26, 2026 and closes Nov 17, 2026; interviews week of Nov 30; decisions Dec 15, 2026. Summer 2027: opens Jan 5, 2027, closes Jan 27, 2027. Fall 2026 cohorts closed Aug 27, 2026.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school AND either live in Oakland or attend an OUSD school or charter, both when you apply and during the cohort. Spring cohorts are for 10th to 12th graders. Summer 2027 is for current 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application that must be done in one sitting (no save). Pick your cohort, upload a resume, and answer short-answer questions (75 words minimum each for spring, 150 for summer). Draft answers first. Then an interview. Questions: healprogram@alamedahealthsystem.org.
notes: As of 2026-10-16, the 2026-27 dates, pay and rules are on the HealthPATH page, healthpath-ahs.org/healprogramapply. That page does not load with https. So this card links to the AHS news post that points to it. Type healthpath-ahs.org/healprogramapply into your browser for the live dates and the form. The page says HEAL is for high school students of color. The written rule is that you live in Oakland or go to an OUSD school. The AHS volunteer program is a different program, and it is for ages 18 and up. The page does not say if you need a work permit for the stipend. Ask the program.

notes: You need earlier BioPark experience. This is a second step after Nature Guides.

name: Engineering and Computing Summer Academy (UNM)

name: Anaheim Community Services Volunteers (ages 13 and up)

name: Anaheim Fire and Rescue Explorer Program

notes: Spots go first to Public Safety Pathways grads. Then to Anaheim residents. Then to Anaheim students. Explorers do not enter burning buildings. They do not replace firefighters.

name: Anaheim Police Explorer Post
pay_detail: Unpaid. The department pays for most of the uniform. You buy a few items, like shoes and a flashlight.

how_to_apply: Email Explorers@anaheim.net to say you are interested. Go to 4 meetings in a row as a guest, in business casual clothes. Then fill out an application. You must pass a written test, an interview and a background check.

Questions: Youth Engagement Coordinator, 714-765-1928. The city volunteer page links to an old Explorer page that is gone, so use the police site.

name: Anaheim Public Library Teen Volunteers

deadline_text: Dates depend on the branch. East Anaheim, Haskett, Heritage Center, Ponderosa and Sunkist take applications year-round. Central Library takes them at the start of summer, fall and spring. Canyon Hills takes them in September, January and May, for summer work. Euclid takes them during the spring semester, for summer work.

The Mobile Library (Bookmobile and STEAM Van) takes summer applications in April and needs volunteers 2 to 6 p.m. on at least one Monday to Thursday. The Teen Podcast takes applications at the start of fall.

name: Anaheim Summer VolunTEEN Program
org: City of Anaheim Community Services Department

Questions: Volunteer Coordinator, 714-765-4994. The city also lists other volunteer jobs for ages 13 and up. Examples are trail work at Oak Canyon Nature Center and youth sports coach assistants.

name: Junior Volunteer Program at Humane Society of Huron Valley
pay_detail: $205 program fee for the 6 session training (training, T-shirt, supplies). Limited scholarships for families with financial need.

Shelter is at 3100 Cherry Hill Rd, Ann Arbor. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Ann Arbor lifeguard certification course and pool jobs

deadline_text: Registration for the course opens Jan 21, 2027. Session 1 starts Friday, April 16, 2027 (Friday 5 to 10 p.m., then Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.). Registration closes 7 days before the course starts. Seasonal job postings for 2027 are not up yet.

name: Volunteer in the Parks (City of Ann Arbor)

deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 15 and were due Mar 22, 2026; internship period June 15 to Aug 21, 2026. The site says 2027 applications open in mid-January and are usually open late January to late March. 2027 closing date is not posted.

name: Volunteer at Alexian Brothers Medical Center (teens 16 and up)

name: Volunteer at Saint Alexius Medical Center (teens 16 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

deadline_text: The page lists no deadline and does not say whether applications are accepted year-round. Call 847-755-8708 to ask.

how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-755-8708.
notes: You need at least 100 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.

name: Assisteens Auxiliary (Assistance League of Newport-Mesa)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

notes: Membership costs are not stated on the program page. The thrift shop and office are at 2220 Fairview Road, Costa Mesa. Awards go to those with 50, 75 and 100 or more hours a year. Events include a spring luncheon and a June Senior Medallion Event.

name: INSPIRE Summer Program (Access ASU)
pay_detail: Free for all students. There is no cost to apply.

deadline_text: Summer 2026 ran June 21 to 25 and applications are closed. Next dates are not stated on the program page.

how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Call 480-727-4948 or use the contact details on the program page.
notes: Students must stay on campus for the whole program. Meals are provided. Next dates are not stated on the program page.

deadline_text: Summer 2026 ran June 14 to 17 and applications are closed. Next dates are not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Students entering grade 11 or 12. No minimum GPA is required, but the page recommends a GPA of 2.7 or higher.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Call 480-727-4948 or use the contact details on the program page.
notes: This is a residential program on the ASU campus. The deposit is not refunded. Next dates are not stated on the program page.

name: Joaquin Bustoz Math-Science Honors Program (JBMSHP)
pay_detail: Free for students in 2026: tuition, room and board, and class materials. The 2027 page lists no fee.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors and seniors. You need a 3.25 unweighted GPA and A or B grades in high school math and science. You must qualify for Arizona in-state tuition and have lived in Arizona for the last 2 years.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You will need financial information from a parent or guardian. Upload a one page personal or career statement. Upload an unofficial high school transcript. Have one recommender send a letter on school letterhead.
notes: The program page lists 2027 dates. Its Spanish section shows 2026 dates for the first and last program days, so confirm the dates with the program.

name: Fleischer Scholars Program
org: Arizona State University, W. P. Carey School of Business
pay_detail: Free to students who apply and are selected.
duration: Online June 14 to 18, 2027, then a Tempe campus visit on June 21, 2027
deadline_text: The program page lists Feb 15 for priority, March 15 for late, and May 6 as the final deadline for the summer 2027 group. It does not write the year for these dates.
who_can_apply: Arizona high school juniors. Picks look at leadership. They look at community service, grades, and family income. They also ask if you are first in your family to go to college.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. A recommendation is optional. A teacher can write it. So can another person who works in education. It uses an online form.
notes: The page names both a 2026 application and a summer 2027 group. Confirm the year and deadlines with the program at 480-965-5187.

name: Summer Youth Leadership Institute at Goizueta (SYLI)
org: 21st Century Leaders with Emory Goizueta Business School
pay_detail: Applying is free. The page says some institutes, including SYLI, may cost to attend, and that financial aid is available. The price is not listed.
duration: About one week, residential (overnight)
deadline_text: The 2026 application window was Jan 5 to Mar 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade who live in Georgia.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link for the institute on the 21st Century Leaders site. Spots are limited and some students go on a waitlist. Acceptance comes by email, so check spam.
notes: Expect applications to open around January again, as they did last year. The same group runs Leadership Connect all year. It is online and self-paced. Seniors who finish 3 levels can get a paid summer internship and a scholarship.

name: ATL Workforce Summer Youth Employment Program
pay_detail: Paid. The page does not state a rate.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: The page says applications open the first week of February through mid-March each year. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in the Atlanta area.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City of Atlanta jobs website when the posting is open. You may be asked to interview, then you go to orientation. Every participant is matched with a mentor.
notes: This is the airport's own summer job program, separate from the Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program. The 2026 City of Atlanta job posting linked from the page was no longer showing. Questions: atlworkforce@atl.com.

name: ATL Workforce Youth Apprenticeship Program
pay_detail: Paid, part-time. The page does not state a rate.
deadline_text: Rolling. The page says applications are accepted based on the airport's needs and may vary each year.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Clayton County, Fulton County, or Atlanta city public schools.
how_to_apply: Ask the work-based learning teacher or the counselor at your school. You can also apply on your own on the City of Atlanta jobs site.
notes: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning Coordinator first, since credit comes through your school. The airport's Registered Apprenticeship is for ages 18 and up, so it is not listed here. Questions: atlworkforce@atl.com.

name: SPEAK Student Volunteers (Atlanta Botanical Garden)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: 50 hours between June 2 and July 24 (2026), including a required 6-hour training day. Shifts Tuesday to Sunday in 2-hour blocks.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: info sessions Jan 13 and Feb 10, application and recommendation due March 1, 2026, group interviews March 21 or 28. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older by June 2 of the summer.
how_to_apply: Submit the online SPEAK application and have a non-relative adult submit a recommendation form. Attend a 2-hour group interview and the mandatory training day. If you also apply to the paid internship, only the internship application is needed.
notes: Application window usually closes March 1 (2026 pattern). The page gives no 2027 dates yet.

name: Summer High School Internship (Atlanta Botanical Garden)
pay_detail: $12 per hour, paid every two weeks.
duration: 7 weeks (June 2 to July 16 in 2026), 18 hours a week, Tuesday through Thursday
deadline_text: The Garden says to check back in December 2026 for Summer 2027 details.
who_can_apply: 16 or older by June 2 of the summer, and a rising sophomore, junior or senior at a Metro Atlanta Title I school. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the internship application and have a non-relative adult (teacher, mentor or boss) submit the recommendation form. Group interview at the Garden, then virtual orientation with a guardian. Questions: lboren@atlantabg.org.
notes: Only for students at Metro Atlanta Title I schools. Work is outside in all weather and includes lifting 40 lbs. Applying here also covers the SPEAK volunteer program. The Garden's Gainesville site has its own separate teen program.

name: Student Business Shadow Project (SBSP)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates or deadline are posted on the page.

how_to_apply: The student fills out the application linked on the program page. A parent or guardian approves it. Call 404-584-8126 to ask about dates and nominations.
notes: Pay, dates, cost and site locations are not listed, so call to confirm first. Atlanta Business League is at 931 Martin Luther King Jr. Dr. NW. The summer season is from the program name on search results, not the page; confirm.

name: CHRIS 180 youth drop-in center and Summit Trail Apartments
pay_detail: Cost is not listed.
deadline_text: No deadline. Drop-in hours were not listed.
who_can_apply: Summit Trail Apartments are for young adults ages 17 to 24. The page does not list ages for the drop-in center.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Need Housing Support form on the CHRIS 180 page, or call 404-486-9034 or 1-800-896-4106. The team says it will reach out privately. Main office: 1030 Fayetteville Road, Atlanta.
notes: Support and housing, not a job. Call to ask about ages for the drop-in center, hours and where it is. If you are in danger right now, call 911.

name: Atlanta College and Career Academy (ACCA)
grades: 10 to 12 for the dual enrollment pathways. The page gives no grade range for the career pathways.
pay_detail: School program. The page does not mention pay. Dual enrollment is through Atlanta Technical College.
duration: Part of the school day: morning group 9:15 to 11:30 am, afternoon group 12:30 to 2:45 pm
deadline_text: The FAQ says students can apply online from November to March. Exact dates and year not posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. For dual enrollment, you must be on track to graduate and have a 2.0 GPA. Early College Essentials and Cybersecurity need a 2.6 HOPE GPA and grade 11 or 12.
how_to_apply: Take the YouScience career quiz (recommended). Talk to your school counselor. Then submit the online application. Students with an IEP or 504 plan also need a team review.
notes: Career paths include HVAC, Culinary Arts, Dental Science and Patient Care. Atlanta Technical College runs the dual enrollment paths. They include Carpentry and Cybersecurity. The page lists more. You can be denied if there is no room or you miss the minimums.

name: Volunteering at the Atlanta Community Food Bank (ages 8 and up with an adult)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
deadline_text: Sign up for a shift on the volunteer calendar. Dates not on the calendar are full or not offered.
who_can_apply: Volunteers 8 and up at most ongoing projects. Anyone under 18 must come with an adult chaperone who stays the whole shift. Groups need 1 adult for every 4 youth ages 8 to 11 and 1 adult for every 8 youth ages 12 to 17. Adults register for shifts themselves.
how_to_apply: An adult signs up for a shift on the volunteer calendar. Then email volunteers@acfb.org or call 404-419-1727 to add the youth to the registration. Groups of 8 or more fill out a group request form.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Wear closed-toe, closed-heel shoes. Stay for the whole shift. Come on time because late volunteers more than 30 minutes cannot serve. Special events may have other age rules.

name: Teen Experience and Leadership Program (TELP)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says TELP is an unpaid educational program and you get documentation of your service hours.
duration: 7 weeks. In 2026 it ran May 26 to July 14, plus 20 hours of virtual learning labs and 40 hours of community engagement a year.
deadline_text: The 2026 application was open Jan 16 to Feb 20, 2026, with the YouScience assessment Feb 23 to Mar 8 and interviews Mar 9 to 27. 2027 dates are not posted; expect a similar January opening.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who have completed 9th grade and want to learn about health care careers. The page lists no residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form online. Add a photo of your face, your shot records, and two forms. A parent or guardian signs one of them. Then take a career quiz online and do an interview. Not everyone gets in.
notes: The page says it is closed for now. If you get in, you need a TB blood test before you start. In 2026 they held free online help hours two days a week while the form was open. Late or missing forms may not be read.

name: Institute on Neuroscience (ION) Summer Research Program
org: Georgia State University, Center for Behavioral Neuroscience
pay_detail: Stipend. The 2025 rate was $4,500; the page says the 2026 rate was not guaranteed. MARTA passes or parking may be reimbursed.
duration: About 6 weeks, 40 hours a week. In 2026 it ran June 22 to a symposium on August 6.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed June 14, 2026, a late, short cycle because funding was delayed. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who excel in science and are interested in research. The minimum age is 16. Competitive.
how_to_apply: Online application form, then an interview. You may not miss any starred program dates and may miss at most one week of lab time.
notes: Funding for 2026 came from the Army Educational Outreach Program, so the dates and stipend can change from year to year. Bring your own meals and get yourself to downtown Atlanta daily. No housing is provided. Join the ION email list on the home page to hear about 2027.

name: The Neuroscience School: Short Courses for High School Students
org: Georgia State University, Center for Behavioral Neuroscience
pay_detail: Costs $275 to $350 per course in 2026. Fee help is available if you qualify for free or reduced lunch (documentation required). Email NeuroscienceSchool@gsu.edu.
duration: 4 or 5 days per course. In person 9:30 AM to 3:45 PM, online 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. 2026 courses ran June 1 to July 23.
deadline_text: In 2026, registration stayed open until classes were full, and classes without enough sign-ups by June 1 were canceled. The 2026 schedule was posted in December 2025. 2027 courses are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed 9th, 10th, 11th, or 12th grade before class starts. In-person courses also require you to be at least 16 by the start of class, with no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Register and pay in the GSU Marketplace Mall store linked from the Registration page. No essay or application.
notes: Online courses are open to younger high schoolers who are under 16. Sign up for the program's newsletter on the home page to hear when the 2027 schedule is posted.

name: Atlanta Teen Leader Program and Parks and Recreation Teen Summer Employment
org: City of Atlanta, Department of Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Teen Leader activities are free. Pay for the summer employment program is not stated in the catalog.
duration: The 2026 Teen Leaders Summer Academy ran June 8 to July 24, Monday to Friday.

That date is a registration cutoff, not a job application. The catalog also says summer 2026 employment registration is closed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Participating sites listed: Adams, Bessie Branham, C. T. Martin, Dunbar, Grove Park, Martin Luther King Jr., Peachtree Hills, Pittman, Rosel Fann, Thomasville, William Walker, Zaban, @Promise South and @Promise MLK. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register for the Atlanta Teen Leader Program. The catalog lists atlantaga.gov/iparcs as the City registration site for its programs. Confirm the steps with your nearest participating recreation center.
notes: Source is the City's 2026 summer catalog, so it does not say which summer the Dec 31, 2026 registration cutoff is for. Ages and pay for the actual summer jobs are not stated. Georgia requires a work permit for any job under 16. The City's iParcs page blocked automated reading.

name: Mentorship and Internship Program (APS Gifted and Talented)
org: Atlanta Public Schools, Gifted and Talented Programs
pay_detail: The page does not say whether you get pay or school credit. It calls Mentorship and Internship classes.
duration: Fall mentorship class, then a 60-hour one-on-one spring internship that begins in January and concludes with the Capstone Celebration in April. Hours per week and days are not stated.
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Mentor meetings usually start in November. Capstone Celebration in April.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at an APS high school that offers the Mentorship and Internship classes. You do not have to be labeled gifted. Your school picks the students.
how_to_apply: There is no separate form on the page. Ask your guidance counselor whether your school offers the class, or call the gifted office at 404-802-7585. The coordinator matches you using a career survey from early fall.
notes: The coordinator matches students to internships after a career survey in early fall. Students and families arrange their own rides. You must finish the fall Mentorship course first.

name: Work-Based Learning (CTAE), Atlanta Public Schools
org: Atlanta Public Schools, Career, Technical and Agricultural Education (CTAE)
pay_detail: Not stated on the district page. You earn high school credit.
duration: Not stated

notes: The phone on the page is (404) 802-5878. The page also lists CTAE career paths. They include Engineering Drafting, Allied Health, Cybersecurity and Culinary Arts. Students in other districts use their own district.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Atlanta, Department of Labor and Employment Services
pay_detail: Paid. The page says competitive wages and does not state a rate.
duration: June 8 to July 16 in 2026 (about 6 weeks). Some positions may extend.
deadline_text: The 2026 program ran in June and July. Registration was listed as a waiting list. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Atlanta youth ages 14 to 24. Documents asked for: original birth certificate, proof of City of Atlanta residency, state or school photo ID, original Social Security card, and a work permit for anyone under 16.
how_to_apply: Register online on the city's SYEP sign-up page with an email address you check daily. Upload your documents in the SYEP portal when asked. You are matched to openings, invited to orientation, and sent an offer letter. Some employers interview first.
notes: A work permit is needed only for ages 14 and 15 (Georgia requires one under 16). You start it after you have a job offer, through your school district. Not guaranteed: the city says selection is competitive. Questions: syep@atlantaga.gov or (404) 546-3000. The registration list asks for an original Social Security card; this is the official city program, so upload documents only inside the SYEP portal and never send them by email or text. The city's atlantaga.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm the 2027 timeline with the SYEP team.

name: YMB Fuel youth business accelerator

notes: Also open to younger kids. Your business needs paying customers already. For newer ideas the site lists YMB Spark (early-stage help) but its page was not read. YMB also holds an annual Summit (two days, ages 11 to 17 can register); dates and cost were not on the page. The page says the program takes place live in Atlanta, Georgia, and may have virtual parts.

notes: The library's teen volunteer page said summer reading volunteers for 2027 apply in the spring. It also lists outside groups that take teen volunteers, with their own age rules.

name: Youth Climate Action Fund microgrants
pay_detail: You do not get paid. Each project can receive a microgrant of $1,000 to $5,000 to carry it out. The money pays for the project, not a wage to you.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Questions: youthservdiv@aurora.il.us.
notes: 10 to 50 projects share $50,000. Funds go out by Nov 13, 2026, and projects end by Apr 15, 2027. Ages up to 24 can apply. Next round not posted.

name: Youth Court (peer jurors)

notes: Training dates are not listed on the page. The page says Youth Court is for youth who committed first time offenses. Teens serve as jurors.

name: Austin Animal Services Volunteer Program (teens)

how_to_apply: Fill out the individual volunteer application, then go to orientation. A criminal background check is part of orientation. Email animalservicesvolunteers@austintexas.gov for help.
notes: Read the volunteer handbook linked on the page first.

name: City of Austin High School Summer Internship Programs

notes: Separate from the Austin ISD / Austin Chamber paid internship. Placements depend on site access and career interest.

name: Austin Fire Explorers Post 370
org: Austin Fire Department with Capitol Area Council, Scouting America
pay_detail: No pay or fee is stated on the page.

deadline_text: No deadline posted. Fill out the interest card to get updates.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest card to get on the email list. You can send questions by email to the fire team at firerecruiting@austintexas.gov.
notes: Teams compete in the DFW Fire Games in the spring and the San Antonio fire games in the fall. Being an Explorer does not hurt you if you apply to be a firefighter later. There are also ways to volunteer.

name: Austin Habitat for Humanity Youth Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Family Build Days happen 3 to 4 times a year. Other timing is not stated.
deadline_text: No deadline. Check the volunteer calendar for dates.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 cannot go on active building sites. They do other projects, and there must be 1 adult for every 5 kids. Ages 16 and 17 may help build new homes. They may not use power tools or work above 6 feet. They must bring a parent or guardian over 21. Home Repair and Blitz Build need 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer calendar (austinhabitat.volunteerhub.com) or the general sign-up page. The youth page does not give its own steps. Call Volunteer Services at 512-472-8788 ext. 106. Or write to volservices@austinhabitat.org.
notes: The age 12 start is for the project ideas listed for 12 and up. Confirm the right sign up path for your age with Volunteer Services.

name: Austin Humane Society Teen Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. One time registration fee of $20 for students ($35 for adults), paid at orientation.
duration: At least 3 months, 2 hours per week
deadline_text: No deadline. Register any time.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. Ages 14 and 15 need a parent or guardian over 21 to train and volunteer with them at all times. Ages 16 and 17 can volunteer on their own with parental consent given on the online application.
how_to_apply: Pay the fee, go to a virtual welcome orientation, finish online training, then take a hands on training session and pick a shift. Start from the Get Started button on the volunteer page.
notes: The youth page does not list a fee, but the volunteer page does. This page does not cover the clinic volunteer program.

name: Austin ISD Summer Internship Program
org: Austin ISD with Austin Ed Fund and the Austin Chamber of Commerce
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend for living expenses
duration: 6 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 23, with a break June 29 to July 3)
deadline_text: The 2026 interest form closed Feb 6, 2026. A banner on the page says 2027 details are coming and the student form opens in December (year not stated, so confirm).
who_can_apply: Austin ISD students who will be in grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Interest Form linked on the page. Students heard by March 30. They had to go to orientations in late April and mid May. Contact Cecilia Gutierrez at cecilia.gutierrez@austinisd.org.
notes: Info sessions in 2026 were held on Google Meet in December and January. The page lists the work period as ending July 23 in one place and July 24 in another.

name: Teen Library Fellowship
org: Austin Public Library with the Austin Library Foundation
pay_detail: $21 per hour on the Foundation page ($22 per hour on the library pages), up to 10 hours of work per month
duration: 9 months (about August to May)
deadline_text: Foundation page: the next cohort application opens in May 2027. The 2026-27 application ran May 1-31, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 17 living in Central Texas who will be a sophomore, junior or senior in the coming fall (homeschoolers welcome). Must be able to work legally in the U.S., or be willing to waive pay on a student-only visa. About 10 teens are hired each year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Foundation's Teen Library Fellowship page when the application opens. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at kathleen.houlihan@austintexas.gov.
notes: Fellows must attend a mandatory monthly Sunday afternoon retreat at the Central Library; travel stipends are available. The Foundation page says ages 15-17 and $21 per hour; library pages say $22 per hour and one library page says ages 15-18, so confirm when applications open.

name: Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Fall (Oct-Dec) and spring (Mar-May): 10 weeks, one 2-hour shift a week. Summer (June-July): 8 weeks, one 2 to 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Windows each year: fall Jul 1-31, spring Dec 1-31, summer Mar 1-31. The fall window has closed; the next one is spring, Dec 1-31 (the page gives these windows without a year).
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 (no younger than 13 and no older than 17 by Aug 1 for fall, Dec 1 for spring, or May 1 for summer). Must pass a background check (fingerprinting for ages 15+ who lived outside Texas in the last seven years) and attend a mandatory orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application posted on the Teen Volunteer Program page during the window. There may be an interview with the volunteer coordinator; you get three business days to accept an offer. Not every applicant gets a placement.
notes: Placement depends on the library branch and supervisor, and the library gets more applicants than placements. Contact: APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov. Limit of two absences per season.

name: Caminos Teen Leadership Program
org: Emma S. Barrientos Mexican American Cultural Center (City of Austin)
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 6 to 10 hours per week
duration: 10 months, mid-to-late August through early June; most Saturdays 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. plus Wednesday evenings
deadline_text: Applications for the Class of 2027 are closed. The next round (Class of 2028) is due in Spring 2027, announced on Instagram @atxcaminos.
who_can_apply: High school students living in Central Texas, ages 16 to 18 (or turning 16 in the year they apply), interested in creative careers and Latinx issues, and able to work legally in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit a personal application, a portfolio and teacher recommendations, then do one-on-one and panel interviews. Questions: caminos@austintexas.gov.
notes: About 10 to 12 teens per cohort. Competitive. The page says the next round is expected in Spring 2027, with no exact date posted.

name: Lifeguard training and hiring
org: Austin Parks and Recreation Department, Aquatic Division
pay_detail: Starting at $22.05 per hour (March 2026 posting)
duration: Seasonal; training happens before the swim season
deadline_text: Spring 2026 hiring open hours were Mar 31, Apr 16 and Apr 28 (4 to 8 p.m.) at 2818 San Gabriel St. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard training and hiring starts at age 15 with no upper age limit. You need a physical Social Security card and Texas-issued ID for the in-person paperwork.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the online lifeguard job application. Step 2: visit the Aquatic Office in person at 2818 San Gabriel St. with your Social Security card, Texas ID and any hiring paperwork emailed to you. Questions: 512-974-9330.
notes: The 2026 posting also offered a $200 stipend for guards trained and working 40 hours before July 4, 2026. One library list says age 16+; the Parks page (dated March 20, 2026) says 15. Texas hour limits apply to 15 year olds.

name: Roving Leaders teen program
pay_detail: Free. The summer camp listing shows a cost of $0.
duration: Summer 2026 camp: June 8 to August 7, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 camp ran June 8 to August 7, 2026, and now shows as unavailable. 2027 dates are not posted. The listing says late additions are always welcome.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 (summer camp listing). The listing does not give other rules.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the city parks registration search for Roving Leaders, or call (512) 974-3927.
notes: Rides are available if you ask. The old city page for Roving Leaders no longer opens after the city site redesign, so this card uses the city sign-up listing. Not a job.

name: Totally Cool Totally Art (TCTA) free teen art classes
pay_detail: Free. The classes cost nothing.
duration: After school. The Montopolis class meets Monday and Wednesday, 6 to 8 p.m. Other centers set their own times.
deadline_text: 2026 to 2027 classes are listed now. Montopolis sign up opened October 1, 2026. No end date is posted.
who_can_apply: Teens. The Virginia L. Brown center listing says ages 13 to 18, and the Montopolis listing says grades 7 to 12. You must sign up first, and space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Register online link on the TCTA page, or call the rec center you want to go to. Centers include Dittmar, Dove Springs, Gus Garcia, Mendez, Montopolis, Northwest and Virginia L. Brown.
notes: Program contact: Clint Hofmeister, TCTA coordinator, 512-978-2476. Each center listing has its own staff contact. Not a job.

name: SAFE Expect Respect Summer Youth Leadership Academy
pay_detail: Paid part-time. The rate is not stated on the page.
duration: 5 weeks, part-time
deadline_text: Registration goes through Travis County's Summer Youth Employment Program, which opens Summer 2027 applications in January 2027 (exact date not posted).
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17. You register through the Austin and Travis County summer youth jobs program.
how_to_apply: Sign up ahead of time through the Travis County summer youth jobs program. SAFE links to it from its page. For questions, email Randy Randolph at Rrandolph@safeaustin.org or call 512-356-1633.
notes: SAFE also leads free talks in schools and clubs if you ask. The county jobs program may look at your family's income.

name: Teen Summer Volunteer Program, St. David's Medical Center
org: St. David's HealthCare, St. David's Medical Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July, two 4 hour shifts a week
deadline_text: The page says applications open March 15 and close April 15 at 11:59 pm, once a year. The year is not stated.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be 15 by June 1 and free for the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online volunteer application. If you are accepted, you get orientation and training details later. Email sdmc.volunteers@stdavids.com. Or call 512-544-4491.
notes: Records are required for 2 MMR doses, 2 chickenpox doses or history, Tdap within 10 years, a TB test within 90 days and a flu shot. Homeschooled teens may apply year round. Up to 2 service day absences may be requested ahead of time.

name: Teen Summer Volunteer Program, St. David's North Austin Medical Center
org: St. David's HealthCare, North Austin Medical Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July. Weekly hours are not stated.
deadline_text: The page says applications run March 1 to March 31 and late materials are not accepted. The year is not stated.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by June 1 and available the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online application. Then you get an email asking for a teen and parent agreement, two letters of support, short essay answers and shot records. Teens who are picked get an invite to interview. Orientation is by invite. Email namc.volunteers@hcahealthcare.com or call 512-901-1223.
notes: St. David's Medical Center in central Austin has a separate teen program with different ages (15 to 18) and dates. Apply to the campus whose rules you meet.

name: VolunTeen Program
pay_detail: Volunteer service. Cost and pay are not stated on the program page.
duration: 60 hours of training plus 40 hours of service
deadline_text: Dates and application window are not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: The VolunTeens link goes to an online volunteer form (Volgistics). The form needs JavaScript. Check it for the current steps.
notes: Thinkery also runs a teen Counselor in Training program for summer camps. Its page was not found (404), so it is not listed here. Check the dates, cost and application window before you apply. On 2026-10-10 the VolunTeens link went to a bare application form with no program text. So the 60 training hours, 40 service hours and 208 VolunTeen figures could not be checked again.

name: Urban Roots High School Leadership Programs
pay_detail: Described as paid youth internships. The amount is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to watch for future opportunities. No dates are posted.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or school or home rules. It says applications are closed and to watch for future chances.
how_to_apply: No application is open now. Contact Urban Roots at info@urbanrootsatx.org or 512-750-8019 to ask when the next one opens.
notes: Details on this page are thin. The page does not name a Summer Farm Program. Ask about ages, pay and season before counting on it. The same page lists free elementary day camps (2nd to 5th grade) and a free middle school Food Lab, which are not for high schoolers.

name: Youth Career Services
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the services. Paid work experience is named only for the SEAL program (students with disabilities ages 16 to 22). Pay amounts are not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline listed on the Youth Services page, and it does not say when you can start.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 (out of school youth services target ages 16 to 24). The page says low income youth. For training scholarships and case managed help, the main page lists U.S. work authorization, living in Austin or Travis County, and one more need related to work, income or school.
how_to_apply: Click Get Started on the Youth Services page. It leads to the Jumpstart Your Career registration form and a career info session. You can also use the contact page or call your local career center.
notes: The Jumpstart form asks for the last four digits of a Social Security number. It uses them to check your info on WorkInTexas.com. Summer jobs through SEAL need year round part in WIOA. No income limit is listed.

name: Austin Youth Council
org: City of Austin Economic Development (Youth Initiatives)
pay_detail: Pay is not mentioned on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings and service events. Term length is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says 2027 to 2028 applications are expected to open in Spring 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students who live in the City of Austin or its Extraterritorial Jurisdiction (ETJ). Students who only attend school in Austin are not eligible. No citizenship rule. A 2.5 GPA or higher is preferred, but applicants are read as a whole.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the application in Spring 2027. Send questions to the program coordinator. Her email is abrianna.citta01@austintexas.gov.
notes: Members may attend national conferences each year, including one in Washington, D.C. The page does not say who pays for travel.

name: Austin Youth Development (AYD)
org: Austin Public Health, City of Austin
pay_detail: Pay, hours and length are not listed on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No application dates are listed.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 22 who live in the Austin and Travis County area. You need a reliable ride. You must be able to get a driver's license within 90 days. You must have a high school diploma or GED, or be working toward one.
how_to_apply: Complete the online interest form linked on the page. Call 512-972-4785 or email AYD@austintexas.gov.
notes: The page says the work is paid work with the City, plus mentoring and career planning. It does not give pay, hours, length or application dates. Call before applying. Office: 1416 Montopolis Drive, Austin.

name: Youth Forest Council
org: City of Austin, Austin Climate Action and Resilience (Urban Forest Program)
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 10 to 15 hours per month
duration: One year, June to May; one full council meeting a month
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 cohort were due March 15, 2026. The page says applications open again in January 2027.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 20 who live in the City of Austin or its extraterritorial jurisdiction and are eligible to work legally in the U.S. No academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Online application (about 1.5 hours), short-answer questions, and one reference who completes a recommendation form. Accepted members become City of Austin employees and must verify work eligibility.
notes: Meetings are held at locations around Austin and transportation help may be available.

name: Teen Volunteers (Volunteens)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Regular volunteers: at least 6 months preferred. Volunteens: summer program.
deadline_text: Varies by branch. The page says Teen Volunteens are recruited in the spring and gives no application dates.
who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Libraries prefer a commitment of at least six months for regular volunteers.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch you want. Volunteers are recruited, interviewed and trained at the local branch.
notes: Not every branch recruits teens, so call first. Volunteer jobs can involve lifting boxes of books and standing for a while.

name: Baltimore City Youth Commission
pay_detail: Not stated on the city page.
duration: Term lasts until December 2028 for current members
deadline_text: No application window is posted. Two district seats (2 and 6) were shown as vacant in the member list.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25. The city page lists seats by council district. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Contact the liaison, Tyron Rice, trice@baltimorecity.gov, 443-827-8421, to ask about open seats and the application.
notes: Members are appointed by the Mayor. Seats are limited, so ask before applying. Check the commission website for the current application.

name: Baltimore Conservation Leadership Corps (BCLC)
pay_detail: Not stated on the Civic Works page. Teens apply through the YouthWorks summer jobs application.
duration: 5 weeks
deadline_text: The page still says enrollment for 2025 opens in April. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students from Baltimore City. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Complete the Baltimore City YouthWorks application, then the BCLC application linked on the Civic Works page.
notes: The Civic Works page looks out of date (it mentions 2025). Check the page in spring, or use its Contact Us page, before relying on dates.

name: Teen Service Learning (Be Involved, Teen Advisory Boards, Buddies)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service-learning hours.
duration: Be Involved is drop-in. Teen Advisory Board and Buddies dates are not posted on this page.
deadline_text: Be Involved is drop-in with no application. Teen Advisory Board and Buddies dates are not posted on this page.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page's teen event filter lists ages 14 to 17. Be Involved is open to any teen at any branch. Teen Advisory Boards and Buddies use applications.
how_to_apply: For Be Involved, check the events calendar and drop in. For Teen Advisory Boards or Buddies, contact your local branch. Questions: yfe@bcpl.net.
notes: Older BCPL announcement pages were not available, so past application windows are not confirmed here.

name: Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline or rolling-application language is stated on the page. Applicants should be prepared for a placement interview.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 who work well with kids and teens and are comfortable talking with the public.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application and send it to the Volunteer Coordinator (volunteers@mdsci.org). Expect a placement interview.
notes: The page links two different youth application PDFs, so ask which one is current. Schedule and hours are not posted. Contact: 410-545-5940.

name: Pre-College Summer Intensive
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $3,850 for 2 weeks or $7,700 for 4 weeks. Commuter $2,725 for 2 weeks or $5,450 for 4 weeks. Scholarships are available.
duration: 2 or 4 weeks (2026: about July 12 to Aug 8)
deadline_text: Summer 2027 dates are coming soon. Tuition is due only after acceptance.
who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 17. Apply with a portfolio of art or design work.
how_to_apply: Online application (a fee applies), submit work samples, then deposit if accepted. Email precollege@mica.edu with questions.
notes: Prices are the 2026 amounts from MICA's 2026 payment page. The main page does not list tuition amounts. Prices for 2027 are not posted. The main page says to submit 6 pieces of work.

name: Summer Academy of Actuarial and Mathematical Sciences (SAAMS)
org: Morgan State University, School of Computer, Mathematical and Natural Sciences
pay_detail: No cost to attend. Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Friday
deadline_text: Application dates are not posted. Students hear a final decision by late May.
who_can_apply: Students about to enter 11th or 12th grade. Recent graduates must plan to study actuarial science at Morgan in the fall. The application is competitive. Students who are considered get a phone interview.
how_to_apply: Apply through the SAAMS program. Some students get a phone interview. Email msusaams@morgan.edu for application updates.
notes: The FAQ says there are no additional costs or fees beyond travel to and from campus for the last week, and it does not say who pays that travel. Phone (443) 885-3964. Check the page for the application window.

name: Youth Exhibit Guide Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. $40 fee for registration and materials if accepted (need-based scholarships are available).
duration: About 6 weeks of volunteering after a training week (2026: June 29 to Aug 9)
deadline_text: Applications for summer 2027 open in December 2026 (exact day not posted). 2026 interviews were held in late February and early March.
who_can_apply: Local high school students who finished 9th grade, are interested in marine biology or environmental science, and can do the full program including the training week and the shifts.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in December. Selected students come to an in-person interview with Aquarium volunteer staff.
notes: Training week is required (2026: June 22 to 26). The page lists both 12 shifts over six weeks and at least 10 shifts across five weeks, so ask which applies. Closing date for 2027 not posted. Students do not work directly with animals except at the Living Seashore exhibit.

name: Branches Paid Internship
pay_detail: Paid. The rate is not stated on the page.
duration: A fall session, Monday to Thursday 4:30 to 6:30 pm (the 2025 session ran Sep 30 to Dec 18)
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Branches Fall 2026 session are open now. No closing date is shown. The session dates on the FAQ are from 2025.
who_can_apply: Baltimore City high-schoolers, per the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Branches Fall 2026 application on the Parks & People page. Contact Sophie Poirier, sophie.poirier@parksandpeople.org, 410-448-5663 x108.
notes: Held at 2100 Liberty Heights Avenue, Baltimore. The page also mentions a summer job part. Ask about the summer and spring sessions. The Branches page says applicants must be able to apply for a work permit, must attend all in-person sessions, and that a family orientation is required. The foundation phone is (410) 448-5663 and the email is info@parksandpeople.org.

name: Teen Library Board
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service learning hours. Dinner is provided at meetings.
duration: 8 months (November to June)
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications closed. Members are told by October 16, 2026. The page says to check back in the spring for 2027-28 applications.
who_can_apply: Teens who live in Baltimore City and are in grades 9 to 12, and can attend the meetings.
how_to_apply: Application on the Pratt Library page when it opens in spring. Not open now.
notes: Meets 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 6:00 to 7:30 pm at the Central Library.

name: Enoch Pratt Youth Collective (EPYC)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service learning hours.
duration: 4 weekly sessions per group
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications have closed. Groups meet Oct 1 to Nov 24, 2026. The next themes and dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Baltimore City teens in grades 6 to 12. Space in each group is limited.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Pratt Library page when a new series opens. Not open now.
notes: Each series has a new theme. The page does not announce the next series.

name: TU Teacher Scholars Summer Institute
pay_detail: Free. Lunch is provided each day.
duration: 4 days, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. (2026: July 13 to 16)
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened in February 2026 and the session ran July 13 to 16. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students interested in teaching. Applicants are selected.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Towson College of Education page when registration opens, likely in February. Contact Assistant Dean Omari Jackson, 410-704-3877.
notes: The 2026 Towson news notice says the program is free, with free daily lunch. The one-credit course is Exploring Careers in Education.

name: Research and Mentoring Program (RAMP)
org: University of Maryland School of Medicine (UMB)
pay_detail: Summer parts can be paid through YouthWorks. Up to $500 for the school-year research rotations.
duration: 2 years: 5 weeks in July and August, about 10 school-year sessions, then a second 5-week summer
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2026-2027. The next window is not posted.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Baltimore City with a strong interest in biology, chemistry, medicine or related fields.
how_to_apply: See the RAMP page for the application process when it reopens. Teens also need a YouthWorks application for pay.
notes: Held on the UMB campus in downtown Baltimore. Scholars earn Stop the Bleed and CPR/AED certifications in summer one.

name: Summer Enrichment Academy (SEA)
pay_detail: Standard prices range from $374 to $499 depending on the course.
duration: 1 week per course
deadline_text: Summer 2026 is over. The page says to check back soon for Summer 2027 registration. In 2026 the one-week sessions ran June 22 to July 31.
who_can_apply: Middle school and high school students. The page gives no age or residency rule.
how_to_apply: Register online on the UMBC SEA page when 2027 registration opens.
notes: The page lists extendedlearning@umbc.edu as the contact. The original link now redirects to youthprograms.umbc.edu.

name: High School Media Classes (Video, Photo, Animation, Illustration)
pay_detail: High school students who attend at least 50% of classes can get a pro-rated stipend (a W-9 form is needed).
duration: Fall 2026 high school classes: Sep 28 to Dec 11 (no classes Thanksgiving week)
deadline_text: The fall 2026 high school session ran Sep 28 to Dec 11. No next session dates are posted. Registration is required, and if a class is full you can sign up for the waitlist.
who_can_apply: High school students. Priority goes to Baltimore City residents and Baltimore City Schools students. Some spots are held for Baltimore County students. Others are considered if space is left.
how_to_apply: Register through Wide Angle (registration is required for all students). Email the programs team or sign up for their newsletter for the next registration.
notes: Wide Angle follows the Baltimore City Schools calendar.

name: MediaWorks Summer Intensive
pay_detail: Described as a paid summer intensive. The rate is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No 2027 dates posted on the program pages.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21. The page does not give a residency rule for this program.
how_to_apply: Contact Wide Angle through their programs page. The details are not listed on the page.
notes: Wide Angle has also been a worksite for Baltimore YouthWorks (a lead, not confirmed here). Ask them how MediaWorks is funded and how to apply.

name: YouthWorks Summer Jobs
org: Baltimore Mayor's Office of Employment Development
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2026 (up to 5 hours a day, 5 days a week, 25 hours)
duration: About 5 weeks (June 29 to July 30, 2027)
deadline_text: 2027 youth application: January 4 to February 27, 2027. Program runs June 29 to July 30, 2027.
who_can_apply: Baltimore City residents ages 14 to 21 (age counted as of mid-March of the program year). Needs identity and work authorization papers.
how_to_apply: Apply online in the YouthWorks portal and upload ID, work authorization and tax forms. Under 18 also needs a Maryland work permit signed by a parent. Applying early does not guarantee a job.
notes: Pay of $15 and the work permit rule come from the 2026 pages. The 2027 pay is not posted yet. Help desk (410) 545-1820. Credit recovery classes can also be a paid worksite.

name: Bard on the Beach Volunteer Program
org: Bard on the Beach Shakespeare Festival
pay_detail: Unpaid. Every 25 hours earns ticket codes and access to dress rehearsals.
duration: Mid-May to mid-September, shifts of 2 to 5 hours
deadline_text: Applications are closed until early 2027.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Can give at least 25 hours between mid-May and mid-September. Basic English.
how_to_apply: Apply when the page reopens. Then you do a 30 minute interview. Orientation is in early April. Training runs April to June.
notes: The day it reopens is not posted. Contact the Volunteer Coordinator through the page.

name: BART Summer Internship (high school)
pay_detail: $20 per hour (high school, 2026)
duration: June 22 to July 31, 2026, 10 to 20 hours a week
deadline_text: 2026 program ran June 22 to July 31, 2026. Direct applications are not accepted. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.

name: Green Teen Community Gardening
org: Cornell Cooperative Extension of Dutchess County
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated.
duration: Hired three times a year: spring, summer and fall
deadline_text: Applications are released on the Green Teen Facebook page in February, May and September.
who_can_apply: Urban youth in Beacon. The page does not list exact ages or other rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the program's Facebook page for the application. Questions: 845-831-4287.
notes: Ages and pay are not on the page, so ask first. Program site: Beacon Recreation Center, 23 West Center Street, Beacon.

name: Teen Library Council
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit. The number of hours is not stated on the program page.
duration: Meets twice a month
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Teens. The program page does not state an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. The library's main phone number is 503-644-2197.
notes: The council meets on the first and third Thursdays, 5 to 6 PM, at Beaverton City Library Main. Members must attend meetings and events.

name: RISE Youth Leadership Program
org: Tualatin Hills Park and Recreation District (THPRD)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work. It can count for school community service hours.
duration: At least 80 hours within a year.
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page. Online trainings are held monthly, with more before summer.
who_can_apply: Youth age 13 and older. You must agree to give at least 80 hours of service within one year of starting. You must attend an initial training held online.
how_to_apply: Fill out the RISE Youth Leader application online. Then attend the virtual training. Questions? Call Melissa Marcum-Fredrick at 503-619-3941.
notes: The same page lists a Junior Lifeguard program for ages 12 and up. It also lists community and cultural events for ages 14 and up.

name: Berkeley High CTE Pathways
fields: health; law-government; arts-media; tech-cs; engineering; trades
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Choose pathway classes during course selection.
who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g rules for getting into college. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.

name: Berkeley Humane Volunteer (teens 12 and up)
deadline_text: No volunteer application deadline is posted, and the page does not say whether orientation sign-ups are ongoing. Internships are 18+ only and are available year-round.
who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

name: Berkeley Pre-College Scholars (Summer Sessions)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $15,987 (8 weeks, June 22 to Aug 14) or $14,687 (6 weeks, July 6 to Aug 14). There is also an application fee. One media scholarship was offered in 2026.
duration: 6 or 8 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 2 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.

name: Berkeley Public Library Teen Volunteer and Youth Worker

name: BLAST: Building Leaders for Advancing Science and Technology (Virginia Tech session)

It describes rising 9th and 10th graders in another place. That means the same thing, since you apply in the school year before. The page lists the window as December 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027.

name: CyberSpark cybersecurity camp (Virginia Tech)

org: Virginia Tech Department of Geosciences with the Fralin Life Sciences Institute

name: Imagination (Virginia Tech engineering camp)

name: futureBOS youth jobs (SuccessLink)

pay_detail: Youth jobs (ages 14 to 18) are paid $15 an hour; leader jobs (19 to 24) $20 an hour. Professional development programs pay a stipend.

City of Boston agency jobs can be onboarded in one visit to the YEO office at 1483 Tremont Street.

Under-18 workers need a Massachusetts work permit for the specific job (a doctor must sign for ages 14 and 15); the city page explains the steps. The $15 rate is quoted from the city FAQ. The state minimum wage statute (M.G.L. c.151 s.1) says a wage of less than $15.00 per hour is presumed oppressive and unreasonable; the current 2026 minimum wage page from the state Department of Labor Standards could not be read (403), so confirm the rate in your job offer. The work permit rule is M.G.L. c.149 s.86.

pay_detail: Full tuition, room and board. $800 stipend the first summer, $200 per week in summers two and three. $3,000 college scholarship after finishing all three summers.

deadline_text: The page does not list application dates.

how_to_apply: Apply online at Harvard Summer School when the application opens December 1, 2026. Financial aid is requested during the application.
notes: Expensive and selective. Residential financial aid is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

name: Jovenes en Accion (Youth in Action)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page.

Other ICA teen programs had no dates set. They are the Teen Digital Cooperative, and the music and photo break intensives. The page does not say whether a work permit applies.

Paid jobs under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page; not on the MGB page).

name: Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI)
grades: Designed for students entering their senior year of high school

The page does not give a final date for the summer application.
who_can_apply: Students who live or attend high school in the United States and finish the online course and the separate summer application. You must be in the US for the July program. The page lists no age or citizenship rule.

Later you need three essays of 500 words or less each. You need a teacher or mentor recommendation. You need parent or guardian information with an electronic signature. You also need to finish the online prerequisite course. Contact: bwsi-admin@mit.edu.
notes: Competitive. The cost wording on the page leaves the $200,000 to $200,001 range unclear, so ask BWSI if you are near that line. The online course is free and stays open to independent learners.

name: MIT PRIMES (math and bioinformatics research)
grades: High school sophomores and juniors (home schooled students count)
pay_detail: Free to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores and juniors who live in the US, including homeschooled students. If you live near Boston, you meet mentors on campus and use the main application. how_to_apply: Use the online application portal linked on the MIT PRIMES how to apply page. It has an online questionnaire. It asks for two or three recommenders. Math teachers or camp counselors are ideal. It asks for a personal statement of up to 2 pages. It asks for lists of math books, courses, camps and computing skills. It also asks for solutions to the PRIMES 2027 Math Problem Set. Apply if you solve at least 70 percent. Upload solutions as one PDF with your name only in the file name.
notes: Competitive and heavy on math. There is also PRIMES Circle, a spring math enrichment program. It is for students within commuting distance of Boston. how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
