name: Canadian Cadets (Sea, Army and Air Cadets)
org: Department of National Defence (Government of Canada)
city: Local corps and squadrons across British Columbia
pay_detail: The program pages do not state a cost. The program page calls it a funded program. Ask the local unit about any fees.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register online and the unit staff contact you.
who_can_apply: Young people who are at least 12 and have not reached 19. Have your health card ready when you register.
how_to_apply: Choose Sea, Army or Air Cadets. Find a unit near you in the Corps and Squadron Directory. Register with the Online Registration Tool. Have your health card and your parents' contact details ready. Then unit staff contact you to check ID and welcome you.
notes: This is a Canada-wide program. The units in British Columbia come from the national directory. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card. A youth program, not a paid job.

name: Foundry Work & Education Program (FWEP)
pay_detail: Free. This is job and school support, not a paid job. Foundry says all its services are free and confidential.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: No dates. Foundry says no referral is needed to use its services.
who_can_apply: British Columbia youth ages 15 to 24 who want to work, go to school or start a training program and face barriers to doing so. You must be legally entitled to work in BC. You should not already be working, in school or in training, or be working less than 15 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up with the online Foundry Work & Education form linked on the Foundry services page. Or find a Foundry centre near you.
notes: Foundry also gives free and confidential mental health and wellness services for youth ages 12 to 24. WorkBC also lists this program. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

name: SkilledTradesBC Youth Trades Programs (Discover, Explore, Train and Work in Trades)
org: SkilledTradesBC, with the Ministry of Education and Child Care
city: Across British Columbia (through your high school)
grades: High school students (grade and age rules are not stated on the program pages)
pay_detail: Youth Work in Trades training is paid, but no wage is stated. The youth programs page says tuition for these programs is covered. SkilledTradesBC and the Ministry fund technical training done in high school.
duration: From 1 high school course to a year-long program, depending on the program and trade
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated on the program pages. Talk to your school for dates.
who_can_apply: Students in high school. The pages give no grade or age rule. Check the Youth Train in Trades Guide and your school for rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school's career educator or work experience coordinator. Train in Trades uses a program guide and a registration form. Work in Trades signs you up as an apprentice with an employer sponsor. It uses a Youth Apprentice and Sponsor Registration Form.
notes: The British Columbia work permit rule for these jobs is not verified. Other ways to find an apprenticeship listed on the site include job boards, WorkBC centres and hiring fairs. Youth Explore the Trades lets you sample several trades. The SkilledTradesBC page, checked on 2026-10-10, is dated January 2024 and does not state a wage or say that Work in Trades is paid.

name: Skills Canada BC Competitions (regionals and provincials)
city: Regional events around British Columbia, provincials in Abbotsford
grades: Jr. Skills Projects are for grades 6 to 9. Other competitions are labelled Sec. (secondary) or PS (post-secondary).
pay_detail: No fees are listed on the program pages.
duration: Regionals in February to March 2027, provincials on April 14, 2027
deadline_text: Regionals run February to March 2027 in communities around the province, exact dates not posted yet. Provincials: April 14, 2027 at Abbotsford Tradex. Nationals: May 27 and 28, 2027 in Calgary. Registration deadlines are not listed.
who_can_apply: Students who are active at a school or college. Your teacher, instructor or career coordinator must sign you up. The exact rules are in the provincial rules document.
how_to_apply: Talk to your teacher, instructor or career coordinator. They sign you up through the Skills Canada BC registration page. It needs a password. You get it from the organization or your regional coordinator.
notes: Students cannot sign themselves up. Regional registration goes through a teacher login. The provincial rule document at skillscanada.bc.ca/competitions/rules-and-regulations/ lists exact eligibility. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

name: King Conservation Science Explorers (middle school)
pay_detail: Not stated. No cost is listed on the page.
duration: Saturdays in October and November (fall) or April and May (spring)
deadline_text: Applications open twice a year: September 1 to October 1 and March 1 to April 1. The fall 2026 window has closed. Years for future windows are not printed on the page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8. Letters of recommendation are not needed but are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the yearly application during an open window. You share your interests and recent wins. You also share your goals for college and a career.
notes: For younger teens. Eighth graders are encouraged to apply to King Scholars at the high school level. Cost is not stated on the page.

name: King Conservation Science Scholars
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include zoo access like a basic membership, ten free admission passes, and discounts. Scholars commit to at least 80 hours a year.
duration: Year-round. At least 80 engagement hours each year.
deadline_text: Applications open twice a year. Fall: September 1 to October 1 (onboarding early to mid November). Spring: March 1 to April 1 (onboarding early to mid May). The fall 2026 window has closed. Years for future windows are not printed on the page.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grade 9, 10, 11 or 12 when they apply. Spring applicants must be in grades 9 to 11. A parent or guardian must attend onboarding.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the fall or spring window. Check the King Scholars page for the application and how to prepare.
notes: The Brookfield Zoo volunteer page says its regular volunteer forms are for adults. It says this program is its chance for high school students. Grade 8 graduates can join KCLA Transitions. Grade 12 students are not accepted in spring. Scholars who take part a lot can apply for seasonal jobs.

name: Brookhaven Police Cadet Program
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Cost is not listed.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursdays 7 to 9 pm
deadline_text: No deadline is listed.
who_can_apply: Residents of Brookhaven or nearby areas, ages 14 to 18 or 19. The page says both, so confirm. You need passing grades and a clean background check. You cannot have criminal convictions or Juvenile Court referrals.
how_to_apply: Download the Cadet Application Packet and the Cadet Agreement Waiver (both PDFs) from the page. The page does not describe the steps after you turn them in.
notes: Meets at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Road. The page lists ages 14 to 18 in one place and 14 to 19 in another. There is a community service requirement. Contact Officer Hawkins through the page or call 404-637-0600. Not a paid job.

name: Brookhaven Police Teen Academy
pay_detail: Free
duration: 5 days, 9 am to 3 pm (July 20 to 24 on the page, year not printed)
deadline_text: The page lists July 20 to 24 but does not print a year or a deadline. Treat it as the yearly pattern and check for the next dates.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19 who live in or around Brookhaven. No grade is listed. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Reserve a spot with the online form on the page, or contact the department. The page says early sign-up is encouraged.
notes: Held at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Rd, Brookhaven, GA 30329. Call Officer Angela Hawkins at 678-296-1904. You can also call the Community Engagement Unit. The number is 404-637-0600, Option 8. This is unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Growing Green Youth Program
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly wage is not stated.
duration: Year-round
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page asks you to email the Youth Education Director.
who_can_apply: Buffalo youth ages 14 to 19. Other rules not stated.
how_to_apply: Email Neena Hussey, the Youth Education Director, at neena@mass-ave.org. Ask about joining as a teen employee.
notes: No application form or deadline is posted, so email first. Office: 387 Massachusetts Ave, Buffalo, NY 14213. Phone: 716-882-5327.

name: Summer Teen Naturalist
pay_detail: $360 for nonmembers, $325 for members
duration: 2 weeks, 6 days total, 10 am to 3 pm
deadline_text: The page says to check back for 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Register Online link on the program page, or call 716-837-3900 to sign up. Questions: 716-995-6143.
notes: Written proof of a negative TB test is required before the program starts, per the page.

name: Volunteer program
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 25 hours of service volunteers can get a complimentary museum membership.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
deadline_text: The page says applications for the volunteer program are open. No deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 16 years old who can volunteer at least six hours a month and is excited about Texas history and welcoming visitors.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. If it is approved you are contacted for an interview, then attend a New Volunteer Orientation.
notes: You must be 16 or older. If you are approved, they contact you for an interview. Then you go to a new volunteer orientation.

name: Burien Green Teens
pay_detail: Stipend. The amount is not stated on this page. You also get a gear kit (pants, boots, shirt, hat, gloves, tools).
duration: 2 weeks, Mon to Fri, 9 AM to 2 PM (2026: Aug 17 to 28)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran May 25 to June 25, 2026. Next year not posted.
who_can_apply: Highline Public Schools high school students at least 16 by August 17, 2026 who live, work or learn in Burien. Priority goes to those who live in Burien.
how_to_apply: Apply online. About 40 applicants get a 20 to 30 minute online interview. Info sessions were held in May and June 2026.
notes: You must be comfortable outdoors for up to 5 hours and walk 1 to 3 miles on uneven ground. Questions: education@mtsgreenway.org. The page states a $1,200 stipend for full attendance.

name: Burke Composite Squadron, Civil Air Patrol cadets
org: Civil Air Patrol, Virginia Wing (Burke Composite Squadron)
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursday nights 6:30 to 9:00
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time. Email the squadron to ask about visiting a meeting.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 (the Virginia Wing page says to be at least 12 and not yet 19, and a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident). The squadron has both teen and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email va-130info@vawg.cap.gov or call (703) 239-4530 to ask about a meeting. The Virginia Wing steps are to visit with your parents. Then go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the cadet application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Meetings are at Irving Middle School, 8100 Old Keene Mill, Springfield, VA 22152, but the location can change for school events, and in August they meet elsewhere. Meetings are cancelled on the same days Fairfax County Schools cancels. The squadron page says it won a 2021 Virginia Wing Squadron of Merit award.

name: Volunteer Program at Burnaby Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One 3-hour shift a week for at least 8 months
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page says some areas may have no openings.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older (18 for the Emergency triage role). Must give 3 hours a week for 8 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online. It takes about 30 minutes. If you are picked, you get an interview. You also need a police record check and references. Then you go to orientation and training.
notes: Call Volunteer Resources at 604-412-6130. The page was last updated on Jan 22, 2025.

name: Become a Lifeguard and Swim Instructor
org: City of Burnaby Parks, Recreation and Culture
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the program page. The page says lifeguard jobs have great pay and flexible hours but gives no rate.
duration: Several courses in a series
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register for courses online or at a pool front desk.
who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13 or older. You must swim 400 m in under 12 minutes. Bronze Cross is 13 or older. First Aid is 14 or older. Lifeguard and instructor courses are 15 or older.
how_to_apply: Check the age and skills table. Then sign up for courses with the City (WebReg). You can also ask at a rec center with an indoor pool. Email questions to the address on the page.
notes: The page says extra certificates help but are not required to be a lifeguard with the City. This covers the instructor and fitness leader certificates. Pay and job age rules are not stated. The page says courses can earn high school credits.

name: Burnaby Village Museum Volunteer Program
org: City of Burnaby, Burnaby Village Museum
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: At least 1 year and 35 hours of service per year
deadline_text: Intakes: February (spring/summer) and September (fall/winter) for costumed interpretation, school programs and events. Camps: February and April. Collections and sewing: ongoing.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. If you are under 18, a parent must say yes. You need good English, health coverage, 2 references and the right to volunteer in Canada. You must be able to walk the 10 acre site.
how_to_apply: Pick a job on the museum volunteer page. Then apply online.
notes: The page lists the intake months but not the year, so confirm the next date. The City of Burnaby volunteer page also lists Camps and playgrounds volunteering for youth 14 and older.

name: American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State)
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.
who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application. Your school recommends you. A local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. California Girls State is a separate program with its own card.
how_to_apply: In junior year, tell your counselor you want to go. Or contact a local American Legion Post. Use Find a Post on calegion.org. The Post picks its delegates. Then each delegate signs up online.
notes: Two separate programs. This one has been coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program. It ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. An old note about a 2020 article and a Sanger phone was out of date.

name: California Highway Patrol Explorer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 25 to 26, 2026.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet. This is the competition age rule. Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.
who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

name: Youth Employment Opportunity Program (YEOP)
city: California (YEOP specialists at local EDD offices)
pay_detail: No pay. The page does not say whether services cost anything.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No application dates. Contact a YEOP specialist any time.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 25 who need extra help to finish school or find work. Examples listed are offense history as a minor and teen parent. Others are foster care or no stable housing, and gang involvement or risk. Minority group, low income, and disability or reading difficulty are also listed. You may still qualify if you do not match these.
how_to_apply: The page has no separate enrollment steps. Use the YEOP Contact Information page. It helps you reach a YEOP specialist in your area. Or contact your local America's Job Center of California.
notes: The page says clearly: this is not a job placement program. It is help and coaching toward school and work.

name: EDD Employment Services for Youth (America's Job Centers of California)
city: California (local America's Job Center of California offices)
pay_detail: The services are free (the page says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost). Work experience can be paid or unpaid; no pay rate is given.
duration: Ongoing, set by each local center
deadline_text: No application dates. Visit or contact your local center any time.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 who meet certain requirements. The EDD page does not list the requirements. It points to the Youth Employment Opportunity Program page and fact sheet for criteria.
how_to_apply: Find your local America's Job Center of California with the EDD Office Locator (edd.ca.gov/en/Office_Locator/). The page also suggests building a resume in CalJOBS and visiting the center to ask about internships, apprenticeships and training.
notes: The EDD page does not say the youth services are free. It says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost. Eligibility criteria are not on the EDD page; it links to the YEOP services and eligibility criteria. Teens under 18 who take a paid job in California need a work permit from their school (CDE page).

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by park
deadline_text: The page lists no application deadline.
who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

name: California Volunteers Youth Service Corps
org: California Volunteers (Office of the Governor), run through partner cities and counties
city: California (23 partner cities, counties and tribes)
regions: los-angeles; oakland; sacramento; san-francisco; san-jose; orange-county; inland-empire; san-diego
pay_detail: At least minimum wage; the rate varies by location (page wording).
duration: Not stated on the state page; set by each local program
deadline_text: The state page does not say whether applications are open. Each partner city or county runs its own application.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 on the first day of service. You must meet at least one of: foster care, justice involved, mental health or substance abuse system, low income, hard time finding work, or unemployed and/or out of school.
how_to_apply: Pick your local program from the partner list on the state page and apply through its link. Or use the state interest form. State office: info@californiavolunteers.ca.gov (say Youth Service Corps) or (916) 323-7646.
notes: Partner list on the page: Anaheim, Antioch, Bakersfield, Chula Vista, Fresno, Irvine, La Puente, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Rancho Cucamonga, Riverside, Sacramento, San Francisco, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Cruz, South Gate, Stockton, Marin County, Monterey County, Mechoopda Band of Chico Rancheria and Ramona Band of Cahuilla. California requires a work permit for minors in paid jobs (CDE page), so under 18 you will need one. The state page does not say whether each city requires you to live there, so check the local program.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.
who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

name: Next-Gen Manufacturing Academy (High School Summer Academy)
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
deadline_text: Page says applications open in January and close in April each year. Exact 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Unpaid. Your county sets a fee, and some projects cost extra. Fee waivers are available.
duration: The 4-H year runs July to June.
deadline_text: Join any time. Animal shows at county fairs have their own deadlines.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18 by Dec 31 of the 4-H year, anywhere in California.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office on the Join page. A parent signs up in ZSuite and pays the county fee.
notes: The old ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H address now goes to this page. Projects and fees depend on your county.

name: California Cadet Corps (school based leadership program)
org: California Cadet Corps, California Military Department
grades: 4 to 12 per the program site; the state military page says grades 6 to 12
pay_detail: Free. The program site says it is fully funded by the state with no cost to families or host schools. Cadets earn up to ten elective credits per year.
duration: Ongoing school year program
deadline_text: No dates. Enrollment follows your school's schedule.
who_can_apply: Students at a school that runs a California Cadet Corps unit. Participation is voluntary. The pages do not say how a student enrolls beyond being at a host school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Cadet Corps unit. The program site says schools that want to start one should email Recruiting@cacadets.org. The site's Contact Us page is cacadets.org/about/contact.
notes: Program pages did not include a school finder, so the best first step is to ask your school office or email the program. The program site says more than 7,000 students are in over 100 schools.

name: California FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
city: California (through school chapters in six geographic sections)
grades: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Not a job. The join page lists no dues amounts.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
deadline_text: No join deadline on the page.
who_can_apply: Students at a California school with an FBLA chapter. The FAQ says FBLA is open to students enrolled in a Career and Technical Education (CTE) business program.
how_to_apply: Ask whether your school has a chapter: email hello@cafbla.org or call (714) 824-4489. If not, fill out the FBLA Interest Form so staff can help your school affiliate; that needs your school administration.
notes: You join through a school chapter, so you need a business pathway or class at your school. If your school has no business program, the FAQ says starting one has to be started with school administration.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.
who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. The pages do not state age or grade rules.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages checked.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
pay_detail: The CDE page does not say whether internships pay or give school credit. Ask the school.
duration: 3 years
deadline_text: The CDE page lists no student application dates. Each school sets its own.
who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy has its own way to apply. Look on the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy. The CDE page links a directory of academies (a spreadsheet updated September 2026). The page does not say how students apply.
notes: Read the CDE page on 2026-10-09. It confirms a three-year program for grades 10 to 12, structured as a school-within-a-school, with academics plus career technical education, business partnerships, mentoring and internships. It posts only school and district grant dates, not student application dates, and does not say whether students from other districts may transfer in. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

name: Community Teen Intern Program
pay_detail: $18.42 per hour
duration: 7 months, late October to late May. About 7 hours a week, including Saturdays and school holidays. You can keep the job each school year until you graduate.
deadline_text: Closed for 2026-27. The page says to check back in August 2027 for the 2027-28 school year.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores and juniors with at least a 2.0 GPA who live or go to school within 3 miles of the California Science Center. Seniors were not taken in the 2026-27 cycle. You must be allowed to work in the US.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program page when it opens. The page says the program is competitive. You need a work permit from your high school if you are hired.
notes: Only for teens near Exposition Park (the 0 to 3 mile rule). No science background is needed. Public speaking helps but is not required. Interns can also apply for the summer Dive Team or Flight Team. The page lists no minimum age.

name: Dive Team Interns
pay_detail: $17.87 per hour
duration: 6 weeks, full time on weekdays, 35 hours a week (June 15 to July 31 last summer)
deadline_text: Closed for Summer 2026. The page did not post application dates. Summer 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors. You need a 2.0 GPA or higher. You must go to one of three schools: Math, Science, and Technology Magnet Academy, Roosevelt High School or Mendez High School. You must be at ease in the water. You must be allowed to work in the US.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program page when it opens. The page says the program is competitive. You need a work permit from your high school if you are hired.
notes: Only students at three Los Angeles high schools can apply. Paid for by a gift from the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page lists no minimum age.

name: Flight Team Interns
pay_detail: $17.87 per hour
duration: 6 weeks, full time on weekdays, 35 hours a week (June 15 to July 31 last summer)
deadline_text: Closed for Summer 2026. The page did not post application dates. Summer 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors. You need a 2.0 GPA or higher. You must go to one of three schools: Math, Science, and Technology Magnet Academy, Roosevelt High School or Mendez High School. You must be allowed to work in the US.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program page when it opens. The page says the program is competitive. You need a work permit from your high school if you are hired.
notes: Only students at three Los Angeles high schools can apply. Paid for by a gift from the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page lists no minimum age.

name: Youth Volunteers Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, usually on the weekend, for 14 weeks (50 or more hours)

notes: School-based, so you need a teacher or school to sign up. Dates are subject to change, the museum says. The museum congratulates students on results at Illinois State History Day and National History Day. Not a job; good for building research and speaking skills.

name: Broadway Youth Center (drop-in, health and housing connections)
pay_detail: The page says services are available regardless of ability to pay.
deadline_text: No deadline. Drop-in hours are Mon 9 to 3, Tue 10 to 3, Wed 1 to 5, Thu 9 to 3, Fri 9 to 3.
who_can_apply: Anyone ages 12 to 24 can come to the center. Online appointment booking is only for ages 18 to 24, and patients under 18 cannot book online.
how_to_apply: Walk in at 1023 W. Irving Park Road, Chicago, during drop-in hours, or call 773-388-1600.
notes: Support center, not a job. The page does not mention job or school programs, so ask staff. If you are in danger right now, call 911.

name: Bronzeville Youth Shelter (emergency shelter for ages 14 to 17)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No deadline. A 24/7 help line is listed.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17 who need a safe place to stay.
how_to_apply: Call the 24/7 crisis line at 866-803-8336 or text 312-625-1858. The shelter is at 3745 S. Indiana Ave., Chicago.
notes: This is a safe place to stay, not a job. The page does not say how a teen gets a bed beyond calling the help line. If you are in danger right now, call 911.

name: Ignite employment and education program (paid internships)
pay_detail: Paid internships. The pay rate is not stated.
duration: 4 weeks of workshops, then 8 weeks of internship
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 26 who have no home or an unsafe home and are signed up with Ignite. The page does not say how to sign up.
how_to_apply: Call the 24/7 line at 866-803-8336, text 312-625-1858, or call the office at 312-568-5700. Drop-in center: 56 E 47th Street, Suite 410-C, Chicago.
notes: For teens who have no stable home. Pay, start dates and who qualifies are not stated on the page, so call first. If you are in danger right now, call 911.

name: Camp Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid service-learning. You get service hours.
duration: About 5 weeks: Session A June 8 to 26 and July 6 to 17 (none June 29 to July 3), Session B July 13 to Aug 14 (2026), plus required training days in spring
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens entering grades 9 to 13 who are 13 to 18 years old by the June start date. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Application link on the page. Two Zoom info sessions were held in Feb and March in 2026.
notes: Camp days run 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday to Friday. Required training days are in April, May and June. Teens also get up to 15 Professional Development Sessions and Teen Bonding Nights.

name: Conservation Ambassadors Board
org: Lincoln Park Zoo with After School Matters
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page. Ask Lincoln Park Zoo.
duration: Two terms a year, March to May and September to November; Saturday meetings (Feb 28 to May 9 in spring 2026)
deadline_text: Spring 2026 application opened Jan 20 and was due Feb 1. A fall term also runs. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago and go to a Chicago high school. You must be at least 16 by the program start. You must be able to come to all program dates.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the After School Matters website and apply there. Use an email you check often. Interviews follow.
notes: Meetings are on Saturdays with a few extra dates. No meetings over CPS spring break. Two absences per semester may be allowed if told in advance. The page does not say whether the board is paid. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Nature Buds Internship
org: Lincoln Park Zoo with After School Matters
pay_detail: Stipend of $17.05 per hour through After School Matters (2026 page)
duration: June to August, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application was to open the week of April 27 on the After School Matters site. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago and go to a Chicago high school. You must be at least 16 by June 1. You must be able to come to all program dates.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the After School Matters website and apply there. Rank "Lincoln Park Zoo - Nature Buds" as your top pick.
notes: Outdoor work. Shifts are four days a week. Pay rate is from the 2026 page and may change. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Malott Family Research Apprenticeship Program
grades: Entering grades 11 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday (June 22 to Aug 7 in 2026), plus a Saturday orientation
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Must live in the city of Chicago, be entering grades 11 to 12 (or a college freshman) in the fall, be 16 to 18 by the June start, and be legally allowed to work in the U.S. with proof of identity. No research experience needed.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the zoo SlideRoom link on the page. The zoo invites strong applicants to a half-day group interview in March.
notes: Introductory research program, so teens with no lab or field experience are welcome. Apprentices do not work directly with animals. You need a way to get to the zoo each day. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Malott Family Zoo Intern Program
grades: Entering grades 10 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday (June 22 to Aug 7 in 2026), plus a Saturday orientation
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago. You must be going into grades 10 to 12 (or be a college freshman) in the fall. You must be 16 to 18 by the June orientation date. You must be allowed to work in the U.S. and have proof of identity.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the zoo SlideRoom link on the page. Invited applicants go to a half-day group interview at the zoo in March. The zoo also held two Zoom info sessions in late Feb and early March in 2026.
notes: Interns do not work directly with animals. You need a reliable way to get to the zoo each day. You can apply to several zoo teen programs at once. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. Contact is listed on the page.

name: Zoo Teens events
pay_detail: Free
duration: Single events on select days through the year
deadline_text: Events: Saturday Oct 31 (Roll for Wildlife, Prism Games, Logan Square) and Saturday Nov 7 (Plants and Prints, Lincoln Park Zoo). The page has no year, but both weekdays match 2026. Register on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 from across the Chicago area. Parents are not allowed at the events.
how_to_apply: Register for each event with the Register Now button on the Zoo Teens page.
notes: Going to an event adds you to the list for news about the zoo's internships and other teen programs. Parking is at 2400 N. Cannon Drive for events at the zoo.

name: Marwen Art@Work summer internship
pay_detail: 2026: $16.20 per hour, 14.5 hours a week for 5 weeks, about $1,174.50 before taxes (may change)
duration: 5 weeks, July to August; 12 hours a week at the site and 2.5 hours at Marwen
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open in spring 2027. For 2026 they were due April 11, 2026.
who_can_apply: Chicago residents ages 16 to 18 by July 1 of the program year. You have taken at least one Marwen course. You can commit to the full schedule. You have a Social Security number or an employment tax ID.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the spring window opens. Selected teens get a 30-minute Zoom interview with Marwen staff in May.
notes: You must have taken a Marwen course first. Marwen classes are no-cost for Chicago students in grades 6 to 12 who face barriers to arts programs. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Teen Creative Agency (TCA)
pay_detail: Up to $1,600 a year
duration: Weekly sessions during the program year; exact months not stated
deadline_text: Applications open in the spring, per the page. Exact dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Chicago teens. The page says ages 14 to 19 in one place and 15 to 19 in another, so confirm the age rule with the museum.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to TCA form (Airtable) on the MCA Teens page when it opens. Questions: Ahmad Bracey, abracey@mcachicago.org, 312-397-4020.
notes: Free museum entry for anyone 18 and under. Teens can also send projects to 21Minus each winter. It is free for ages 21 and under. The page does not say if a work permit is needed. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: CPS Student Advisory Council (Mikva Challenge)
grades: Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program pages. Ask Mikva Challenge.
duration: Summer council with policy work; exact length not stated
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: A city-wide teen council. The page gives ages 16 to 18; the application page says Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders.

name: Safety and Justice Council (Mikva Challenge)
grades: Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page. Ask Mikva Challenge.

how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: The council includes young people affected by the juvenile justice system. The age range here is 16 to 20, so some members are over 18 and teens work alongside older youth.

name: Mikva Student Election Judge Program
org: Mikva Challenge Illinois with Chicago election officials

The Chicago Board of Election Commissioners website blocked our reader, so pay, age and sign-up rules there were not checked. Confirm with Mikva or the Board.

name: Mikva Summer Fellows

grades: Placed after senior year of high school

deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

notes: For young people after their senior year. The page does not state an age limit. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Teen Health Council (Mikva Challenge)

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
pay_detail: The program page does not mention pay or a stipend. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around pay.
duration: Spring, fall and winter: 8 weeks, 6 hours a week. Summer: 6 weeks, 30 program days.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who live in Chicago.
how_to_apply: Contact the staff at the park you are interested in to start the application. The process is an application, an interview, a mentoring curriculum and performance check-ins.
notes: Re-read on 2026-10-09: ages 13 to 15, Chicago residence, the apply step (contact the park) and the 2026 session dates all match the page. The page says RIT is a job readiness program and participants are not Park District staff. It does not mention pay, so the pay type was changed from stipend to no pay stated. The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older for lifeguards, recreation leaders, special recreation leaders and junior laborers. The page does not state a residency rule, so check with the Park District.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Park District job site. Use the Learn More and Apply Now links on the Summer Jobs page. Or go to a Teen Opportunity Fair. Applications must be in by the closed date on each job posting.
notes: Work permit: Illinois requires employment certificates only for minors under 16 (Illinois Dept. of Labor FAQ). All of these jobs start at 16. Teens 13 to 15 should see the Recreation Leader in Training program. Fair email: teensinthepark@chicagoparkdistrict.com.

name: Rush University Medical Center volunteer program
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 100 hours you can ask a staff member for a reference letter.
duration: At least 6 months, 4 hours a week
deadline_text: New volunteers are always welcome, per the page. No deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 17 years old who can give four hours a week, Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., for at least six months in a row. Needs TB test and MMR and chickenpox records.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the page. Rush replies by email in 5 to 7 business days. The email has steps for orientation and a health screening. Contact: volunteer_services@rush.edu, (312) 942-5574.
notes: No summer-only volunteering. No weekend or evening shifts. Volunteer Services does not offer internships or externships. Under 17 does not qualify here. The page lists general hospital numbers for Rush Copley (630-978-6200) and Rush Oak Park (708-383-9300). These are not volunteer lines. Contact Volunteer Services at (312) 942-5574.

name: SAIC Early College Program (ECP) courses
org: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
grades: High school; college credit only for those who finished sophomore year
pay_detail: Noncredit 10-week course $661; 1.0 college credit course $1,982; supplies about $50 to $200 extra. The Smith Scholarship covers 100% of noncredit course tuition for Illinois students. Limited need-based aid.
duration: 10-week courses in fall and spring; the page does not state a summer course length
deadline_text: Register online for each term. No fixed deadline stated on the program pages.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18. The 1.0 college-credit option is for juniors and seniors ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses on the Early College Program page. For the Smith Scholarship, fill out the scholarship form. Upload your household 1040 and send in three pieces of art to SlideRoom. For need-based aid, say yes at sign-up and upload the 1040 in DocuSign.
notes: Costs money unless you win the Smith Scholarship or aid. Aid is first come, first served.

name: SAIC Early College Program Summer Institute (ECPSI)
org: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,908 for 1 week, $3,816 for 2 weeks and $7,632 for 4 weeks. The page also lists housing and meal plan costs, supplies and personal spending. A $100 non-refundable tuition deposit applies to students who apply for aid or scholarships. Merit scholarships and limited need-based aid (US residents) are offered.
duration: 1, 2 or 4 weeks. 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31.
deadline_text: Page says registration opens November 1 (year not stated; (year inferred from the next cycle)). The 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31. A priority deadline is mentioned but not dated on the program page.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed their sophomore year by the time of the program. Merit scholarships are open to all students; need-based aid is for US residents.
how_to_apply: Register online when sign-up opens November 1. When you sign up, you can also apply for a merit scholarship or need-based aid.
notes: The page says registration opens November 1 but gives no year. It probably means this coming November for summer 2027, so confirm. The site menu also lists an online version (ECPOSI). Its details were not on the page.

name: Steppenwolf Young Adult Council
pay_detail: Weekly meetings appear unpaid; the page says community engagement and extra leadership work is paid. Rates not stated.
duration: Weekly Wednesday meetings at Steppenwolf
deadline_text: Page says applications are closed. Next dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students from the Chicago area. The page lists no age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the Young Adult Council page for the next application. Questions: teenprograms@steppenwolf.org.
notes: Members see Steppenwolf plays and many Chicago plays for free. Steppenwolf also runs free Step In theatre workshops and Teen Takeover nights, which have cheap tickets to shows. Join the teen email list on the Teen Programs page for updates.

name: Chicago Summer Business Institute (CSBI) Summer Internship
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. Ask the office.
duration: Six weeks
deadline_text: The portal is open Feb 1 to Mar 31 (the page gives no year but names the 2027 summer program, so expect Feb 1 to Mar 31, 2027).
who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents who are sophomores, juniors or seniors in 2026-27. You need a B or 3.0 average and a household income under $80,000 a year. You must be able to keep the daily schedule.
how_to_apply: Sign up at the apply portal. Upload your transcript, resume, essay and an income form signed by a parent or guardian. Name two people who will recommend you. Contact: info@chicagobusinessinstitute.org or (312) 545-7855.
notes: The site shows two email endings, org and com; use the org address on the apply page. The apply page does not state pay or job sites. The home page says the program was founded to provide paid summer internships and mentions placements (one student interned with the City of Chicago), but no pay amount is given, so ask the office. Two recommendation letters are needed, so ask early. Illinois work permit rule not checked.

name: CPS-UChicago Program
org: University of Chicago with Chicago Public Schools
pay_detail: $800 tuition plus $75 lifetime transcript fee (books not included) if household income is over $60,000. $0 tuition, with books and fees covered, if under $60,000.
duration: Autumn, Winter and Spring Quarters; one course per quarter
deadline_text: For 2026-27 the application opened June 8, 2026 and closed July 15, 2026. 2027-28 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must have been in CPS this year and last year. You will be a junior or senior. You have a strong record in the hardest courses you can take. You are ready for college work.
how_to_apply: Fill out an online application. It has short essays, a graded work sample, a teacher recommendation and transcripts. It also has an online interview in mid-August. For the $0 tuition option, you need financial aid papers.
notes: UChicago classes do not follow the CPS calendar, so you attend even when your high school is on break. Many students stop after Winter Quarter.

name: Chicago EYES on Cancer
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center
grades: High school sophomore, junior or senior (or college freshman or sophomore)
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $5,000 per year
duration: Two summers of 8 weeks (2027: June 14 to Aug 6, 35 to 40 hours a week) plus monthly 2 to 4 hour online sessions from Feb 2027 to Dec 2028
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Nov 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. In-person interviews Jan 4, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who are at least 16 by June 14, 2027 and live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana. College freshmen and sophomores can also apply. Must commit to both summers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in recommendations. At least one must be a teacher or professor. Up to 12 applicants are accepted.
notes: You must find your own housing and ride to UChicago. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. One application covers all the UChicago cancer pathway programs that fit you.

name: Healthcare Experience and Research in Oncology (HERO)
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend
duration: 2 weeks, July 12 to 23, 2027, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to noon CT, online
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Mar 1, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Interviews in April 2027.
who_can_apply: Full-time high school students who live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, and can attend every weekday, 4 hours a day. Up to 20 students per year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: Virtual program run with Kentucky, Michigan, Penn and UT Austin. No minimum age is listed. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for the stipend.

name: UChicago Medicine student volunteer program
grades: High school, college and graduate students
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for at least 6 months or one school year; 100 hours within a year
deadline_text: Fall window ran Aug 25 to Oct 1, 2026 (may close early). Next cycle starts Jan 10, 2027; closing date not posted.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old (some roles need 18+). Applicants for the Summer Volunteer Program must be at least 18 at the time the application is submitted. Must interview, pass health screening, a drug screen and a background check, and not hold certain visas (B-1, B-2, H-1B, H-4).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Volunteer application. Do it when a recruiting window is open. The form is in Volgistics. Then you talk with Volunteer Services in an interview. For questions, write to vservices@uchicagomedicine.org. You can also call 773-702-4421.
notes: The page says student volunteers must be at least 16, and some opportunities need 18 or older. The page says summer applicants must be at least 18 when the application is submitted. Summer applications open early March 2027. Next student cycle starts January 10, 2027.

name: researcHStart
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center with UIC, UIUC, Northwestern and Rush
grades: High school junior or senior at time of application
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $4,000
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027, 35 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Jan 11, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. On-campus interviews in February 2027; acceptance notices March 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, are at least 16 by June 14, 2027, and can commit to all 8 weeks. Max 30 students across all sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Pick your site: UChicago, UIC, UIUC, Northwestern downtown or Rush. Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: No housing or ride is provided, so pick only sites you can reach. The application asks for your GPA and a transcript. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: University of Chicago Summer Session pre-college programs
grades: High school (programs open depend on your current grade)
pay_detail: Costs in 2026: Enrichment $3,000; Career Insight $5,890 ($4,100 commuting); Immersion $9,300 ($6,100 commuting); Practicum $15,200; online 3 to 5 weeks $4,980. Need-based partial aid is offered (not full), and Enrichment fees can be waived for income under $125,000. $75 application fee.
duration: Varies by program. Online courses run 3 to 5 weeks and the language institute runs 6 to 8 weeks; the page does not state a length for enrichment.
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines: priority Feb 11, regular Mar 12 (Practicum priority only). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. The application shows which programs you are eligible for based on your current grade. Chicagoland students can choose to commute for Career Insight and Immersion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a profile, transcript, writing sample, supplement and one recommendation letter. It also needs a parent okay and the $75 fee. Test scores are not required. You may rank up to four program choices but can be admitted to one.
notes: Expensive, not a job. Apply by the priority deadline if you need financial aid. Aid is limited and first come, first served.

name: UIC Business high school summer days (Accounting, Finance, Tech and AI, Marketing)
org: University of Illinois Chicago, College of Business Administration
city: UIC, 601 S. Morgan St., Chicago, IL
grades: Entering grades 10, 11 or 12 (from the Tech and AI day page)
pay_detail: The Tech and AI day was free with breakfast and lunch. Cost for other days was not stated.

deadline_text: The 2026 programs ran June 23 to 26, 2026 and registration was full and closed. The page does not say if they will run again.

how_to_apply: Email bizsummer@uic.edu or call 312-996-2700 to ask about 2027. The 2026 events used an online registration form on the UIC events site.
notes: Seats were limited and filled. Grade and GPA rules above are from only one of the four days, so confirm before applying.

name: Windy City Harvest Youth Farm
org: Chicago Botanic Garden, Windy City Harvest, with After School Matters
pay_detail: Stipend: 4 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 hours a week in summer. Rate not stated.

deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

notes: Run in partnership with After School Matters. Confirm ages, dates and pay before relying on this. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.
who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job. The youngest age in the whole program is 14, but most summer jobs are for 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.

Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.

name: High School Summer Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: 7 weeks, 16 hours a week in 4 blocks, Monday to Thursday, 112 hours in all
deadline_text: The 2027 dates are not posted. Last cycle, the application opened Jan 26, 2026 at 4 p.m. and closed Feb 2, 2026 at 4 p.m. The program ran June 22 to Aug 6, 2026.
who_can_apply: Students who have finished their freshman year of high school and are 15 to 17 years old by the orientation date (June 14 last cycle). The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the one-week window. Write two short answers (150 words each) and one essay (300 words). Give the emails of two teachers, counselors, coaches or mentors. Then a video interview with a parent, a health screening and a full-day orientation.
notes: The window is only one week, so mark late January on your calendar. This is not job shadowing or an internship, and contact with patients who stay in the hospital is limited. You need full shot records, a TB blood test and a drug and alcohol screening. No weekend shifts. You may not miss more than one week. Questions: Volunteer Resources, 323-361-2317, Volunteers@chla.usc.edu.

name: Samuels Family LA-HIP High School Internship
org: Children's Hospital Los Angeles, The Saban Research Institute
pay_detail: Stipend, plus a Metro card and meals at the hospital. The page does not give the amount.
duration: Summer lab work, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, for 7 weeks. College counseling runs from April through senior year.
deadline_text: Last cycle the application opened Nov 3, 2025 and closed Feb 1, 2026. Offers went out in late March. The 2027 dates are not posted yet, so expect a similar window from November to February.
who_can_apply: Current juniors at a public high school in Los Angeles County. You need papers to work legally in California. You should have strong grades and a real interest in science.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need an essay, a transcript and one letter from a science or math teacher or a counselor. Your letter is only asked for after the rest is done, so finish early. Info sessions are held in November and January.
notes: Very competitive. If you accept, you must turn down all other summer programs and go to every required meeting. The page mixes dates from different years, so check it again in November. Questions: Danielle Nunez, danunez@chla.usc.edu. Ask whether you need a work permit for the stipend.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
deadline_text: Rolling.

how_to_apply: Email the East Sacramento Explorer advisor, Sergeant John Daubner (JDaubner@chp.ca.gov), or call the office at (916) 464-1450 to get an application. After you apply you need a background check and a medical exam by a doctor.

It has an Explorer section and the advisor's email. The office is at 11336 Trade Center Drive, Rancho Cordova. The eligibility rules come from CHP's careers site (linked from chp.ca.gov). Ages differ: the eligibility page says 15 to 20 and the office page says 15 to 21, so ask the advisor. Meeting times are not posted. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition.

name: Junior Ambassador Program (high school volunteers)

name: Living Coast Discovery Center Volunteer (ages 16 to 17)
pay_detail: Unpaid

how_to_apply: Submit the 16-17 volunteer application. Then go to the next orientation. They tell you about it by email.
notes: The center does not take court-ordered community service right now. If you have questions, write to volunteers@thelivingcoast.org.

name: 10x10 Teen Volunteer Team (Cincinnati Art Museum)

They are at Newport and Covington in Kentucky. There is also a Western & Southern Workforce Development Center.

Prepare a 60 to 90 second monologue from a published play written after 1950 and two songs (one from a musical written before 1970, one written after 1970). Send a 30 to 60 second video of you dancing alone.
notes: Housing is optional and costs extra. Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu. Tuition assistance may exist; ask CCM Prep.

notes: Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu.

The CRC page says ages 14 to 24 and residents of the city or surrounding communities; an older City HR FAQ says only City residents ages 14 to 18, so confirm. The CRC FAQ still lists 2019 start dates, so ignore those. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

The youth opportunities page says ages 13 to 18 may apply. It did not repeat the closed for 2026 wording. Check the status before you plan around it.
