how_to_apply: Apply online, then an interview and a health screening.
notes: You can get volunteer credit for scholarship applications. The page does not say which hospital sites take teens. Ask when you apply.

name: Colorado FFA Association
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher about dues.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your school's ag program.
who_can_apply: Students in school ag education programs. No age or grade limits are stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's agriculture teacher about an FFA chapter. Use the Chapters page to find one. The Become a State Officer page explains the state officer role.
notes: The Colorado FFA Foundation helps the group, CSU Ag Education and ag teachers. Dates and fees were not on the program pages.

name: Governor's Summer Job Hunt
org: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, with local Workforce Centers
pay_detail: The service is free. The jobs it lists set their own pay.
duration: Summer season
deadline_text: Not stated. Register at any Workforce Center.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 per the Denver city page. No income rules. You must show proof of age and U.S. citizenship.
how_to_apply: Visit any Workforce Center in Colorado to register. Bring proof of age and U.S. citizenship.
notes: The Denver page and the Jefferson County workforce page both say ages 14 to 24. The state page (cdle.colorado.gov/jobs-training/youth/gsjh) would not load. If you are 14 or 15, call your local Workforce Center to check the age rule.

name: Forge and Form Summer Studio (Mines Labriola Innovation Hub)
org: Colorado School of Mines, Labriola Innovation Hub
pay_detail: $850, lunch included. Bring a laptop if you can; loaners are available.
duration: One week, 9 AM to 4 PM. 2026 sessions: July 13 to 17 and July 20 to 24.
deadline_text: The 2026 applications closed March 1 at 11:59 PM MST. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are at least 16 during camp.
how_to_apply: Apply online; the 2026 page lists a waitlist form. Questions: innohub@mines.edu.
notes: The page blocked our reader, so it was read through a page summary tool. Confirm the cost and dates on the Mines page.

name: Colorado Springs Chief's Youth Advisory Council
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Meets once a month
deadline_text: Dates are not stated on the page. Use the Download Applications link on the page.
who_can_apply: High school students across Colorado Springs. The page does not list ages or a deadline.
how_to_apply: Download the form on the city page. Send it as shown. Email ira.cronin@coloradosprings.gov with questions.
notes: A news story said under 18 students need a parent signature. That detail is not on the city page, so ask the contact.

name: Space Ambassador Volunteer (Space Foundation Discovery Center)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: At least two shifts a month, Tuesday through Saturday
deadline_text: The page says it is still taking applications. The museum plans to reopen in January 2027.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old. A background check is needed if you are 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the page. Call 719-319-3678 or email volunteer@spacefoundation.org with questions.
notes: You can apply while the museum is closed. The museum plans to reopen in January 2027.

name: Summer Teen Volunteering (Colorado Springs Parks)
org: City of Colorado Springs Parks, Recreation and Cultural Services
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Several weeks. Hours differ by job.
deadline_text: Most jobs show 2026 dates only. Rock Ledge Ranch spots were filled for 2026, and its application window was March 1 to 21. The Pioneers Museum Junior Docent lists June to August 2027, with applications due early May 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages depend on the job: 10 and up for Junior Docent at Rock Ledge Ranch, 13 and up for Spray Ground Assistant, Teen Volunteer and Therapeutic Recreation Discovery Camp roles, and 15 and up for Junior Park Docent at Garden of the Gods and Junior Docent at the Pioneers Museum.
how_to_apply: Register on the page for the job you want. Junior Park Docent at Garden of the Gods signs up by email to gardenofthegods@coloradosprings.gov. Some jobs need an interview and training.
notes: Junior Docents at the Pioneers Museum earn a $300 Education Stipend at the end of the summer if they do at least 40 hours. Teens ages 12 to 15 can only volunteer from 7 am to 7 pm in the school year, and until 9 pm in summer. North Cheyenne Canon teens must finish the free online Leave No Trace 101 course.

name: Colorado Youth Advisory Council (COYAC)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says lodging and meals are provided at the retreat and travel money is available for the Capitol day.
duration: Two year term. Monthly virtual meetings on the second Thursday, 7:45 to 9:15 PM.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 to 2027 are closed. The page says applications open again in spring 2027 for the group that starts July 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19. You go to a Tribal or Colorado school (online or charter too). Or you are in a home based, high school equivalency or diploma program.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in spring 2027. Contact COYAC to get a notice when applications open.
notes: The COYAC site blocked our page reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. The retreat for the current group is August 29 to 30, 2026 in Denver; the Day at the Capitol is March 1, 2027.

name: Teen Volunteering at Bexley Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
deadline_text: The page says the teen volunteer program is currently full and that applications for summer volunteering will open April 1. No year is shown.
who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 13 years old or in grades 7 to 12 during the 2026-2027 school year. The page says the teen program is currently full.
how_to_apply: Email teen@bexleylibrary.org to join the teen volunteer email list. That is how you hear about openings. The summer application opens April 1.
notes: The page says the library is postponing adult volunteering for now. Call the youth department with questions.

name: Youth Advisory Council (health grants)
pay_detail: No pay stated. Time can count toward community service hours needed to graduate.
duration: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: The page posts no deadline and does not say whether applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. It does not confirm 2026-2027 membership.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12 who live in the Columbus area can join.
how_to_apply: Download the member form from the page. Email it to youthcouncil@cmafohio.org. You can also mail it to the Youth Advisory Council Coordinator at 1390 Dublin Road, Columbus, OH 43215.
notes: Time can count toward the community service hours you need to graduate. Ask the foundation if seats are open for 2026-2027. Email youthcouncil@cmafohio.org or call 614-240-7410.

name: College Credit Plus at Columbus State
pay_detail: Courses and textbooks are free for public school students. Transportation and other costs are the student's.
duration: Semester courses
deadline_text: Public school students must submit a Letter of Intent to their high school by April 1. Homeschool and non-public students apply for state CCP funding by April 1. The page does not state the year of the next deadline.
who_can_apply: Ohio residents in grades 7 to 12. New students need a 3.0 unweighted GPA, or ACT or SAT scores that qualify, or Columbus State placement test scores that qualify. Middle schoolers must take the reading and writing placement tests. They must reach the needed score in at least one area.
how_to_apply: Give your school a Letter of Intent. Apply to Columbus State. There is no fee or essay. Finish online onboarding. Show that you meet one of the eligibility rules. Then sign up for classes with your counselor.
notes: The college application asks you to have your Social Security number ready. Use a personal email, not a school email. Send your unofficial high school transcripts or ACT/SAT scores to your CCP advisor.

name: Ready 2 Earn (Franklin County summer youth jobs)
org: Franklin County Job and Family Services with partner nonprofits
pay_detail: Ages 14 to 15: $1,500 stipend plus up to $300 in incentives for finishing the 6 weeks. Ages 16 to 18: wages up to $15 per hour.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications were listed as full at every partner. Dates for summer 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21 in Franklin County. In general, families must meet the income rules for TANF cash help. Ages 14 to 15, 16 to 18 and 18 to 21 have their own tracks.
how_to_apply: Apply through one of the partner groups on the county page. They are Columbus Urban League, Godman Guild, Lead the Way Learning Academy, Nationwide Children's Hospital and Saint Stephen's Community House. Each lists its own phone and email.
notes: Check the partner pages in winter. The county page says nothing about work permits. Nationwide Children's and Columbus Urban League already have their own cards in this guide. Godman Guild and Lead the Way phone numbers are on the county page: 614-294-5476 and 614-915-0434.

name: Godman Guild Youth and Young Adult Workforce Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the Godman Guild pages. The Franklin County Ready 2 Earn page lists a stipend for ages 14 to 15 and wages for ages 16 to 18 through its partners.
duration: Monthly sessions Nov 2026 to May 2027. Summer 2026 Ready 2 Earn ran 5 weeks and 60 hours.
deadline_text: The page has a Youth and Young Adult Workforce Program interest form but does not say whether it is open now or has a deadline. Monthly events run from Nov 18, 2026 to May 6, 2027. Summer 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: The page says the program serves young adults in grades 9-12 and after high school graduation. Exact age rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth and Young Adult Workforce Program interest form on the Godman Guild page.
notes: Events listed: Entrepreneur Night Nov 18, Community Service Dec 3, Resume Building Jan 27, Public Speaking Feb 24, Money Skills Apr 7, Showcase May 6. Phone 614-294-5476. The Godman Guild site has an older Ready 2 Earn link that gives a 404. Use the teen page.

name: Volunteer Program (teen volunteers ages 16 and 17)
pay_detail: Unpaid. New volunteers pay a one-time $50 mission investment.
duration: 4 hours a month minimum
deadline_text: The page gives no registration deadline and does not say when sign-ups open.
who_can_apply: Teens 16 and 17 can volunteer on their own. A guardian must sign a Junior and Teen Volunteer Waiver and Release. Ages 12 to 15 can join only as junior volunteers, with an adult volunteer partner over the age of 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the New Volunteer Registration form. Then use the emailed link to book an in-person STEPS orientation in Hilliard. Next, finish species training and mentoring. Then start to book shifts.
notes: The FAQ lists a junior option for ages 12 to 15. It needs an adult volunteer partner over 21. Email volunteer@columbushumane.org with questions.

name: Summer Reading Challenge VolunTeen
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: June 1 to July 31 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: 2026: application opened April 13 at 3 p.m. and the program ran June 1 to July 31. 2027 dates are not posted. The library's regular volunteer application for Fall 2026 opened August 10.
who_can_apply: Youth in or entering grades 6 to 12 who are at least 12 years old. High school students 18 or older must be returning to a traditional high school and may need a background check.
how_to_apply: Online VolunTeen application, first come first served by branch. If your branch is missing from the drop-down, it is full.
notes: Openings vary by branch. Current or recent youth volunteers should talk to the Summer Reading coordinator at their branch. The library also has School Help, Reading Buddies and Creation Station volunteer roles; the page lists the age rule only for the summer VolunTeen role. Ohio's work permit rules for unpaid public library volunteering are not stated on the page.

name: Metro Parks Volunteer Program (Junior Volunteers at Inniswood)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Flexible schedule by assignment and park
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Volunteer Information sessions are held twice a year; the Inniswood training is held in March.
who_can_apply: Most assignments are for ages 16 and up. Ages 11 to 15 can help only at Inniswood Metro Gardens, as Junior Volunteers. The Inniswood training is in March.
how_to_apply: Attend a Volunteer Information session and complete the volunteer application. A background check including fingerprints is part of the process.
notes: Slate Run Living Historical Farm lets children volunteer with a parent or supervising adult. Scouts can set up group service days by email. For Inniswood contact the volunteer coordinator at 614-895-6226.

name: Volunteer with Mid-Ohio Food Collective
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up for open shifts any time.
who_can_apply: Sort and pack and the Kitchen are for ages 13 and up. Markets and kids' meals are 16 and up. The garden is 16 and up, or 14 and up with a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Click Find an Opportunity on the volunteer page and pick a shift on the volunteer sign-up site. Groups use the group button on the same page.
notes: Sort and pack is in Grove City (3960 Brookham Drive). Other sites have no address on the page. Call 614-277-3663 with questions.

name: Mount Carmel Health Teen Program (volunteer)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: One shift (about 4 hours) a week. Summer: weekdays 8 am to 4 pm. School year: weekday evenings 4 to 7 pm or weekends 8 am to 8 pm.
deadline_text: The Teen Program runs year-round. No deadline is listed.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. A parent or guardian must take part in the TB test step.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online part of the Teen Program form. Mail or hand in the paper part to Volunteer Services. Then you interview and take a TB test. You go to a volunteer orientation and a unit orientation.
notes: Sites listed: Mount Carmel Dublin, East, Grove City, St. Ann's and New Albany. Phones: East 614-234-6658, Grove City 614-663-6700, St. Ann's 380-898-4097, New Albany 614-663-6334. Completing the application does not guarantee a spot.

name: CMA//Next Teen Program
pay_detail: $1,250 stipend, paid in two installments
duration: Select Saturdays, Sept 26, 2026 to May 30, 2027
deadline_text: The application for the 2026-27 session has closed. The page says to stay tuned for future opportunities and gives no new dates.
who_can_apply: "Arts-interested youth." The page gives no age or grade rule. Selected teens join a cohort.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Call the museum at 614-221-6801 or watch the page for the next call.
notes: Meetings are at CMA Short North, CMA at The Pizzuti and the Broad Street location (480 East Broad Street). Ages are not stated, so confirm with the museum before you plan on it.

name: Teen Studio (free, ages 13 to 19)
pay_detail: Free; includes museum admission
duration: Every second Thursday, 5 to 7 pm. Teen Studio: Unwind is quarterly, 5 to 7 pm.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Specific dates for Unwind are not listed on the program page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19. Free registration; drop-ins are welcome.
how_to_apply: Register for free on the museum events listings, or drop in.
notes: Teens 13 and older can also visit the museum on their own at any time, per the page.

name: Teen Volunteering at Nationwide Children's Hospital (summer)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: 10 weeks, June to mid-August, one 2 to 3 hour shift a week
deadline_text: The 2026 application opened February 2, 2026 and has reached capacity. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens who are 15 by June 1 and currently in high school. Competitive, with limited spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Get references who are not family to fill out an electronic form. Go to a group interview. Sign a commitment form. Send your shot record, including flu. No waivers are allowed. Then finish an online orientation and training for your job.
notes: You can miss no more than 2 shifts. You need to be there 80 percent of the time. Contact Family and Volunteer Services at 614-722-3635 or Volunteering@NationwideChildrens.org. The page has no direct application link.

name: OhioHealth hospital volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. The background check, TB screening and flu shot are free for volunteers.
duration: Ongoing. The page does not set a number of hours.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. At Riverside Methodist, the steps from applying to starting take 6 to 8 weeks.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up when you apply. Some roles need you to be 18. You need a Social Security number or ITIN, a background check, shot records (MMR and chickenpox), a TB screening and a yearly flu shot.
how_to_apply: Pick a hospital on the OhioHealth volunteer site. Fill out the online form. Then you have a reference check, training and an orientation for new volunteers. Hospital volunteers wear a uniform.
notes: Hospitals on the list include Riverside Methodist, Grant, Doctors and Dublin Methodist. Others are Grove City Methodist, Pickerington Methodist, Westerville and Grady. The rest are Berger, Marion General, Mansfield, Shelby, Hardin and O'Bleness. OhioHealth also has SARNCO and HomeReach Hospice volunteers. This card does not cover them.

name: STEM Institute (Ohio Supercomputer Center)
pay_detail: $600 per student ($60 per day) for housing, meals, tuition, trips and insurance. OSC says the real cost is about four times that.
duration: 2 weeks, June 6 to 17, 2027
deadline_text: Applications open January 15 and close April 1, 2027. Accepted students are told in April.
who_can_apply: Ohio residents in their freshman, sophomore or junior year of high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online STEM Institute application when it opens. Email si-contact@osc.edu.
notes: Two phone numbers show on OSC pages, so email is safer. The page says OSC pays much of the cost. It says there are no one-on-one scholarships. The program used to be called the Summer Institute.

name: Arts and Sciences Summer Exploration Program
org: The Ohio State University College of Arts and Sciences
grades: Entering 10 to 12 for high school courses (7 to 9 for middle school courses)
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per one-week course, with lunch and snacks. The 2027 fee is not posted.
duration: 1 week per course
deadline_text: Check back in early January 2027 for the summer 2027 course list and registration form.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2027 can take high school courses.
how_to_apply: Make a free account in the online application system. Then apply. Sign up for updates on the page to learn when applications open.
notes: Questions: ExploreASC@osu.edu or 614-292-6390. The page says some need-based aid may be available. Ask for it on the program application. Other department camps are on the department summer page. They cover philosophy, language science, humanities and mind science.

name: HRS Camp (Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, Ohio State)
org: School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, The Ohio State University
pay_detail: Free for students. Breakfast and lunch are provided.
duration: 3 days, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran June 1 to 3, 2026. The page lists an April 24 deadline (no year given, matching the 2026 dates), decisions April 27 to May 8, and orientation May 28. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: All high school students interested in a career in healthcare. The page gives no grade, age or residency rule. A parent or guardian must attend the required orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application (Apply Now form on the camp page). Use the Contact Us link on the camp page for questions.
notes: Free and short, so a good first health-career step. Watch the page for 2027 dates.

name: Humanities and Cognitive Sciences Summer Institute (HumCog)
org: Center for Cognitive and Brain Sciences, The Ohio State University
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page. It says financial aid, including partial and full scholarships, is available.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 program ran July 13 to 17, 2026. All 2026 materials were due May 31, 2026, with decisions by June 14. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the next application.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10, 11 or 12. A student who just finished freshman year can also apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send a high school transcript, a personal statement and a note from a teacher.
notes: The page has a few date mix-ups (one spot says 2025), so confirm the 2027 dates and cost with ccbs@osu.edu.

name: MD Camp at Ohio State
org: The Ohio State University College of Medicine
pay_detail: Tuition is $325. Full and partial scholarships are given based on need and application quality.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran June 8 to 26, 2026. 2026 applications were due March 17, 2026 (late ones not accepted). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ohio residents who will be high school sophomores, juniors or seniors and want a health career. The page suggests a 3.0 GPA overall and 3.3 in math and science. You also need two letters of support. One must be from a math or science teacher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks about school and other activities, essays and a transcript. You also need two signed letters of support. They are sent through a separate form.
notes: You must find your own housing and rides. The page only covers 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting.

name: Ohio State Wexner Medical Center K-12 health care career exploration
org: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center
pay_detail: The page does not say if there is a cost or pay.
duration: Varies; shadowing is a one-time visit and internships repeat
deadline_text: Student experiences run during the school year only. Schools should send requests at least 60 days ahead.
who_can_apply: K-12 schools ask for these experiences, not students or parents. Central Ohio schools and schools with a Workforce Partnerships agreement come first. Internships need a recommendation from a school district staff member.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or career teacher to fill out the request form on the page. The medical center asks that parents and students do not send requests for their school. New Workforce Partnerships agreements are full right now.
notes: You must be 18 to volunteer at this hospital. So for teens, this school route is the way in. Internships can be in nursing, imaging, lab work, rehab, sports medicine and research.

name: Young Scholars Program (Ohio State)
org: The Ohio State University Office of Undergraduate Education
pay_detail: No cost stated for the program. Ohio State financial aid is offered after graduation if requirements are met.
duration: Grades 8 through 12
deadline_text: The page says applications are accepted from prospective 8th graders each year. The 2026-27 deadline is not stated on the part of the program page.
who_can_apply: Ohio residents in 8th grade at Columbus City Schools, Cincinnati Public Schools or seven other listed city districts. You must be the first in your family to go to college. Family income must be under the limit. You must earn mostly A grades.
how_to_apply: Apply in 8th grade through the Young Scholars Program page. Questions: YSP@osu.edu.
notes: Only 8th graders can start. The page says there are no costs for the pre-college portion.Other districts on the list: Akron, Canton, Cleveland, Dayton, Lorain, Toledo and Youngstown. Check the page for the income table and the current deadline.

name: Student Volunteers at Pickerington Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid. A VolunTeen Scholarship is open to high school students with outstanding volunteer service.
duration: On-going, 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week.
deadline_text: The page lists no volunteer application deadline and does not say whether applications are accepted year-round.
who_can_apply: Student volunteers must be at least 12 years old or in grades 7 to 12. You must have a Pickerington Public Library card and go to an orientation. You must keep a steady schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for about 3 months or longer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply to Volunteer link on the volunteer page. Then go to an orientation. The Volunteer Coordinator runs it.
notes: Two locations: Pickerington Main Library and Sycamore Plaza Library. Homework Help is open Monday to Thursday, 3 to 6 pm, in the school year. The VolunTeen Scholarship form is open December 1 to January 30.

name: APPS Job Readiness Program
pay_detail: $15 an hour, up to 20 hours a week
duration: Mostly summer; some participants may continue in fall and winter
deadline_text: 2026 participant applications ran Feb 2 to Feb 17, 2026 and are closed. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Columbus residents (or people who pay Columbus taxes) ages 14 to 23. Must pass a drug test; a background check applies at 18 and older. Required documents: birth certificate and/or Social Security card, plus a state or school photo ID.
how_to_apply: Apply during the winter window listed on the program page. If you have questions, email AJRP@columbus.gov or call 614-724-2038.
notes: Work experiences vary and are matched to career interests where possible. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. The page does not say how to submit the application beyond the schedule, so confirm the method with the program.

name: City Leaders Academy
pay_detail: No pay; cost not stated on the page
duration: Sept orientation, then 12 monthly meet-ups Oct 2026 to May 2027; ceremony May 15, 2027
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Wednesday, July 1, 2026. 2027-28 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: City of Columbus residents (getting City trash and recycling service counts) entering grades 6 to 10 in Fall 2026 who keep a 2.8 GPA. Selected applicants interview with the program directors.
how_to_apply: Email the application, last school year's report card and a letter from a teacher, administrator or community leader to CBMcGhee@columbus.gov, or drop it at Blackburn Community Center (263 Carpenter St.). Selected applicants interview.
notes: Includes middle schoolers (grades 6 to 10). There is a mandatory guardian and youth orientation on Sept 19, 2026. You can miss no more than three meet-ups without an excuse. The page says applications began May 1, 2025. That looks like a typo for 2026.

name: Seasonal Lifeguard
pay_detail: $20 an hour (seasonal)
duration: Summer season; dates not stated
deadline_text: The City says it is currently hiring lifeguards for seasonal positions. The page gives no closing date and no season dates.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older with the swimming skills needed. Must finish the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course (the City waives the course fee if you are hired). Completing the course does not guarantee a job.
how_to_apply: Submit the Lifeguard Interest Form, take the pre-course swimming skills test, finish the Red Cross course, then submit the employment application.
notes: The City also offers Red Cross lifeguard training for ages 15 and older. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) says school-age minors need an age and schooling certificate (work permit). In the summer, 16 and 17 year olds can show the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead.

name: Ross Mathematics Program (Otterbein University site)
pay_detail: $7,500, covering tuition, housing and meals. Financial aid is offered for students who need it.
duration: 6 weeks (summer 2026: June 14 to July 24)
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application window has closed. Summer 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Pre-college students who are passionate about mathematics. First-year students range in age from 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Ross Program website when the window opens. Email ross@rossprogram.org with questions.
notes: The page lists two sites. One is Otterbein University in Columbus, OH. The other is Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology in Terre Haute, Indiana. The 2026 dates were June 14 to July 24. Ask about 2027 dates when they are posted.

name: TECH CORPS Computing Career Corps and IT On Ramp+
pay_detail: $15 per hour for IT On Ramp+ (6 weeks), per the Franklin County page. Pay for Computing Career Corps is not stated, but students earn Work Based Learning hours.
duration: IT On Ramp+ is 4 weeks, full day. Computing Career Corps meets weekdays 9 am to 3 pm.
deadline_text: The page lists IT On Ramp+ sessions June 1 to 26 at Whitehall-Yearling High School and July 6 to 31 at Franklin Heights High School. The page gives no year. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: 9th and 10th graders. The county page says IT On Ramp+ is for TANF-eligible Franklin County 9th and 10th graders.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the TECH CORPS Work-Based Learning page. Phone 614-583-9211, email info@techcorps.org.
notes: The county page lists a 6-week length and $15 per hour for IT On Ramp+; the TECH CORPS page lists 4 weeks. Ask TECH CORPS which is right for the next session. Ages are not stated, only grades 9 and 10. The TECH CORPS page gives no pay.

name: Summer Writing Camp Interns
pay_detail: Unpaid. Thurber House can sign off on service hours. Interns provide their own transportation and lunch.
duration: Monday to Friday, at least 1 week (camp runs 8 weeks)
deadline_text: The page does not post an application deadline or interview dates. Contact Meg Brown by email.
who_can_apply: High school and college students. The page does not state a minimum age or grade.
how_to_apply: Email Meg Brown. She is the Director of Children's Education. Her address is megbrown@thurberhouse.org.
notes: The page says counselors must be 21 or older and gives no minimum age for interns. Confirm the age limit by email.

name: Teen Summer Writing Intensive
pay_detail: $825 (includes all fees, snacks, a journal and a t-shirt). Payment plans on request. A very limited number of scholarships are given by lottery (you pay a $25 registration fee to enter).
duration: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday (July 20 to 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 registration closed July 6, 2026. The page says to check back in the new year for 2027 information.
who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade through rising college freshmen.
how_to_apply: Register online. For a scholarship, click "applying for a scholarship" in the online registration. Questions go to Meg Brown (megbrown@thurberhouse.org).
notes: Bring a sack lunch.

name: Young Writers' Studio (teens, grades 9 to 12)
pay_detail: $17 per session, with a discount for the whole season. A limited number of scholarships are available.
duration: 6 evening sessions, 6:30 to 8:30 p.m.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 sessions are on Tuesdays: Sep 1, Sep 15 and Sep 29 have passed. Oct 13, Oct 27 and Nov 10, 2026 are still ahead. The page has a Register button but no deadline and no closed notice. It does not say whether you can still join mid-season, so check with Thurber House before you plan on it.

who_can_apply: Current 10th and 11th graders at a district-run CPS school; priority goes to 10th graders. Must attend an information session and submit a recommendation from a trusted adult who is not a family member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google application form, a signed Student and Parent Expectations and Consent Contract and a Recommendation Form, then email everything to ChicagoBuilds@cps.edu.
notes: It is an Illinois Works Pre-Apprenticeship site and offers the Master Builder program with City Colleges of Chicago. Classes meet during the school day in an AM or PM cohort. Contact: 773-534-0909.

name: CPS Cooperative Education (senior-year work study)
pay_detail: Students earn wages; the rate is not stated on the page.
duration: One school year, at least 180 hours a semester (about 10 hours a week); 3 elective credits
deadline_text: Students must apply during junior year. Application dates not stated on the page.
who_can_apply: High school seniors at least 16 years old with a 2.0 GPA, excellent attendance and a counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply in 11th grade through your school; contact the citywide Cooperative Education coordinator (773-553-2108) for the process.
notes: Placement and training partners listed on the page include Genesys Works and Urban Alliance. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age is 16. Cutting school or work can cost credit.

name: CPS Early College: dual credit and dual enrollment at City Colleges of Chicago
org: Chicago Public Schools and City Colleges of Chicago
pay_detail: Free college credit. The page says you earn college credit for free.
duration: Per semester; dual enrollment is one course per semester at a City Colleges campus
deadline_text: Register once per academic year. Deadlines not stated; talk to your counselor early.
who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled at a Chicago Public Schools high school, including home-schooled students per City Colleges. A 2.5 GPA and strong attendance are typical requirements. If your GPA is lower, the page says recommendation letters are accepted. Under 16 needs a principal recommendation and approval from the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, get approval from the dual enrollment coordinator at your City Colleges campus, complete the City Colleges application and pick classes. Do not pay for or enroll in a class before talking to the Early College team.
notes: Undocumented students are eligible (CPS page). Some courses need ACT, SAT or City Colleges placement scores; many courses have no prerequisites. Jumpstart Pathways and Runway 606 are related CPS options. Seven campuses; each has a dual enrollment coordinator.

name: Chicago Police and Firefighter Training Academy (CPFTA)
org: Chicago Public Schools with Chicago Police, Fire and City Colleges
grades: Apply in 10th grade; program runs 11th and 12th grade
pay_detail: Free: uniforms, materials, snacks and transportation help provided; scholarships possible. A paid summer internship between junior and senior year is possible (pay not stated).
duration: Two years; Tuesday and Wednesday 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., September to May
deadline_text: The application for the class of 2028 is closed. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February; recruitment events run in February and March. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in the city of Chicago. A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and a background check.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February. Provide 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and pass a background check. Questions: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.

name: California State Summer School for the Arts (CSSSA)
org: California State Summer School for the Arts (state program)
city: California (the 2027 campus is not named yet)
pay_detail: Tuition and fees for California residents were $5,174 for 2026; 2027 rates 'will be posted soon'. Need based aid is available to California residents (nearly half of past students had much of tuition covered). $20 application fee, with fee waivers for students with financial need.
duration: About one month: first day of classes July 5 and graduation July 31, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 application opens in November (timeline lists Nov 1, 2026). Application and scholarship priority deadline is Feb 28, 2027, 6 pm, with no extensions. Session: registration July 3, classes July 5, graduation July 31, 2027.
who_can_apply: California residents in grades 8 to 12. Up to 20 students from out of state and other countries may also be enrolled. Each department has its own assignments.
how_to_apply: Apply online by department. A full application has the form and two teacher references, not peers. It has an unofficial transcript and department assignments. It has the $20 fee. It has the financial aid request if you want aid. Students can apply to more than one department. Each needs a full application.
notes: Students who finish can get 3 units of college extension credit from the California State University system (per the FAQ). Not a job. The pages did not name the 2027 campus, so check before planning travel.

name: STEM Research Experience (CU Boulder Science Discovery)
org: University of Colorado Boulder, Science Discovery
pay_detail: The page does not post the cost yet. Limited scholarships for students with financial need; say so on the application.
duration: June 2 to July 30, 2027; 15 to 20 hours a week
deadline_text: Application opens mid-December 2026. Deadline March 16, 2027 at 11:59 PM MT. Notified by March 23, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 by June 2, 2027, with no exceptions. It is a commuter program with no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Admission is competitive. Payment is due when you accept. Contact Steven Denham (email link on the page).
notes: No refunds after you enroll. Students match with CU Boulder mentors in May and at orientation on June 2, 2027. Poster session July 30, 2027.

name: Science Discovery Summer Classes for High School (CU Boulder)
org: University of Colorado Boulder, Science Discovery
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.
duration: One week per class. The 2026 classes ran June to July.
deadline_text: The page refers to high school classes for summer 2026. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Open to all high school students, including rising 9th graders. Classes at CU Anschutz Medical Campus are for grades 10 to 12 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through Science Discovery when the next season opens.
notes: The same page lists STEM Pathfinders (two weeks, bioscience June 1 to 12, 2026, engineering July 13 to 24, 2026) for the 2026 season. Check the price and 2027 dates on the program page.

name: Pre-Collegiate Development Program (CU Denver)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.
duration: Multi-year. Summers: 2 weeks after 10th grade, 5 weeks after 11th grade.
deadline_text: No dates are posted. Contact the program manager before completing any forms.
who_can_apply: Ninth graders through high school juniors. You must be a first-generation college student (neither parent finished a 4 year degree). You must attend a target high school. You need at least a 2.5 GPA (freshmen without a GPA are asked to apply). You also need one more thing listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Call or email the program manager first. Norma Marquez, 303-315-7070, PCDP@ucdenver.edu.
notes: The 5 week summer program has college credit classes (ENGL 1020 or ENGL 1010) and fast track math.

name: College Now
pay_detail: Free. The CUNY page describes College Now as a FREE program.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
deadline_text: Each campus sets its own deadline. CUNY says spring applications are typically available October to early February, summer March to June, and fall late March to mid-September.
who_can_apply: Students at NYC public high schools. Grades 11 and 12 with an 80+ GPA can take courses on the partner campus. A 70+ GPA opens some courses. Grade 10 with a 70+ GPA can take non-credit college and career awareness courses, student development courses, and a few gateway college credit courses in some programs. College Now is for NYC Public Schools 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply to a specific CUNY campus's College Now program. Talk to your school's College Now liaison if your school has a partner campus, or contact a campus program directly. Many programs are first come, first served.
notes: Graduating seniors cannot join summer sessions. Students in Early College high schools can only join in summer. Costs beyond tuition (like textbooks) are not described on the CUNY page, so ask the campus.

name: Cupertino Leaders in Training (LIT)
org: City of Cupertino, Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says payment is collected after you are accepted, and your spot can be taken back if fees are not paid on time. The fee amount is not stated on the page.
duration: Volunteers are encouraged to help for 4 to 8 weeks in the summer, after a required in-service training week.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 closed on Friday, March 27, 2026. The page says the next application opens in February 2027. The 2027 closing date is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Teens who will be at least 14 by the first day of in-service training. The page describes it as a program for Cupertino teens. No other residency or school rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The form opens in February. It has a few extra questions. Staff pick teens by their answers, a talk with staff, and the weeks they are free. If you get in, you get a TB test and fingerprints, pay the fee, and sign forms. Ask Robert Kaufman: robertk@cupertino.gov.
notes: You must attend the in-service training week and get yourself to and from program sites. Program assignments come out in late May. The 2027 dates are based on last year's pattern. The page does not list the fee, so ask before you apply.

name: Cupertino Recreation Event Volunteers (REV)
org: City of Cupertino, Parks and Recreation
duration: School year. Members help at 2 or more major events and 2 or more minor events, and go to monthly meetings.
deadline_text: Recruitment is open now. Applications are reviewed four times a year, around September, December, March, and May.
who_can_apply: Students in 9th to 12th grade for that school year who are at least 14. No residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, including two short questions (300 words max each). You hear back after the next review period.
notes: Some events fall on holidays, weekends, and evenings. Members who do more events are recognized at Bronze, Silver, and Gold levels.

name: Cupertino Techie Teens
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. If picked, you pay $30 to cover fingerprinting, a program shirt, a name tag, and training materials.
duration: In 2026: training on June 8, then a 2-hour shift every week from June 10 to August 7.
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application closed Friday, March 27, 2026 at 4 p.m. The page says the next application opens in February 2027. The 2027 closing date is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Anyone ages 14 to 18 may apply. You must be at least 14 by the first day of training. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Send the form, the signed volunteer agreement, and your answers to a few extra questions. Staff pick teens by their answers, a talk with staff (mid April in 2026), and the times you are free. Late forms are not taken.
notes: You must attend all training, be fingerprinted and cleared, and bring your own ride (VTA and Silicon Valley Hopper are options). Staff can sign off on service hours. 2027 dates will likely follow the 2026 pattern.

name: Cupertino Teen Commission
duration: Two-year staggered terms
deadline_text: The city page says recruitment is currently closed. No reopening date is stated.
who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are in 7th to 10th grade now. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday. It meets in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term. The 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.

name: Cupertino Youth Activity Board (YAB)
org: City of Cupertino, Parks and Recreation
duration: One school-year term (for example, the 2027-28 term).
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 term closed Sunday, May 3, 2026. The page says applications for the 2027-28 term open in March 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 for the next school year. Anyone in those grades may apply. Students who live in Cupertino get picked first.
how_to_apply: Answer four short questions (up to 300 words each). Send one letter from someone who is not family, on their work paper, to robertk@cupertino.gov. Share a one minute YouTube video about you. It can be private or unlisted. Late items are not taken.
notes: Past events: Hack Cupertino, Pizza and Politics, a teen speaker series and the Cupertino Spelling Bee. Members plan an event about every other month. The 2027 last day is not posted. Last year it closed in early May.

name: Zoo Crew Teen Volunteers at Dakota Zoo
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens buy an $11 Zoo Crew t-shirt and need a zoo membership. The membership price is not listed on the program page.
duration: Summer. At least 12 hours in June and July and 5 hours in August. Monthly meetings on the first Tuesday, 6 to 7 pm.
deadline_text: No start date or application deadline is listed on the program page.
who_can_apply: Middle and high schoolers ages 13 to 17 as of June 1. Each member needs an individual or family zoo membership and an up-to-date tetanus shot.
how_to_apply: To apply, call (701) 223-7543 ext. 3. Or send an email to educate@dakotazoo.org. Ask for the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Ask the zoo when the next sign-up opens.

name: Town of Danville Volunteer Program
org: Town of Danville Recreation, Arts and Community Services
pay_detail: Volunteer role.
duration: One-time events or longer projects
deadline_text: New chances are posted through the year. Each posting shows its own dates.
who_can_apply: Volunteers 12 years and up. If a posting has its own age rule, it is listed in that posting. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Volunteer Agreement.
how_to_apply: Make a volunteer profile on the town website. Look at the open events and service projects. Sign up for one. For a long project, you send an interest form and town staff contact you.
notes: The Teens page says the town has volunteer chances for ages 13 and up. The volunteer page says 12 and up. Check each posting. Verification of community service hours is emailed by request after a volunteer event.

name: Danville Youth Council (DYC)
org: Town of Danville Recreation, Arts and Community Services
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: Monthly meetings, September to May
deadline_text: The page does not give application dates for 2026-27. It lists the 2025-26 meetings: second Monday of the month, September to May, 4:30 to 5:30 PM.
who_can_apply: Any Danville resident can join. So can any student enrolled in a Danville middle school or high school. The page gives no age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Danville Youth Council application. It is an online form linked on the program page.
notes: Meetings are at the Town Offices, 500 La Gonda Way, Danville. The Teens page says the Town is recruiting for part-time positions in youth and teen programming. It does not give an age for those jobs.

name: Lifeguard Training, Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor
pay_detail: Summer 2026 fees: Lifeguard Training $275, Junior Lifeguard Training $185, Junior Swim Instructor $100. Check the current Rec Guide or online registration for new prices.
duration: varies by course
deadline_text: Courses are offered throughout the year. Check WebTrac for sessions.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the class. On day one you take a swim test. Swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes with only your legs, then swim 50 yards. You also bring up a 10 pound brick in a timed test. Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor are for 11 to 15 year olds. Junior Lifeguarding has a swim check on day one.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: These classes can lead to city pool jobs. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later. You may get to volunteer after the class. The page does not promise a job. To get a lifeguard card, you must come to every class and pass the tests. City lifeguard jobs start at 15. Swim teacher jobs start at 15, or 14 if you did Junior Swim Instructor. That is from the 2026 job posts. See the City of Davis Seasonal Lifeguard and Swim Instructor Jobs card.

name: Davis Junior Basketball Coach, Official and Score Keeper
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: $17.39 an hour
duration: 6-week season starting the week of January 18, 2027
deadline_text: The posting is open continuously. Mandatory training is the week of January 4, 2027 and a coaching clinic on January 9, 2027.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.

name: Rec Leader in Training (RLIT) and Outdoor Education Camp Volunteers
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: Unpaid, and there is a program fee. Summer 2026 fees: RLIT $247 (Session 1) or $264 (Session 2). Returning RLIT $66. Outdoor Education Volunteer $122, paid only after you are accepted.
duration: RLIT 2026: Session 1 June 15 to July 2, Session 2 July 13 to 31, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., with week three spent volunteering at a camp (about 30 hours, 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.). Outdoor Education Volunteers work at least three weeks between June 15 and August 21.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 dates are not posted. Last cycle: summer 2026 registration for camps and programs other than Camp Putah, Trekkers and Horse Camps opened Wednesday, March 11, 2026 at 7:00 a.m. for Davis residents. Outdoor Education Volunteer applications were due Friday, March 27, 2026 by 4:00 p.m.
who_can_apply: RLIT: ages 13 to 15. Returning RLIT: ages 13 to 16, only if you finished RLIT before and were invited back. Outdoor Education Volunteer: ages 14 to 16 in the Summer 2026 RecGuide (the 2026 Summer Camp Handbook says 13 to 16); you need your own bike and helmet and must ride at least 10 miles a day. RLITs must clear a local records check.
how_to_apply: RLIT: sign up on the city's WebTrac site when summer sign ups open. Returning RLITs must be approved first. Outdoor Education Volunteer: fill out the online form. The link is on the city's volunteer page. Then go to a group interview. Questions? Call 530-757-5626 or email csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: These facts come from the Summer 2026 Rec Guide and the 2026 camp handbook. The summer 2027 guide is not out yet. After RLIT, you go on a list for more volunteer hours. You may be asked back as a returning volunteer. The city's paid camp leader job starts at 15. So RLIT is a good first step. You need a bike and helmet for RLIT and Outdoor Education. Davis residents sign up first. Others sign up the next Monday. As of Oct 16, 2026, the volunteer page did not list camp volunteers.

name: City of Davis Seasonal Lifeguard and Swim Instructor Jobs
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services (Aquatics)
pay_detail: 2026 rates: Lifeguard $17.83 to $18.27 per hour. Swim Instructor $16.97 to $17.39 per hour. Temporary part-time, no benefits.
duration: 2026 pool season: May 18 to September 7 for lifeguards. Swim lessons ran May 18 to August 16, 2026.
deadline_text: No aquatics job is posted as of Oct 16, 2026, and 2027 dates are not posted. Last cycle: the Lifeguard (2026) and Swim Instructor (2026) postings both opened Jan 28, 2026. Lifeguard closed Apr 12, 2026 and Swim Instructor closed Apr 21, 2026. Expect new postings around late January 2027. A separate Off-Season Lifeguard posting ran Dec 3, 2024 to Jan 31, 2025.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard: 15 or older. You must pass a swim skills test before you start. When hired, you need Red Cross Lifeguard Training with First Aid, CPR and AED. You also need First Aid for Public Safety (Title 22). Swim Instructor: 15 or older, or 14 if you did the city's Junior Swim Instructor class. You must be at ease in the water. You need some time spent with kids. Babysitting, tutoring, camp or volunteering counts.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Paper forms are not taken. If you get an interview, lifeguards must turn in their cards. The best fits get an interview, alone or in a small group. Everyone who applies hears back by email.
notes: 2026 mandatory trainings: lifeguards the weekend of May 16 and 17 and the week of June 15 to 18; swim instructors May 2 and 3 and June 15 to 18. You must be free on those dates to be considered. Lifeguard shifts fall between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., any day of the week, and planned vacation is capped at 14 days and must be approved before summer. To get certified first, the city's Red Cross Lifeguard Training course needs you to be 15 by the last day of the course (summer 2026 fee $275, per the Summer 2026 RecGuide). The Off-Season Lifeguard job (fall to spring) needs weekday morning and noon availability. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.

name: Davis Senior High CTE Pathways
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Enroll through your counselor during normal course selection.
who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab. See the Internship and Career Development Course.
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.

name: City of Davis Summer Camp Recreation Leader Jobs
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: 2026: $16.97 per hour (Community Services Specialist I). Temporary part-time, no benefits.
duration: June through August. 2026 camps ran ten weeks, June 15 to August 21, Monday to Friday. Summer Playgrounds shifts fall between 7:30 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. (schedules vary).
deadline_text: No camp job is posted as of Oct 16, 2026, and 2027 dates are not posted. Last cycle: Summer Playgrounds Recreation Leader (2026) opened Feb 16, 2026; the posting listed a final filing date of Friday, Feb 27 or until filled, and a closing date of Mar 3, 2026. Recreation Leader, Outdoor Education (2026) opened Feb 19, 2026 with an application deadline of Mar 16, 2026 or until filled. In 2025 these jobs opened Feb 4 and Jan 22. Expect new postings around late January to February 2027.
who_can_apply: Summer Playgrounds camps (Rainbow Summer, Summer Quest, Kids in the Kitchen, Arts and Crafts, Kinder Camp, PM Kids Club, Teen Camp): 15 or older before camp starts. Outdoor camps (Camp Putah, Summer Sampler, Backyard Adventures): 16 or older. You must own a bike and ride up to 10 miles a day. Both jobs need CPR and First Aid cards before camp starts.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Paper forms are not taken. Good fits get an email to set up an interview. In 2026, Summer Playgrounds picks had to be free on Friday, March 13 for a group interview day.
notes: In 2026, all staff had to come to training on June 6. More trainings ran June 1 to 13. Staff also met on Monday or Tuesday nights in summer and took online trainings. Other leader jobs open to teens: Inclusion Recreation Leader (2025 post: 15 for level I, 16 for level II, open Jan 22 to Apr 1, 2025). There is also a fall leader job for the Davis Children's Nutcracker. It needs you to be 15 with a work permit and pays $16.97 an hour. The 2026 post ran Aug 31 to Sep 28, 2026, and the work runs Nov 9 to Dec 13. Senior leader and Camp Putah leader jobs need you to be 18 or a high school grad. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.

name: Teen Leadership Council
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period was extended to Oct 2, 2026 and is now closed. The next call is not posted.
who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.

name: Summer High School Volunteer Program
city: Washington, DC (main hospital, Michigan Avenue NW)
grades: Current high school student returning in the fall (not a rising 9th grader, not a senior)
pay_detail: Unpaid. At least 50 service hours.
duration: 6 weeks, 2 shifts a week (Tue/Wed or Wed/Thu), 10am to 3pm
deadline_text: The application is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027. 2027 session dates are to be determined.
who_can_apply: 15 or older by the start of the program, and a current high school student who returns to high school in the fall. The page does not set a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Online application with one professional reference (name and email).
notes: Located in Washington, DC, so it is a commute for Maryland teens. Check back in February 2027 for the application.

name: De Anza College Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply for admission before the quarter you want; see the De Anza academic calendar.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.

name: DECA (high school division)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join anytime through your advisor.
who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.

name: DECA high school chapters and competitions
grades: High school (grade levels not stated on the page)
pay_detail: Membership cost is not listed on the page. Ask your chapter advisor.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your school chapter any time. 2026-27 national events: Ultimate DECA Power Trip Nov 20 to 22, 2026 (Louisville KY); Sports and Entertainment Marketing Conference Jan 27 to 31, 2027 (Orlando FL); International Career Development Conference Apr 17 to 20, 2027 (Anaheim CA).
who_can_apply: Students at schools with a DECA chapter. A school without one can request a new chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask the DECA advisor at your high school. If there is no chapter, use the Start a Chapter link on the page or contact info@deca.org or (703) 860-5000.
notes: State groups run the local contests. This guide already lists California, Georgia and Illinois DECA. Dues, travel and conference costs were not on the page, so ask your advisor.

name: DeKalb County Fire Rescue Explorer Post 901
pay_detail: $50 yearly fee, due after you are fully admitted. Not a paid job.
duration: Year-round, with a 2-week summer Cadet Training
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Meeting times are not listed.
who_can_apply: DeKalb County youth ages 14 to 18 who are in school. You keep at least a C average and have good attendance and behavior.
how_to_apply: Get the DCFR Explorer application packet from the page. Send it in with 3 job references and your latest report card.
notes: Contact frexplorers@dekalbcountyga.gov. Not a paid job, so no work permit.

name: Teen Advisory Board (DeKalb County Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours for attending meetings.
duration: Monthly meetings for the school year; at least one meeting must be in person
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-2027 school year are closed. The page does not say when the next application opens.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who live in DeKalb County.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps; check the library's Teens Get Involved page and volunteer page for the next cycle.
notes: Meeting dates were listed as coming soon. Members can miss a meeting by telling advisors through Slack or the pre-meeting survey. A search result also described a separate Teen Library Board Trustee seat, but that was not on the page.

name: DeKalb Parks Youth Sports Support Volunteer
org: DeKalb County Recreation, Parks and Cultural Affairs
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Ongoing. Weekday afternoons and Saturdays.
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteer any time.

name: Junior volunteer program at Del Sol Medical Center

name: Delaware Valley Job Corps Center

A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Teen Studio at the Denver Art Museum
pay_detail: $450 for museum members and $500 for nonmembers for a full-day workshop. One full scholarship is offered per camp.

notes: Costs money. The 2026 scholarship applications are closed. The Story in Focus workshop is full and has a waitlist, according to the program page.

pay_detail: Unpaid

notes: Also on the page: Junior Counselor Program for ages 13 to 15 (1 full week of camp, Monday to Friday 8:30 to 4:30). Also Gardens Teen Leaders, a school year group for teens who finished the summer program. The page gives no exact ages for the summer program. It only says high school.

name: Job Shadowing Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short shadowing experiences
deadline_text: The application was closed after July 31, 2026. The page says it is expected to reopen in early November 2026 for winter break shadowing.

how_to_apply: Apply online when the application reopens. All required documents must be in by the deadline.
notes: Denver Health is at 777 Bannock Street, Denver. Students who cannot shadow can look at the MC2 internship (rising juniors).

name: Medical Career Collaborative (MC2) High School Internship
org: Denver Health with Children's Hospital Colorado
city: Denver metro and Colorado Springs, CO
pay_detail: Paid internship. The hourly rate is not stated on the page.

notes: Sites are Denver Health and Children's Colorado at Anschutz in Aurora. Others are in Broomfield, Highlands Ranch and Colorado Springs. Contact marisa.valeras@dhha.org. Or call 303-602-2685.

name: Mayor's YouthWorks Initiative

name: Teen Science Scholars

pay_detail: $1,803 per session in 2026. The page says it is to cover expenses, not wages.

who_can_apply: Sophomores or juniors (the page ties this to the 2025-2026 school year). Ages 14 to 17 during the internship. You must be free Monday to Friday for a full session. It is for high schoolers from underserved or underrepresented communities or schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens. Pick your top two tracks and a session, and give your household income and size. No transcript or recommendation is needed.
notes: The museum site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. Out of state students can apply if they are at the museum for the whole program. Housing is not provided. RTD buses are free for riders 19 and younger. Phone 303-370-6478.

name: Denver Parks and Recreation Lifeguard Training and Hiring

notes: The pay and steps were read through a page reader, so confirm the pay on the city job posting. The page says the city needs early morning and daytime guards who can work year-round.

name: Denver Parks and Recreation Volunteers: Free Youth Meals and Recreation

notes: The page says all volunteers must be at least 15, finish an application and pass a background check. It also lists other jobs, like park clean-ups and mountain park projects. It gives no age rule for those.

name: ArtLab Paid Arts Internship

notes: Orientation is each August. Interns stay for one year.

pay_detail: Unpaid. Snacks are provided.

how_to_apply: Fill out the TAB interest form. Then follow up with the branch you want to join.
notes: Meetings are in person or online at some branches. The program runs only in English right now. Questions: tab@denverlibrary.org.

name: Teen Volunteering at Denver Public Library

notes: The main volunteer page says most roles are for adults 18 and older, but teen roles exist. Positions fill up, so email the volunteer office to ask when more open.

name: Western National Roundup (4-H and FFA contests)

name: Teen Volunteers at the Animal Rescue League
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

name: Des Moines Art Center Teen Arts Academy and Teen Clay Academy

name: Summer Concurrent Enrollment (DMACC Career Advantage)

name: Youth and Young Adult Services (IowaWORKS, WIOA Youth)

deadline_text: The program page still shows 2026 dates: group interviews on March 26, April 7 and April 11, and training on April 18. The volunteer page says applications will reopen in early 2027. Exact dates are not posted yet.

name: Des Moines Parks and Recreation Lifeguard Class and Seasonal Jobs

notes: The Dec 4 to 6 class date is shown without a year on the program page. Iowa work paper rules for teens were not checked. Summer camp staff jobs may have a higher age limit, so confirm before you apply.

name: Summer Camp Sidekick Volunteer (Polk County Conservation)

how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and one more set of questions. Then do an online training and orientation. Staff will contact you after they get your form. Send questions to heidi.anderson@polkcountyiowa.gov or call 515-323-5360.

name: Youth Corps Crew Member (Polk County Conservation)

who_can_apply: Crew members are ages 14 to 18 in Polk County, Iowa. You must be able to work outside in all kinds of weather and get yourself to a daily meeting site.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the next application. For questions, email youthcorps@polkcountyiowa.gov.
notes: Summer 2026 sessions ran June 8 to 26 and July 13 to 31. The program provides transportation, a daily snack, lunch on Saturdays and all summer days, safety gear, and uniform shirts. Crew members are paid for days they show up to work.

name: Des Moines Public Library VolunTeens

name: Concurrent Enrollment for High School Students at Diablo Valley College

who_can_apply: High school students, including home-schooled students. You need a Special Admissions Recommendation Form each term. You, a parent, and your principal or their designee must sign it. Students on an F-1 international visa cannot be in high school and DVC at the same time.

name: Discovery Cube Los Angeles Teen Volunteer
