deadline_text: Teen application is closed right now. The page says to check back on December 1, 2026 for winter/spring 2027 details.
who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need service hours that are checked. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.

name: Internship and Career Development Course
fields: any; health; education; engineering; law-government; arts-media
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. 2026-27 sites are listed now.
who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.

name: Douglas County Young Adult Employment Program (DCYEP)
pay_detail: Services are free. Paid internships are offered, but the pay rate is not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Virtual information sessions are held three times a month. October 2026 sessions are Oct 1, Oct 23 and Oct 28.
who_can_apply: Douglas County residents ages 15 to 17, or ages 18 to 25 with a minor in the household. The minor does not have to be related to you. You need U.S. citizenship or lawful presence. Household income must be $75,000 a year or less.
how_to_apply: Use the interest form linked on the program page to see if you are eligible. Virtual information sessions are held about three times a month. You can also call 720-874-5130 or text 720-853-1837.
notes: Only for Douglas County residents. The office is in Centennial, south of Denver. Other help includes GED support and tuition help for short job training.

name: Lyman Woods Volunteers (camp and program helpers, ages 14 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: Camp volunteers help during the summer. Other roles are ongoing.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Call 630-963-9388 for Lyman Woods volunteer details.
who_can_apply: Camp volunteers and general program volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Other roles do not list an age on the page. Everyone fills out a volunteer waiver. The page says teens to seniors can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lyman Woods application for the role you want. Also fill out the volunteer waiver. Program and camp volunteers send in an application and go to an interview and training. A criminal background check is only for program volunteers 18 or older.
notes: REAP restoration workdays need an RSVP. The park district also runs Counselor in Training (C.I.T.) camps for teens. The teen camps page lists no CIT sign-up fee; it lists only a $5 or $10 per-camp withdrawal service fee. Ages for most teen camps are not listed.

name: Lamont Summer Academy
org: University of Denver, Lamont School of Music
pay_detail: Residential $2,850. Commuter $2,000. Commuter PLUS $2,200. There is also a $75 application fee. Almost 70 percent of students get aid.
duration: Two weeks, June 16 to 29, 2027
deadline_text: The program page lists three dates for the 2027 session: Dec 15 for priority decisions, Feb 15 for scholarship consideration, and Mar 15 for regular applications. The page does not write the year.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 18. You send audition videos. Composers send three original works.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload audition videos and pay the $75 fee. Ask one teacher to email a recommendation. For need-based aid, email a tax form.
notes: This costs money, but scholarships exist. You must meet the Feb 15 date to be considered for them.

name: City of Dublin Volunteer Program (Community Programs, Special Events, Sports Leagues)
org: City of Dublin Parks and Community Services
duration: Community Programs: ongoing, a set day and shift weekly, every other week or monthly (Senior Center shifts are usually 2 to 4 hours). Special Events: one-time shifts. Sports: one season.
deadline_text: Ongoing. The Community Programs Volunteer posting opened Aug 13, 2026 and lists no closing date.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for Community Programs, Special Events and Sports Leagues. You do not have to live in Dublin. Volunteers under 18 need a signed parent consent form. Younger kids can join park cleanup projects with an adult.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the city's volunteer posting (you make a free account). Staff review your application within 2 business days and reply within 8 business days. Then go to orientation and start your shift. Questions: recreation@dublin.ca.gov or (925) 556-4500.
notes: The city guide says Splatter (September) has short shifts that are good for teens. Volunteer coaches must have AED certification. Staff can write a letter verifying your hours for school or clubs; allow 5 to 7 business days. The Special Events listing on the volunteer page said 'currently unavailable' on Oct 16, 2026.

name: Dublin L.E.A.D. Summer Program
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.

name: Dublin Library High School Teen Program Proposals
duration: One program you lead. Presentation dates are set later.
deadline_text: The fall window closed Oct 19, 2026. The next window is May 17 to June 21, 2027, for programs in October 2027 to January 2028.
who_can_apply: Students in high school with a program idea. Programs must be free, open to the public and non-commercial. You may not sell or promote products or collect attendees' contact info.
how_to_apply: Fill out the library's online Program Proposal form, linked on the event page, before the window closes. A proposal does not guarantee a spot.
notes: The page does not say if presenters are paid; treat it as unpaid. Library programs are booked at least 3 months ahead. The proposal windows open on the third Monday of their months. Questions: dublin@aclibrary.org or (925) 803-7252.

name: Dublin Police Services Teen Academy
pay_detail: Free.
duration: One week. In 2026 it ran June 8 to 12, 9 a.m. to noon.
deadline_text: 2026: applications were due Friday, May 29 at 5 p.m. for the June 8 to 12 session. 2027 dates are not posted yet. Expect a late May deadline again.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 interested in criminal justice. You must pass a background check and have parent consent. Up to 25 teens.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form linked on the Teen Academy page. Questions? Call the Crime Prevention Unit at 925-833-6677 or 925-833-6686.
notes: It used to be called the Youth Academy. The 2026 form is on the city site. A new form will likely go up for 2027. The police office is at 6361 Clark Avenue, Dublin.

name: Dublin Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
grades: Enrolled in middle school or high school
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 seats are filled (term June 2026 to May 2027). The city page does not post a recruitment date for the 2027-28 term.
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.

name: Duke Cell Biology Academy (CeBA)
org: Duke University Department of Cell Biology
pay_detail: $2,400 awarded on completion of the program
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 31), about 9 am to 5 pm on site
deadline_text: The page says Summer 2026 applications are closed and Summer 2027 applications will be accepted in January 2027. 2026 deadline: the flyer says March 20, 2026 and the FAQ says March 27, 2026 at 5 pm.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors in 2026-27 who are at least 15 by June 1, 2027 and from the Research Triangle area. Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN to receive the stipend. Students must provide their own transportation.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a recommendation letter (links on the CeBA page). Applicants hear back in mid-April.
notes: The 2026 deadline is stated two ways. It is March 20 on the flyer and March 27 in the FAQ. The page says there is no housing or transportation help, so only local students are considered. The $2,400 is a completion award. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: Duke Health Youth Symposium on Healthcare Careers
org: Duke Health Volunteer Services (Duke Regional Hospital and Duke Raleigh Hospital)
duration: 2 days (2026: June 23-24 at Duke Regional in Durham; June 24-25 at Duke Raleigh Hospital)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened 8 pm Friday April 10 and closed 8 pm Monday April 13, 2026; acceptance emails by May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or 17 (16 by June 24 in 2026). Students must attend both days at one site. Space is limited to 25 slots at each site.
how_to_apply: Student completes the online application and a parent or guardian completes the Participation Agreement (both on Qualtrics links on the page). No late or incomplete submissions.
notes: Both Duke pages are titled Junior Volunteer Program but describe this event for 2026. The application window was only 3 days, so watch the page in early April. Questions: DRHVolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Durham) or DRAH_VolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Raleigh). Duke University Hospital says it no longer offers a junior volunteer program for high school students.

name: MaryAnn Black Summer Internship at Duke Health
org: Duke Health and Duke Community Affairs, with Durham YouthWorks
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: 3 weeks (2026: July 6-24, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: Durham YouthWorks application opened January 23 and closed February 21, 2026; orientation in March. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Durham City or Durham County residents between 14 and 24 as of June 30, 2026, per the Duke page. The Duke article describes participants as Durham-area high school students.
how_to_apply: Submit the Durham YouthWorks application and select the healthcare category (link on the Duke Community Affairs page). Contact: Kimberly Monroe, kimberly.monroe@duke.edu.
notes: Applications go through Durham YouthWorks (City of Durham), whose own page could not be read (blocked). The article says about 50 students were planned for the latest class. North Carolina requires a Youth Employment Certificate for anyone under 18 who works; the employer starts that process.

name: Duke Pre-College Programs (High School)
org: Duke University, Office of the Provost
pay_detail: 2027 residential fee not yet posted (Duke lists it as to be determined). Enrollment deposit: $500 before April 2, 2027, or $1,500 after April 1. Airport shuttle $45 each way; extra nights $120 each.
duration: Three sessions; dates to be announced in October 2026
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Session dates, courses and fees for 2027 will be announced in October 2026.
who_can_apply: High school students in current grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 to attend. (The page also lists middle school programs for grades 6-8.)
how_to_apply: Join the information request list on the Duke Pre-College page to be told when 2027 dates and courses open.
notes: Courses, session dates and fees for Summer 2027 were not posted on 2026-10-09. Check back after the October 2026 announcement.

name: Junior Counselor Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer position, no cost. You can ask for a letter documenting your hours.
duration: Asked to commit to a 5-day camp week, but you can work any days you are free. Full day 9:00 am to 4:00 pm or half day 9:00 am to 1:30 pm.
deadline_text: The page says applications opened in Spring 2026. No deadline is listed. If applications are closed, your info is kept until the next open period.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up at Dunwoody Nature Center (15 and up at Island Ford). Be mature, reliable, flexible and energetic. You must attend a pre-camp orientation, in person the first time.
how_to_apply: Write to the Junior Counselor Coordinator. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org.
notes: Phone 770-394-3322, info@dunwoodynature.org. The first email link on the page goes to a different address, so use the one in the FAQ (juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org). Camp dates are not listed on the page. Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Teen and Junior Volunteers
grades: Junior program: junior high students. Teen/adult program: 14 or entering high school.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: Teen shifts start at 2 hours. Junior: one weekend day (Friday to Sunday) each week for 3 months.
deadline_text: Junior volunteers are recruited in September and January. Teen and adult openings are posted on the museum site.
who_can_apply: Teen and adult volunteers: age 14 or entering high school. Junior volunteers: junior high school students.
how_to_apply: Junior volunteers fill out the online application, permission form and photo release. Teen and adult volunteers check openings on the museum volunteer page. You can also call or email Jessica Greenlaw.
notes: Experience with kids is helpful but not required. Summer teen volunteering is not mentioned on the page, so ask. The minimum age for the junior program is not given, only junior high.

name: Volunteer Programs (teen openings)
org: Forest Preserve District of DuPage County
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: One-time workdays or long-term roles with a yearly minimum of hours
deadline_text: No single deadline. Some roles have deadlines and limited space. New volunteer orientation is held monthly at district headquarters (second Wednesday evening).
who_can_apply: One-time community events: ages 8 and up with an adult. Long-term roles are generally 18 and up, with limited openings for ages 13 to 17. Family roles are ages 10 and up with an adult.
how_to_apply: For long-term roles, apply online through the volunteer portal. Then meet with program staff for an interview. After that, go to orientation and training. For one-time restoration workdays, find a date on the events calendar and register.
notes: Getting started for a long-term role takes about 2 to 3 months. The FAQ page says background checks apply to people 16 and older in one place and 18 and older in another. Ask the Volunteer Services office what applies to you. Call 630-933-7233 or write to volunteer@dupageforest.org. The page does not list which long-term roles take people under 18.

name: Durham County Library Maker + STEAM Volunteers
org: Durham County Library, Maker + STEAM Services
duration: You choose hours per week on the form
deadline_text: No deadline. Capacity is limited, so you may be put on a waitlist.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 13, or have a guardian's permission to fill out the form. The form lets you pick the age group you want to work with, including teens 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer form (skills, preferred age group, days and times, hours per week, emergency contact). Questions: Maker_STEAM@dconc.gov.
notes: Days offered are Monday to Saturday. Time options are morning, afternoon or evening. The page does not describe a teen-only volunteer track.

name: Durham County Library Teen Volunteers
duration: Ongoing, set with the branch
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Each branch decides whether it can host volunteers; availability is not guaranteed.
who_can_apply: The For Teens page says the program is for all tweens and teens in grades 6 to 12. The general volunteer page says all volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Contact the teen librarian at your preferred branch. The general volunteer page also says to fill out the volunteer application form (PDF) and bring it to your nearest library.
notes: The two Durham County Library pages disagree on age: the teen page says grades 6 to 12, the general volunteer page says 14 or older. Ask the teen librarian which applies. The library says it cannot currently host court-mandated community service hours.

name: Durham Aquatic School (free lifeguard certification)
pay_detail: Training is free. City of Durham pool lifeguard jobs started at $18.90 an hour on the outdoor pools page.
duration: About 6 hours of online work, then in-person sessions (Spring 2026 courses ran March 30 to April 2)
deadline_text: Spring 2026 course: pre-course swim test Sunday, March 15, registration deadline March 15 at 10 am. New dates are posted each season.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 years old (bring proof of age to the pre-course swim test). The page also says candidates must be at least 15 on or before the last class session, so ask which rule applies. You must pass the pre-course swim test: a 150 yard swim-tread-swim, then a timed event with a 10 pound object retrieved from 7 to 10 feet deep.
how_to_apply: Sign up online at dprplaymore.org (Register Online). Or sign up in person at any Durham Parks and Recreation site. Then pass the swim test before the course. Apply for lifeguard jobs on the City of Durham career page.
notes: Search ActiveNet for DAS for current dates. Space is limited and filled by order of pre-course test registration. Questions: DPRAquatics@durhamnc.gov, 919-560-4444. Whether teens under 18 need NC working papers was not checked.

name: Teen Volunteers (Durham Parks and Recreation)
pay_detail: Unpaid. DPR can give you a record of service hours for school or scholarships.
duration: Shifts as listed on the volunteer opportunities page.
deadline_text: No deadline. Browse and sign up for open shifts.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. No experience is required.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer page and sign up for an open shift. Or email DPRVolunteers@DurhamNC.gov about the role you want. Then fill out the online volunteer application.
notes: Phone 919-560-4355. DPR also lists tutor and mentor roles with youth at recreation centers (after school and summer camp assistants); the page does not give an age for those, so ask.

name: Durham Tech Apprenticeship Skills Achievement Program (ASAP)
pay_detail: Pre-apprenticeship may or may not be paid. Apprenticeship pays a wage scale that increases with experience. Tuition waiver while in the apprenticeship.
duration: Varies by field
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. High school graduate, equivalency holder, or currently in a program leading to a diploma. GPA of 2.00 or above.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student interest form on the Durham Tech page. Or contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator, Dr. Norman Collins, at 919-536-7200 ext. 1402.
notes: Open to students 16 and up, including current high school students. Which fields are offered is not listed on this page.

name: Career and College Promise (dual enrollment at Durham Tech)
pay_detail: Tuition-free
duration: One semester at a time
deadline_text: Spring 2027: application opened Sept 11 and closes Nov 9 (2026). Paperwork due Nov 23. Last day to register Dec 1. Spring semester starts Jan 11, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. Need a 2.8 or higher unweighted GPA, or test scores showing college readiness. The career path also accepts a written recommendation from your principal. To stay in, you must keep at least a 2.0 college GPA after two college courses.
how_to_apply: Go to an interest meeting. Talk to your school counselor and the Durham Tech liaison. Then send the CCP application and papers. These are the waiver and pathway forms, test scores and transcript.
notes: Students at Middle College High School, City of Medicine Academy and Durham School of Technology use a different path and deadline. The pages state no North Carolina residency rule. Check with the college. The eligibility page confirms the 2.8 GPA or test score rule. It also confirms the principal waiver for the career path.

name: Durham YouthWorks
org: City of Durham, Office of Economic and Workforce Development
pay_detail: Earn up to $880 and beyond if you finish both Part 1 (training) and Part 2 (summer work).
duration: Part 1 training in the spring, then Part 2 summer work experience.
deadline_text: The page says applications open at the start of the year. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens and young adults ages 14 to 21 who live in Durham or Durham County. You need an email address that you check often.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open early in the year. Spots may be chosen by lottery.
notes: In 2026, more than 500 youth finished Part 1 and 120 were placed in hybrid or in-person jobs, so not everyone gets an in-person job. Questions: youthworks@durhamnc.gov. The city has a Getting Prepared Guide on the page.

name: EBAYC Volunteers and Student Internships
deadline_text: Not posted
who_can_apply: Not stated.
how_to_apply: The home page has a Sign Up button for volunteers, but the volunteer page it links to showed a 404 error on 2026-10-09. Contact EBAYC directly (offices in Oakland and Sacramento are listed on the home page).
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says EBAYC has many volunteer opportunities and welcomes volunteer groups and student internships, but it gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it (ebayc.org/volunteer/) returned a 404 error on Oct 7 and again on Oct 9, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

name: EBMUD High School Summer Internship (HSSI)
city: Oakland, CA and EBMUD service area
pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)
duration: 6 weeks, mid-June through August, about 16 hours a week
deadline_text: 2026 East Bay program: no direct applications, referrals from partner groups only. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.

name: Junior Lifeguard Cadets (Ages 14 to 17)
city: Hayward, CA (Don Castro Regional Recreation Area)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Financial aid is offered through the Regional Parks Foundation Campership program.
duration: 2 weeks per session, about 4 sessions each summer
deadline_text: The program page said 2026 cadet applications were due May 6 and accepted cadets had to register by June 12. The next dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. The program page does not list a swim test or a home city rule.
how_to_apply: Download the Junior Cadet application packet from the program page. Turn it in by the deadline. If you are picked, register by the second deadline.
notes: This is a training class, not a paid job. Sessions are full day only. The program page does not list session dates. It also lists Junior Lifeguards for ages 8 to 12 and Junior Lifeguard Aides for ages 13 to 15, with no details. Call 1-888-327-2757. For lifeguard jobs at age 16 and older, see the district lifeguard jobs page.

name: Leaders-in-Training (LIT) at Park'n It Day Camp
city: Alameda and Contra Costa Counties, CA (regional parks)
pay_detail: $50 for the one week. A limited number of $30 scholarships are available. The page lists 35 community service hours and does not mention pay.
duration: 1 week
deadline_text: The program page says applications open in 2027 and gives no date. Interviews are in late April. Accepted teens hear back by mid-May.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The program page does not list a grade or home city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply when applications open in 2027. If you are picked after the interview, you then register for the week. Ask about the $30 scholarship through the park district financial aid line.
notes: The program page says teens earn 35 community service hours, build job skills and may get a future camp job. It does not name the parks. Contact: Stewart Reid, Recreation Coordinator, 510-544-2558. Financial aid: 1-888-327-2757, option 2.

name: East Bay Regional Park District Lifeguard Jobs and Lifeguard Academy
city: Alameda and Contra Costa Counties, CA (regional parks and lakes)
pay_detail: Paid. The program page says a competitive wage but gives no hourly rate. The 10 day Lifeguard Academy is paid, so there is no tuition.
duration: 10 day paid academy, then a seasonal job
deadline_text: The program page gives no application dates. The Lifeguard Academy begins in late April. Check the job portal for open posts.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older when the Lifeguard Academy starts in late April. You must swim 550 yards in 10 minutes or less. The district also tests a deep dive and carrying a 150 pound person in open water.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the park district job portal. Pick the lifeguard posting. You must be free for all 10 days of the academy.
notes: Lifeguard I is the entry job at age 16. Head lifeguard jobs need age 18 and a finished 12th grade. The program page does not say if a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds, so ask HR. The district also lists younger water programs: Junior Lifeguard Aides (ages 13 to 15) and Jr Lifeguard Cadets (ages 14 to 17), with no details on that page. Call 1-888-327-2757.

name: East Bay Regional Park District Youth and Student Jobs
city: Oakland, CA and parks across Alameda and Contra Costa counties
pay_detail: Pay is not posted on the youth pages. See each job posting.
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No jobs were posted on governmentjobs.com on Oct 7, 2026. Watch ebparks.org/jobs/youth and governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks.
who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.

name: Elgin Community College Dual Credit
pay_detail: Accelerate College: no tuition for district-approved courses. Independent enrollment and Dual Enrollment: students are usually billed tuition. Career tech courses the district does not approve require tuition.
duration: Per semester
deadline_text: No deadline on the ECC page. Talk with your high school counselor about dates.
who_can_apply: Students at participating schools: U-46 (Bartlett, Elgin, Larkin, South Elgin, Streamwood), District 300 (Dundee-Crown, Hampshire, Jacobs), District 301 (Burlington Central), District 303 (St. Charles East, St. Charles North, Compass Academy), Cambridge Lakes Charter and St. Edward Central Catholic. The tracks are for juniors, seniors, or juniors and seniors, depending on the track. Talk with your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk with your parents and your high school counselor first, then use the online Dual Credit application (Apply Now). Independent enrollment also needs approval from the ECC Dual Credit office. Contact: DualCredit@elgin.edu or 847-214-7887.
notes: Accelerate College students may need to qualify for college-level courses and testing may be required. Each district publishes a Dual Credit Guide listing what its schools support. The ECC page also lists Upward Bound, Educational Talent Search and College and Career Readiness workshops.

name: Educational Talent Search
pay_detail: A federally funded TRIO program. The page does not state a cost, pay or stipend.
duration: Ongoing through high school
deadline_text: No deadline. Spots are first come, first served, so apply as early as possible.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 at certain schools. The middle schools are Abbott, Ellis, Kimball, Larsen, Carpentersville, Canton and Tefft. The high schools are Elgin, Larkin, Streamwood and Dundee-Crown. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You must show money need or be a possible first-generation college student.
how_to_apply: Send in the Talent Search application with your papers. You can do this online, by email to talentsearchtransition@elgin.edu, by mail or by fax. You can also get a paper copy from your school counselor. A guardian helps if you are under 18.
notes: Contact: 847-214-7764, Building K Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin. Only the schools named above are served. The page does not state a cost or federal funding; the pay_detail wording is not confirmed by the page.

name: Upward Bound at Elgin Community College
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.
duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.

name: Escondido Public Library Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens on the Review Crew earn 1 community service hour for every 2 qualifying book reviews.
duration: A regular schedule is expected
deadline_text: The page does not list an application window or deadline.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Volunteers need fingerprinting and a background check. Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board members do not need them. You must have an interview with the Volunteer Coordinator. The library does not accept court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Go to the City of Escondido volunteer website. Fill out the application there. You can call or email the City Community Engagement Liaison with questions. The number is 760-839-4523.
notes: Some roles on the page are for adults only. They are shelver, Friends shop and literacy tutor. The Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board do not need fingerprinting or a background check.

name: Lane Community College Summer Early College Camps
grades: Middle and high school (high school camps run separately)
pay_detail: Free. Transportation and food are on your own; parking is free and LTD buses come to campus.
duration: Monday to Thursday, about 4 days (2026 high school dates: Aug 10 to 13 and Aug 24 to 27)
deadline_text: 2026 registration is closed and most camps were full. Page says registration info is updated before each summer; check in spring.
who_can_apply: Oregon middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. A parent or guardian fills out the interest form. Spots go by lottery and a student can attend only one camp per summer.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian sends in the High School Registration Form for the camps the student wants. A lottery picks who gets in. The parent hears back.
notes: Lane also runs free summer academies for students of color in Lane County. They are called Rites of Passage. There are 4 of them. They are African American, Asian and Pacific Islander, Bridge of the Gods and Puertas Abiertas. See the Lane Community Education pages.

name: Lane-Metro Youth Corps summer crew
org: Looking Glass Community Services (Riverfront School and Career Center)
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on the page.
duration: 9 weeks, 32 hours a week
deadline_text: Current-year dates not posted on the page. The page says the crew is a 9 week program at 32 hours a week, and to fill out the interest form for an application.
who_can_apply: Applicants ages 16 to 21 who can work in a group of young adults from different backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Lane-Metro Youth Corps page. You get more info and a form to apply.
notes: The program page has no date (it has a 2021 example). Confirm the current ages, pay and dates with Looking Glass before you apply. School credit is available. It runs with the Oregon Youth Conservation Corps. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.

name: Looking Glass Youth Job Training Program
org: Looking Glass Community Services (Riverfront School and Career Center), funded by Lane Workforce Partnership
pay_detail: $17 per hour for the paid work experience, limited to one placement capped at 200 hours.
duration: Youth are usually in the program a year or two; must meet a case manager at least once a month
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Fill out the interest form any time.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who are low-income and face barriers to employment.
how_to_apply: Complete the interest form on the Job Training Program page. Questions: Hailey Johnston, 458-319-2968, hailey.johnston@lookingglass.us.
notes: Office: Riverfront Career Center, 1666 West 12th Avenue, Eugene. Bus passes or gas cards are offered. Spanish speaking case managers are there. Funded by WIOA. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.

name: Northwest Youth Corps Youth Camping Crews
pay_detail: Up to $450 a week with bonuses, after $70 a week is deducted for food. $300 tuition fee, with need-based assistance.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks living outdoors (2026: June 13 to July 18; July 25 to Aug 29 or 30)
deadline_text: 2026 dates are posted. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. No experience needed. Crews start and end in Eugene, OR or Boise, ID. You provide your own transportation to and from orientation.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the Youth Camping page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: This is hard: you camp and work in all weather. If you leave before graduation you get a share of the stipend and lose the bonuses. The page lists possible high school credit. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.

name: Northwest Youth Corps Youth Urban and Community Forestry Crews (Eugene)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 dependability and $20 safety weekly bonuses. Tuition fee $200, with need-based assistance.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 32 work hours a week (2026 Oregon: June 15 to July 17 or July 21 to Aug 21)
deadline_text: 2026 dates are posted. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 in the Eugene area. Teens commute to a central meeting place each day; local housing is not provided.
how_to_apply: Use the Eugene Apply link on the program page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: Possible high school credit (ask your counselor). Same program also runs in Boise and Tacoma. Dates may change. NYC is based in Eugene. Oregon BOLI says minors age 14 to 17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon (employers need a certificate to employ minors). A sibling card for the Tacoma crew uses the youth-ucf page; this card uses the program guide so the urls differ.

name: Eugene Science Center Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include a free membership after 40 hours of service and free planetarium shows.
duration: Scheduled shifts after an orientation; length not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Openings vary by season.
who_can_apply: The page says volunteers range from high school students to retirees. A minimum age is not stated; ask the Science Center. A criminal background check is part of onboarding.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now on the volunteer page. Then go to a volunteer orientation.
notes: The page gives no minimum age. It lists high school students among volunteers. Email the Science Center to ask if your age is OK for the role you want. The volunteer page now sends you to eugenesciencecenter.org/volunteer.

name: Student Academy to Inspire Learning (SAIL) at the University of Oregon
grades: Rising 9th to 12th grade (day program); rising 11th and 12th (residential program)
pay_detail: Free summer program. UO scholarship opportunities are listed.
duration: One week (2026: residential July 12 to 17; day program July 20 to 24)
deadline_text: 2026 summer programs were full. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Oregon residents in high school who have low income (for example SNAP, WIC, TANF or Pell eligible). Live on campus program: rising juniors and seniors. Day program: any rising 9th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Check that you qualify. Pick a program. Use the Register Here link on the SAIL page when sign up opens.
notes: You can get high school credit. Sign up early because programs fill.

name: Teen Board at the Evanston Art Center
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members volunteer at least 25 hours a year and earn volunteer hours.
duration: School year. About 8 to 12 meetings per semester.
deadline_text: The page says "APPLICATIONS ARE CURRENTLY OPEN!" but gives no closing date. Its board photo is captioned 2023-24.
who_can_apply: Evanston or Chicago-area high school students who love art. You can come to meetings on Wednesdays from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Apply. Then do a short interview, take a tour of the art center and meet current members. To ask about the current application, contact Catie Bryant at cbryant@evanstonartcenter.org.
notes: The page has no closing date, and its board photo is captioned 2023-24. Email before you plan around it.

name: ASPIRE Evanston: Careers in Healthcare
org: City of Evanston with Endeavor Health, Evanston Township High School and Oakton Community College
pay_detail: Summer internships are described as paid. The amount is not stated.
duration: Summer internship. Length not stated.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the program pages.
who_can_apply: Mainly under-resourced high school students and community members. The city workforce page says ages 17 and older. The ASPIRE page does not list exact rules, so email to ask.
how_to_apply: Write to aspire@cityofevanston.org and ask how to join. The workforce page also has a Workforce Division Engagement Form.
notes: The city workforce page says ASPIRE works with NorthShore HealthSystem. It serves ages 17 and older. Email aspire@cityofevanston.org to ask about high school students. Also ask your school counselor.

name: Work-Based Learning at Evanston Township High School
pay_detail: Internships may be paid or unpaid.
duration: A few weeks to a semester or a year
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Contact the Early College and Career Experiences office.
who_can_apply: Students at Evanston Township High School. The page is written for ETHS students.
how_to_apply: Talk to the Early College and Career Experiences office in Room W220. Contact Abronia Young. Call 847-424-7735 or write to younga@eths202.org. You can also call the post-secondary counselor, Michelle Vazquez, at 847-424-7163.
notes: ETHS also has a Work Permits page. It says Illinois law requires minors under 16 to get a work permit before working. Permits are by appointment only, and students aged 14 to 15 in school-approved work-based learning programs do not need one.

name: Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP)
org: City of Evanston Youth and Young Adult Division
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rate is not stated on the page. Confirm with the city.
duration: Up to 9 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: youth had to register ahead for the job fair on Saturday, February 28, 2026 (9 a.m. to 2 p.m., Robert Crown Community Center). 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who live inside Evanston Township High School District 202.
how_to_apply: Register online ahead of time for the winter job fair, then meet employers there. Employers use a separate job request form.
notes: Illinois law says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate), per the Evanston Township High School work permit page. The page says the program began in 1992 and last year over 40 employers offered over 300 jobs. Pay and exact summer dates are not on the page. The registration link is the 2026 form; look for a 2027 form around winter.

name: Evergreen Valley College Dual Enrollment and CCAP
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only
duration: By semester
deadline_text: The page does not state application deadlines or 2026-2027 term dates.
who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED. You need approval from your school counselor or principal.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.

name: EXP Internship Program (paid summer internships for 11th graders)
city: Los Angeles and Long Beach area, CA
pay_detail: EXP lists 171 paid internships for Summer 2026. The hourly pay is not stated.
duration: Port of LA placement is 2 to 6 weeks; other placements not stated
deadline_text: No application dates posted. EXP says to email internship@expfuture.org.
who_can_apply: 11th graders at high schools that EXP supports. The 2025-2026 list includes Carson, Gardena, Lawndale, San Pedro, Phineas Banning and Sato Academy. It also lists some Long Beach schools: Cabrillo, Jordan, Lakewood, Long Beach Poly and Wilson. Some schools in Orange County and Barstow are listed too.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to the Port directly; placement goes through EXP. Ask your school counselor if your school is an EXP school, or email internship@expfuture.org.
notes: Only for students at partner schools. Phone: 424.368.7100. The Port of Los Angeles Summer Internship (10 weeks, paid) is college students only. The page does not mention work permits.

name: Exploring (Learning for Life career posts)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Fees are not stated on the site; ask the post.
duration: Meets regularly
deadline_text: The program pages do not state application dates.
who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line. apply_url is the joinexploring.org home page, which has an Enter ZIP Code box for Exploring posts and clubs near you. On exploring.org, the Council Locator heading links to the contact page, and the scouting.org Local Council Locator finds a council, not a unit.

name: High School Internships (Facciotti Lab)
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.
deadline_text: No application process or dates posted.
who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.

name: Fairfax County IT Internship for High Schoolers
org: Fairfax County Department of Information Technology
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Mid-June until a week before school starts
deadline_text: Recruitment generally starts in April. No 2027 dates posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in Fairfax County.
how_to_apply: Email DITHR@fairfaxcounty.gov to ask how to apply.
notes: The county page has only a short note. Ask about pay, age and how to apply by email in March or April.

name: Lifeguard jobs with free training
pay_detail: Weekday opening and midday shifts start at $15.00 per hour; weekday evenings and weekends range from $12.41 to $15.00 per hour. Training is free (listed as a $250 value).
duration: Part-time; hours vary by Rec Center
deadline_text: Open positions posted on the page; no deadline stated. Training dates are shared at the interview.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 15 at the start of the course. Must pass the lifeguard course and its swim prerequisites (swim 100 yards, retrieve a 10-pound brick, tread water without hands for one minute) and a criminal background check. No prior certification needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Park Authority Aquatic Certification page, then interview. Questions: FCPAJOBS@Fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Employment is contingent on passing the course. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Fairfax County Public Library volunteering (youth 12 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: The library's volunteer guide is for adults, youth ages 12 and over, corporate groups, and people who need to fulfill a service requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator for your branch (the guide lists names and phone numbers) or use the Volunteer Login link in the library's volunteering guide.
notes: The guide does not spell out the sign-up steps for teens, so call your branch coordinator first. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Fairfax County Youth Leadership Program (FCYLP)
org: Fairfax County Department of Management and Budget
pay_detail: $1,000 for completing the 3-week internship
duration: Monthly meetings from Feb 2027 plus a 3-week internship in July (40 hours per week)
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027-2028 class are due 11:59 p.m. Sunday, Nov 8, 2026. Decisions emailed in mid-December.
who_can_apply: You must be a junior now in a Fairfax County public school. You should be doing well in class. You should care about local government. You cannot also do the Governor School Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send one letter of support. It can come from a teacher, scout leader, boss or someone like that.
notes: Meetings are Wednesdays 4 to 6 pm starting in February. You get yourself to meetings and the internship. Questions: DMBYLP@fairfaxcounty.gov or 703-324-4062. Page does not give the internship year; it is July 2027 for this class.

name: Educating Youth through Employment (EYE) summer program
org: Fairfax County Department of Family Services Workforce Development and Virginia Career Works Northern Region
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate is not stated on the program pages.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: The 2026 program ended with a recognition ceremony on Aug 14, 2026. The county says employer recruitment for the next summer begins in spring 2027. Youth sign-up dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. You must be legally allowed to work in the U.S. You must be getting services from a referring group or the WIOA Youth Program. You must want to find work. You must be able to work at least 20 hours a week and go to the workshops.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply alone. A sponsoring group or the WIOA Youth Program picks you. Email DFSEYE@fairfaxcounty.gov or see vcwnorthern.com/eye-programs/ to find a referring organization.
notes: Referral only. The county page also lists a WIOA Youth program for ages 17 to 24 who are out of school or close to graduating. In summer 2026, 133 youth worked with 100 local employers. Virginia work permit rules were not checked.

name: ACCESS Academy AI Summer Camp
pay_detail: No cost to students. Lunch provided daily. You provide your own transportation.
duration: One week, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. daily (2026 sessions: July 13-17, July 20-24, July 27-31)
deadline_text: 2026 application closed because spots filled; applicants were told their week starting the week of June 8, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students in the Commonwealth of Virginia.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the ACCESS Academy page when it opens again. If you have questions, write to Dr. Roberto Pamas. He is the ACCESS Academy Director. His email is rpamas@gmu.edu.
notes: Held at Fuse at Mason Square, 3401 Fairfax Dr, Arlington, VA. It filled up in 2026, so apply early next year.

name: AI in Health Summer Camp (George Mason University)
org: George Mason University, Department of Health Administration and Policy
pay_detail: The camps list at Mason says it is a free, five day program. The camp page itself does not list a cost.
duration: 5 days, 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. each day
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran July 27 to 31, 2026 and applications are closed. No 2027 dates are posted. The page offers a Future Programs Interest Form.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students. No coding, health care or technology experience is required.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Fill out the Future Programs Interest Form on the camp page to get updates. Contact: Maria Uriyo, muriyo@gmu.edu.
notes: This is a day camp at George Mason University's Fairfax campus, 4400 University Drive, Fairfax, VA 22030. Not a job.

name: Conflict Resolution Youth Summit (CRYS)
org: George Mason University, Carter School for Peace and Conflict Resolution
pay_detail: $1,390 without college credit, or $1,500 with 1 college credit. Scholarship review is possible.
duration: Four days, overnight (page lists July 25 to 29 for Summer 2027)
deadline_text: Page says applications for 2027 open in January (2027) and the summit is in Summer 2027, July 25 to 29. Closing date not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who like leadership, making peace, community work or social sciences. Students come from all over the country.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. If you are admitted, you get steps to sign up and pay a deposit. For a scholarship, check the box. Then send a personal statement and your parents' most recent 1040 tax form.
notes: Contact: Averi Jordan, ajorda22@gmu.edu. In 2026, 63 students went to the summit.

name: Health Services Mentorship Program (HSMP)
pay_detail: Free. 100% virtual.
duration: Spring 2027 cohort starting Jan 20, 2027 (details to be decided); year-long track for fellows and interns
deadline_text: Applications open for the 2027 spring cohort. Deadline Dec 20, 2026; accepted until full.
who_can_apply: High school students (GMU's camps list says ages 13 to 17). Virginia applicants must go to certain schools. Students whose family income is under 400% of the federal poverty level get priority. The researcher track is for students with no research experience. It is also for students with few health chances at school.
how_to_apply: Send the online application form. Allow about 14 days for email replies. Some applicants are interviewed. Send questions to the program director, Jonathan Sanchez. His email is jsanche@gmu.edu.
notes: The page also mentions that acceptances begin July 1, 2026. That does not fit with the December deadline. Check the timeline with the director.

name: Mason Game and Technology Academy (MGTA) classes
pay_detail: $595 per fall class. Scholarships page exists but gives no details.
duration: Fall 2026: six Saturdays 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at Fairfax; summer classes are five days, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: Most Fall 2026 Fairfax teen classes are closed. Fall 2026 Manassas Intro to Python (ages 9 to 12) showed registration open. No registration deadline listed; classes cancel with a full refund if too few sign up. Summer 2026 registration closed, 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Fall 2026 classes by age: 9 to 17 for 2D art, 11 to 17 for Unity, 13 to 17 for advanced Python (needs prior programming). Younger-only classes run in Manassas. Typing and basic computer skills expected.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the MGTA page when registration opens for a class.
notes: Not a job or internship. Listed because it is a real university program for teens in tech and game design. Check the page for the next session.

name: VALHEN STEM Academy (George Mason University)
org: George Mason University College of Science, STEM Academy
grades: Rising high school juniors (current 10th graders when applying)
pay_detail: Free for selected students. Overnight students get two nights of dorm housing, meals and a daily snack. A limited number of day-only slots exist. You arrange your own transportation.
duration: 3 days, 2 nights
deadline_text: The 2027 program is tentatively July 28 to 30, 2027, with final dates confirmed in January 2027. The application opens in February 2027. No deadline is posted yet.
who_can_apply: Virginia residents in a public or private high school, or home-schooled in Virginia. You need a GPA of 2.5 or higher. You cannot have attended the 2026 STEM Academy (VSA) or Leadership Academy (VLA). You cannot attend another VALHEN summer program in 2027. A recommendation is required. It should come from a teacher, counselor, coach or community leader. That person must not be related to you.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in February 2027. Essays must be your own work (no AI generated or third-party essays). Contact STEM Academy Director Kerin Hilker-Balkissoon at khilkerb@gmu.edu.
notes: The camps list at Mason describes this program for ages 14 to 16 (rising sophomores and juniors). The page itself says rising juniors, so use the page. Competitive: students are selected. It is statewide for Virginia residents but held in Fairfax. It may also be on a Virginia-wide list.

name: Washington Journalism and Media Conference (WJMC)
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the program pages. A scholarship is offered.
duration: One week (July 11 to 16 or July 18 to 23, 2027)
deadline_text: 2027 session dates are listed. The page shows a scholarship deadline of Feb 16, 2026 (looks left over from last cycle). No general deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Highly engaged high school students. GMU's camps list says rising 11th and 12th graders. Students can register or be nominated.
how_to_apply: Use the Register page (wjmc.gmu.edu/register). Scholarship details are at wjmc.gmu.edu/scholarships/. A Nominate link is also on the site.
notes: Check the cost and deadlines with the program before you apply.

name: Washington Youth Summit on the Environment (WYSE)
org: George Mason University with the Smithsonian's National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Ask the program: 703-993-5010.
duration: One week (June 27 to July 2, 2027)
deadline_text: 2027 dates are listed (June 27 to July 2, 2027). No application deadline or cost is posted on the program pages.
who_can_apply: Highly engaged high school students. GMU's camps list says rising 11th and 12th graders. Students can register or be nominated.
how_to_apply: Use the Register page on the WYSE site, or have someone submit a nomination (wsp.gmu.edu/nominate). Call 703-993-5010 for cost and deadlines.
notes: The site shows a Register button for the June 27 to July 2, 2027 session, but the page does not say whether registration is open. Confirm the status and cost with the program before applying.

name: Mount Vernon Volunteer Program
org: George Washington's Mount Vernon (Mount Vernon Ladies' Association)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get discounts at the estate's shops and restaurants and special tours.
duration: At least 25 hours a year to stay active.
deadline_text: The page says volunteer applications are currently closed. No reopening date is posted.
who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page to see when it opens again. You can also call Joan Flintoft at 703-799-8605.
notes: About 250 active volunteers. Some roles, like driving, need an adult with a license, so not every role is open to teens. There is no archaeology fieldwork for volunteers right now, only lab work.

name: Neighborhood and Community Services Volunteers (age 13 and up)
org: Fairfax County Neighborhood and Community Services
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by opening
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. You must finish a county volunteer orientation and a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Make a profile at volunteer.fairfaxcounty.gov and search the word NCS. Apply to openings. Go to an NCS Volunteer Orientation and pass the background check. Email ncs-volunteers@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: The page has no teen-only section or list of teen roles, so ask the volunteer office what is open for 13 to 17 year olds. The phone number printed on the page has a non-Virginia area code; use the email.

name: E-Summer Program at NOVA
city: Manassas and Sterling, VA (NOVA Manassas or Loudoun campus)
pay_detail: No tuition or pay listed. Textbooks are free, lunch is provided, parking pass for drivers. You arrange your own transportation.
duration: Six weeks, Mon and Wed 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. (June 22 to July 29 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened March 10 and closed May 1, 2026 (lottery selection). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are 16 by the first day of class and meet dual enrollment readiness (for example a 3.0 GPA, or set test scores). Needs a current high school transcript and parent e-consent. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply to NOVA for the summer term. Then fill out the Dual Enrollment Portal form in myNOVA. You pick courses, upload papers and get a parent to say yes online. Contact DualEnrollment@nvcc.edu or 703-503-6291.
notes: Selection is by lottery. The page shows 2026 dates; check in March for 2027.

name: Rec-PAC Counselor-in-Training (C.I.T.)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts as volunteer hours. The FAQ lists a $160 fee for the whole summer at school-based Rec-PAC sites.
duration: At least one week encouraged, up to the full summer; school sites run 8:15 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday
deadline_text: FAQ says Rec-PAC applications were due June 14 (page does not give a year). Rec Center sites: contact the site to set an interview.
who_can_apply: Any teen aged 14 to 17. Rec-PAC school sites have no interview; camp sites at Rec Centers and parks need an interview.
how_to_apply: Rec-PAC school sites: fill out the application and return it to the Rec-PAC office. Rec Center and park camp sites: contact the site for an interview. All CITs attend a 3-hour training and pass a knowledge test.
notes: This FAQ page looks old. It links to 2019 Rec-PAC sites. Check the fee, dates and deadline with the Park Authority at 703-324-8700 before you apply.

name: Future Women Leaders in Law Enforcement (Fairfax County Police)
pay_detail: Free of charge. Transportation help is offered case by case.
duration: Summer weekdays
deadline_text: The page says the 2026 class has graduated and to check back next year for 2027 session information. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school age girls in Northern Virginia (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: For girls only. Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to go to all classes. Not a job.

name: Fairfax County Police Public Safety Cadets
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs for uniforms or gear are not stated on the page.
duration: Ongoing unit membership
deadline_text: The 2026 First Nighter meetings were Sept 1 to 3, 2026 (one for each unit). The page asks you to fill out an interest form for updates on future First Nighter dates. No deadline for 2027 is posted.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 20 who like the idea of a career in law enforcement. There are four units. They are the Criminal Justice Academy (Chantilly), West Potomac High School, Annandale High School and South Lakes High School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Public Safety Cadets interest form on the page. The page also links an application. It links a waiver. It links a recommendation form. Email fcpdpsc@fairfaxcounty.gov with questions.
notes: An older Fairfax County police page called these units Explorer posts. They had the same unit numbers. That page no longer loads. Ask the cadet email about the current rules, such as citizenship, grades and costs. The page links an application, a waiver and a recommendation form.

name: Fairfax County Teen Police Academy
pay_detail: Free. Transportation help is offered case by case.
duration: Summer weekdays, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
deadline_text: The page says the 2026 class has graduated and to check back next year for 2027 session information. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Fairfax County high school age students (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Police Academy application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to attend all classes. Not a job.

name: Fargo Park District Lifeguard Jobs
pay_detail: $17 to $19 per hour
duration: Summer. Exact start and end dates are not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. You also need a current American Red Cross lifeguard certificate. The page links to upcoming classes.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the lifeguard page, which goes to the district's job portal. Questions: isinkler@fargoparks.com (Aquatics team).
notes: Take the Red Cross certification class first. The page links to the class list. Fargo Park District also has other seasonal jobs and an internship program on its Employment page. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.

name: Fargo Public Library Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: One session of 2 hours (1 to 3 pm) on the first Saturday of each month, October to May.
deadline_text: Register for each session. Upcoming dates on the page: Nov 7, Dec 5, Jan 2, Feb 6, Mar 6, Apr 3 and May 1. Locations switch between the Main Library and the Dr. James Carlson Library.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18. A parent or guardian must sign the Teen Volunteer Permission Form.
how_to_apply: Register for each session at programregistration.library.fargond.gov or call 701.241.1495. Bring the signed permission form to your first session. The form is on the City of Fargo website.
notes: The page lists the month and day for each session but not the year. A good fit for a first volunteer experience; no commitment beyond a single session.

name: High School Fed Challenge
org: Federal Reserve Bank of New York (national), Chicago Fed (regional page)
pay_detail: No pay. No fee is listed.
duration: Registration Sept 10, 2026 to Feb 15, 2027. Paper due Mar 15, 2027.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12, entered as a team. A faculty advisor registers the team. Each school may enter one team and one submission. Team size and other rules are in the rule book, which the page links to.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to be your team advisor. The advisor signs up the team online. The advisor also emails a form from your principal to nyeconed@ny.frb.org. The page covers team entries only.
notes: The Chicago Fed page says teams register through the same national process and lists the same Feb 15, 2027 deadline. Good for a club, econ class or debate team.

name: Fermilab PRISM (Program for Research, Innovation, and STEM Mentorship)
grades: Rising high school senior (senior in 2027-28) or 2027 high school graduate
pay_detail: $500 per week stipend. Housing is not provided; transportation assistance is available.
duration: 4 weeks, July 12 to Aug 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications open Jan 12, 2027 and close Mar 1, 2027 (recommendation letter also due Mar 1). Offers Apr 12, 2027; accept by Apr 21, 2027.
who_can_apply: Illinois high school students who will be seniors in 2027-28 or who graduate in 2027. Must be a U.S. citizen and have proof of medical insurance. No STEM prerequisites. Age and GPA are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal, a supplemental questionnaire, a PDF list of your STEM courses uploaded in the Resume section, and one letter from a STEM teacher or STEM club advisor. You cannot upload missing items after you submit.
notes: The apply link only works during the application window. Recommenders get an email upload link. It is sent only on weekdays during business hours, so line up your letter writer early. A walkthrough video is on the page.

name: Saturday Morning Physics
pay_detail: Free
duration: 11 Saturdays, 9 a.m. to noon. Fall 2026 ran Sept 12 to Nov 21.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed and the session is full. The Spring 2027 session will be announced in November. The program announces fall in May and spring in November.
who_can_apply: High school students in public, private or parochial schools, and home-schooled students with high school standing. Students attend in person. A physics course and two years of algebra help but are not required. A unique email address is required.
how_to_apply: Watch for the news in November. Then fill out the online application. If you have questions, write to saturdaymorningphysics@fnal.gov.
notes: Lectures are at Wilson Hall in Batavia. Some lectures may be off-site. Spring 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Saturday Morning Quantum* in Chicago
pay_detail: Free
duration: Saturdays 1 to 4 p.m., February 6 to April 24, 2027 (no sessions March 20 and 27)
deadline_text: Applications for Spring 2027 will open in late fall 2026. Classes run February 6 to April 24, 2027.
who_can_apply: Open to all high school students across Illinois. No science prerequisite. You must attend at least 8 sessions, with no excused absences.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the application. It opens in late fall 2026. If you have questions, write to Saturdaymorningquantum@fnal.gov.
notes: Classes are held at the Olive Harvey Learning Center, 3055 East 92nd Street, Chicago. The page gives no exact open or close date for applications.

name: Fermilab VALOR JROTC Summer Internship
grades: Illinois JROTC high school junior, senior or recent graduate
pay_detail: $18 per hour. No onsite housing or transportation reimbursement.
duration: 6 weeks, June 28 to Aug 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications opened Oct 5, 2026 and close Feb 5, 2027. Offers Mar 15, 2027; accept by Mar 22, 2027.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in an Illinois high school JROTC program, and an Illinois high school junior, senior or recent graduate when you apply. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal with an unofficial transcript, a resume and three short essay answers (under 200 words each). Then give contact info for one recommendation writer; the letter is due by the close date. Questions: Internships@fnal.gov.
notes: Only for cadets in an Illinois JROTC program. You cannot upload missing items after you submit, so gather everything first. Reference emails go out only on weekdays during business hours.

name: Fernbank Youth Interpreters (FYI) Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time $50 fee after acceptance, which can be waived for those who qualify.
duration: One year, June 1 to May 31, at least 45 hours
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications are closed. The museum expects to post information on the 2027-28 program in February 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 by September 1 and no older than 17 by June 1. Volunteers who turn 18 during the year may finish it.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application, an essay written by the teen, and two reference forms. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Contact: FYI@FernbankMuseum.org or 404-929-6360.
notes: Described as very competitive; teens who are not accepted are encouraged to reapply the next year.

name: Florida 4-H Junior Camp Counselor Program
city: Camp Cloverleaf and Camp Timpoochee, FL
pay_detail: Junior counselors pay the full early bird camp fee for each week they attend. They can apply for state camp scholarships.
duration: At least 1 camp week, Monday to Friday
deadline_text: The 2026 cycle ran Dec 1, 2025 to March 15, 2026. Applicants were told by April 1, 2026. Training was online in April and May.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 16 (age counted on September 1 of the 4-H year). You do not have to be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It names the camp and the weeks you want. Upload a resume. List two adults as references. They do not have to be from 4-H.
notes: Apply to Camp Cloverleaf, Camp Timpoochee or both. Weekly themes and prices are on each camp's page. Teens pay the camp fee, so this is not a paying job.

name: Florida 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: $20 per year for community club members ages 8 to 18. Some counties charge a different amount.
duration: 4-H year runs Sept 1 to Aug 31
deadline_text: Enrollment for each 4-H year starts August 1. No closing date stated.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18. Your age is counted on September 1. You can also stay until you finish high school.
how_to_apply: Call your county Extension office. Then join online in 4-H Online. Paper forms are also available.
notes: State events include iLEAD and 4-H University Legislature Day at the Capitol. Florida has three 4-H camps: Cherry Lake, Cloverleaf and Timpoochee. You do not have to be a member to go to their summer camps.

name: Volunteer Services
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 4 hours a week, flexible
deadline_text: Most sites say they are accepting applications now. Altamonte Springs, Apopka, East Orlando and Orlando were listed as accepting.
who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. At least four hours a week. Some sites are full; check the list on the page.
how_to_apply: Step 1: online volunteer orientation. Step 2: online application. Step 3: contact them to set up an interview. Call 407-543-4047.
notes: Pick a location that is accepting applications. The internships on the same page are for college students getting credit, not high school.

name: Junior Camp Counselor Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Summer term, 2 days a week
deadline_text: The 2026 applications were due February 28, 2026 at 5 PM. Expect a similar late winter deadline for 2027 (not posted).
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. Competitive. Two full 8 hour days a week for the summer term (June 1 to July 31 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Send in a form with a video. Also send in a recommendation form. A Level 2 background check is required.
notes: Parents are asked to let the teen be the main contact. Fingerprint fees are reimbursed for those who finish. Max 3 excused absences.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
pay_detail: $14 per hour
duration: About 8 weeks, June to early August
deadline_text: The 2026 application period is closed. The 2026 program ran June to August 2026. Watch the page for the 2027 window.
who_can_apply: Broward County students ages 16 to 18. You must be able to work in the US and have a valid ID. Your family must meet the income rule (economically disadvantaged). Picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window is open. Income and a random lottery decide who gets in. Chosen youth get a packet by mail and go to training.
notes: Funded mainly by the Children's Services Council of Broward County. Remote work is not offered. Next year dates are not posted, so check the page in winter.

name: Teen Team
org: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
pay_detail: Unpaid; $30 fee for training materials and uniform
duration: Training in June; volunteering on weekends and school breaks
deadline_text: Applications open in February and close in April. Interviews are in May and training is in June. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 (13 by the first June class). Must apply, interview, attend multi day training and pass a final exam.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form when it opens in February. Attach 3 papers. Then interview.
notes: Teens are expected to handle their own email and schedule. Volunteer Office: 407-323-4450 ext. 127.

name: Summer VolunTeen Program
pay_detail: Free; unpaid volunteer role
duration: 6 weeks (June 7 to July 23 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was May 31, 2026. Expect a similar spring deadline for 2027 (not posted).
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and up. Must attend at least 5 of 6 sessions and volunteer 6 hours a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online VolunTeen form with a letter of commitment. Contact Simone Crawley, 727-623-4731.
notes: Hours may count toward service requirements; ask the museum.

name: Florida Envirothon
city: Statewide, FL (state contest in Live Oak)
pay_detail: $300 per team, flat rate.

who_can_apply: High school students on a team from a school, homeschool group, 4-H group or nature center group. A full team has 5 competing members. The team registration fee covers up to 2 advisors. Each county sends one team.
how_to_apply: Join your regional contest first. Regional leaders sign up the winning teams. Then advisors finish signing up and pay.
notes: The key dates page is titled 2026 but lists an April 2027 contest, so confirm the year with organizers. Teams of 4 or fewer can take part but not compete for places.

name: Paid Summer High School Botany Internship
pay_detail: Stipend at the end of the program (amount not stated)
duration: 5 weeks (July 1 to Aug 2 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed March 6, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 16. You like botany, plant biology, ecology or gardening. It is run through the Miami-Dade County Public Schools Summer Youth Internship Program. Only Miami-Dade public school students get school credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add 1 letter of recommendation from a science teacher.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Look for a similar spring deadline. Recent undergraduate and graduate internships on the same page are not for high schoolers.

name: Florida FFA
pay_detail: National dues $7 per year plus state dues $10 per year. Local chapters may add dues.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No deadline. Join through your school's agriculture class.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in an agriculture course at their school. Joining a chapter in a nearby school district is a state and local decision.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher to enroll you in an agriculture course. Use the Chapter Locator on the site.
notes: For overnight events, an advisor or an adult your school approves must come with students. You also need a permission form and a medical form. Event fees pay for lodging and meals at most events.

name: Your Shores
org: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Miami-Dade County Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12 who are at least 16 years old. Upward Bound Math and Science (UBMS) students apply first; other students can be accepted if they agree to join UBMS. Applicants must be willing to get a scuba certification.
how_to_apply: Use the Join the Program link on the Your Shores page to start the application. The page lists no deadline.
notes: The page shows Saturdays from September 23 to May 25 with no year, so confirm dates with the museum. A medical checklist form and swim requirements apply. The page says participants earn a stipend but gives no amount.

name: Everglades Youth Conservation Camp Leadership Camp

pay_detail: The camp lists programs from $400 to $515 per week. The Leadership Camp price is not listed separately on the program page.

name: Suncoast Youth Conservation Center Teen Day Camps

notes: Capacity is 20 per teen week, so spots go fast. Address: 6650 Dickman Rd, Apollo Beach, FL. Phone 813-922-7961.

name: Genesys Works Jacksonville

notes: The page says the Jacksonville program works with Duval County Public Schools to recruit students. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The first Jacksonville class launched in 2025.

name: Volunteer with Parks

notes: Scouts can use the Scout Project Application. Camp host applications for fall and winter 2026-27 will only be considered for spring and summer 2027.

name: Mayor's Youth at Work Partnership (MYAWP)

name: Teen Volunteers

notes: Not everyone who applies is picked. Group volunteering: JPLVolunteers@coj.net. Teen specific openings are listed on a teen page that was not read.

name: Volunteer at the Library

name: Summer Youth Internship Program (SYIP)
