notes: Students may earn school credit if they pass the review and finish their work. The page says to check back for 2027 sign up details.

name: MOCA Teen Council

notes: Return for Summer 2027 is hoped for, not promised. Confirm before planning around it.

name: Youth Volunteers

notes: The museum only signs volunteer hours for students who are 14 (going into high school) or older.

name: North Miami Youth Council
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: School year term (length not stated)

who_can_apply: North Miami residents ages 15 to 18 at the time of appointment, in grades 10 to 12, with at least a 2.0 GPA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add a resume, school transcript, a minor participation form, a photo and video form, and 2 short answers (200 words each).

name: Teen Volunteer League

name: Lifeguard Training and Summer Jobs

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. You need a reliable ride and must pass background and drug screens. You must be free to work the whole summer. You must pass a swim test (200 yards, tread water 2 minutes, get a 10 pound brick).

name: Catalyst Youth Volunteer Program

how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it opens (it opens about twice a year, for Summer and School Year). Questions: volunteer@osc.org.

name: City of Orlando Summer Youth Employment

name: Junior Volunteer Summer Program

name: Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

deadline_text: Applications are due by noon on March 1 (start by May 1) and July 1 (start by Sept 1). The page gives no year.

name: CONNECTED Youth Leadership Program (CYLP)
org: Fulton County Government, Community Development (with 21st Century Leaders)

name: Teen Volunteers (Fulton County Library System)
org: Fulton County Library System (Atlanta-Fulton Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts after orientation
deadline_text: Applications are always accepted, but most projects are full and most locations have a waitlist.
who_can_apply: Youth under 18 may apply with a parent or guardian signature. The page does not state a minimum age, so ask Volunteer Services.
how_to_apply: The page (last updated 2026/10/07) says most volunteer projects are filled. Most places have a waitlist. You can still apply. Under 18: download and print the PDF application, sign it, get a parent or guardian signature, and return it to Volunteer Services by email, mail, fax or drop-off. Then attend orientation. Email vol.services@fultoncountyga.gov or call 404-613-0125.
notes: The page says the library is on hold for community service hour requests. Students who need school hours must contact Volunteer Services early. Some branches have Teen Advisory Boards; ask the Youth Services Librarian. Library systems for DeKalb and Cobb counties are separate.

name: Marshal's Junior Deputy Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost not listed.
duration: 1 week (June 23 to 27 in 2025)

how_to_apply: Send in the application with a one-page essay. The topic is on the application. Add a letter of recommendation from a school administrator.
notes: The page still shows 2025 dates, so call to confirm the current year. Contacts on the page: FCMD.JuniorDeputy@fultoncountyga.gov, 404-612-4462 or 404-612-4147.

name: Work-Based Learning, Fulton County Schools
pay_detail: School credit. The district page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.

who_can_apply: Fulton County Schools students who are at least 16, in 11th or 12th grade, and following a defined career pathway. Individual schools may add rules. Students in Atlanta Public Schools use their own district.

notes: District contact listed on the page: Leslie McHann, 470-254-0466. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Fulton County Youth Commission
pay_detail: Volunteer. The page does not mention a stipend.

notes: Contact on the page: 404-612-7386 or the county line 404-612-4000. The length of a term is not stated.

name: Teen Volunteers at Gail Borden Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short sessions, about 1 hour each; you pick the ones you want
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A teen volunteer orientation is listed for Sunday, Oct 18, 1:00 to 1:30 PM at the Main Library Conference Room (the page does not print the year; Oct 18 is a Sunday in 2026).
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. Bring an ID (school ID, driver's license or library card).
how_to_apply: 1) Fill out the online teen volunteer application. 2) Register for a one-time Teen Volunteer Orientation. 3) Sign up for open sessions on the teen volunteer calendar. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead.

Grove Ave. (homework help, college readiness, job hunting help; phone 847-695-7577), but parts of that page look out of date, so call first. The volunteer page lists a contact email that is hidden in the page text; use the library's Contact Us page.

name: Montana Cybersecurity Summer Initiative (CSI) Camp
pay_detail: Free. Not a paid job.
deadline_text: 2026 camp was June 15 to 19. 2027 dates are not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Montana middle school and high school students (grades 6 to 12 in fall 2026 for the 2026 camp).
how_to_apply: Use the "Learn more & register for CSI camp" link on the MSU Continuing Education youth page.
notes: Held at the Gallatin College East Campus IT Cybersecurity Lab in Bozeman. Camp has no cost.

name: Camp Grove Counselor-in-Training (Garden Grove)
org: City of Garden Grove Community Services Department
pay_detail: You pay $60 for each week. Week 8 costs $120 and week 9 costs $85, and those two fees are not refundable. The weekly cost includes the camp trip fee.

deadline_text: The 2026 application was due Monday, May 4, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 17 years old. You must fill out the application yourself.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Counselor-In-Training application linked on the program page. Fees are due two weeks before your assigned week. Call the recreation counter at 714-741-5200 to ask where to turn it in.
notes: This is a program you pay to join. It is not a paid job. Camp Grove is at Edgar Park, 12781 Topaz Street.

name: Garden Grove Recreation Leader Jobs (Atlantis Play Center and Sports)
org: City of Garden Grove Community Services Department
pay_detail: Recreation Leader pay is $17.00 to $19.00 an hour. Recreation Specialist pay is $18.50 to $20.50 an hour.
duration: Part time. Hours vary with the program.
deadline_text: The page lists 2026 age cutoff dates. It gives no closing date. Use the Apply link to see which jobs are open now.
who_can_apply: For the Atlantis Play Center and Sports jobs, you must be at least 16 years old by May 20, 2026. Day camp and resource center jobs on the same page are for ages 18 and up, by May 20, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the city page to apply on the city job site.
notes: Lifeguard and Instructor Guard jobs are on the same page. The page does not state a minimum age for them. Atlantis Play Center and Sports jobs are year round. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.

name: Garden Grove Teen Action Collaborative (GGTAC)
org: City of Garden Grove Community Services Department
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee is listed on the program page. Members can apply for scholarships.
duration: September 2026 to April 2027, one meeting a month
deadline_text: Applications are accepted September 1 through November 19, 2026. Meetings are the 3rd Thursday of each month, 4:00 to 5:00 p.m.
who_can_apply: Teens who are 13 to 17 years old by November 19, 2026. The page calls it a program by and for Garden Grove teens. A parent or guardian must sign the forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and the contract. A parent or guardian signs them. You can email them to ggtac@ggcity.org. You can also drop them off at City Hall, 11222 Acacia Parkway. Or bring them to the next general meeting.
notes: Members must go to the monthly meetings and join at least 2 volunteer events. Meetings are at the Community Meeting Center, 11300 Stanford Avenue, and food is provided. Planned events include Foods of Garden Grove Live, Jack O Lantern Jamboree and Winter in the Grove. To win a scholarship you must go to at least 4 meetings and volunteer at 2 GGTAC events. Questions: 714-741-5360.

name: Work-Based Learning (Internships), Gwinnett County Public Schools
pay_detail: School credit. The GCPS page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: One semester at a time as a school elective
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Forms go to your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator; ask when the next semester deadline is.
who_can_apply: Gwinnett County Public Schools juniors and seniors who are 16 by September 1 and have coursework that matches their career choice. The school reviews grades, attendance and discipline.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. Forms: electronic agreement, WBL application, recommendation form and job site information form. Forms are uploaded in the WBL class when the semester starts. Apprenticeships need a post-high-school plan.
notes: No home-office or private-residence placements. The program cannot guarantee a job. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Genesys Works Bay Area Internship Program
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
deadline_text: No dates posted. Applicants get an interview, then summer skills training.
who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.

name: Volunteens at Geneva Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Fall 2026 session: Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026
deadline_text: Fall 2026 session runs Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026. No registration deadline is listed. Dates for the next session are not posted.
who_can_apply: Geneva Public Library patrons in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register as a Volunteen using the sign-up form on the page. Contact: geneva.library@gpld.org or (630) 232-0780, 227 S. Seventh St., Geneva.
notes: Service hours are flexible and are not listed as a set number. The page does not describe the registration steps beyond the sign-up form.

name: High School Volunteers, St. David's Georgetown Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 3 to 4 hours a week, up to 8 weeks in summer
deadline_text: Summer session dates and deadlines are not listed on the page checked.
who_can_apply: High school students 15 and older who can work on their own after training. Year round spots are few. They mostly go to homeschool, hybrid or similar students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get an email in 24 to 48 hours with next steps. They are an interview with the Student Volunteer Committee, a background check, a drug test and shot records. Call 512-942-4777 or email sdghvolunteers@hcahealthcare.com.
notes: Georgetown is in Williamson County, north of Round Rock. Shifts can be evenings and weekends. Vaccines listed: flu, Tdap within 10 years, TB, 2 MMR and 2 chickenpox or history.

name: Georgia 4-H
city: Georgia (county Extension offices statewide; state office in Athens, GA)
grades: Ages 8 to 18 (Senior Project Achievement is grades 9 to 12)
pay_detail: Not a job. The page says 4-H does not require a uniform or club fees. Camps and some activities may have their own costs, not listed on this page.
duration: Ongoing; clubs, projects, camps and conferences run through the year
deadline_text: No enrollment dates listed. Ask your county Extension office.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Cloverbud programs for ages 5 to 7 exist in some counties only.
how_to_apply: Contact your local county UGA Extension office, or Georgia 4-H at 706-542-4444 or ga4h@uga.edu. The site has a 'Find Your Local Club' page.
notes: The home page lists teen options. They are Ambassador Program, Leadership in Action, Step Up and Lead, Senior Conference, State Council and State Congress. The pages did not give dates or ages for each. Check with the county office.

name: Teen Volunteer Program (Georgia Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid. $45 administrative fee (check or money order) once accepted. Perks: volunteer pass, free parking on shifts, 5 one-time daily tickets after finishing.
duration: 4 months per session: Spring (Jan to Apr) 60 hours, Summer (May to Aug) 80 hours, Fall (Sep to Dec) 60 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 session starts onboarding with information sessions in October 2026; dates not posted yet. The 2026 summer/fall cycle on the page: info sessions in July, application deadline Aug 1, interviews Aug 16, orientation Sept 12.
who_can_apply: High school or home school students ages 15 to 17 at the time of application. Teens need their own transportation and a parent or guardian must join the info session.
how_to_apply: Register for one mandatory virtual information session (email volunteer@georgiaaquarium.org or use the page's Contact Us interest form). A parent or guardian must attend with the teen. If chosen, attend a group interview. Bring birth certificate and photo ID.
notes: Not every applicant gets an interview. No behind-the-scenes roles for teens and no court-ordered or school service hours. The page lists the group interview as both three hours and four hours, and its weekday names for the 2026 dates do not match the calendar, so confirm exact dates with the Aquarium. Last-year dates are shown for reference only.

name: Georgia Boys State (American Legion)
pay_detail: Not a job. The 2026 memo says delegates pay a one time $5.00 'state tax' at registration. The sponsoring Legion post handles transportation. The page does not list a program fee.
duration: One week. 2026 session was June 7 to 13, 2026, about 400 delegates.
deadline_text: 2027 information is listed as 'coming soon'. The 2026 session ran June 7 to 13, 2026. The 2026 memo says the Samsung scholarship application was due online by the first day of the program.
who_can_apply: Male high school rising seniors. The home page says to contact your local American Legion Post or your Guidance Counselor for more information.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion post or school guidance counselor. Chosen students then use the 'Request to Attend' form. They also use a permission form. Both are on the Georgia Boys State site. Questions: administration@dogboysstate.org or 229-938-9352.
notes: Boys only (Girls State is a separate program run by the Auxiliary). The program is not a paid job, so no work permit. The 2026 memo says the week includes an evening devotional, and families who object may decline the invitation. Delegates must stay all week.

name: Georgia C.R.E.W. (Cultivating the Rising Experienced Worker) for foster youth
org: Georgia Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS)
pay_detail: Summer participants get a paid incentive for attending weekly sessions. The amount is not stated.
duration: Summer program with weekly sessions
deadline_text: The 2026 summer registration ran March 2 to April 17, 2026. Next dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth in Georgia foster care ages 14 to 21. The 2026 summer program was for ages 15 to 17 on June 1, 2026 (not turning 18 before July 1, 2026), with a Georgia photo ID and U.S. citizenship, permanent residence or a work card.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Georgia C.R.E.W. application on the DFCS site. Everyone, including returning youth, must apply. Call 877-423-4746 (main DFCS number).
notes: Only for youth currently in Georgia foster care. A Career Resource Connection for ages 14 and up and state ID help are also offered. The youth page still showed 2024 dates, so rely on the main page and call to confirm. Ask your caseworker.

name: Georgia DECA
grades: Not stated on the program pages

duration: Membership is for one school year
deadline_text: No join deadline listed. The state calendar lists a Fall Rally on October 21, 2026 at Six Flags Over Georgia.
who_can_apply: Students at a Georgia school with a DECA chapter. The state page does not list grade or age rules.
how_to_apply: The state page is written for school advisors. Chapters sign up and renew members online at deca.org. Ask a business or marketing teacher if your school has a chapter. A school can start one using the Start a Chapter page. The page says the Georgia DECA minimum is 15 members.
notes: Contact the state staff through the Contact Us page at gadeca.org.

name: Georgia DNR Career Academy
org: Georgia Department of Natural Resources (with Georgia 4-H)
grades: Current sophomores and juniors (the page also says rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: $100, which covers all meals and lodging. The page does not mention scholarships.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are current sophomores or juniors. The page does not list an age limit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a permission form from a guardian. Add one letter from an adult who is not family.
notes: Camp sites are Charlie Elliott Wildlife Center in Mansfield and Camp Jekyll on Jekyll Island. Students can earn college credit for Intro to Wildlife Management (FWMT 1000) at no cost. Check YES on the application.

name: Georgia Envirothon
org: Georgia Envirothon (Georgia Soil and Water Conservation Commission and partners)
pay_detail: $250 registration fee per team. Lunch is included.
duration: 1 day contest
deadline_text: Training day Oct 28, 2026 (Eastanollee, GA). Competition registration deadline March 20, 2027. Competition April 27, 2027 at Tugaloo State Park.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school teams of 4 to 6 students. The page does not give grade rules.
how_to_apply: Go to the Resources tab of the Georgia Envirothon site. Use the sign-up section.
notes: Late registration may mean no lunch count or no team shirt. The page also lists October 9, 2026 as a training day registration date.

name: Georgia FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
grades: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not a job. Dues are not listed on the program page.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
deadline_text: No join deadline listed on the page.
who_can_apply: Georgia students interested in business careers. The home page does not list grade, age or dues.
how_to_apply: The page says 'Joining is simple!' and links a chapter finder to see which FBLA chapters are close to you. Students join through a local chapter.
notes: Ask your school whether it has an FBLA chapter. The page does not list the state conference dates or dues.

name: Georgia FFA Association
org: Georgia FFA Association and Georgia Agricultural Education (Georgia Department of Education)
grades: Students enrolled in a Georgia agricultural education class (middle and high school)
pay_detail: Not a job. The membership page lists a yearly affiliation fee of $9.05 per high school student ($5.05 national, $4.00 state) and $900 per chapter for middle school. The page does not say whether families pay it.
duration: Ongoing during the school year
deadline_text: No membership deadline listed on the page. Enrollment follows your agriculture class schedule.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education classes at a Georgia school with an ag program. The membership page says every student in those classes becomes an FFA member.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an agricultural education class at your school. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. The state page says a student is expected to be in ag classes to join FFA.
notes: If your school has no ag program you cannot join through it. The state site links a 2026-2027 state agricultural education calendar for event dates.

name: New Fresh Urban Farmers (NFUF) Paid Internship
pay_detail: $10 per hour, about 8 to 12 hours per week during the school year.
duration: September to May: two Saturdays plus after-school hours
deadline_text: The page said Accepting Applications NOW. No closing date stated.
who_can_apply: High school students in Dougherty County, GA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Apply Here form on the NFUF page.
notes: A USDA city farming grant pays for it. Office: 125 Pine Avenue, Suite 150, Albany, GA. Phone: 229-352-6591. Email: info@flintriverfresh.org.

name: Georgia Independent Living Program (GA-RYSE, Chafee services)
org: Georgia Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS)
pay_detail: Not a job. Cost is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Youth 14 or older who are in foster care, or were in care for at least 6 months.
how_to_apply: Use the Find help near you map on the site to find your Independent Living Specialist (ILS) by region or county. If you have trouble, email askilp@dhs.ga.gov. Your caseworker can also help.
notes: The page lists no phone number. For paid summer jobs for foster youth, see the Georgia C.R.E.W. card. Ask your ILS about the Education and Training Voucher (ETV) for college or training.

name: Georgia Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Georgia
grades: Girls who have completed their junior year of high school
pay_detail: $350.00 registration fee, usually paid by the sponsoring unit or organization. The page says sponsors are listed for each girl.
duration: About one week. 2026 session was June 7 to 12, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: the 'I Want In' page said fee due April 20 and applications complete by May 20, 2026, while the Selection Criteria page said applications and fee due May 1, 2026. The two pages disagree, so plan for the earlier date and ask your unit. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Girls who finished junior year. You need high moral character and above-average school standing. An American Legion Auxiliary unit must sponsor you. Another group that a unit approves can sponsor you too. Each high school is limited to 12 girls.
how_to_apply: Contact the unit president or Girls State Chairman of a local American Legion Auxiliary unit. This is how you get sponsored. A selection committee picks the girls. Then the application is completed online. The school checks that you are eligible before school ends. Email georgiagirlsstate@gmail.com or call 678-289-8446.
notes: Girls only. The site shows 2026 dates and the 'I Want In' page says last updated 12/3/2022, so confirm with your unit before relying on the dates. Not a paid job, so no work permit.

name: Georgia Governor's Honors Program (GHP)
org: Georgia Governor's Office of Education, Workforce and Strategy (GOEWS)
city: Georgia (summer residential campus; host campus not named on the program page)
grades: High school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Free to apply. The page says required costs are travel to the semifinalist event and the host campus, basic supplies and optional spending money. Meals and rooms are provided.
duration: Mid-June to mid-July (residential)
deadline_text: Not open to students yet. You cannot apply directly. Local school nominations run August to early November (ask your school's GHP Coordinator now). Nominees get the online application link Nov 13, 2026, info session Dec 3, 2026, application due Jan 8, 2027, and semifinalists are told Feb 5, 2027. The page gives weekdays but no year; the years were matched by weekday. Confirm with GHP.
who_can_apply: Skilled and talented high school sophomores and juniors. A Georgia public school district, independent school or state charter school must nominate you. Home school students go through their local school district.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply directly. Ask your school counselor or GHP Coordinator to nominate you. Nominees then complete an online application with a parent permission form, a recommendation and a transcript. GHP project manager: (404) 444-7062.
notes: Local nomination dates differ by school district and the page says they run August to early November, so move fast. Standardized test results are no longer required. The application page is marked updated 08/2026.

name: Georgia Senate Page Program
org: Georgia State Senate (Office of the Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of the Senate)
pay_detail: $20.00 honorarium paid at the end of the day, plus a certificate of service (2025 welcome packet). A 2026 amount is not posted, so confirm it.
duration: One legislative day. Report about 1.5 hours before the Senate convenes. The Senate usually convenes at 10:00 AM (check the Senate schedule the night before).
deadline_text: No application deadline found. Pages choose a legislative day while the General Assembly is in session. The packet says the first 20 days of session fall in January and February. 2027 dates not read.
who_can_apply: Students at least 12 years old. The packet says there are no exceptions. A page is sponsored by the Lieutenant Governor or one Senator.
how_to_apply: The 2025 welcome packet says to contact your sponsoring Senator's office when you register. Staff contact: kim.campbell@senate.ga.gov or illana.burkhart@senate.ga.gov, 404-657-7004. The program web page needs a browser to load, so check it for the current form.
notes: Source is the official 2025 Senate Page welcome packet (the program web pages on legis.ga.gov only showed a loading screen to the reader). Under Georgia law cited in the packet (O.C.G.A. 20-2-692) page service counts as present at school. Dress code is business or business casual. Cell phones are not allowed while paging. The Georgia House has its own page program at legis.ga.gov/house/page-program, which could not be read.

name: Dual Enrollment at Georgia State University (Atlanta Campus)
org: Georgia State University, Office of Undergraduate Admissions
pay_detail: State funding (Georgia Student Finance Commission) pays tuition and mandatory fees for up to 15 credit hours a semester from the approved course list. You pay lab fees, supplies, meals and travel. Joint enrollment (not dual) is paid by the family.
duration: By semester: spring, summer and fall
deadline_text: Deadlines listed without a year: Spring Nov 1, Summer Apr 1, Fall May 1. Late applications are not guaranteed a decision.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors or seniors on track to graduate. You need a recalculated GPA of 3.0 or higher. You need test scores unless your GPA is 3.4 or higher. You need approval from your counselor and a parent. You also need proof of lawful presence.
how_to_apply: Submit the undergraduate application online. Send test scores if they are asked for. Have your counselor send your transcript through GA Futures. Perimeter College has its own application. It has five campuses.
notes: You must earn a C or better in every class to keep funding. The page gives two test score minimums. The lower ones are in the requirements list. The higher ones are in the step on test scores. Ask admissions which apply. Perimeter College lets dual students take 1000 and 2000 level classes at its campuses or online.

name: Dual Enrollment at Georgia Tech
org: Georgia Institute of Technology, Office of Undergraduate Admission
city: Atlanta, GA (online and some on campus)
pay_detail: Most Georgia students get state funding that covers enrollment (30 credit hour limit). Self-pay in fall 2026 is $353.93 per credit hour for Georgia residents, plus fees ($531 for online-only).
duration: By term: fall, spring and summer (summer is distance computer science only)
deadline_text: Windows listed without years: Fall apply May 15 to June 15. Spring apply Sept 25 to Oct 20. Summer (distance CS only) apply March 1 to 31.
who_can_apply: Students in a Georgia high school or Georgia home school. You need a 3.5 unweighted GPA and ACT, PSAT or SAT scores. You need precalculus and two finished college-level courses (AP, DE or IB). You also need proof of lawful presence in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the Georgia Tech Dual Enrollment application in the term window. Add your high school transcript and test scores. Add AP scores if needed and proof of lawful presence. Apply for state funding at GAFutures.org.
notes: Competitive. Funding can be denied if you used your 30 hours, your high school does not take part, the course is not eligible (on-campus), or you are not a U.S. citizen, eligible non-citizen or Georgia resident. Out-of-state tuition is $1,153.46 per credit hour. Decisions come about 3 weeks after the window closes.

name: STEP: Science, Technology and Engineering Program (Georgia Tech Aerospace Engineering)
org: Georgia Tech Daniel Guggenheim School of Aerospace Engineering
pay_detail: Free to students (funded by industry donors). No stipend stated. Students provide their own daily transportation.
duration: 2-week day program (not residential); Atlanta session July 6 to 17 in 2026
deadline_text: 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are at least 16 years old by the program start. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the STEP page before the deadline. Questions: outreach@ae.gatech.edu.
notes: Read on the Georgia Space Grant Consortium page that hosts the STEP information; the Georgia Tech Aerospace page itself returned a 403 block. Other sessions listed for 2026 were in Augusta and Albany.

name: Summer Engineering Institute (Georgia Tech College of Engineering)
pay_detail: Free to participants in 2026 (page wording). Participants stay on campus.
duration: 2026 session was June 7 to 15, 2026, overnight on campus
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026 session is closed. No application deadline is shown. Next session dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are rising 11th and 12th graders. You should like engineering, science, math or technology. The page does not mention a GPA rule.

name: Youth Volunteers, Innovation Center Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Board

duration: Teen Advisory Board: monthly meetings and 3 to 5 programs in a one year term

name: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
org: George Mason University, College of Science
pay_detail: $25 application fee and, if offered an internship, $1,299 tuition for 3 undergraduate credits. Both can be waived with demonstrated financial need.

notes: The Admissions Committee may ask for test scores or transcripts from other dual enrollment credits. The page also lists Youth Leadership Conferences and Educational Travel Programs, which were not read in detail.

name: Grizzly Youth Academy (National Guard Youth ChalleNGe)
org: California National Guard / California Military Department
city: San Luis Obispo, CA (residential; serves listed central and southern counties)
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).
duration: The page states a 17 1/2 month residential program. The length of the follow-up phase is not stated on this page; ask the academy.
deadline_text: No class start dates or deadlines on the program pages. Start with the online Interest Form and a required virtual orientation.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.

name: High School Summer Internship (Georgia Tech Research Institute)

notes: Course costs are not listed, so ask. Email Lifeguard@GwinnettCounty.com or call 770.822.8000. The page does not mention work permits. The season is listed as part-time seasonal, with no months given.

name: Gwinnett Parks Summer Camp Aide (volunteer)
org: Gwinnett County Parks and Recreation / Community Services
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. $21 for two required camp t-shirts, paid after you are accepted.

how_to_apply: Download the Summer Camp Aide Volunteer Application from the Day Camps page. Fill it out with a parent or guardian. Email it to CommunityServices@GwinnettCounty.com or Parks@GwinnettCounty.com, or drop it off at the camp site you want. Use a separate form for each camp site.
notes: Day camps are for children ages 5 to 13. The minimum age for aides is not stated, so call 770.822.8000 to check. Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Gwinnett County Police Explorer Post 1808
pay_detail: One-time registration fee of $61. Not a paid job.

deadline_text: No deadline is listed.

how_to_apply: Pay the sign-up fee and do an interview. Contact the Community Affairs Section to start.
notes: Sponsored by Learning for Life. Contact Cpl. Juan Reyes at 678.442.6520 or PDCommunityAffairs@GwinnettCounty.com. Community Affairs Section: 3125 Satellite Boulevard, Duluth, GA 30096. The page has no Explorer page of its own. Details come from the outreach programs page.

name: S.M.I.L.E. Gwinnett (Summer Mentoring in Legal Education)

how_to_apply: There is an Application link on the page. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page does not list exact dates, ages or the application steps. Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay / Silicon Valley: Volunteer
org: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley

notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sacramento: Individual Volunteers (Construction and ReStore)
org: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)

notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.

name: Hack Club

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
pay_detail: Free
duration: All of October 2026

who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.

notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.

name: Teen Volunteer Program

how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form and do a short interview. Then finish a longer application. It needs a counselor reference, a personal reference, a doctor form and a drug test. Then do the online and in-person orientation.
notes: Full attendance is expected without exception. Phones are not allowed on shifts. Parents cannot send the application for the teen.

name: HandsOn Bay Area Youth Volunteering (HandsOn Tomorrow paused)

notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), will not be running in summer 2026. The page does not say when it returns and does not use the word paused. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.

name: ZooTeen Program at Happy Hollow Park and Zoo
org: Happy Hollow Park and Zoo (City of San Jose)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.

name: Junior Camp Counselor in Training
org: Lower Paxton Township Parks and Recreation

notes: Only one spot per camp. Dates are for the 2026 season, so check the page in early 2027.

name: Harvey Mudd College Summer Session (high school students welcome)

how_to_apply: Use the Apply page of the Summer Session site. You send a registration application with a transcript and pay fees before the course starts.
notes: Costs money and the courses are college level. Check the site in winter for 2027 dates and prices.

name: Hawaii 4-H Youth Development
org: University of Hawaii at Manoa CTAHR Cooperative Extension Service
city: Oahu, Maui, Kauai and Hawaii Island

name: State-Funded Paid Internships for Public High School Students

how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Call the HIDOE main line at 808-784-6200 or ask your school.
notes: Act 251 (2025) gave $1.8 million for fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27. The state pays companies back for the time they spend training and supervising interns. No program contact is listed besides the main HIDOE phone line.

name: Hawaii DOE Student Summer Internships (DOE Offices and Schools)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

notes: The positions list is a separate sheet linked from the program page.

name: Kupu Aina Corps
pay_detail: $20 an hour, plus health insurance for 20+ hours a week, a retention bonus ($200 to $800) and paid time off.

notes: Most positions take ages 17 to 38 for the whole term. Jobs are on Hawaii Island, Kauai, Maui, Molokai and Oahu. The older HYCC Summer program (17 and up) is paused. Kupu also runs the Conservation Leadership Development Program. Hawaii requires a child labor certificate (work permit) for working minors under 18. It is free. It is a Certificate of Employment for 14 and 15, and a Certificate of Age for 16 and 17.

name: Rep. Matsumoto High School Legislative Internship
org: Office of Hawaii State Representative Lauren Cheape Matsumoto
pay_detail: The program page says these are non-paid positions.

deadline_text: Not stated on the program page.

how_to_apply: Send an application, a resume, a news-style writing sample and one recommendation letter. You can apply online through the link on the page, or mail or email the materials. Phone: 808-586-9490.
notes: This is one lawmaker's office. The page does not say if you must live in her district. The email link on the page may point to the wrong address, so use the phone number to confirm.

name: Senator Schatz High School Internship Program (Hawaii)
org: Office of U.S. Senator Brian Schatz
pay_detail: Pay is not stated for the high school internship on the program page.

who_can_apply: Hawaii students at public, private, charter or homeschool. You need a GPA of 2.5 or better and email access. Students in their last year of school get strong preference.
how_to_apply: Check the program page in spring 2027 for the new application. Questions: HighSchool_Internship@schatz.senate.gov or the Hawaii office at 808-523-2061.
notes: Interns are picked for work in the community and a mix of interests. You do not need student government experience. This program is virtual.

name: UH Early College (College Classes at Your High School)
org: University of Hawaii System and Hawaii State Department of Education
pay_detail: Free to students at Hawaii public schools in the program, thanks to state funding. You are not paid.
duration: Classes run during the school year
deadline_text: Deadlines are set by each UH campus. Ask your counselor.
who_can_apply: Students at a participating Hawaii public high school. Each high school decides which classes it offers, so ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Meet with your high school counselor first. Then fill out the UH System application and the online Dual Credit Application. Get the signatures, and send both to the UH campus by its deadline.
notes: The program page says 53 public high schools offered Early College in the 2023 to 2024 school year. Classes are face to face, online or mixed. Classes at the 100 level and above earn college credit.

name: UH Running Start (College Classes for High School Students)
org: University of Hawaii System and Hawaii State Department of Education
pay_detail: Varies. Student or family, the high school, or a scholarship may pay. A GEAR UP scholarship for students with low family income covers tuition, fees and books for one class, but the page says it will not be offered after the Summer 2026 term.
duration: One college class per term in fall, spring or summer
deadline_text: Deadlines are set by each UH campus. Ask your counselor.
who_can_apply: Students at a Hawaii public or charter high school who meet the college campus admission rules and are under 21 on September 1 of the school year. UH Manoa does not take part in Running Start.
how_to_apply: Meet with your high school counselor first. Then fill out the UH System application and the online Dual Credit Application. Get the signatures, and send both to the UH campus by its deadline.
notes: Nine UH campuses take part. You must also pass the placement tests the campus asks for. Private school students may be able to use an Early Admit program instead. Ask the UH campus.

name: Hayward Area Historical Society Volunteers

notes: The program page does not describe orientation, training or required hours. Phone: 510-581-0223, extension 161. The internships on the same page are for college and graduate students, not high school.

name: H.A.R.D. part-time jobs (Lifeguard at 15+, Program Aide at 16+)
org: Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.)
pay_detail: Lifeguard: $18.63 to $25.14 per hour. Program Aide: $17.74 to $23.94 per hour. Lead Lifeguard: $21.61 to $29.17 per hour.
duration: Part time. The Program Aide job is up to 12 hours a week on Saturdays and Sundays, year-round. Lifeguard shifts can include weekends, early mornings, evenings and holidays.
deadline_text: Jobs are posted on the district's job board as needed all year. The Lifeguard posting has no closing date. The Program Aide posting says it may close at any time.
who_can_apply: Each job lists its own age. Lifeguard: at least 15. Program Aide (Mobile Recreation): 16 and up. Lead Lifeguard: at least 17. Many other district jobs are 18 and up. If you are under 18 you need a work permit from your school.
how_to_apply: Go to the job openings link on the H.A.R.D. Employment page and apply online. You can also make a profile to be considered for future openings. Questions: Human Resources, (510) 881-6708.
notes: Lifeguards need a lifeguard card, a CPR card for lifeguards and a first aid card. They also need a TB test that comes back clear. Program Aides get first aid and CPR training in their first two weeks. Workers 18 and up are fingerprinted. Camp and swim teacher jobs for summer go up in spring. A 2026 summer flyer (not on the district's site) said 15 and a half and up, so check each job's age. Pool upkeep, nature, ropes course and gym coach jobs are for 18 and up.

notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).

name: Hayward Police Department Summer Youth Academy
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. The page also points to Teen Library Council meetings on the library calendar; none was listed on Oct 22, 2026.

name: HUSD YEP Youth Professionals Program (paid internship)

how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the HUSD page. Qualified students are invited to a group interview, then may be placed at a school site.
notes: Only for HUSD students. The 2026-27 window has passed, so ask the YEP office if late spots open. Contact: Larry Ewings, YEP Operations Supervisor, (510) 723-3857 ext. 34157. Students who turn 18 and graduate can apply to be a YEP Program Leader (starting at $28.98 per hour).

name: Hayward Youth Commission

pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.
