deadline_text: The site banner says it is accepting applications but gives no dates, and its document library page still shows a 2022 summer banner. Call EWDD at 213-744-7300 to confirm the current cycle.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF (2024 version) lists the other rules on who can join. Check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before you count on a summer 2027 spot. The home page Youth section says ages 14 to 30. That does not match the 14 to 24 overview used here, so check the current age range. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24. They offer school help, job readiness and some paid internships. Ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps. Checked 2026-10-10: the home page still says "Accepting Applications for" with no year or dates, so left unconfirmed.

name: Hoag Jr. Auxiliary / Candystripers (High School Volunteer)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The program is full. The page says to check back January 2027 for when interest forms will be taken again.
who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. The page does not state the weekly hours.

name: Hoffman Estates Park District Swim Instructor (16 and up)
pay_detail: $14.50 per 30-minute group class and $17 per 30-minute private class.
duration: About 5 to 10 hours a week, weekday afternoons, evenings and weekends
deadline_text: Posted on the park district job board with no closing date. Apply while the posting is up.
who_can_apply: At least 16 years old. You need to be a strong swimmer and good with kids. Experience helps but is not required.
how_to_apply: Open the Swim Instructor posting on the park district job board and apply online. You may need to work at least one weekend day.
notes: You need CPR and AED training within 60 days, and the park district gives its own pool training. A lifeguard card is a plus. The club is at 5050 Sedge Blvd. The park district's volunteer page has no teen roles.

name: Zoo Corps Teen Volunteers (Hogle Zoo)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee is listed on the page.
duration: Summer season, June to August. At least one day a week.
deadline_text: The page says Zoo Corps applications are due April 13 with interviews April 17 and 18. It does not name the year, so this is the usual pattern.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. You need 2 letters of recommendation, a negative TB test and a TB screening each year. You also go to new volunteer orientation and training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Zoo Corps application on the zoo volunteer page. A Zoo Corps description PDF is linked there.
notes: The zoo site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. Confirm the dates with the zoo volunteer office.

name: Holy Cross Health volunteer program (high school students)
org: Holy Cross Health (Silver Spring and Germantown hospitals)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Not stated on the main page
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 16. High school students use a separate application and must attend an in-person orientation. Needs a health screening (MMR, varicella, flu, TB testing) and availability to start within one month of applying.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form for high school students from the Holy Cross volunteer applications page, then complete a screening interview and orientation.
notes: Another site named holy-cross.com is Holy Cross in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; use holycrosshealth.org for Maryland. Background checks are required for volunteers 18 and older. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Friends of the Library of Hawaii Volunteer
org: Friends of the Library of Hawaii
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.
duration: Not stated. Commitments can be once a day, once a week, or as often as you can come.
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page. Book sales are in January and June.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. The online form also asks you to say you are over 18, so ask the group which rule applies to a 16 or 17 year old.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form, or print the PDF form and mail it in. Then go to an orientation. Questions: admin@friendsofthelibraryofhawaii.org.
notes: This is the Friends group, not the state library system. The state library page says to contact your local branch to ask how you might participate.

name: Hawaii Foodbank Warehouse Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts.
duration: Warehouse shifts Monday to Friday except holidays and the second Thursday afternoon of each month, plus Saturday packings. Shift length not stated.
deadline_text: No deadline. 2026 Saturday packing dates are listed on the page. Reserve by email.
who_can_apply: Warehouse minimum age is 8. Anyone 15 or younger must come with an adult age 18 or older. Some distribution sites require 13 or 14 as the minimum age. Groups of three or more can apply.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the volunteer page for warehouse shifts. Or email volunteer@hawaiifoodbank.org to save a spot for a Saturday packing.
notes: The warehouse is at 2611 Kilihau St., Honolulu. All new warehouse volunteers must go to orientation. The page lists a minimum age of 13 or 14 for some sites where food is given out.

name: Hawaii Pacific Health High School Volunteer Program
org: Hawaii Pacific Health (Kapiolani, Pali Momi, Straub Benioff, Wilcox)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: 3 months for high school students, one weekly 4-hour shift (or two 2-hour shifts). Summer volunteers commit two months.
deadline_text: Student summer applications close in the beginning of April, and summer placement is limited. Other applications are taken as posted.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. High school students (16 to 17) must commit to a regular weekly schedule for three months and complete onboarding health requirements.
how_to_apply: Download the High school form (Oahu and Kauai) from the Hawaii Pacific Health volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer Services. The page lists it in its volunteer section.
notes: Summer student applications close in early April and the page does not give a year. Other application windows are not stated on the page, so check back.

name: Hawaiian Humane Society Junior Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $15 Junior Volunteer Application Fee.
duration: The page asks for a weekly shift for three months. Some roles need a teen to volunteer with an adult. Check each role for its time commitment.
deadline_text: No deadline. Allow about 6 weeks for the application and training. Applications are kept for 6 months.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17. Check each role in the Opportunities Directory for its age rule. Teens who cannot give a weekly shift for three months go through the Youth and Education Department instead.
how_to_apply: Pick a role in the Opportunities Directory. Finish the Junior Volunteer Application Process. It has a $15 Junior Volunteer Application Fee. Training has a 2 to 3 hour in person class and shadow shifts. You also take online courses that can take about 5 to 6 hours.
notes: The page does not state an application window or year. It says to check back and apply at a later time. Youth who want service hours can go through the Youth and Education Department.

name: Teens4Animals Council
pay_detail: Unpaid. The 4-day training fee is waived for council members.
duration: One-year term (2026-2027), with 4-day summer training and quarterly meetings
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications are closed. The page does not say when the next application opens. The 2026 training was June 22 to 25, 2026.
who_can_apply: Students. The page does not state ages or grades; check the application. Members serve a one-year term, volunteer at events and attend quarterly meetings.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teens4Animals Council form when it opens.
notes: Members attend quarterly meetings and field trips on topics such as responsible fishing and ethical farming. The page does not state an age or grade rule.

name: HPU 600: College Classes for High School Students
pay_detail: $600 per class
duration: Fall 2026 terms: 8 weeks or 16 weeks
deadline_text: Fall 2026 terms: Term A Aug 31 to Oct 25, Term B Oct 26 to Dec 20, or a 16 week term Aug 31 to Dec 20. The registration deadline is not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the link on the program page.
notes: Classes and grades appear on your college transcript and can transfer to other colleges. The web address says hpu-500 but the page is titled HPU 600 and lists $600.

name: Kupu Community Program
pay_detail: Not stated as a wage. The page lists eligibility for paid on-the-job training placements and/or financial help with vocational training.
duration: Year-long program
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 who lack support. The page lists who can get paid on the job training and help with job school costs. Check the Apply Here link for the full list of rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the Kupu Community Program page.
notes: It is based at the Hookupu Center in Kewalo Basin Harbor, Honolulu. It works with Honolulu District public schools and McKinley School for Adults. They help with the diploma and with HiSET or GED tests.

name: Lieutenant Governor High School Internship Program
org: Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Hawaii
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not provided.
duration: 5 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9am to noon
deadline_text: The 2026 internship ran June 15 to July 16, 2026. Its deadline was Apr 15, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Hawaii residents who are 16 by the start, have finished sophomore year, and are full-time high school students. Students from any island can apply but must pay for their own housing and travel.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application. Email it with your unofficial transcript, one letter of recommendation and an essay of 500 to 700 words. Send it to ltgov.internships@hawaii.gov. Some students are then interviewed.
notes: Very small group: the page says six students are picked. The page and form differ on the start date (June 15 or June 16), and its FAQ still shows some 2025 dates, so confirm with the office.

name: Volunteer Program (high school students can apply)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings depend on what each museum department needs.
who_can_apply: The application has a box for high school students and a parent or guardian consent part. The program page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. High school students check the high school box. A parent or guardian signs the consent part. Expect a short interview and a background check.
notes: The museum matches volunteers to openings, so you may wait to hear back. Teen roles are not described on the main program page. The older application form is what shows the high school box, the parent consent part, the background check and the interview.

name: ʻAha ʻŌpio o OHA
pay_detail: Free for chosen students. OHA pays interisland airfare, lodging, meals and program travel. You are not paid.
duration: Six days, overnight. The 2026 program ran June 21 to 26.
deadline_text: The next program is listed as Summer 2027, dates to be set. The online application link says coming soon. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Students now in high school or the same level. Rising seniors get first pick. Your application is checked through the OHA Hawaiian Registry Program. A parent or guardian fills it out with you.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the online application. You write short answers and an essay, and a teacher, counselor, mentor or boss fills out a recommender form. New applicants also finish the Hawaiian Registry Program application. Call (808) 594-1835 for help.
notes: The program page does not spell out an ancestry rule, but it uses the Hawaiian Registry Program to verify applicants. Ask OHA if you are not sure you qualify. You get yourself to the airport.

name: Summer Fun Junior Leader (Honolulu Parks and Recreation)
org: City and County of Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page. Paid summer aide jobs are listed separately (see the Summer Swim Aide card).
duration: 2026 program ran June 8 to July 24
deadline_text: 2026 kid registration was May 11 to 15. Junior Leader sign up is through each site; 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Junior Leaders must be 13 before August 1 and no older than 17 by the camp end date (2026: July 24).
how_to_apply: Contact your local Summer Fun site (see the Summer Fun site map). Sign up as a Junior Leader.
notes: The page does not say whether junior leaders are paid or whether their hours count as volunteer service. Ask the site.

name: Summer Swim Aide (City of Honolulu pools and ocean sites)
org: City and County of Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: $19.23 an hour
duration: Seasonal full-time or part-time. The page does not give start or end dates.
deadline_text: The page says applications are accepted online with no closing date listed. Current status not confirmed.
who_can_apply: Open to applicants as young as 16. You need a valid American Red Cross Lifeguard Training, First Aid and CPR/AED for the Professional Rescuer certificate. You also need work with children and teens.
how_to_apply: Apply through the online application link on the Summer Fun Jobs page.
notes: Work sites: 21 pools and 3 ocean recreation sites. Hawaii requires a child labor certificate (work permit) for working minors under 18. It is free. It is a Certificate of Employment for 14 and 15, and a Certificate of Age for 16 and 17.

name: The Queen's Medical Center Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: At least 100 hours; summer student program also offered
deadline_text: Dates not stated on the page. Call Volunteer Services (Mon to Fri, 8 am to 4 pm) for the next start.
who_can_apply: Teens 15 to 17 need parent permission and a shot record for MMR and varicella. All volunteers commit to at least 100 hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteers form (or the High School Summer Student Program form) linked on the Queen's volunteer page. Or call Volunteer Services (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm).
notes: The page lists Teen Volunteer forms for 3 sites. They are Queen's Medical Center, Queen's West O'ahu and Queen's North Hawai'i Community Hospital. The page does not say if applications are open now.

name: UH Manoa Early College Scholars
org: University of Hawaii at Manoa Outreach College
pay_detail: The program page says there are no tuition or fee costs to students. You are not paid.
duration: One college course per term
deadline_text: Final deadlines: Spring 2027 is Nov 20, 2026. Summer 2027 and Fall 2027 are Apr 15, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 with a 2.8 or higher GPA, at a Hawaii high school that offers a UH Manoa course. A 2.8 GPA is a minimum and does not guarantee a spot.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school college counselor first. The program page sends you to its How to Apply page for the steps.
notes: Your high school must offer a UH Manoa course. The college work is hard, and past grades in college classes may be looked at. This program was called Manoa Academy before.

name: Marine Science Investigations at the Hawaii Institute of Marine Biology
org: University of Hawaii at Manoa Outreach College and Hawaii Institute of Marine Biology
pay_detail: $750 for Hawaii residents, $1,500 for non-residents (2026).
duration: One week (2026: June 1 to 5), with a boat from Heeia Kea Boat Harbor to Coconut Island each day, weather permitting
deadline_text: 2026 application opened in March for the June 1 to 5 program. 2027 not posted. Email summer.programs@hawaii.edu to get notified.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 and recent graduates. 24 spots.
how_to_apply: Use the application form on the Outreach College program page. Contact summer.programs@hawaii.edu or 808-956-9246.
notes: The cost is lower for Hawaii residents. Programs on Coconut Island run if the weather allows.

name: Medical Diagnosis and Treatment summer program (JABSOM)
org: University of Hawaii John A. Burns School of Medicine and Outreach College
pay_detail: $575 on the program page (Kamaaina discount of $50). The high school summary page lists $525 for Hawaii residents and $575 for non-residents.
duration: One week (2026: July 6 to 10)
deadline_text: The page says the application opened in March 2026 for the 2026 program. 2027 information not posted. Email summer.programs@hawaii.edu to be notified.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12. The page lists the program as a week-long summer program for students interested in health professions.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the Outreach College program page when the next application opens. Contact Noelani Ching, nching@hawaii.edu, 808-692-0948.
notes: The two pages show different prices. Confirm the cost when applications open.

name: UH Manoa Summer Scholar Program
org: University of Hawaii at Manoa Outreach College
grades: Finished grade 10 or 11 (rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Student pays tuition, fees and materials at UH Manoa resident undergraduate rates. A $1,200 need-based scholarship is available to Hawaii students who get free or reduced-price meals or school financial aid (first come, first served).
duration: Courses in sessions: May 26 to July 2, July 6 to Aug 14, or June 15 to July 24 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was April 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Students who will have finished their sophomore or junior year. You need a 3.5 GPA, the maturity for college work and approval from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Apply to the Summer Scholar Program. Once you are in, sign up for UH Manoa summer classes. Contact sscholar@hawaii.edu or 808-956-9246.
notes: No on-campus housing. Courses can be cancelled for low enrollment.

name: Waikiki Aquarium High School Teen Educator Program
org: Waikiki Aquarium (University of Hawaii at Manoa)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for 5 weeks
deadline_text: The page said Summer 2026 applications were open, with no closing date listed. Summer 2027 not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students. The aquarium says regular volunteers must be 18, with exceptions for teen programs.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the aquarium volunteer page when it is time. If you have a question, send an email to volunteer@waikikiaquarium.org.
notes: The page does not state the exact age range or application dates. The aquarium is open during repairs. Other aquarium volunteer roles are for 18 and older.

name: Hawaii High School Model Youth Legislature (YMCA of Honolulu)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Need based scholarships are available.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: Dates and deadlines are not stated on the program page. See the state calendar link on that page.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The program page does not give other rules.
how_to_apply: Send your name through the interest form on the program page. If cost is a worry, use the Financial Assistance link on that page.
notes: Contact aball@ymcahonolulu.org. You can also use yaghawaii@ymcahonolulu.org. The page lists no cost or dates. Ask before you plan.

name: Honolulu Youth Commission
org: City and County of Honolulu, Office of the Mayor
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page
duration: One or two year term, depending on who appoints you
deadline_text: The online application portal is closed until 2027. New dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 at the time of appointment. If you are under 18, you need a parent or guardian's permission.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Honolulu Youth Commission application page. It reopens in 2027. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Seats are chosen by the Mayor or by City Council members. An earlier call for applicants in July 2026 gave a July 22 deadline. Expect a similar time next year, but this is not confirmed.

name: Honolulu Zoo Junior Leader Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: At least one full Zoo Camp week (Mon to Fri, 8:00 am to 2:30 pm, with extended hours to 5:30 pm). Camps run in spring, summer, fall and winter.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. First-time volunteers are asked to start in spring, fall or winter camp if possible.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 16 who can volunteer at least one full week of Zoo Camp.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application. Upload a signed Waiver of Liability and a current photo. Then set up an interview. It can be in person or on Zoom. Training is the general volunteer orientation and a zoo safety class.
notes: Regular zoo volunteer roles are 18 and older; this is the teen exception. Check the page for the current camp schedule.

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
grades: Secondary and college students (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your health science teacher.
who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.

name: Humane Society Silicon Valley Student Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.

name: Bolsa Chica Conservancy Volunteer Days
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Restoration events are the last Saturday of each month, 9 a.m. to noon. Long-term volunteers start with a monthly 3 hour training.
deadline_text: No deadline. Events happen monthly.
who_can_apply: Restoration days are for ages 8 to adult. Kids under 14 need an adult with them. Age rules for long-term volunteer roles are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Come to a restoration day (wear closed-toe shoes and bring water) or sign up for the monthly volunteer training. A waiver form is on the volunteer page. Contact Kenny at 714-846-1114.
notes: The Conservancy internships are unpaid. They need a related degree or college enrollment, so they are not for high schoolers.

name: Huntington Beach Public Library Teen Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
deadline_text: Most roles take online applications with no deadline. The Teen Tech role lists applications Aug 29 to Sep 12 and interviews Sep 15 to 18, printed with no year. The page was last updated Oct 3, 2026, so that window is over for 2026 and no new Teen Tech dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens, with their own age rules. They are Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center and OC Coastkeeper cleanups. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.

name: Huntington Beach Ocean Lifeguard I (Recurrent)
org: City of Huntington Beach Fire Department, Marine Safety Division
pay_detail: $22.50 to $27.50 an hour in the 2026 posting. Lifeguards are paid during the academy.
duration: Seasonal, as-needed work with weekends and holidays
deadline_text: The 2026 summer posting opened Aug 12, 2025 and closed Apr 13, 2026. The exam was April 4, 2026. The 2027 summer dates are not posted on this page.
who_can_apply: You must be 17 years old by July 1 of the year you are hired, with proof. You must pass a 1,000-yard pool swim in under 15 minutes and an 1,800-yard ocean run-swim-run.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city job site before the exam. Pass the exam and go to an interview. The best scorers join the paid training academy.
notes: A 16-year-old can apply only if they were a Huntington Beach Junior Guard last summer. Marine Safety must also back them. New hires get a uniform, fins, sunglasses and a beach parking pass. Check the city job board for the 2027 posting. Paid work under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.

name: Huntington Beach Police Explorers
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: Monthly training on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month. Volunteer at least 4 hours a month.
deadline_text: No dates are posted. Start with the interest form on the program page.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 20. The page also says the maximum age to apply is 19. Ask the department which age applies to you. You must be in high school or a graduate. Keep a 2.0 GPA. Pass a medical exam and a background check. You cannot have a felony conviction.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form. An advisor emails you. Go to an information meeting. Turn in the application and a Hold Harmless form. Pass a medical exam. Then take an agility test, an oral interview and a background check.
notes: The agility test has a 1-mile run, sit-ups, push-ups and a flex arm hang. The city also runs a Fire Explorer program.

name: Huntington Beach Youth Collaborative
grades: High school (can apply the summer before 9th grade)
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a volunteer board
duration: 1 year term, from the start of the school year to May. Members can reapply until graduation.
deadline_text: The page says applications are now available, with no end date listed.
who_can_apply: Local high school students. These are HB Union High School District students. They also include Huntington Beach residents who go to private school or are homeschooled.
how_to_apply: The page says applications are now available. It links the word Applications to its Notice of Vacancies page. No deadline is listed. For questions, contact the city staff liaison, Molly Uemura. She is at the Community and Library Services Department. The email is on the page.
notes: Application dates and the form are not on the page. Confirm with the city first.

name: Cancer Research High School Program
org: Huntsman Cancer Institute, University of Utah, with the American Cancer Society
pay_detail: Up to $500
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 12:30 PM Mountain time (2026: July 6 to 17)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran February 10 to April 25, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in Utah, Nevada, Montana, Idaho or Wyoming. You must be a rising sophomore or junior. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens.
notes: You must attend all 40 hours. A lab kit is mailed to your home. Contact: Monica Salas Jimenez, Monica.Salas@hci.utah.edu, 801-587-7885.

name: HCI-RISE: Remote Immersive Science Experience
org: Huntsman Cancer Institute, University of Utah
pay_detail: Up to $400
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 AM to noon Mountain time (2026: July 13 to 16 and 20 to 23)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran February 10 to April 25, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Utah or Wyoming who finished at least freshman year. Rural students are very welcome. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens. Parent consent is required.
notes: It is online only. The program manager is Jill Christian. Her email is Jill.Christian@hci.utah.edu.

name: PathMaker Scholars Summer Research Program
org: Huntsman Cancer Institute, University of Utah
pay_detail: Up to $4,000 for 10 weeks (depends on education level). Housing and meals are paid for out-of-state students. Travel help for students outside Salt Lake City.
duration: 10 weeks, 40 hours a week (2026: May 25 to July 30)
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was February 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: The program page does not list eligibility rules. It says the program aims to reach young learners, including students from rural and frontier areas of the Mountain West. Check the application for the full rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Online Application link on the page. The program manager is Liz Morales. Her email is liz.morales@hci.utah.edu and her phone is 801-581-3088.
notes: Accepted students who finish are accepted back the next summer. High school students should check that they count as advanced seniors.

name: Know Your Government (KYG) Conference
org: University of Idaho Extension 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: 2026 delegate fee was $230. Bus transportation to Boise is provided; steering committee members and chaperones can get up to $75 in help.
duration: Weekend (2027: February 13 to 15)
deadline_text: 2027 conference is February 13 to 15. Registration opens in December (day not stated).
who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 10 who are enrolled in 4-H and in the Know Your Government project this year. You can attend as a delegate two years.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H and the Know Your Government project, then register online when it opens in December. Questions: Mike Knutz, mknutz@uidaho.edu.
notes: The event page says grades 8 to 10. Ask your county 4-H office to confirm.

name: Idaho 4-H State Teen Association Convention (STAC)
grades: Youth who have completed 8th through 12th grade
pay_detail: 4-H members pay $335 if they sign up April 10 to May 15, or $395 May 16 to May 31. Non-4-H members pay $390 or $435. Price includes lodging, meals and transportation.
duration: 4 days
deadline_text: The 2026 event was June 22 to 25, 2026. The last price window ended May 31. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth who have completed 8th through 12th grade. Both 4-H and non-4-H members can come. Adult chaperones must be certified.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say how to sign up. Email fourh@uidaho.edu or call 208-885-6321 to ask.
notes: Not stated on the program page: the exact location and a closing date. Plan to sign up by mid May, because prices go up on May 16. Teens do not have to be in 4-H.

name: Junior Zoo Crew
org: Idaho Falls Zoo at Tautphaus Park (City of Idaho Falls)
pay_detail: Registration fee of $90 per 3-week session ($72 for Tautphaus Park Zoological Society members), nonrefundable. You get a uniform shirt and zoo admission during your session.
duration: 3-week sessions, three days a week, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
deadline_text: Applications are closed for 2026. The page says applications open February 1st. In 2026 they closed April 18 at 4:00 p.m.
who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 by May 31 and no older than 17 during the program. First-time applicants need a letter of recommendation (not from a family member) and an interview.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application. If this is your first time, you also upload a letter of recommendation. Then you go to the zoo for an interview. If you have questions, email zooeducation@idahofallszoo.org.
notes: The 2026 sessions started June 9, June 30 and July 21. Fees cannot be refunded.

name: The Idaho Foodbank Volunteer Shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Shifts are booked in advance (length not stated on the program page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Book a shift any time.
who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 8 and up. Volunteers 15 and younger must be with an adult volunteer. Each person makes their own account.
how_to_apply: Make an account and book a shift in the VolunteerHub system. Wear closed-toe, closed-heel shoes. Download the minor waiver if you are under 18.
notes: The warehouse is not heated or cooled, so wear layers. Groups of more than 18 use the group request form.

name: Natural Resources Camp (University of Idaho Extension)
pay_detail: $310 for students. It covers food, lodging and medical insurance. Rides to camp are not included. Scholarships are offered through local Idaho Soil Conservation Districts.
duration: 6 days (June 15 to 20 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran June 15 to 20, 2026. The $310 fee was due by May 20. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 16. Teachers can also attend.
how_to_apply: Mail three things to the camp director at the University of Idaho in Moscow. Send a signed application, the health and medical release form, and the fee. If cost is a problem, ask about scholarships first.
notes: The camp is at the Central Idaho 4-H Camp north of Ketchum. Parents must drive campers to and from camp. The program page lists no closing date other than the May 20 payment date. Scholarship contact is Randy Brooks at 208-885-6356.

name: Idaho Science and Aerospace Scholars (ISAS)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Students may earn one science credit.
duration: Online course during the school year. Summer academy is one week for chosen students.
deadline_text: The 2026-2027 application is open. A closing date is not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: High school juniors. Other rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the 2026-2027 ISAS application online. If you are not a junior yet, join the email list on the program page. Questions: isas@sde.idaho.gov.
notes: The program is competitive. Summer academy dates and cost are not stated on the program page. Program contact is Erin Lanigan at 208-885-1232.

name: GEM High School Internship
org: Idaho State Museum (Idaho State Historical Society)
pay_detail: $500 stipend paid in two parts (December and June), as listed for the 2025 to 2026 program.
duration: The 2025 to 2026 run was November 4, 2025 to June 16, 2026, with Tuesday meetings from 4 to 7 p.m. and at least 3 volunteer shifts
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 to 2027 were due September 23 and group interviews were October 6 to 8. Dates for the next round are not posted.
who_can_apply: The program is titled a high school internship. Age or grade rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected students then have a group interview. It is at the Idaho State Museum. Questions? Email shseducation@ishs.idaho.gov. Or call (208) 334-2120.
notes: Pay and dates shown are from the 2025 to 2026 program details on the page; the 2026 to 2027 dates may differ. The page has an interest form for teen programs.

name: iJAG (Iowa Jobs for America's Graduates) School Career Class
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the program pages.
duration: A semester-based elective class.
deadline_text: No dates posted. Sign up through your school.
who_can_apply: Your school has to offer the class. The program pages do not say which grades can join or how students are picked.
how_to_apply: Check the schools list on ijag.org to see if your school offers iJAG. Questions: (515) 216-3140 or info@ijag.org.
notes: iJAG is not a job or internship by itself. It is a class that connects students to employers. Whether your school has it depends on your district.

name: Illinois 4-H Creative Collective Art Ambassadors
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
duration: One-year term; Zoom meetings the last Tuesday of each month
deadline_text: The page has an apply link but gives no dates.
who_can_apply: Enrolled 4-H members ages 14 to 18 as of September 1 of the 4-H year, with strong visual or performing arts skills.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page. Contact Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Must attend at least 75 percent of the monthly Zoom calls.

name: Illinois 4-H Food Advocacy Ambassadors
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
duration: One Zoom meeting a month (Sunday, 7 pm) and 1 to 2 in-person meetings a year
deadline_text: Application due December 31, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens who are 13 or older, enrolled in or past their first year of high school, with some community service. Needs a reference from an Extension staff member, school staff member or youth worker.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Illinois 4-H Ambassador Application (the Apply for the Illinois 4-H Food Advocacy Team button, which opens form.jotform.com) and get a reference. Questions: Mark Becker, mbbecker@illinois.edu.
notes: Cost to attend in-person meetings is not stated.

name: Illinois 4-H Healthy Living Ambassadors
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
duration: Virtual meeting once a month for 1 to 2 hours, plus a 1 to 2 day retreat each year
deadline_text: The page has an apply link but gives no dates.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 when applying. Must be committed to 4-H values and passionate about healthy living.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page. Contact Illinois 4-H at Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Members must attend at least one day of the Illinois State Fair. Whether you must be a 4-H member is not stated.

name: Illinois 4-H Influencers Team
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings (recording available)
deadline_text: The page has an apply link but gives no dates.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 as of September 1 of the application year.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page (an application tip sheet is linked). Contact Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Whether you must be a 4-H member is not stated on the page.

name: Speaking for Illinois 4-H
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
duration: 6-hour training, offered about three times a year; a spring update call each year
deadline_text: Training dates are not listed on the page. Use the register link.
who_can_apply: 4-H members who are at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the page for the next training.
notes: Teens must attend one training to be on the state roster and join a spring update call to stay on it.

name: Illinois 4-H clubs and teen leadership teams
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the page. Ask your local Extension office.
duration: 4-H year starts September 1. Teen team terms are about one year (stated for the Art Ambassadors).
deadline_text: No sign-up deadline is posted. Teen team applications and dates are not posted on the main teen page.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 join a 4-H Club. Your age on September 1, the start of the 4-H year, decides how you join. Teen teams: Creative Collective Art Ambassadors is ages 14 to 18, and Illinois 4-H Influencers is for high school age youth. Other teams do not list ages on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the Join 4-H page with a parent or guardian. Your local Extension office then contacts you with next steps to register. Returning members renew in Zsuite.
notes: This is club membership and volunteer leadership, not a paid job. Cost, grades and teen team application steps are not stated on the pages. Call Illinois 4-H at (217) 333-0910 or email Illinois4H@illinois.edu.

name: Illinois Boys State (American Legion)
grades: High school juniors (finished at least one semester of 11th grade)
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
duration: Session starts June 12, 2027, at 4:00 PM (90th annual session). The registration page lists no end date.
deadline_text: The registration page says registration for the 2027 session closes at 4:00 PM on June 12, 2027, when the session starts. Ask your local Legion post about its earlier sponsor deadline.
who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.

name: Illinois Education and Training Voucher (ETV) for college and training
org: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services
pay_detail: Up to $5,000 a year for school costs. Good for five years (in a row or not) or until age 26, whichever comes first, with satisfactory academic progress.
deadline_text: No deadline stated in the FAQ.
who_can_apply: Youth who meet one of these: DCFS has legal guardianship, you aged out of care at 18 or older, or you were adopted or placed with a guardian from care at 16 or older. Use it at any U.S. accredited school, in state or out of state.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Illinois Education and Training Voucher Funds on the Kaleidoscope site. File a FAFSA each year. Finish any forms your school asks for. Questions: DCFS.ETVCoordinator@illinois.gov.
notes: This is for college or training after high school, so it matters most for teens 16 to 18 who are planning ahead. It is money for school, not a job. Ask your caseworker.

name: Illinois DCFS Employment, Job Training and Apprenticeship Incentive Program
org: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services
pay_detail: The page says it gives financial services but does not list the amount.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Youth in DCFS care ages 17 to 20 who work 20 hours a week or 80 hours a month. Youth in job training or an approved apprenticeship can also apply. Older former foster youth have a separate apprenticeship rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out form CFS 449-2. Then email it to the DCFS Office of Education and Transition Services, or fax it to 217-524-2101. Ask your caseworker for help.
notes: Only for youth in DCFS care (or certain former foster youth). Call 312-814-6800 or 217-785-2509 for help. DCFS Advocacy Office: 800-232-3798.

name: Illinois DECA chapters and state conference
org: Illinois DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
pay_detail: $17 per member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local fees (not stated).
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Illinois DECA conference is March 4 to 6, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency O'Hare in Rosemont, IL. No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Members must have an interest in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism or finance. A chapter needs a certified local educator as advisor. Grades and ages are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA chapter and advisor. If your school has none, the Illinois DECA site has a Start a Chapter page. Membership runs through the DECA membership portal linked on ildeca.org.
notes: Not a paid job. Dues and conference dates come from the DECA Inc. page for Illinois. The state site ildeca.org did not repeat them. Mailing address on the state site: 2460 Dundee Road, Box 1001, Northbrook, IL 60065.

name: Illinois FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
grades: High school (also middle level and college chapters exist)
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages.
duration: School year
deadline_text: 2026-27 dates: State Leadership Conference Apr 9 to 10, 2027; Summer Leadership Experience Jul 29 to 31, 2027; National Leadership Conference Jun 23 to 26, 2027 in Columbus OH. Regional dates are in the calendar PDF.
who_can_apply: Students at a school with an FBLA chapter. The page lists high school, middle level and college chapters. How to join is not explained on the program pages.
how_to_apply: Ask a business teacher about a chapter at your school. The chapters page lists active chapters by region. Use the Contact page on ilfbla.org to ask how to join or start a chapter.
notes: Dues and how to start a chapter are not on the program pages. The national FBLA site blocked automated reading, so national rules were not checked.

name: ALA Illini Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Illinois
pay_detail: $400 per delegate, paid by the sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit or another sponsor, not the family. Bring some spending money for the week. If you drop out without telling the Department before June 1, the sponsor loses the fee and may ask you to pay it back.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: Next session is June 20 to 26, 2027. There is no fixed deadline: the FAQ says applications are accepted until the program is full, so apply early.
who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.

name: Hire the Future
pay_detail: This is job search help, not a job. Pay is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline. Visit an IDES office any time.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24.
how_to_apply: Make a free account on IllinoisJobLink.com to search for jobs. For job readiness help, use the IDES Office Locator to find the nearest office.
notes: The page also links to free tools to help you pick a career. It links to pages about staying safe at your first job, too.

name: SRELO summer research at IMSA
org: Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (IMSA), Aurora
city: Aurora, IL (open to Illinois students statewide)
pay_detail: No pay and no program cost are stated. The Research Fundamentals course has a fee that is refunded when you finish the course and program. A need-based scholarship exists for that course.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026 the sessions ran June 1 to 12, June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17.
deadline_text: The 2026 application portal showed closed. No 2027 dates are posted. Sessions in 2026 were in June and July.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are Illinois residents. You need earlier research experience (a research program, course or science fair). If you do not have it, you must finish an online Research Fundamentals course first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the IMSA page when the portal opens. Questions go to Dr. Anita White at awhite@imsa.edu or 630-907-5949.
notes: Residential students live in IMSA halls and get all meals. Commuters get breakfast and lunch but must drive to the Aurora campus. Topics change each year.

name: ISBE Student Advisory Council
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: One school year. Members meet several times a month, online and in person.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed June 30, 2026 and late applications were not considered. Finalists were emailed in July for a video interview.
who_can_apply: Students who are a sophomore, junior or senior at a charter or public high school in Illinois. You must be in that grade during the year you apply.
how_to_apply: Make a Submittable account with a personal email, not a school email. Then send in the online application. Finalists do a video interview. Returning members apply again. They skip the interview.
notes: The ISBE page is marked archived, so watch the page for the next call for applications. Next year's dates are not posted; the June 30 date is from the last cycle.

name: Illinois State Fair Volunteer Program
org: Illinois State Fair, Illinois Department of Agriculture
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free fair T-shirt, admission and parking
duration: 3 to 10 days, 15 hours minimum (2026 fair Aug 13 to 23)
deadline_text: The 2026 fair was Aug 13 to 23. The page does not post 2027 fair dates or volunteer application dates.
who_can_apply: Open to volunteers who apply. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Download the Information Booth Volunteer Application PDF from the volunteer page. Call the Special Events Office at 217-782-0777. There is an optional one-hour training workshop.
notes: Ask the Special Events Office if volunteers under 18 are allowed. The page also lists paid seasonal jobs. They are in the grandstand, customer service, grounds and security. It gives no minimum age or pay, so they are not listed here.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Illinois Wing
pay_detail: Dues and uniform costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask the squadron.
duration: Weekly meetings all year
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and not yet 19. Members under 18 join a cadet or composite squadron, not a senior squadron.
how_to_apply: Find your local squadron with the unit locator or the Illinois Wing units page. Contact the unit to confirm a meeting. You usually go to about three meetings. Then you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. The national page says ages 12 to 18; the Illinois page says at least 12 and not yet 19. Illinois Wing HQ: 630-524-4400 or wa@ilwg.cap.gov.

name: Illinois YMCA Youth and Government
city: Springfield, IL (state conference), delegations across Illinois
pay_detail: $455 program fee. Your delegation decides how it is collected (full payment, deposit, or register first). Scholarships are available through the registration application.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
deadline_text: The scholarship portal closed October 1, 2026 (decisions come before November 1). The program page does not say if you can still register, and it posts no general registration deadline or conference dates. Ask your Delegation Advisor or the state office before you count on a spot.
who_can_apply: High school students. Legislative Assistant and Press Team are open to freshmen through seniors. Lobbyist and Attorney are for sophomores to seniors. Legislator is for juniors and seniors. Anyone can be a Clerk-Bailiff.
how_to_apply: Get the registration link from your local Delegation Advisor. A student and a parent or guardian both sign the code of conduct. You pick a preferred role and give your State Senator and State Representative. Contact the state office if you have no delegation.
notes: Not a job. State office: 1315 Butterfield Rd, Suite 218, Downers Grove, IL 60515, (630) 833-9622, ilyag@ilymcayg.org.

name: IMSA AI Credential (online course)
city: Online, run by IMSA in Aurora, IL
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.
duration: September 28 to December 18, 2026
deadline_text: The September 2026 cohort runs September 28 to December 18, 2026, and has already started. The page lists registration for September 2026 only and gives no next date. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu to ask about the next cohort.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. No prerequisite courses.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up link on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. To ask about cost and openings, email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: Asynchronous course with weekly office hours. Only the September 2026 cohort is listed for sign-up.

name: Research Fundamentals (online)
city: Online, run by IMSA in Aurora, IL
pay_detail: $200. Scholarships are based on financial need. Students who get an SRELO mentor and finish the course get the fee reimbursed.
duration: 2026 session: March 9 to May 29, 2026
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened January 26, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list grades for this course. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a need-based scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: IMSA does not provide a mentor or lab space in this course. Students must complete all assignments by the deadlines to earn the certificate and refund.

name: RISE: Research, Inquiry Skills and Experimentation
city: Online, run by IMSA in Aurora, IL
pay_detail: $1,200. Scholarships based on financial need (free or reduced lunch or SNAP) require a $150 fee, with $100 refunded if you finish.
duration: September 7, 2026 to May 31, 2027
deadline_text: The page says registration opened Thursday, July 30, 2026 at noon and has a Register button. It posts no closing date and does not say if new students can still join. Spots are limited. Full refund (less the $100 fee) through mid-September 2026; no refunds after September 30, 2026. Ask IMSA before you pay.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. You must find your own research mentor and lab space if needed. IMSA cannot provide them.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a scholarship instead. Do not pay if you apply for a scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: It is a hard program. Daily work is expected and you must meet firm deadlines. Failing three deadlines means removal without a refund. IJAS fair entries must be made as an IMSA RISE student for Region 5. Program is non-credit.

name: 4-H Academy @ Purdue
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.
duration: 3 days (June 10 to 12 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 conference ran June 10 to 12, 2026. Registration dates are not posted on the page and 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Open to all youth in grades 9 to 12. Register through your local Purdue Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Purdue Extension office if you need help signing up.
notes: The page says "contact your local Extension office for registration assistance". Confirm cost and the sign-up steps with Extension.

name: Indiana 4-H Day at the Statehouse
pay_detail: $25 per person, or $50 with overnight stay
deadline_text: 2026 event was Feb 10. Registration closed Jan 19, 2026. The page does not say when the next event is.
who_can_apply: Indiana 4-H youth in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register through 4-H Online by the deadline.
notes: The flyer was marked coming soon, so start time and details were not posted when read.

name: 4-H Round-Up at Purdue
grades: Youth who have completed grades 7 and 8
pay_detail: Registration fee was $250 by May 8, $275 for May 9 to 15 and $300 for May 16 to 22 (2026 prices).
duration: 3 days (June 10 to 12 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 event ran June 10 to 12, 2026. Registration was open through May 22, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth who have completed grades 7 and 8 (so they are entering 9th grade).
how_to_apply: Sign up through 4-H Online. Contact your local Purdue Extension office if you need help signing up.
notes: Aimed at incoming 9th graders, so it fits the early end of the guide age range.

name: Indiana 4-H Ambassador Program
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Not stated on the page. Training is July 30 to August 1.
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due April 15, 2026. Interviews were in the first two weeks of May and ambassadors were notified in the last week of May. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Current 4-H members in grades 9 to 11 with strong leadership and 4-H advocacy. You must have been a member for at least 2 years before applying.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has a short questionnaire. It also has a video about why you want to be an ambassador. Use the Apply Now link on the page. Then you have an interview.
notes: You need to be in 4-H first. Find a local club through the Indiana 4-H page.

name: Indiana 4-H State Fair Exhibit Hall Worker
pay_detail: Minimum wage
duration: About 4 weeks (July 31 to Aug 25, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 work dates were July 31 to Aug 25 (fair Aug 7 to 23). No application deadline was stated, and 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older; college-age young adults can also work. Workers are expected to live in the reserved dorm space during the job.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the page. Read the schedule for shows with no animals. Email Megan Skiba, skiba0@purdue.edu.
notes: Indiana work permit rules were not checked. Housing is required to be on site.

name: Indiana 4-H
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: Join any time. State programs have their own dates.
who_can_apply: Indiana youth in grades 3 to 12 (Mini 4-H is K to 2 in most counties).
how_to_apply: Start with the club membership page or contact your county or district 4-H office.
notes: Fees are not listed on the page.

name: Indiana DECA chapters and state conference
org: Indiana DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
pay_detail: $15 per member: $7 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Indiana DECA conference is February 26 to 28, 2027 at the Indianapolis Marriott Downtown. No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Members must be in a business or marketing class now or have been before. The Indiana Department of Education must recognize chapters. They must have business courses. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher. Ask about joining or starting a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Indiana DECA advisor. Use indianadeca@gmail.com.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is indianadeca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Indiana.

name: Volunteer with Indiana DNR (youth volunteer agreement for under 18)
city: Indiana (state parks, nature centers and other DNR properties)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. The page also lists unpaid internships for school credit.
deadline_text: No deadline. Schedules are flexible and set with the property.
who_can_apply: Open to adults and youth. If you are younger than 18, a guardian fills out the Youth Volunteer Service Agreement. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Create a Volunteer Profile and send the signed Youth Volunteer Service Agreement (guardian signs) to dnrvolunteer@dnr.IN.gov. Check CERVIS for current projects or contact a property near you. Phone 463-203-6562.
notes: Ask the park or property near you what age it takes. The list of tasks on the page is general and not every property offers every task.

name: WorkOne young adult (youth) services
org: Indiana Department of Workforce Development, WorkOne Career Centers
city: Statewide, with WorkOne centers in Lafayette and other Indiana cities
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Contact a WorkOne center.
who_can_apply: The state page says in-school young adults ages 14 to 21 and out-of-school young adults ages 16 to 24 may be eligible. Eligibility rules beyond age are not stated.
how_to_apply: Connect with your local WorkOne Career Center (Lafayette office serves Tippecanoe County; schedule by appointment through the WorkOne West Central site). Ask about the young adult program.
notes: This is the state workforce agency's WIOA-style youth help, not a single job. The WorkOne West Central about page (older) says a youth program for ages 16 to 24 is offered; the newer state page says 14 to 21 in school. The WorkOne South Central page (Bloomington region, read 2026-10-17) says many resources are for young adults 16 to 24, in or out of school, if they meet WIOA rules, and lists JAG for high school students only. Call before going. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the state page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.

name: Indiana FFA membership through your school ag class
pay_detail: State dues are $14 per active member per year (includes national, state and district dues). Local chapters set their own local dues.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Indiana FFA says affiliation declarations are due October 1, rosters November 1 and student test numbers December 1. These are chapter deadlines for the teacher.
who_can_apply: To join FFA, you must be enrolled in an agriculture course at your school. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher about enrolling in an agricultural education class. The Indiana Agricultural Education site explains how to start a program if your school has none.

pay_detail: Free. The national site says it covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The application process usually takes about two months.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. The national site says you must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated to succeed. The program pages do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Brunswick center: 4401 Glynco Pkwy, Brunswick, GA 31525. Turner center: 2000 Schilling Ave, Albany, GA 31705. Neither center page showed a closure notice on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. That is normal for this federal program, but only enter it on the official jobcorps.gov site with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds. The Atlanta center is not listed here because its page could not be confirmed.

name: Job Corps: Hubert H. Humphrey Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages do not explain parent consent for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Fill out the application. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Examples are proof of income and proof of citizenship or residency. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Address: 1480 Snelling Ave N, St. Paul, MN 55108. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. After applying, the national site says the review includes a background check (1 to 2 weeks) and a campus review (about 30 days).

name: Job Corps Sacramento Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).
deadline_text: Ongoing enrollment. No dates posted on the Sacramento page.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.
