name: Job Service North Dakota Youth Employment and Training Program (WIOA Youth)
city: Statewide (offices in Fargo, Bismarck, Grand Forks and more), ND
pay_detail: Work experience pays at least minimum wage, paid through Job Service. Pay covers up to 25 hours per week.
duration: Work experience can happen any time of year. Length is not stated.
deadline_text: No deadline stated in the handbook and brochure.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 24 who face barriers to employment. Meeting the rules does not guarantee a spot. Funds are limited and staff pick youth who are 'most in need' and likely to succeed.
how_to_apply: Contact a youth case manager at the nearest Job Service North Dakota office. Fargo: 1350 32nd St S, 701-239-7300, infojsfg@nd.gov. Bismarck: 1601 E Century Ave, 701-328-5000, infojsbis@nd.gov. Grand Forks: 1501 28th Ave S, 701-795-3700, infojsgf@nd.gov.
notes: Not for every teen. The handbook says the program is not an entitlement. The exact list of barriers and income rules was not in the program pages, so ask the case manager. The handbook is dated 10.21 in its file name, so confirm details by phone. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.

name: John Muir Health High School Student Volunteer Program (Walnut Creek Medical Center)
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
deadline_text: No application window is stated on the official page. Contact a partner high school (for example Acalanes, Campolindo, Las Lomas, Miramonte, Monte Vista, San Ramon Valley or Ygnacio Valley) to ask about the next intake.
who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.

name: Johnson County Library Teen Volunteers
city: Overland Park and Johnson County, KS
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library records and verifies service hours weekly for schools.
duration: One-time, short-term or weekly shifts
deadline_text: Sign up any time in the volunteer portal. Summer teen opportunities are posted in late April.
who_can_apply: Most volunteer positions take youth 14 and older. Summer teen volunteer jobs are open to ages 13 and older as of June 1. Each job posting lists its own minimum age.
how_to_apply: Register in the library's volunteer database. This is a Samaritan volunteer profile. Then sign up for an opening with the Sign Up button. If no shift is listed, the Volunteer Coordinator follows up with you.
notes: Quote from the page: We welcome and encourage youth volunteers 14 years and older for most volunteer positions. The page says over 900 teens through adults volunteer each year. You can also become a Swift Volunteer for last-minute needs, with no obligation.

name: Junior Achievement of Northern California (high school programs)
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No central deadline; ask JA.
who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages, so ask JA.

name: KP LAUNCH High School Program
city: Northern California Kaiser Permanente service areas
regions: silicon-valley; san-jose; peninsula; fremont; east-bay; oakland; san-francisco; sacramento
grades: Current high school student (priority to juniors and seniors) or Class of 2027 graduate
pay_detail: $25 per hour minimum, paid every two weeks, up to 40 hours a week
duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
deadline_text: Opens Nov 16, 2026 at 9am Pacific; closes Jan 8, 2027 at 5pm Pacific.
who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive. A Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, which is not confirmed here. Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.

name: Kaiser Permanente Redwood City Medical Center High School Volunteer Program
duration: One year
deadline_text: Closed. On 2026-10-16 the page said: not accepting applications, check back in 2027. No 2027 date is posted.
who_can_apply: High school students 16 years or older (the kp.org page says ages 16 to 17). Applications open only when shifts are available. One-year commitment.
how_to_apply: When it opens again, sign up on the Kaiser volunteer site under Redwood City. You need one or two references from a teacher, coach or tutor. Then you do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. A parent must come. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Phone: 650-299-3135.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site and the kp.org Redwood City page on 2026-10-16. The two pages do not agree. kp.org says 4 hours a week for 6 months. The volunteer site says one year for high school students. Plan on one year. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing. The kp.org page also lists roles like the ER, art, pet visits and surgery. These differ by site.

name: Kaiser Permanente San Jose Medical Center High School Volunteer Program
duration: One year
deadline_text: Closed now. On 2026-10-16 the page said the high school program is full and applications are closed, and the High School Programs listing said they are not accepting high school applicants at this time. The page says applications for minors are accepted sporadically during the year when shifts open up. No reopening date is posted.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 years or older to apply. The time commitment is one year. One or two professional references from a teacher, coach, tutor or similar are required.
how_to_apply: When it opens again, apply on the Kaiser volunteer site under San Jose. You need one or two references. Then you do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. Bring a parent. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Volunteer office: 408-972-7230.
notes: Read on Kaiser Permanente's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. The high school program is full. Check the page every few weeks, since minors are taken only when shifts are free. Kaiser does not offer job or clinical shadowing (physician, nursing, radiology, PT or OT). The kp.org page still links to volunteer-ncal.kaiserpermanente.org, which no longer works; use kpvolunteer.samaritan.com.

name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center High School Volunteer Program
city: Santa Clara, CA (Homestead campus, 710 Lawrence Expressway)
duration: One 4-hour weekday shift a week for a planned one year
deadline_text: No deadline posted. On 2026-10-16 the Santa Clara High School Programs listing showed an Apply button.
who_can_apply: Volunteers 16 years and older. The page lists separate steps for 16 and 17 year olds. You must give at least one 4-hour shift each week, Monday to Friday between 8 am and 6 pm, for a planned one year commitment.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Kaiser volunteer site. Look under High School Programs at Santa Clara Homestead. Then do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. A parent must come with you. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Volunteer office: 408-851-1717.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. The kp.org Santa Clara page links to it at kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. Shifts are on weekdays only, 8 am to 6 pm. Most students would need a free period, a late afternoon or summer days. A background check with a Social Security number is only for people over 18. The page asks for shot records. It does not say which shots, if you need a TB test, or if there are fees. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing.

name: Kaiser Permanente South San Francisco High School Volunteer Program
city: South San Francisco, CA (1200 El Camino Real; also Daly City and San Bruno offices)
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, for the rest of high school
deadline_text: Not open to high school students right now. On 2026-10-16 the page said high school applications are accepted sporadically during the year based on shift availability, and that after a system upgrade it is taking a very limited number of applications, with adults 18+ applying to Hospital Services. No date is posted.
who_can_apply: High school students 16 years or older (the kp.org page says ages 16 to 17). Commit to one 4-hour shift a week, same day and time. The time commitment spans your high school career.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 650-742-2678. Ask when high school spots will open. Then apply on the Kaiser volunteer site under South San Francisco.
notes: Read on Kaiser Permanente's volunteer site and the kp.org page on 2026-10-16. The kp.org page says a few hours a week for a few months, but the volunteer site says the high school commitment spans your high school career; plan on the longer one. The Daly City Medical Offices page has the same high school rules. Kaiser does not offer job or clinical shadowing. The page does not list vaccine, TB test or fee rules.

name: Kaiser Permanente Walnut Creek Medical Center High School Volunteer Program
city: Walnut Creek, CA (1425 South Main St)
duration: One 3 to 4 hour shift a week, for the rest of high school
deadline_text: No deadline posted. On 2026-10-16 the Walnut Creek High School Programs listing showed an Apply button, but its Status line was blank.
who_can_apply: High school students age 15 or older. You must give one 3 to 4 hour shift a week on the same day and time, and stay in the program for your whole high school career. The high school track is at Walnut Creek Medical Center only.
how_to_apply: Go to the Kaiser volunteer site. Open High School Programs at Walnut Creek and click Apply. You will log in or sign up as a new volunteer. Questions? Call 925-295-5487.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. kp.org links to it at kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. This is a long commitment. The page says it lasts all through high school. The page does not list shots, a TB test or fees. It does not say if a parent must sign. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing. Adult volunteers here also cover nearby offices. The high school track is at Walnut Creek only. Kaiser's old volunteer link no longer works, so use kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. The Pleasanton and San Ramon offices said on 2026-10-16 that they are not taking high school students right now.

name: Volunteer Restoration Workdays (all ages)
org: Forest Preserve District of Kane County
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: Workdays are monthly. Cancelled when it is below zero.
deadline_text: No deadline. See the monthly list of workdays on the volunteer page.
who_can_apply: Workdays are described as for all ages, individuals and families. No sign up needed unless you come with a group of 10 or more. Age rules for the longer volunteer roles are not on the pages.
how_to_apply: For workdays, just show up 5 to 10 minutes early and sign in with the leader. For longer roles, fill out the volunteer application on the site. Volunteer Office: 630-762-2741, volunteer@kaneforest.com.
notes: Bring boots or sturdy shoes, a water bottle and gloves. Info on Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects is in the Resources section of the volunteer page. Questions about workdays: Stewardship Specialist, 630-200-1290.

name: Kane County Workforce Development Youth Services (WIOA Youth)
city: Kane, DeKalb and Kendall Counties (Elgin area), IL
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one of the services; pay rate is not stated.
duration: Varies by provider
deadline_text: No dates posted. You contact a provider and they explain how to start.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc. Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.
notes: Starts at age 16, so it fits older high schoolers. The page names one contact person but lists an email that does not match that name, so phone first. Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.

name: Kansas 4-H Discovery Days
org: Kansas 4-H Youth Development, Kansas State University
duration: About 3 days (June 3 to 5 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 event was June 3 to 5. The program page says registration is closed and does not list 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 as of January 1 of the event year.
how_to_apply: Registration for 2026 is closed. The page tells youth to let their Extension unit know which class session they choose. The page does not say how to register next year. Email kansas4h@ksu.edu with questions.
notes: Not stated on the program page: whether you must be a 4-H member. Ask your county Extension office.

name: High School Summer Volunteer

how_to_apply: Watch the program page in spring 2027 for the application.
notes: Spots are limited. Other high school chances are on the hospital's For High School Students page.

name: Summer Training in Academic Research (STAR 2.0)
pay_detail: $2,600 stipend
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (2026: June 15 to July 23)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Dec 15, 2025 to Jan 9, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect a similar winter window.
who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who live in Missouri or Kansas. You go to a public or charter school. You do not need research experience. Shots must be up to date. First choice goes to students from poorer neighborhoods.
how_to_apply: Fill out the STAR 2.0 student form on the program page in the winter window.
notes: Held at 2401 Gillham Road, Kansas City, MO. You must attend the whole 6 weeks.

name: Teen Arts Council
pay_detail: $100 per month stipend. Free to join.
duration: Alternate Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., Sept to Nov and Jan to May (2026-27)
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 term are closed. Interviews were in August 2026. Next application dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Any high school student in the Kansas City metro area, any art form. If picked for an interview you must be free in August.
how_to_apply: Use the form on the KemperTeens site when it opens again. Then interview in August.
notes: Meets at 4420 Warwick Boulevard, Kansas City, MO. You must get yourself to meetings and events. Page does not say which month applications open.

name: VolunTeen Student Summer Volunteer Program
org: The University of Kansas Health System
pay_detail: Volunteer program.
duration: Rising sophomore to senior: one 2-week session, Monday to Thursday. Rising freshman: half days on Friday mornings, at least 6 Fridays.
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was March 6, 2026. The program page does not list 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: Students going into 9th grade can join the rising freshman program. Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade can join the other program. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: Use the application link for your program on the program page. You must go to an in-person orientation. Email VolunteerApplications@KUMC.edu or call 913-588-6560.
notes: 2026 sessions ran June 1 to July 30. There is also a program page for the Olathe location.

name: Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Museum store discounts.
duration: Three sessions a year: spring, summer and fall
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. Spring session dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school age students. Exact ages not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: See the volunteer page for the form when a session opens. Questions: volunteer@theworldwar.org or 816-888-8115.
notes: Adults must be 19 or older for the regular program, so this is a separate youth track. Ask about the age rule.

name: Teen Council
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer experience.
duration: not stated
deadline_text: Page says applications are now open. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Students from schools across Kansas City. Age or grade not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Council application form linked on the museum's teen programs page. Questions: teens@nelson-atkins.org.
notes: Teens also get $5 tickets to special exhibitions. The same page lists Teen Open Mic Nights (free, bi-monthly) and Teen Drop-In Art Making.

name: ProX Summer Internship Program
org: ProX (Professional Experiences for Kansas City Youth)
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend
duration: 5 weeks (2026: June 1 to July 2)
deadline_text: Page says check back in early January 2027 for summer 2027 applications (exact date not posted). 2026 applications closed Feb 20, 2026; the hiring fair was Mar 21, 2026.
who_can_apply: Current 9th to 12th graders ages 14 to 19. You live and go to high school in Jackson, Clay, Platte or Cass counties in Missouri, or Johnson or Wyandotte counties in Kansas. You must meet employer hiring and work rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form. Finish the paperwork. Go to a prep workshop. Then interview at the spring hiring fair.
notes: The 2027 close date and hiring fair date are not posted yet.

name: Teen volunteering at Kansas City Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings depend on the branch.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Talk to the teen volunteer coordinator at your branch to ask if they have openings.
notes: Openings depend on the branch.

name: STAHR High School Scholars
pay_detail: Free. Students who meet expectations get a stipend, a scholarship, or both. Amounts not stated.
duration: 2026: June 8 to July 17, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus August to April
deadline_text: 2027 application opens Nov 15, 2026. The page prints a Feb 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm CST deadline, which appears to belong to the earlier cycle. No 2027 deadline is posted yet.
who_can_apply: Current sophomores and juniors with at least a 3.0 GPA. You must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. You must like a health job (nursing does not count). You must also have money or school disadvantage. Family income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty line.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online STAHR form. Send a transcript with unweighted GPA. Send 1 professional recommendation through the online reference form (letters are not accepted). Questions: stahr@umkc.edu, 816-235-6169.
notes: Questions: stahr@umkc.edu or 816-235-6169.

name: VolunTEEN
pay_detail: Unpaid. Trailblazers need 60 hours in summer and 18 hours each in fall and spring.
duration: May through April. Three seasons: summer, fall, spring.
deadline_text: Applications open November 2026. The page gives no close date.
who_can_apply: Students in 8th to 12th grade at the time of application. Seniors can join for the summer season only. Mature, responsible teens who like working with the public and care about animals.
how_to_apply: Apply online for a pathway when applications open. See the zoo's VolunTEEN page.
notes: The zoo page says applications open November 2026. Exact dates are not posted.

name: Leaders in Training and Counselors in Training
pay_detail: 2026 cost for five nights: LIT $800, $700 or $600 by tier. CIT $650, $550 or $450 by tier. The page says the program can be attended at no cost through a donation to the Kansas 4-H Foundation.
duration: Five nights
deadline_text: 2026 sessions ran June 7 to 12, June 14 to 19, July 5 to 10 and July 12 to 17. The program page does not list 2027 dates or a deadline.
who_can_apply: LIT is for ages 14 to 16. CIT is for ages 16 to 17. The page says CIT is especially for rising 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Letter of Interest for LIT or CIT on the program page. You then get instructions on how to register. Call 785-257-3221 with questions.
notes: A camper scholarship (campership) form is linked on the page. Check the page in early 2027 for new dates and prices.

name: King County Library System Teen Advisory Boards
city: King County, WA (branches outside the city of Seattle)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit, and can ask for a reference letter after 10 hours of volunteering within 6 months.
duration: Ongoing; meeting schedules vary by branch
deadline_text: No deadline. The page lists upcoming meetings (for example Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way); contact the local library to join.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state ages; ask the teen librarian at your branch. Each board sets its own meeting schedule.

notes: KCLS serves King County outside the city of Seattle (its branches include Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way). The Seattle Public Library volunteer page showed no current volunteer openings when read on 2026-10-09. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: Health Science Explorers Academy
org: University of Nebraska at Kearney Health Sciences
pay_detail: $100 for the program, with financial help available. Lunch is provided. Students who finish earn a $1,000 UNK scholarship.
duration: September to May, first Wednesday of each month, 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: Registration for the 2027-2028 school year opens January 4, 2027. Close date not stated.
who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade who are interested in a health care career. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens on January 4, 2027. Use the link on the Health Science Explorers page. Contact the coordinator listed on the page with questions.

name: Keck Medicine of USC Summer Youth Volunteer Program
org: Keck Medicine of USC, Office of Volunteer Services
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: 8 weeks, at least 8 hours a week and 60 hours total
deadline_text: The page lists the application period as Feb 1 to April 30, with recommendation letters due April 30 (year not stated). Orientation is the second week of June.
who_can_apply: Currently enrolled high school students ages 16 to 17. Must be 16 or older when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need a self-portrait photo, proof of COVID-19 vaccination and a questionnaire. Recommenders email letters to volunteer@med.usc.edu by April 30. If accepted, you do an interview. Then you get a health screening with a TB test, an orientation and a tour. Phone (323) 442-8436.
notes: Check the page in January for the next year's dates.

name: Kennesaw Police Public Safety Cadet Program
pay_detail: Volunteer program. The page lists no fees.

notes: Busiest months are May to September. Younger teens can ask about parent-accompanied options.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Massachusetts Wing

The program page does not state the income limit, the eligibility factors or the age 14 minimum; those come from the FAQ PDF, which could not be read in this check, so confirm them with the local program.

name: Mesa Police Cadet Post 2055
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page. No fee is listed.
duration: Weekly meetings on Thursday nights
deadline_text: The post recruits twice a year. The program page says the next recruitment window is October 2025.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, and you must have finished 8th grade. Stay in school until you graduate. Keep a 2.0 GPA or higher. No serious police record.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest form on the Mesa cadet page. A cadet advisor then contacts you. For help, call 480-644-4869 or email PDCadets@mesaaz.gov.
notes: Members can stay in the Post until they turn 21. Cadets also do community service. Ask the post for the next recruiting date.

name: Teen Library Volunteer
org: Montgomery-Floyd Regional Library (Blacksburg and Christiansburg branches)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and return it to the front desk. An application does not guarantee acceptance. Missing 3 shifts without notice removes you from the schedule.
notes: The page was last updated Nov 12, 2024, so call your branch to confirm. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Michigan Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Michigan
pay_detail: Cost to the student is not stated on the program pages. The page asks people to donate to send a young woman to Girls State.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
deadline_text: The 86th session is June 13 to 19, 2027 at Michigan State University. The 2027 application is posted online. No closing date is stated on the flyer or page.
who_can_apply: Female high school students who will finish their junior year in spring 2027. You must have at least one more semester before graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online delegate application. The link is on the Michigan Girls State page and the 2027 flyer. Questions go to the Girls State chairman, Beryl Robbins, at berylrobbins1980@gmail.com or (313) 318-6845.
notes: Not a job. A closing date was not on the page or flyer, so apply early. The page also lists a Samsung scholarship and a government manual to read before attending.

name: American Legion Michigan Boys State
city: Hillsdale, MI (2026 session at Hillsdale College); office in Lansing

notes: Not a job. Dates, fees and the deadline above are from the 2026 brochure and flyer, so confirm the 2027 details with the office. The resources page still showed a May 1, 2024 deadline, so it is out of date. Office address: 212 N. Verlinden Ave., Lansing, MI 48915.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services for blind and low vision students (BSBP)
org: Bureau of Services for Blind Persons, Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Programs run throughout the year
deadline_text: No deadline. Check the program calendar on the page for current programs.

how_to_apply: Contact your local BSBP office or your school special education office. You can also fill out the form at the IEP meeting.
notes: Programs may target a certain age group, interest or skill.

name: Volunteer at Cranbrook Institute of Science
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: A regular schedule is welcome but not required. Special event shifts are short.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A volunteer open house is offered.

how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form on the page, sign up for an open house, or contact the Volunteer Coordinator at 248-341-2756 or CIS_volunteer@cranbrook.edu. Required paperwork is needed.
notes: Special Events Volunteer is a good short option for community service hours. Nature Zone shifts are weekends and select holidays.

name: Teen Volunteer at Dearborn Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. The program page says the library is only taking teen volunteer applications at this time.
who_can_apply: Students who are at least 13 years old and enrolled in a Dearborn school. Volunteer spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Watch the orientation video. Then print the form and bring it to any Dearborn library.
notes: The library does not take court-ordered service. It cannot take all requests, so spots are few.

name: Michigan DECA chapters and state conference
org: Michigan DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
pay_detail: $17 per student member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Michigan DECA conference is March 11 to 13, 2027 at Huntington Place in Detroit. No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a marketing, management, finance, hospitality or entrepreneurship course. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Michigan DECA advisor, Dave Wait. His email is dwait@emich.edu.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is mideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Michigan.

name: Detroit at Work Year-Round Youth Program
pay_detail: Free to join. Offers paid and unpaid work experiences, plus stipends for training and career exploration. Amounts not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Call 313-962-9675 to ask.
who_can_apply: Must live in Detroit and be 14 to 24. You must show papers that prove age, residency and eligibility. Some programs also take Highland Park and Hamtramck residents.
how_to_apply: Call 313-962-WORK (9675) or visit a Detroit at Work career center (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.). Bring documents that prove age and where you live.
notes: Summer jobs are a separate track (Grow Detroit's Young Talent). Pay rates and the work permit rule for this program are not stated on the page.

name: Grow Detroit's Young Talent (GDYT)
pay_detail: Wage jobs pay $12.50 to $15 per hour, paid every two weeks. Stipend jobs pay $1,500 to $2,000.
duration: About 6 weeks, up to 120 hours, usually early July through August
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran March 13 to May 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Detroit. Ages 14 to 24. You can apply at 13 if you turn 14 by July 1.
how_to_apply: Express interest at GDYT.org. Picks are made by random lottery. If chosen, finish enrollment forms and upload documents (including a work permit for ages 14 to 17), then attend orientation.
notes: The FAQ lists a work permit for ages 14 to 17 as a required document. Up to 8,000 spots in 2026, so a lottery decides. Next year's window is likely spring 2027.

name: RYSE MED (Readying Youth Scientists for Excellence in Medicine)
pay_detail: The page says stipends or wages may be available for high school students but are not guaranteed. The program is free.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 28 to Aug 7, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) plus monthly meetings September to May
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 group are closed. Details for the 2027-28 group come 'in the new year.'
who_can_apply: First-time participants who go to high school or live in metro Detroit, in 10th or 11th grade, age 16 or older by program start, GPA 2.5 or higher, and allowed to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Email HAPE@hfhs.org with questions.
notes: The page says students under 18 must get a work permit. Teens must also join at least one year-round track.

name: Department of Surgery High School Mentorship Program
pay_detail: Program is free. Summer interns get a $1,000 stipend for 7 weeks.
duration: 7-week summer internship. Saturday sessions during the school year.
deadline_text: 2026 internship application closed April 30, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Detroit-area high school students who are curious about health care. No medical experience needed. Grades and school districts are not listed.
how_to_apply: Submit the online internship application form linked on the summer internship page. For the program, email iokerek1@hfhs.org or call 313-916-2698.
notes: Very competitive: the page says 331 applied and 25 were chosen in 2025. The application link may be the 2026 form, so check the page for the next one.

name: Medical Mentors Pathway Program (M2P2)
org: Wayne State University School of Medicine, Karmanos Cancer Institute and MI-AHEC
pay_detail: Pay and cost not stated on the program pages
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 24 to August 6)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed. Applicants were told by April 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (going into 12th grade) and college freshmen, sophomores and juniors.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the program site. A 2-day orientation comes first. Students finish assignments and weekly classes.
notes: Rising seniors and college students apply to the same program. Contact: medicalmentorspipeline@gmail.com. Cost was not stated, so ask before applying.

name: Volunteer at the Michigan Science Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Time commitment not stated
deadline_text: The page does not state a deadline or whether applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Use the online volunteer application.
who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who passes a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then wait for an interview to find the best fit.
notes: The page does not list specific roles or hours. Ask the volunteer team (volunteers@mi-sci.org) about teen roles.

name: Beginners' Investment Camp 101
org: University of Detroit Mercy, College of Business Administration (Charlton Center)
grades: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors
pay_detail: Free. Materials, breakfast, snacks, lunch, a T-shirt and a backpack are included.
duration: One week. In 2026 it ran June 22 to 26, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily.
deadline_text: The 2026 camp has passed. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students from Metro Detroit with little or no investing knowledge.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application packet. Add two letters of recommendation and the signed forms. Email it to edwarddj1@udmercy.edu.
notes: Held on the McNichols Campus, 4001 West McNichols Rd. The camp page still says applications are open, but the 2026 camp dates have passed. Ask the camp director before you apply.

name: Youth Health Exploration Camp
org: University of Detroit Mercy, College of Health Professions
pay_detail: Free. Breakfast, lunch and snacks are included. Campers also get a lab jacket and a blood pressure cuff.
duration: One week. In 2026 the high school week was July 27 to 31, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
deadline_text: The 2026 camp is full. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who want to explore health careers. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: The 2026 camp is full, so you cannot apply now. The program page does not post 2027 sign-up dates. Questions can go to Nina Favor at favornf@udmercy.edu.
notes: Held at the STAR Center on the McNichols Campus. The middle school week was July 20 to 24, 2026. The high school week was July 27 to 31, 2026.

name: Biomedical Career Advancement Program (BCAP)
org: Wayne State University School of Medicine and MI-AHEC Southeast Regional Center
pay_detail: Students who finish may get a monetary award. It depends on funding and is not guaranteed.
duration: 6 weeks. Monday to Thursday up to 5 hours a day, plus Friday events 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications ran Feb 23 to Apr 24, 2026 (5 p.m.). Program ran July 6 to Aug 14, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in 10th, 11th or 12th grade with a GPA of 2.75 or higher. Priority goes to Wayne County residents, Detroit Public Schools Community District students, and students from disadvantaged backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and write a 300 to 400 word personal statement. An official transcript is needed if you are accepted.
notes: Program dates may change. Contact: BCAPstudentgroup@gmail.com or (313) 577-1584.

name: Summer Academy high school camps
org: Wayne State University, Anderson College of Engineering
pay_detail: Price not on the program pages. A scholarships page is listed.
duration: 1 week per camp. You can mix topics across weeks.
deadline_text: The page says all summer 2026 sessions are complete. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. Choose camp I or II of a topic, not both.
how_to_apply: Register through the Summer Academy pages. Use the question link to reach the Director of Community Engagement.
notes: Cost was not stated on the pages. Ask about the scholarship page before you decide.

name: Zoo Corps (teen volunteers)
pay_detail: Cost not listed
duration: Summer track: 60 hours June to August. Year-round track adds shifts September to May.
deadline_text: Page says applications are now closed. No new dates posted. Past cycle closed in late spring.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 by June 1. You need your own ride to the zoo.
how_to_apply: Send the application and documents on the zoo page. A parent and teen must do a phone or video interview. Go to one mandatory virtual meeting, then a full training week (9 a.m. to 4 p.m.) in late June or early July.
notes: Work is outdoors in all weather. Training hours count toward the 60. A separate Counselor in Training program is listed but the page gave no details. Questions go to the zoo education department.

name: Michigan FFA membership through a school ag class
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 21 who are enrolled in a state-approved agricultural education course. The page does not list grades.
how_to_apply: Use the chapters and regions page to find a chapter near you, then ask that school about its agriculture class. Questions can go to the state office.
notes: Not a job. The homepage says there are over 10,000 members in 137 chapters. State office: association@michiganffa.org or (517) 353-9221.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) in Michigan
pay_detail: Registration cost not stated. Scholarships are listed through FIRST.
duration: Build and competition season
deadline_text: No 2027 dates are posted on the FRC page. It only shows 2026 events.
who_can_apply: Teams of high school students. The page does not give an age or grade rule. It links to Start a Team and Run a Team.
how_to_apply: Join an existing school or community team or use the Start a Team link on the FIRST in Michigan site. Contact on the page: Gail Alpert, 248.425.4148.
notes: Ask your school if it has a team. FIRST in Michigan also runs FTC and FIRST LEGO League for younger students.

name: Forgotten Harvest Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. School service hours can be signed off.
duration: Shifts are 9 am to 12 pm or 1 pm to 4 pm, Monday through Saturday
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Volunteers sign up online ahead of time for a shift.
who_can_apply: Volunteers in the distribution center must be at least 10. Volunteers under 18 must come with a parent or guardian. Other roles outside the warehouse need volunteers who are at least 14.
how_to_apply: Register online for a shift before you come. You get an email with the place, parking and dress code. Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes.
notes: You must stay for the whole shift. Bring school service paperwork so hours can be signed. The kids program is on hold. Some roles, like Harvest Heroes drivers and site monitors, are 18 and older.

name: Summer Youth Program (volunteer)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 8 weeks, at least one 4-hour shift a week (2026: June 8 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. No 2027 dates posted.

how_to_apply: Apply on the hospital page when it opens. Spaces are limited and picks are made after an interview. Orientation is required. The application includes a health screening checklist, and a parent must be there for any shots.
notes: Jackson is west of Ann Arbor and south of Lansing, so it may be a drive. Teens must commit to all assigned shifts.

name: Summer Teen Volunteering at Henry Ford Providence Novi
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: 9 weeks, one 4-hour shift per week
deadline_text: Apply from March 1 to March 15, 2027 for summer 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students and 2027 high school graduates who are ages 16 to 17. You must be 16 by June 16, 2027. You must be free for 9 or more weeks in June, July and August 2027.
how_to_apply: Send the information form from March 1 to March 15, 2027. Go to an information session. Pass a background check. Do a health screen. Finish a training packet. Letters of recommendation are optional.
notes: Only a limited number of teens are accepted. Others go on a wait list. Selected candidates need a TB test and TDap and MMR shots. The hospital covers the cost.

name: Summer Teen Volunteering at Henry Ford Providence Southfield
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: 9 weeks, one 4-hour shift per week
deadline_text: Apply from March 1 to March 15, 2027 for summer 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students and 2027 high school graduates who are ages 16 to 17. You must be 16 by June 16, 2027. You must be free for 9 or more weeks in June, July and August 2027.
how_to_apply: Send the information form from March 1 to March 15, 2027. Go to an information session. Pass a background check. Do a health screen. Finish a training packet. Letters of recommendation are optional.
notes: Only a limited number of teens are accepted. Others go on a wait list. Selected candidates need a TB test and TDap and MMR shots. The hospital covers the cost. In fall, winter and early spring, on-site spots are only for teens who already volunteer.

name: Summer High School Volunteering at Henry Ford West Bloomfield
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: 10 weeks in 2026, one 4-hour shift per week
deadline_text: The 2026 window was March 1 to March 15, 2026, and it is closed. Dates for summer 2027 are not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: High school students and graduates who are ages 16 to 17. In 2026, you had to be 16 by June 17, 2026 and free for 10 or more weeks in the summer.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for next year. In 2026 you sent an information form between March 1 and March 15. Candidates went to an information session. They passed a background check and a health screen. They also finished a training packet.
notes: The page says only 30 candidates will be picked for the summer program. Letters of recommendation are optional, and the page says they can help a lot. Chosen candidates need a TB test and TDap and MMR shots. The hospital covers the cost.

name: Michigan HOSA (Future Health Professionals)
grades: Middle school, high school and college students
pay_detail: Dues and fees not stated on the home page
duration: School year. State conference in April 2027 at the Grand Traverse Resort.

who_can_apply: Students interested in health care, through a school chapter. The site also says you can start a chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your school health or CTE teacher about a chapter, or use the Join MI HOSA link on the site. Contact: hosa@mhc.org or (517) 347-8088.
notes: The site lists more than 10,000 Michigan members.

name: Metroparks Volunteer Workdays
city: Southeast Michigan (parks include Hudson Mills, Dexter-Huron, Stony Creek, Willow)
pay_detail: Free, unpaid
duration: About 2 hours (10 a.m. to noon)
deadline_text: Workdays run through the year. Sign up by noon the day before each one. The workdays listed on the page were July 11, Aug 22 and Sept 26 (the page does not show the year).
who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Children must come with a registered adult.
how_to_apply: Pick a workday on the volunteering page and register online by noon the day before. For regular volunteering, send the application and waiver to volunteer@metroparks.com.
notes: Dress for dirt: long pants, closed-toe shoes, layers. Poison ivy can be present. Children must come with a registered adult. Volunteers under 14 must have an adult with them for the whole shift, and a parent or guardian must sign the waiver for volunteers under 18. The volunteering page does not mention seasonal paid jobs.

name: Jump-Start Jackson
pay_detail: Paid on-the-job training; rate not stated

how_to_apply: Use the Youth and Young Adult Application link on the Jump-Start Jackson page.
notes: The Summer Youth Employment page lists it as one of the Michigan Works! Southeast summer programs. Jackson is west of Ann Arbor. Ask about dates and pay.

name: YouthWorks (Livingston County summer jobs)

pay_detail: Paid; the page does not state the hourly rate
duration: 2026 program: June 15 to August 14
deadline_text: 2026 program ran June 15 to Aug 14, 2026. Application dates for 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Livingston County. Juniors and seniors in high school, or anyone 24 or younger regardless of graduation.
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us link on the YouthWorks page, or call the Michigan Works! Southeast office.
notes: Livingston County is northwest of Ann Arbor (Howell and Brighton area). The page does not state the work permit rule for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services for students with disabilities (Michigan Rehabilitation Services)
org: Michigan Rehabilitation Services, Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity
pay_detail: MRS pays for services in your employment plan. Not a wage.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 26 who are in school or have been accepted at school after high school. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign a consent form. Your school fills out a form that shows the disability.
how_to_apply: Use the MRS Online Application. Forms MRS-4.0a (parent consent) and MRS-4.0b (school verification) are on the page. Phone 517-241-5324 or toll-free 800-605-6722.
notes: Work-based learning is one of five services. Ask your school transition coordinator or counselor too.

name: Michigan Tech Summer Youth Programs
org: Michigan Technological University, Summer Youth Programs
grades: Middle and high school (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Exploration programs start at $1,175 live-in (tuition, fees, meals, room and board) or $700 commuter. A $150 non-refundable deposit is due at registration. Pathway program fees vary. Scholarships exist.
duration: Week-long programs
deadline_text: 2027 registration and program dates are not posted yet on the program pages. Balances are due in full by May 1 and most scholarships are reviewed on a rolling basis.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from around the world. The cost page lists no grade rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Now link on the Summer Youth Programs page and pay the $150 deposit at registration. Pathway programs have nothing due at application. Contact syp@mtu.edu or 906-487-2219.
notes: Extra costs can include lab fees, a $20 weekly parking pass and charter bus service. Check the Course Catalog and Scholarships pages on the SYP site for current offerings.

name: Oakland NEXT paid internships and career exploration
city: Oakland County, MI (Pontiac and other service centers)
pay_detail: Internships are typically paid. Pay rate not stated.
duration: Not stated. Offers summer and year-round internships.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Fill out the Oakland NEXT application and staff will contact you.
who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in Oakland County. Other rules are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Oakland NEXT application on the Youth page. Or call 248-858-5520 or email oaklandcountymiworks@oaklandcountymi.gov.
notes: The county reported 164 paid work experiences with 60 employers in 2024. The page also lists an IAmPontiac summer internship; details were not read. Ask about the work permit rule for ages 16 and 17.

name: Oakland County Parks Teen Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. A parent or guardian fills out the online application for the teen.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian completes the teen online application. Choose your site and your areas of interest. Open roles are posted on Idealist.
notes: Court-ordered community service is not offered. Groups of 10 or more use a separate group form. Adults 18 and older use a different application.

name: Wolverine Pathways
city: Detroit, Southfield, Ypsilanti and Grand Rapids, MI
grades: Apply in 6th or 9th grade; join in 7th or 10th grade
pay_detail: Free.
duration: From 7th or 10th grade through 12th grade; up to seven Saturdays a semester plus 2 to 4 summer weeks
deadline_text: The next application window opens in December 2026. Last cycle, Southeast Michigan applications closed February 28, 2026 and Grand Rapids applications closed March 20, 2026.
who_can_apply: Students in 6th or 9th grade with at least a 3.0 GPA (3.2 for 9th graders) who live inside the Detroit Public Schools, Southfield Public Schools or Ypsilanti Community Schools district. The school you attend does not matter. The home page also lists Grand Rapids.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in December. Join the mailing list for info sessions. Questions: wp-admissions@umich.edu, (734) 647-3848.
notes: No exceptions are made for the Southeast Michigan deadline. You must keep strong grades and attendance to stay in. In 10th to 12th grade you can pick summer courses, camps or internships.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Michigan Wing
pay_detail: Annual dues are $40 for cadets. The page estimates a fully active cadet could spend $300 to $600 in the first year, minus help for uniforms and overnight fees.
duration: Ideally a 2-hour squadron meeting each week plus about one Saturday event a month. A week-long summer encampment is encouraged.
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Contact it to confirm a meeting. Go to about three meetings before you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Wing HQ mailing address: 43401 N. Jefferson, Bldg. 825, Rm 317, PO Box 450048, Selfridge ANGB, MI 48045-0048. School comes first; the page says school-based squadrons may differ.

name: WIOA Youth Program through your local Michigan Works! agency
org: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity, delivered by local Michigan Works! agencies (Michigan Works! Southeast for Washtenaw County, Capital Area Michigan Works! for the Lansing area)
pay_detail: Not stated. The state page lists both paid and unpaid work experiences, including summer employment, as possible services.
duration: Varies by local agency
deadline_text: Operated year round by local Michigan Works! agencies. No state deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low income and have at least one listed barrier (for example basic skills deficient, English language learner, homeless or foster youth, pregnant or parenting, disability). Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with a listed barrier.
how_to_apply: Call Michigan Works! at 1-800-285-WORKS (9675). Or find your local agency by ZIP code at michiganworks.org. Then ask about WIOA Youth eligibility.
notes: Not open to every teen: eligibility depends on income and barriers, so a short call to the local agency is the real first step. The state page does not list a local application form or local youth contacts. Capital Area Michigan Works!' own site (camw.org) mentions WIOA and says 259 youth were served but does not describe its youth program in detail. Work experience for anyone under 18 in Michigan needs a work permit under the state's youth employment law.

name: YMCA Michigan Youth in Government
pay_detail: The base fee is not stated on the program page. A $25 late fee applies to late Lansing registration. A financial aid application is linked on the page.
duration: Fall district conference, then a Lansing conference of about four days
deadline_text: Fall district conferences run Oct 2 to Nov 9, 2026. Sign-up closes about two weeks before each one. District 6 (Detroit, Nov 9) closes Oct 26, 2026. Sign-up for the other fall districts has ended. Lansing sign-up opens Nov 10, 2026. February Lansing conference (Feb 18 to 21, 2027): regular sign-up closes Dec 27, 2026, late sign-up Dec 28 to Jan 13 with a $25 fee. April Lansing conference (Apr 22 to 25, 2027): regular sign-up closes Feb 28, 2027, late sign-up Mar 1 to 17 with a $25 fee.
who_can_apply: High school students (a separate middle school program exists). The pages do not list grades. You join through a school or YMCA delegation.
how_to_apply: Check the map on the YMCA page to see if your school or YMCA has a delegation. If not, use the Contact us page to start one. Then register for the conferences your delegation attends.
notes: Not a job. The deadline date is the end of regular sign-up for the February Lansing conference. Lansing sign-up opens Nov 10, 2026. Fall conference sites include Marquette, Grayling, Allendale, Saginaw, Kalamazoo and Detroit. As of Oct 13, 2026, only the District 6 fall conference in Detroit is still open. The February and April Lansing windows are not open yet.

name: Michigan Youth Challenge Academy (MYCA)
org: Michigan National Guard, Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
pay_detail: Free to parents. No obligation to join the military.
duration: 5.5 months residential plus 12 months after. Cycles start mid-January and mid-July.
deadline_text: Two cycles a year. The January start application opens Aug 1. The July start application opens Feb 1. The application takes place over the 4 to 5 months before each cycle. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 1/2 to 18 on day one (15 1/2 means you turn 16 during the cycle). Must be a Michigan resident and a U.S. citizen or legally present, not yet have a high school diploma, not be on reporting probation, and have no felonies. Ages 15 1/2 can only do credit recovery and return to their high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Inquiry Form on the MYCA site. Then follow the steps on the Admissions Process list.
notes: It has a military style setup, but the page says you do not have to join the military. The page calls it a program for at risk youth who want to finish high school.

name: Opportunity Youth Program, Middlesex College
pay_detail: Paid training and work experience are listed; the wage is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates listed.
who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Middlesex County and meet additional eligibility criteria. Not for teens currently enrolled in high school.
how_to_apply: Email opportunityyouthprogram@middlesexcollege.edu to start. Office: 550 Jersey Avenue, New Brunswick, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
notes: The page does not name the funding source. Teens under 18 who are not in school should check eligibility with the office. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.

name: Milpitas Fire Explorer Program
duration: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No dates are stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Call the Milpitas Fire Department at 408-586-2800 to get involved or ask questions.
notes: The page is short and gives no meeting times, requirements or application form. Call first to ask if the program is active and taking new Explorers.

name: Milpitas Lifeguard / Swim Instructor (part-time, ages 15+)
org: City of Milpitas Recreation and Community Services
pay_detail: $18.50 to $25.77 per hour
duration: Part-time, year-round and seasonal. Shifts are usually 4 hours. August to June: Monday to Saturday, 5:30 am to 8:30 pm. Summer: daily, 5:30 am to 9 pm.
deadline_text: Closing date: Continuous. Open until filled and may close at any time. Applications are screened on a regular basis.
who_can_apply: At least 15 at the time of hire. You must pass a swim skills test through a Lifeguard Academy before you are hired. Experience with kids and adults is preferred, not required.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Milpitas city job board. Before you are hired, you must pass a swim test at a Lifeguard Academy.
notes: This posting first opened Sep 3, 2024 and is still listed as continuous. Its application questions still mention 2024-25 shifts, so call 408-586-3090 to check current hiring. A TB test is required. Fingerprints are only required if you are 18 or older.

name: Milpitas Police Explorers
duration: Ongoing, with meetings twice a month.
deadline_text: No application dates are stated on the page.
who_can_apply: The city page says ages 14 to 20 in one place and 16 to 20 in another, so ask. You need at least a 2.0 GPA, no major criminal convictions, and no substance abuse. You do not have to live in Milpitas.
how_to_apply: Get the Explorer form, the history form and the health form from the page. Or pick up a form at the police station, 1275 N Milpitas Blvd. You must pass a talk with officers and a background check. Call 408-586-2400 with questions.
notes: The info sheet on the page is from 2010. It still names the Boy Scouts as a sponsor. Call 408-586-2400 to check that the program takes new members.

name: Milpitas Recreation Leader (part-time, ages 16+)
org: City of Milpitas Recreation and Community Services
pay_detail: $18.50 to $25.77 per hour
duration: Part-time, year-round and seasonal. Usually Monday to Friday, 2 to 6 pm, with some nights, weekends and holidays. Up to 1,000 hours a year.
deadline_text: Opened May 5, 2026. Open until filled and may close at any time. Applications are screened on a regular basis.
who_can_apply: At least 16 at the time of hire. You must have some experience working with elementary school age kids.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Milpitas city job board. Or mail a paper form and a resume to the Milpitas Community Center, 457 E Calaveras Blvd. Call 408-586-3210 with questions.
notes: You need a TB test and Red Cross First Aid and CPR within 60 days of hire. Fingerprints are only required if you are 18 or older. Perks include a free Milpitas Sports Center membership and paid sick leave after 90 days.

name: Milpitas Volunteer Program (teen-friendly roles)
org: City of Milpitas Recreation and Community Services
duration: Ongoing. Some jobs are one day, others are longer projects.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline.
who_can_apply: All ages. Volunteers under 14 need a parent or adult with them. Some jobs have their own rules. Volunteers 18 and older need fingerprint clearance for some jobs.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. You do not need a form for park cleanups. Call 408-586-3210 or email volunteers@milpitas.gov with questions.
notes: The Alviso Adobe likes high school helpers, but most tours are on school day mornings. Teen Center tutoring is on weekdays from 4 to 7 pm. The page's list of events and cleanups looks old (the last cleanup shown is from January 2024). Watch the monthly emails for new ones.

name: Milpitas Youth Advisory Commission
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)
deadline_text: The city says commission applications are accepted year-round, and appointments are made as needed. No closing date is stated.
who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.

name: Teens at Mingei
pay_detail: $750 for full participation
duration: 15 sessions, twice a month on Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., October to May
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications ran March 2 to April 1, 2026, with interviews April 20 to 24 and notices in August. Next cycle not posted; expect a similar spring window.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17, entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2026, and attending a San Diego County high school.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a mandatory in-person interview and group interview if advanced. Contact the museum's Education Specialist or see the program PDF on the page.
notes: Closed for the 2026-2027 cohort. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Step Up (Foundations level)
org: City of Minneapolis, Community Planning and Economic Development
pay_detail: Paid by the City of Minneapolis (Foundations level); hourly rate and weekly hours not stated on the page. Teens not matched can do a 5-week online Career Exploration Program and earn up to $599 plus elective credit.
duration: About 2 months (June 22 to August 21 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 window was Jan 5 to Mar 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted; the city says applications open each January and offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.
who_can_apply: Minneapolis residents ages 14 to 21 who are not enrolled in college. The Foundations level is for ages 14 to 21; the Pro level is for ages 16 to 21 with previous work or volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the January window. Accepted students (notified by about Mar 10) complete a required in-person orientation in March and April, then are matched with an internship.
notes: Step Up Director phone 612-673-5041; program phone 612-673-5118. The page does not mention work permits. Not every applicant is matched with a paid internship.

name: Minnesota 4-H
org: University of Minnesota Extension, Minnesota 4-H Youth Development
grades: Kindergarten through one year past high school (grade 13)
pay_detail: Minnesota 4-H does not charge a state membership fee. Some local clubs or programs charge dues, and help may be available.
duration: One 4-H year runs Oct. 1 through Sept. 30. You re-enroll each year.
deadline_text: No fixed deadline on the Join page. Membership lasts Oct. 1 to Sept. 30 and you re-enroll each year.
who_can_apply: Anyone from kindergarten through one year past high school. Independent membership means you are not in a club. It needs 6th grade or older and at least two years of 4-H club experience. It also needs an adult 4-H volunteer as your mentor.
how_to_apply: Get in touch with local 4-H staff near you, or fill out the interest form. Then complete your enrollment online or with a paper form.
notes: Clubs and costs can differ by county, so contact your county 4-H staff first. This is a youth club and learning program, not a paid job.

name: Minnesota American Legion Boys State
pay_detail: Fees are paid by the sponsoring American Legion Post or other community group. No dollar amount is listed. Spending money for the camp store is optional.
duration: One week. 2027 session: check in Sunday June 13, check out Saturday June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted. Each sponsor sets its own. Ask your school counselor or a local American Legion Post.
who_can_apply: Young men who have just finished their junior year of high school. The Legion says picks are based on merit and ability. A sponsor, usually a local American Legion Post, chooses from students your school recommends.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Post. Forms and delegate information are on mnboysstate.org. For questions, call 651-291-1800 or email jkelley@mnlegion.org.
notes: Boys State is for boys. The 2026 session was June 14 to 20 at Saint John's University. Girls State is a separate program run by the American Legion Auxiliary. The Boys State pages give no age number, only the junior-year rule.

name: Minnesota DECA (high school)
org: Minnesota DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
pay_detail: Student dues are $13 total: $5 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapters may add costs.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership deadlines are set by the state advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 28 to Mar 2, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency Minneapolis.
who_can_apply: Students at a Minnesota high school with a DECA chapter. Chapters must have business and marketing courses and an advisor employed by the school. The official pages list no grade or age rule, so ask your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, usually a business or marketing teacher. The advisor registers members online. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Jacklyn (Jackie) Schiller.
notes: DECA's page lists 86 chapters in Minnesota (high school and college counts are not split). The state site mndeca.org lists phone 218-847-5355 and posts role play and judging information. It does not explain joining, so start with your advisor.

name: Minnesota FFA
pay_detail: National FFA dues are $7 a year. Minnesota State FFA dues are $11 starting in 2026. That is $18 for both. Local chapters and regions may charge more.
duration: School year, tied to your ag class
deadline_text: No application deadline. You join through your school's agriculture program.
who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in an agriculture, food and natural resources (AFNR) course at a school with an agricultural education program. The page lists no age or grade rule. If your school has no program, the site links to how to start one.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher and sign up for an agriculture course. Joining FFA goes through that class.
notes: The home page reports 218 agricultural education programs in Minnesota. Ask your counselor whether your school has one.

name: Minnesota House High School Page Program
org: Minnesota House of Representatives, Sergeant at Arms Office
pay_detail: Small meal stipend. The program pays for the hotel. You pay your other personal costs.
duration: One week (Monday to Friday) in Saint Paul. 2027 weeks run from Jan 25 to May 14, 2027.
deadline_text: Complete applications are due by end of business on Nov 10, 2026 for the 2027 session. Selected students are told by email by mid-December.
who_can_apply: Any Minnesota high school junior. Public, private and homeschooled students can apply. Each fall the program picks students from the applications. You send a 500 word essay and one letter from a teacher, counselor or advisor.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 Page Application PDF from the House Sergeant at Arms site. Email it to EducationalPrograms@house.mn.gov. You also need a 500-word essay. You need one letter of recommendation. It can come from a teacher, counselor or academic advisor.
notes: Participants stay together as a group each evening at the program-designated hotel. Questions: Sergeant at Arms office, 651-296-4860.

name: Minnesota State Fair Employment
pay_detail: State Fair department jobs start at $11.50 per hour; vendors set their own pay
duration: 12 fair days (2027 fair: Aug 26 to Sept 6)
deadline_text: The Employment Center runs June to August for fair applicants. The page says to check back in June 2027 for registration updates.
who_can_apply: The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Sign up online or at the Employment Center (1640 Como Ave, St. Paul). Then confirm your sign-up in person. You do a 5 minute screening. Then you may be sent to interviews. Email employment@mnstatefair.org or call 651-288-4475.
notes: The FAQ dates and the page header disagree on the year, so confirm the dates. Jobs are not guaranteed. The pages do not mention work permits, so check Minnesota rules for under 18.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Minnesota Wing
city: Statewide, MN (squadrons in Duluth, St. Paul, Alexandria and more)
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Ideally a 2 hour squadron meeting each week, one Saturday event a month, and one week-long encampment in summer. School-based squadrons may differ.
deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron meeting first.
who_can_apply: At least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first. Cadets can stay until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the Civil Air Patrol unit locator or the Minnesota Wing Locations page. Visit a meeting with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. Ask whether you can apply online.
notes: Example squadrons: Duluth (MN-016), St. Paul (MN-042), Alexandria (MN-135). Wing office: 6275 Crossman Lane, Inver Grove Heights, MN 55076. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

name: Minnesota Youth Council
pay_detail: The Council pages do not mention pay or a stipend.
duration: Two-year term. You travel to the Twin Cities area at least five times a year for retreats, Youth Day at the Capitol and hearings.
deadline_text: The 2026 round (for the 2026 to 2028 term) took applications from January to March 2026: Feb 28 for priority consideration, Mar 31 for all applications. No 2027 dates are posted. Seats also open when members graduate or step down.
who_can_apply: Minnesota residents ages 13 to 19 who attend a middle or high school in Minnesota. Four representatives come from each of the eight congressional districts, plus at-large seats. Applicants should be active in their community and know the three branches of Minnesota government.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview in spring. Selected applicants meet the Council director with a trusted adult in May and are sworn in. You may get a follow-up call or text.
notes: The apply page has a caption with an older appointment date from the last round, so trust the Feb 28 and Mar 31 dates above. Full Council meetings are usually one Sunday afternoon a month. Check the apply page again in January 2027.

name: Minnesota Youth Institute (MNYI)
org: University of Minnesota College of Food, Agricultural and Natural Resource Sciences
pay_detail: Free. Participants are eligible for a $1,000 CFANS scholarship.
duration: Paper due early April; event on one day in May
deadline_text: 2026: register by March 27, paper due April 3, event May 14, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 who live in Minnesota.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the online form. Pick a topic and write the paper. Send it in with the permission form.
notes: Participants get Borlaug Scholar recognition.

name: ZooTeen volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
deadline_text: Applications for the Summer 2026 ZooTeen camp season are closed. The page says to check the website in 2027 for next summer.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.

name: Mission College High School Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines listed on the page. Follow the term dates.
who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.

name: Mission Hospital High School Auxiliary (Providence)
city: Mission Viejo and Laguna Beach, CA
pay_detail: Unpaid. You pay a one-time $125 membership fee for an ID badge, polo shirt and jacket. You also buy black khakis and shoes.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, year round, until you graduate
deadline_text: Applications open September 1 and close the 3rd Monday of October each year. The window for the 2027 group ended October 19, 2026. The next window is September 1 to October 18, 2027.
who_can_apply: You must attend a local high school. You must be a freshman, sophomore or junior when you apply. You must turn 15 by February 1 of the following year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form for the 2027 group. The link is on the program page. Add two recommendation letters: one from a teacher and one from a coach, mentor or supervisor. Add a resume with no photo. Add a personal statement of at least 300 words. Answer the short essay questions. Some students then get an interview.
notes: Chosen students need a TB test and proof of vaccines. They also go to registration, orientation, training and shadowing shifts. The earliest start is usually March. Shifts are Monday to Friday 4 to 8 p.m., or on weekends. There are no summer-only spots. Email MHAuxiliary@providence.org or call 949-364-1400 ext. 7944.

name: Teen Art Project (TAP)
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the program pages.
duration: Summer program. Fall 2026 project: 8 weeks, Thursdays 2:30 to 5 PM, Oct 1 to Nov 19, 2026
deadline_text: The page says applications for Summer TAP 2027 will open in spring 2027. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled high school students (per the summer program page). The Fall 2026 event page does not list ages.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to the museum newsletter to hear when enrollment opens. For the Fall 2026 project use the Register button on its event page. Museum phone: 406-728-0447.
notes: It is not clear if the Fall 2026 project is part of the same program as Summer TAP. Ask the museum.

name: Volunteer with the Montana Natural History Center
pay_detail: Volunteer roles. No pay is mentioned.
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page.

how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application form on the volunteer page, or stop by the center. Call 406-327-0405 to ask about age rules.
notes: Call to confirm the minimum age for the role you want. The page does not state one.

name: Lifeguard and Summer Jobs at Splash Montana and Currents

pay_detail: The city reimburses the Red Cross training course if you accept a lifeguard or Water Safety Instructor job. Hourly pay is not stated on the program page.

deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page says summer jobs will be posted soon on the City of Missoula jobs portal.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 and up to lifeguard. Ages 16 and up to be a Water Safety Instructor. You need average swimming ability. Other pool jobs have no lifeguard rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply for a posted job on the City of Missoula jobs portal. Questions: 406-552-6000 (TTY 406-552-6131).
notes: The page said summer jobs were "posted soon", so check the portal for current openings.

name: Teen Library Community (TLC)
