duration: Meets Thursdays, 3:30 to 5:30 PM, in the Art Box on level two
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email children@missoulapubliclibrary.org. Ask for more info. Ask to join the email list. Main library phone: 406-721-2665.
notes: Snacks are free at every meeting. The page does not say how many volunteer hours you can earn.

name: Summer History Institute for High School Students
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: One week, 9 AM to 4 PM (2025: July 21-25)
deadline_text: Not offered in 2026. The page says it returns in summer 2027 with details expected in January 2027. In 2025, applications were due June 6.
who_can_apply: Any Montana high school student in any grade who likes history, law and government. Students from outside Missoula can apply. They must plan their own travel and place to stay.
how_to_apply: Not offered in 2026. Fill out the interest form on the program page to get news. Contacts: Professor Claire Arcenas or Professor Jody Pavilack. They work at the University of Montana.
notes: Based on the 2025 page. The topic may change in 2027.

name: TRIO Upward Bound Summer Academy
pay_detail: Free. No stipend is mentioned on the program page.
duration: Six weeks
deadline_text: The page says students must be accepted by May 21, 2027 for the 2027 Academy. The page title still says Summer Academy 2026.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 19 who go to Big Sky, Browning, Heart Butte, Hellgate or Sentinel High School. You must be a likely first-generation college student or from a family that meets the income rules. The page describes the program for college-bound students with a GPA of at least 2.5. You must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page for the program on the University of Montana site. Call the TRIO Upward Bound office at 406-243-2219. Or use the email on the page: jonathan.carter@umontana.edu.
notes: Check the dates with the office. Page dates and title do not match.

name: Missouri 4-H Civic Engagement Ambassadors
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: One calendar year starting at State Congress
deadline_text: The 2026 window was Feb 15 to 5:00 PM on Apr 1, 2026. The page does not say when the next window opens.
who_can_apply: Missouri youth ages 14 to 18 (age range from the Get Involved page; the program page itself does not state age).
how_to_apply: Answer short essay questions. Have two reference forms sent in. One is from 4-H staff or faculty. One is from a teacher, coach, boss or mentor.
notes: Cost is not stated. Contact 4hyouth@missouri.edu or 573-882-9359.

name: Missouri 4-H Legislative Academy
pay_detail: No registration fee. 4-H covers lodging, meals and travel during the event. Families pay to get to the check-in spot.
duration: 3 days (March 4 to 6, 2026)
deadline_text: Offered in even-numbered years. Applications open Sept 15 and close Nov 1 in the fall before the event (the page does not state the year). Zoom interviews are Nov 12 and 13.
who_can_apply: Current Missouri 4-H members in grades 9 to 12. You need a recommendation from 4-H staff. Time on State Council or a national trip is a plus, not a must.
how_to_apply: Online application with three 250 to 300 word essays and one reference form from 4-H staff (not a family member). Finalists do a Zoom interview.
notes: No registration fee. 4-H covers lodging, meals and travel during the event. Families pay to get to the check-in spot. The page says it is held in even-numbered years, so the next one would be March 2028.

name: Missouri 4-H
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Missouri youth, per the 4-H program page. SPIN clubs take ages 5 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use Join 4-H and Enroll now on the program page, or contact your county 4-H office. Statewide questions: 4hyouth@missouri.edu, 573-882-9359.
notes: Costs are not listed on the page.

name: Jobs League Program

how_to_apply: Call and ask for a Youth Specialist at your regional workforce board. Examples listed: Full Employment Council in Kansas City 816-471-2330 ext. 1256, St. Louis City 314-657-3557, Workforce Development Board of St. Louis County 314-615-6010.
notes: Income limits come from the page and may change. The page lists regional boards across the state for other areas.

name: Missouri FFA
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The page does not say who can join or state grades or ages.

notes: 26,830 members (per the page). Camp page says Missouri FFA hires college-age students for camp staff, so that job is not for most teens. Dues are not stated.

name: MOCA Teen Program (paid)

pay_detail: Teens are paid. The page does not give an amount.

how_to_apply: Not open now. See mocateens.org and the MOCA Teens page for the next call.
notes: Competitive. Check the page in summer for the next cycle.

name: Montana 4-H Congress
pay_detail: $285. It covers lodging for 3 nights, 7 meals, program costs and a t-shirt. Campus parking costs extra.
duration: 4 days (July 14 to 17, 2027)
deadline_text: The next Congress is July 14 to 17, 2027. Registration opens May 1. The state registration deadline is June 15. Ambassador officer applications are also due June 15.
who_can_apply: Montana 4-H youth who are at least 13 years old as of October 1 of the 4-H year. Chaperones must be certified 4-H volunteers or MSU Extension staff, age 21 or older.
how_to_apply: Register online in the 4-H Zsuite system. Each county has its own deadlines and steps, so call your county Extension office early.
notes: You do not have to enter a contest. Youth State Awards are due May 1.

name: Montana 4-H County Ambassador and State Ambassador Officer
city: Statewide, Montana (county offices; state team based in Bozeman)
pay_detail: Unpaid leadership role. Cost not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: County ambassador: apply through your county 4-H (dates set by each county). State officer applications are due, postmarked, by June 15.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 by October 1 of the current year, enrolled in 4-H for at least 2 years and this year, and be or have been a Junior Leader or club officer. A maximum age is not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: County level: fill out an application. Then interview with the County Council. State officer: send the application to the Montana 4-H Center. It must be postmarked by June 15.
notes: You must already be in 4-H. The state team page lists five state officer jobs (for example President and Publicity Chair). Contact your county extension office. The state officer page does not state the term length for officers.

name: Montana 4-H Fall Leadership Training
pay_detail: $195. It covers lodging (2 to 4 people per room), Saturday and Sunday meals and program costs. Friday dinner is on your own.
duration: Weekend (November 6 to 8, 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 training is November 6 to 8 in Butte. State registration closed October 19, 2026. It is held every fall.
who_can_apply: Montana 4-H youth who are at least 14 years old as of October 1 of the 4-H year. Counties send ambassadors and teen leaders. Chaperones must be certified 4-H volunteers or MSU Extension staff, age 21 or older.
how_to_apply: Register online in the 4-H Zsuite system. Call your county MSU Extension office for county rules. Fill in your info and waivers before the event.
notes: Cancel before sign-up closes for a full refund. Dress is business casual on Saturday. Dress for the banquet is business professional to semi-formal.

name: Montana 4-H Foundation Youth Representative
pay_detail: Unpaid board seat. Cost not stated on the program page.
duration: Two-year term (the page says it will change to one year)
deadline_text: Send the application before November 1. The page does not name the year, so check the date with the 4-H Foundation.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You must be a 4-H member in your home county for at least three consecutive years. You need your county agent's approval.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and send it. Email is preferred. You can also text 406-624-9835, fax 406-994-5417 or mail it to Montana 4-H Foundation, Inc., PO Box 173580, Bozeman.
notes: The page lists two at-large youth seats. Ask your county agent early because their approval is required.

name: National Park Service Expeditions (Youth Program)
city: Bozeman and Kalispell, MT (Yellowstone and Glacier)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer crew. $100 service award and up to 64 service hours on successful completion. The program is free to join.
duration: 9-day sessions
deadline_text: Applications are closed for 2026. 2027 youth program applications typically open in February. The page does not state a 2027 deadline.
who_can_apply: Montana teens ages 14 to 18. You must live in Montana. Teens from other states will not be considered.
how_to_apply: Online application filled out by the teen and a parent or guardian. The parent or guardian must sign a Youth Program Release form that is emailed after you submit. Email youthprograms@mtcorps.org with questions.
notes: Yellowstone sessions leave from Bozeman and Glacier sessions leave from Kalispell. Next dates not posted yet.

name: Youth Corps (Helena, Missoula, Flathead)
pay_detail: Living allowance of $1,200 every two weeks before taxes, plus an AmeriCorps education award ($1,565.08 for the 2026 crews).
duration: About 8 weeks (2026 crews: mid June to early August)
deadline_text: Applications are closed for 2026. 2027 youth program applications typically open in February. The page says 2026 interviews began early April.
who_can_apply: Montana teens ages 17 to 18. Montana residency is required. You must commit to the full summer.
how_to_apply: Online application. A parent or guardian must sign the Youth Program Release that is emailed after you submit. Interview, then a decision within 2 weeks. Email youthprograms@mtcorps.org with questions.
notes: 2026 crews were in Helena, Kalispell (Flathead Youth Corps) and Missoula. Participants must commit to the full summer. Next dates not posted yet.

name: Montana Tech Materials Science and Engineering Summer Program
grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: Free. Lodging, meals and course materials are provided. You must arrange your own ride to campus.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 26 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 program ran June 21 to 26, 2026. The application closed March 31, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Montana high school students who are rising juniors or seniors and want a career in science or engineering. No GPA or age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. Questions: metcamp@mtech.edu.
notes: The dates and deadline come from the 2026 news release on the Montana Tech site. The program page says Montana high school students are invited to apply. Watch for a new release around February 2027.

name: Montgomery County Recreation seasonal part-time jobs
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page says only 'We're currently hiring for' and lists positions.
who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. The page checked for this card does not state a minimum age for these jobs. It lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the 'apply here' link on the Recreation employment page to see the seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Summer RISE
org: Montgomery County Public Schools, Department of Partnerships
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
deadline_text: Student registration opens in January and runs January to February. No year is given; the program runs June 21 to July 23, 2027. Placements are announced in April or May.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

name: TeenWorks Employment Program
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
deadline_text: Application windows on the page: Jan 2 to Mar 30 (spring/summer) and Aug 1 to Nov 30 (fall/winter). The page prints no year and says to apply when the posting is available, so we cannot confirm the fall/winter window is open. Call 240-777-8080 to ask.
who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Montgomery Parks volunteering and Student Service Learning hours
city: Montgomery County, MD (park sites countywide; office in Wheaton)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Only opportunities approved by MCPS and the Montgomery County Volunteer Center give SSL hours.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Browse the opportunities list and sign up for events.
who_can_apply: Volunteers without a parent or guardian must be 14 years old. Some jobs have higher age limits. Younger children can volunteer with a parent. This is the Family Volunteer program. The adult must register separately.
how_to_apply: Open the SSL Opportunities list on the Montgomery Parks site. Pick an event approved for SSL hours. Then register. You log in or create a volunteer account. Email parksvolunteers@montgomeryparks.org with questions.
notes: If you need many SSL hours in a short time, the page says that is only sometimes possible. Contacts on the page: Montgomery Parks Customer Service (301) 495-2595, and Volunteer Services 301-495-2504 on the main volunteer page. Office: 2425 Reedie Drive, 12th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902.

name: Monument Health VolunTEEN Program
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: One 2 to 4 hour shift a week, same day and time, for 10 to 12 weeks (at least 30 hours).
deadline_text: Sessions start in October, February and June. Applications are due by the last business day of the month before a session starts, so the February 2027 session needs an application by the end of January 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens must be 16 to 18 years of age before graduating high school. A parent must sign a consent form.
how_to_apply: Submit the online VolunTEEN application. Also send in the VolunTEEN Program Guidelines and the Parental Consent Form. Then you do a job shadow. After that, you go to an orientation and an interview. You also do onboarding and health steps.
notes: Adults 18 and older use a different program with 30 hours in three months. The page says the wait from application to first shift is about six weeks for adults. Sturgis, Custer, Lead-Deadwood and Spearfish hospitals have their own volunteer contacts; the page does not say they take teens.

name: Counselor in Training (CIT) and Future Leaders Programs, Moraga Day Camp
org: Town of Moraga Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: $250 per session for Moraga residents. $270 per session for non-residents.
duration: 4-week blocks with weekly AM or PM shifts; most weeks have one full day, 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM
deadline_text: The 2026 interviews were April 13 to 17, 2026. The page lists the sessions as June 15 to July 11 and July 14 to August 8, with no year. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: In 2026, Future Leaders was for age 12 or 13. Counselors in Training was for age 14. Ages were counted on June 8, 2026. You must go to a required orientation and a week of training. You must also interview, and an interview does not promise a spot.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an interview time in the Moraga Parks and Recreation online catalog. The link is on the program page. An interview does not promise you a spot. If chosen, you pick the weeks you can come.
notes: In 2026 the orientation was May 7 and training was June 8 to 12. The page says CITs gain hands-on experience that prepares them for possible future jobs with Moraga Parks and Recreation. The town website also has a Summer Jobs page.

name: Moraga Police Cadets
pay_detail: Community service role. You volunteer at least 4 hours a week.
duration: At least 4 hours per week
deadline_text: No application dates are stated on the employment page.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens ages 16 to 22 who are in high school or college with a 2.5 GPA or better. You need a valid California driver license and a good driving record. You must pass an oral board and a background check. You must volunteer at least 4 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Contact Lt. Steve Borbely at 925-888-7052 to ask about the Police Cadet Program and how to apply.
notes: The cadet program is on the town employment page, below the police officer and reserve officer jobs. Good character and good health are also on the list. Ask the department if it is taking cadets now.

name: Moraga Youth Involvement Committee (MYIC)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The 2026-2027 application period is closed. The page says applications for the 2027-2028 term will be available in July 2027.
who_can_apply: The page does not list ages, grades or a residency rule. Ask the Parks and Recreation office before you apply.
how_to_apply: Applications for the 2027-2028 term will be available in July 2027. Contact Jasmine Bateson at the email link on the program page to ask how to apply.
notes: The committee meets at 7 PM on the 2nd Thursday of every month at the Hacienda de las Flores, 2100 Donald Drive, Moraga. Its service projects change each year.

name: MSM S.T.E.A.M. Academy (Grades 9 to 12)
grades: Rising 9th to 12th (3-week option). Rising 10th to 12th (6-week research option)
pay_detail: 3-week option $1,000. 6-week research option $1,500. No stipend listed.
duration: 3 weeks (June 1 to 19, 2026) or 6 weeks (June 2 to July 10, 2026), 9 am to 3 pm
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 26 and closed Mar 25, 2026 (reviewed on a rolling basis). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school students with interest in STEAM, health or biomedical research and a 3.0 GPA or higher. The research option also needs your latest report card.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. For the research option, also send your report card, an essay about lab research and two recommendation forms. One must be from a science teacher. Some applicants are interviewed.
notes: Costs money. A session can be cancelled if too few students sign up. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. Ryan Clark, 404-752-1843. Dates shown are from summer 2026.

name: Summer Pre-College Program
pay_detail: $3,500 flat fee for up to three courses, plus up to $100 per course for books and a $30 non-refundable application fee
duration: About 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026, finals July 6 to 10)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Jan 5 to Mar 15, 2026, decisions Apr 5, payment due May 1. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or older when they apply, in 10th to 12th grade, with at least a 3.2 GPA.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. Add your official high school transcript and one recommendation from a teacher or counselor. List your top three course choices. Test scores are optional.
notes: Costs money. The page also calls the group rising juniors and seniors in places. Confirm your grade with the Summer Academy (academicsuccess@morehouse.edu). Dates shown are from the 2026 summer. The page says the program serves students from across the metro Atlanta area and beyond, and that courses are offered online.

name: Summer Junior Volunteer Program
org: Atlantic Health System, Morristown Medical Center
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: June 25 to August 13, 2027. Two 4-hour shifts a week, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 1 pm or 1 pm to 5 pm.
deadline_text: 2027 application window: opens March 1, 2027 and closes March 7, 2027. Selection is by lottery.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. Needs two letters of reference and proof of vaccines (MMR, Tdap, TB, flu). Do not apply if you expect three or more absences in the eight weeks.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the Volunteer Services page. The page says it leads to the adult volunteer application. Call Volunteer Services at 973-971-5475 if you are not sure.
notes: Applications are selected by lottery. Check the exact open and close times on the page.

name: Youth Volunteer Program
grades: New applicants enter 7th, 8th or 9th grade this fall (Tree Monitor spots for new people are for high school age)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: June through August, with some optional fall weekends
deadline_text: The page says applications are reviewed in April each year. An exact deadline is not posted. Email youthvolunteers@mortonarb.org to get deadline notices.
who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th, 8th or 9th grade in the fall. Volunteers can return each summer through high school. After one year, you can move to Science Camp or Tree Monitor.
how_to_apply: Write to youthvolunteers@mortonarb.org and ask about the application. Ask about the deadline too.
notes: Weekday daytime shifts at most branches. Shift hours, fees and training are not listed on the page. The Arboretum's paid science fellowships are for college students, so they are not in the guide. Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects are taken by emailing volunteer@mortonarb.org.

name: City of Mountain View Teen Volunteer Summer Program
org: City of Mountain View, The View Teen Center
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid
duration: 1 to 3 weeks minimum, depending on role
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 Teen Summer Volunteer Program open in late winter or early spring 2027. No closing date posted yet.
who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.
how_to_apply: Follow the application steps on the city page (online account, email, or mail/drop-off at Mountain View Community Center, 201 S. Rengstorff Ave). Questions: TheViewTeenCenter@mountainview.gov.
notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.

name: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated

name: GROW CELLS Cancer Research Summer Program

deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application deadline May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

notes: Costs money. The same page lists a separate college track, which is not for high schoolers. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. J. Wesley Lockhart, 404-752-1197.

name: Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy (MTC)

notes: Adult volunteers must be 18 or older, but this junior program is for ages 15 to 18. Applications open January 1 and close when the program is full.

name: Teen Volunteers (Rutherford County Library System)

pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

name: Murrieta Youth Advisory Committee
org: City of Murrieta Community Services Department

who_can_apply: Teens who live in the City of Murrieta and are in 9th to 12th grade at a Murrieta Valley Unified School District school. You need two references.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application with five short answers and two references. Turn it in at the Murrieta Youth Center (40644 California Oaks Rd) or email it to the city contact on the sheet. Questions: Community Services at (951) 304-PARK, ext. 6117.
notes: Confirm first: the only sheet found is for the 2024-25 term. Members must go to all mandatory city events. Meetings were on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday evenings.

name: Summer Camp Youth Volunteer

notes: The camp-specific application page returned an error, so the camp schedule, requirements and deadline were not confirmed. The general volunteer perk is a free membership after 100 hours in a year (not confirmed for youth).

name: NAACP/JMRL Paid Library Internship and Scholarship
org: Jefferson-Madison Regional Library and Albemarle-Charlottesville NAACP

pay_detail: $3,000 stipend for 200 hours, plus eligibility for a $2,000 yearly scholarship toward an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree (up to $5,000 a year total)
duration: 200 hours of library work

Whether a Virginia Employment Certificate is needed for 14 and 15 year olds was not stated (applicants are 17 or entering 12th grade).

name: Library Volunteers, ages 13 and up (Nampa Public Library)

name: Naperville Community Job Fair

name: Teen Pitch Program

name: Mayor's Chief of Staff Internship (KidsMatter)
pay_detail: Not stated. The city news post and the boards page were checked on 2026-10-10. Neither says anything about pay. Ask the city.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. Selected students start at the KidsMatter Leadership Academy on Saturday, Nov. 7 (this fall). The city post is dated August 10, 2026. Next year's call is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Up to 8 sophomores and juniors who live in Naperville. You must live inside the city limits. Freshmen and seniors cannot apply. Students who served on a board or commission cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button on any board or commission page of the city site. Answer yes to the Mayor's Chief of Staff question. Upload a resume or a note about your interest. Say that you are free all year.
notes: The news post does not say whether it is paid. Ask Rachel Pruneda (prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018). A full job description is on the city boards page.

name: Seasonal and Part-Time Jobs (Centennial Beach, camps, parks)
pay_detail: Pay is listed on each job posting, not on the main employment page.
duration: Seasonal. Summer jobs include Centennial Beach and the Paddleboat Quarry.
deadline_text: The page's table says Centennial Beach jobs (lifeguard, concession, swim instructor), paddleboat jobs, camp counselors and Knoch Knolls nature camp jobs are usually posted in mid December. Other jobs post in May, June or August. The Community Job Fair is held the first Saturday in January.
who_can_apply: Minimum age differs for each job. Check the age listed on the posting.
how_to_apply: Find a posting on the district job board and fill out the online application for that job. Mail, email or fax is not accepted. Apply for each job separately.
notes: Only applicants chosen for an interview are contacted. The page has a table of when each job is usually posted. Ages and pay are on each posting, so check them before you apply. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.

name: Volunteer Programs and Events (ages 14 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The district can sign off on volunteer hours for school.
duration: Dates listed this fall (no year printed; the weekdays match 2026): Kids' Night Out on Fridays, Nov 20 to Dec 18, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m. Santa's Workshop on Dec 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17 and 20.
deadline_text: Apply at least two weeks before the date you want to volunteer. Santa's Workshop runs December 1 to 20, 2026 and Kids' Night Out runs Fridays, November 20 to December 18, 2026. The weekdays on the page match 2026.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Volunteers 13 and under may volunteer alongside a parent or guardian. BINGO volunteers must be at least 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Application (17 and under) and approve a DCFS background check, at least two weeks ahead. Then email Becca (address on the Programs volunteer page) to sign up for a program. You cannot just show up, except at Nature Champion days.
notes: Volunteer hours can be confirmed by email, a signed letter or a school form.

name: Police Cadet Program
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Cadets help with security and traffic control at events.
duration: Ongoing, two meetings a month
deadline_text: No deadline is stated on the page.
who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, finished 8th grade, and not older than 21. Needs a C average or better, and no serious arrests or convictions.
how_to_apply: Download the cadet application and turn it in at the front desk, 1350 Aurora Ave. A committee checks references and does a background check and an interview. Questions: NPDCadets@naperville.il.us.
notes: The police internship on the same site is for college students, so it is not listed. The department points younger people to the cadet program.

name: Youth Academy
grades: In high school or entering high school
pay_detail: Free
duration: 6 weeks, Thursday nights 6 to 8 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 class: June 11 to July 23, 2026, applications due June 4, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students in high school or going into high school in fall 2026. You live in Naperville or go to high school there. You need parent permission and your own ride. You need good standing at school and no criminal contacts.
how_to_apply: Print and fill out the application and waiver at naperville.il.us/youthacademy. Send the signed forms to Sergeant Greg Rink at rinkg@naperville.il.us. Or drop them off at 1350 Aurora Ave.
notes: First come, first served and space is limited.

name: Student Representatives on City Boards and Commissions
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer role.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term; most boards meet in the evening
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. Selected students start at the KidsMatter Leadership Academy on Saturday, Nov. 7 (this fall). The city post is dated August 10, 2026. Next year's call is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students who live inside Naperville city limits. You are a sophomore, junior or senior. Freshmen cannot apply. If you already served on a board or commission, you cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Click Apply on any board's page on the city Boards and Commissions site. Fill in the profile and the student rep questions. Upload a resume or a short statement. You can apply to up to three boards.
notes: 24 positions, two per board. Contact: Rachel Pruneda, prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018. The dates come from an August 2026 city news post.

name: NASA Citizen Science Projects
pay_detail: Free
duration: Whenever you want
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.

name: NASA GeneLab for High Schools (GL4HS)
city: Virtual (hosted by NASA Ames, Mountain View, CA)
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (and college freshmen)
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.
duration: 12 weeks, June 1 to Aug 28 in 2026
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026, or until 1,000 applicants. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.

name: Nasher Teen Council
org: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University
pay_detail: Free. Snacks, dinner and parking are provided at every meeting.
duration: Thursdays 5:30 to 7:30 PM, October to April
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed. The page does not say when the next group is recruited.
who_can_apply: Any high school student in Durham County in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Watch the Nasher Teen Council page for the next application. The page does not say when it opens. Meetings are every Thursday evening during the school year.
notes: Durham County students only. Watch the page for the next application.

name: Volunteer at Adventure Science Center
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free membership after 100 hours.
duration: No minimum hours stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Sign up any time on the volunteer portal.
who_can_apply: People over age 14 can take the Open Opportunities shifts. The 21+ events are not open to teens.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the museum's volunteer portal. Then sign up for a volunteer orientation. If you have questions, send an email to volunteer@adventuresci.org.
notes: The museum also runs Youth CR3W, a youth program with its own form. The CR3W page does not state ages, pay or schedule. Ask volunteer@adventuresci.org before you assume it fits you.

name: Junior Volunteer Summer Program (Hospital West)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: 6 weeks. The program begins in June.
deadline_text: The window listed on the page is January to March. Applications close March 28 or when the program is full. The year is not shown.
who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who are still in high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the West junior volunteer application between January and March. The hospital also asks for an interview. You must wear a uniform.
notes: Call 615-222-2127 for Midtown and West. Ascension Saint Thomas Rutherford has its own junior program. That program runs three weeks in July.

name: Belmont Science and Mathematics Summer Camps
org: Belmont University College of Sciences and Mathematics
pay_detail: Most 2026 camps cost $425. The RISE research camps cost $1,700. One camp, VISIBL, was $0 for Metro Nashville students nominated by a science teacher. Email Beth Bowman if cost is a problem.
duration: One-week camps. RISE ran about four weeks.
deadline_text: Registration for 2027 opens in December 2026. The 2026 camps ran June 8 to July 17.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 and older for the 2026 camps. The RISE research camps also need a 3.0 overall GPA and a 3.0 math and science GPA.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the newsletter on the camp page to hear when registration opens. Then register for the camp you want.
notes: Camps for 2027 may differ from the 2026 list. The page asks you to email Beth Bowman at beth.bowman@belmont.edu with questions.

name: Cheekwood Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines are posted.
who_can_apply: Teens age 16 or older. Younger teens (10 to 17) can volunteer through the Family Team program with a parent or other adult family member.
how_to_apply: Download and fill out the Teen Volunteer Application. Then do the orientation training you must take. Call the Volunteer Manager at 615-353-6966 with questions.
notes: The page says the teen program is for age 16 or older and does not give an upper age. The application PDF on the page is dated June 2025, so ask the Volunteer Manager if it is the current form.

name: Songwriting Camp (2027)
org: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
pay_detail: 2026 fees on the page: $505 for museum members and $595 for non-members. 2027 fees are not posted. Need-based aid can lower the fee to $297 or $30.
duration: 1 week: June 14 to 19, 2027 (beginner to intermediate) or July 12 to 17, 2027 (intermediate to advanced)
deadline_text: Camp dates are June 14 to 19 and July 12 to 17, 2027. The page says the application period opens Jan 5, 2027 (needs-based aid applications are due Mar 31 for June camp and May 5 for July camp). Whether registration itself opens the same day is not stated.
who_can_apply: Songwriters ages 12 to 18. July applicants also send a recording of 1 original song. People who have never come before get first pick.
how_to_apply: Email camp@countrymusichalloffame.org for 2027 sign up info. If you want aid, apply for it before you sign up. For the July camp, send up to 5 minutes of audio or video of 1 original song with lyrics.
notes: Costs real money. Campers who have been to two or more camps may be waitlisted.

name: Teen Team Volunteers
org: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: About one assignment per month
deadline_text: No application deadline or session dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 or high school freshmen to seniors. You must pass a background check, which the museum pays for. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Today on the Teen Team page. Or sign up for an info session. Email volunteer@countrymusichalloffame.org with questions.
notes: The museum also runs a Songwriting Camp for ages 12 to 18 (June 14 to 19 and July 12 to 17, 2027). In 2026 fees were $505 for members and $595 for non-members, with need based aid.

name: Friends of Warner Parks Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: No deadline. Upcoming events are listed on the page. Examples are Oct 17, 2026 and Nov 7, 2026.
who_can_apply: Litter pick-up is open to all ages. Trail work, invasive plant removal and stream clean-up are for ages 18 and up, or ages 13 and up with an adult. School groups in grades K to 12 can volunteer with two or more chaperones.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile in the Friends of Warner Parks volunteer database. Fill out the information form and sign the waiver.
notes: Under 18 means you need an adult for most work. The Ambassador program is 18 and up. The page does not give an age rule for the seasonal SWEAT trail crew. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the page.

name: Teen Arts Action Group (TAAG)
pay_detail: Not stated. The museum says TAAG time may count toward required service hours.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the TAAG or Teens pages. Email the museum to ask when the next group applies.
who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 18 who want to work with peers and professional artists.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe the application. Email teens@fristartmuseum.org with questions.
notes: The Frist also runs free Teen ARTlabs (art sessions with professional artists). Ages and dates for those are not listed on the Teens page; see the museum's teen events calendar.

name: Genesys Works Nashville
pay_detail: Paid internship. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a year-long internship
deadline_text: Application dates are not stated on the program page. The Nashville page says the first class launches in 2026.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors. Genesys Works partners with specific schools. Nashville is working with Metro Nashville Public Schools for its first class.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application, then interview, then confirm you accept. Click Apply Now on the Genesys Works application page and pick the Nashville location. Email nashville@genesysworks.org with questions.
notes: This program is new in Nashville. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The page does not say if a work permit is needed for teens under 18.

name: Hands On Nashville Youth and Teen Volunteering
org: Hands On Nashville (United Way of Greater Nashville)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick projects as they are posted.
who_can_apply: People 13 and older can have a Hands On account. Each project has its own age rule, so check the listing. Kids under 13 volunteer through the family page.
how_to_apply: Make a Hands On account and sign up for a project. A parent or guardian must sign the Hands On waiver. Bring the waiver to the project and check in with the Volunteer Leader.
notes: For school credit, bring your school's form. Ask the volunteer coordinator to check your hours.

name: Future Presidents of America Youth Leadership Camp
pay_detail: $350 per student, or $300 for Hermitage members. Lunch is not included. Limited financial help is offered.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. each day.
deadline_text: The page lists the 2026 camp as June 15 to 19 and says applications opened January 1. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 16.
how_to_apply: Send the finished application to Erin Adams. Staff review the forms. Then they invite students to an interview.
notes: The page still says 2026 applications are open, but that camp has passed. Ask about 2027 through the contact link. The camp is an initiative of the Benjamin Harrison Presidential Site.

name: STriVe Summer Teen Volunteer Program
org: Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: Not taking applications now. The hospital says the next recruitment period will be Spring 2027.
who_can_apply: The program page does not state an age range. Read the STriVe online guide for details.
how_to_apply: Watch the hospital volunteering page for the application in Spring 2027. Read the STriVe online guide first.
notes: Applications may close early if the hospital gets many. The Caring Hands Crew is for anyone 16 and up who wants to help the hospital's mission.

name: POWER Youth Summer Employment (Experience Work and High School Internships)
pay_detail: $12 per hour (Experience Work, ages 14 to 15). $15 per hour (High School Internship).
duration: About 7 weeks (June 1 to July 17 in 2026)
deadline_text: In 2026 the portal was open Feb 9 to Apr 24. Next year's dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Youth who live in Davidson County. Ages 14 to 15 apply for Experience Work. Ages 16 to 18 apply for High School Internships.
how_to_apply: Pick Experience Work or High School Internships on the POWER Youth job portal, search the job list for your age group, apply and check your email for a confirmation. Call 615-862-8860 for help.
notes: The program page says it serves ages 14 to 22 overall and lists High School Internships for ages 16 to 19. The job seekers page says 16 to 18, so this card uses 18. Confirm with Metro Action. This card covers the teen tracks only. Neither page says whether a work permit or ID is needed, so ask Metro Action. Office is at 1281 Murfreesboro Pike, Nashville.

name: Nashville Public Library Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Weekly shifts for at least 6 months or 50 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are handled in the order received.
who_can_apply: Anyone age 13 or older. Volunteers under 18 need permission from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form for 1 person. Then watch your email for next steps.
notes: The library says it does not take every applicant. It places volunteers by what each site needs. It also asks you to keep a set weekly schedule, so check you can. The page says shorter jobs can be found through Hands On Nashville.

name: Youth Volunteering at Second Harvest Food Bank
org: Second Harvest Food Bank of Middle Tennessee
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: Shift length is not stated on the program page. Stay for the full shift.
deadline_text: Book any open shift on the online volunteer calendar.
who_can_apply: Standard food sorting is for ages 12 and older. Cold food sorting is for ages 16 and older at the Martin site. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign a waiver. Volunteers under 16 must come with an adult.
how_to_apply: Book a shift ahead of time on the online volunteer calendar. Bring a signed Youth Volunteer Waiver if you are under 18. Groups of 5 or more need a leader who is 18 or older.
notes: The food bank asks for 1 adult for every 7 volunteers under 18. Walk-ins may not be accepted. The sites named on the page are Martin, Nacarato and Camden, and shift days differ by site.

name: Seasonal Jobs at Nashville Shores
pay_detail: Pay rate not stated on the program page. The page says you get daily pay.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the program page. Season dates and job fair dates are not listed.
who_can_apply: Hiring starts at age 15 for most jobs. Many jobs need you to be 16 or older. Only a limited number of jobs are open to 15-year-olds.
how_to_apply: Use the online careers portal. Send one application only, for the department you want most. A hiring manager will contact you if your application fits, so check your contact info.
notes: Do not apply to more than one department. Do not call to ask about status. The page does not say if a work permit is needed for teens under 18, so ask the employer.

name: Engineering Exploration Camp (EEC)
org: Tennessee State University College of Engineering
pay_detail: $400 per student. It is not refundable. Meals are provided.
duration: Dates are June 7 to July 3, 2026. The length in weeks is not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The page lists the 2026 camp as June 7 to July 3, with rolling admission until full. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Say if you want residential or day. Upload your transcript, test scores if you have them, a one-page essay and one recommendation letter. Incomplete packets are not considered.
notes: Run with Cummins as a partner. Contact Dre Davenport at ddaventp@tnstate.edu or 615-963-5389.

name: National Summer Transportation Institute (NSTI)
org: Tennessee State University College of Engineering, funded by TDOT
pay_detail: Free to students. Pay or a stipend is not stated on the program page.
duration: 4 weeks: 3 weeks on campus, then 1 week online.
deadline_text: The page lists the 2026 program as June 15 to July 10. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload your transcript, test scores if you have them, and a one-page essay. Your teacher or counselor emails one recommendation letter to Professor Kang Du.
notes: The Tennessee Department of Transportation runs and funds this program. Contact Professor Kang Du at kdu@tnstate.edu. Or call the College of Engineering at 615-963-5401.

name: Vanderbilt Summer Academy (VSA)
pay_detail: One-week tuition on the PTY page: $2,150 (grades 7 to 8), $2,850 (grades 9 to 10), $2,950 (grades 11 to 12). Tuition covers course, materials, housing and meals. $50 application fee ($100 international).
duration: One week. The tuition page lists several 2027 session dates in June and July.
deadline_text: The page lists 2027 session dates in June and July, and admission notices in a priority window of Jan 29 to Feb 16 (2026 dates). The application deadline for 2027 is not clearly posted.
who_can_apply: Open to grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $50 fee. If you are placed in a course you pay a 20% deposit one week after the admission notice. Check the box for aid if you want to apply for it.
notes: It costs money. The page offers aid for families with adjusted gross income of $105,000 or less or severe hardship. It offers a payment plan for everyone. The page mixes 2026 deadlines with 2027 session dates. Confirm both with precollege@vanderbilt.edu.

name: Vanderbilt Observational Experience (high school)
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is no application fee.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: Apply at least 30 days before the day you want to observe. Teens ages 16 and 17 must apply at least two weeks before.
who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16. Your school must have an affiliation agreement with VUMC. Homeschool students need an agreement with their homeschool group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application in one sitting. It does not save. Upload your health insurance card, a health form, a safety quiz certificate and signed forms.
notes: Minors cannot observe in some places. These are operating rooms, emergency departments, pediatric intensive care units and the Vanderbilt Psychiatric Hospital. If your school has no agreement with VUMC, you are not eligible. Email VOE@VUMC.org with questions.

name: ZooTeen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo's page mentions a one-time fee that includes a uniform, but no amount is posted.
duration: Summer: one shift a week for at least 7 weeks plus one week of Zoo Camp. School year: at least 4 hours each semester plus one special event.
deadline_text: The last posted cycle opened Feb 1 and closed Mar 20. Dates for next year are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Teens from age 13 to high school seniors.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send 1 recommendation form from someone who is not a relative or family friend. Then go to a 60 minute group interview and all training sessions.
notes: The zoo's page and its info sheet differ on small things (how many recommendations, the fee). Send an email to volunteer@nashvillezoo.org before you apply. The dates on the info sheet are from the last cycle posted. They are interviews Mar 28 and 29 and Apr 11 and 12, and a summer start on May 26.

name: National Economics Challenge
pay_detail: No pay. Cash prizes. Cost to enter is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: 2026-27 registration is not open yet. No dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. David Ricardo is for first-timers with no more than one economics course. Team size and school rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form on the challenge page (choose Teacher, Parent, Student or Friend) to get a message when registration opens. Phone: 212-827-3600.
notes: Few details are posted yet. Ask an economics teacher to be your team contact. Confirm first.

name: Job Corps (free career training for ages 16 to 24)
org: U.S. Department of Labor, Job Corps
pay_detail: Free for students. A living allowance is paid every two weeks and goes up as training moves along. Amount not stated.
duration: Between 8 months and 3 years, depending on the training
deadline_text: Apply any time. The site says the decision usually takes about two months.
who_can_apply: Mostly low-income 16 to 24 year olds. You must be a U.S. citizen, a legal resident or allowed to work in the U.S. If you are under 18, a parent, guardian or approved adult must agree and meet an admissions rep. Some rules apply about drug use and criminal history.
how_to_apply: Make an account on the sign-up site. Fill out the application. Interview with an admissions rep. Send papers such as your ID and proof that you are a citizen or resident. A campus review can take up to 30 days.
notes: The FAQ says you may get in faster if you are homeless. It does not name foster youth, so ask an admissions rep. Only enter your ID or Social Security number on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. Check that your nearest campus is open before you plan around it.

name: YouthBuild (find a local program)
pay_detail: Not stated on the national page. Ask the local program.
deadline_text: No dates on the national page. Each local program sets its own.
who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 who are out of school and out of work. YouthBuild mainly serves people without a high school diploma and with little money. Local sites set their own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the program map on the YouthBuild site to find a program near you, then contact it.
notes: The site says more than 300 programs run in seven countries. The program pages do not confirm a site in Elgin, Chicago, Atlanta, New York or Los Angeles. Use the map.

name: High School Career Academy
pay_detail: Paid; amount not stated
duration: November to April; two evening sessions a month (4:30 to 8 p.m.)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026-2027 is closed. 2027-28 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Franklin County and surrounding areas.
how_to_apply: Register when the program reopens; contact HNHFWorkforceDev@nationwidechildrens.org.
notes: The hospital's student opportunities page also lists Project SEARCH (a 9-month internship for students with disabilities) and Upward Bound Math and Science. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Youth and Young Adult Employment Program (paid summer work experience)
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated
duration: 4 or 8 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 30)
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened Feb 2 and closed March 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 21. Participants must be at least 16 years old at the time of registration.
how_to_apply: Register online during the registration window. Questions: HNHFWorkforceDev@NationwideChildrens.org.
notes: Popular: the page says there is overwhelming interest, and about 108 young adults took part in 2025. Schedules are Monday to Friday starting at 9 or 10 a.m. All participants are 16 or older, and Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) lets 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer give proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead of a work permit; the hospital may still ask for paperwork, so confirm.

name: North Carolina 4-H teen programs
org: North Carolina 4-H, NC Cooperative Extension (NC State and NC A&T)
city: Statewide, North Carolina (local 4-H office in every county)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Programs and events vary by county and have their own dates on the NC 4-H calendar.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 can join the teen programs. Age is counted as of January 1 of the program year. You join through your local county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H program. Then enroll through 4-H Online. That is the system for joining, renewing and signing up for events.
notes: The teen page was updated April 30, 2026. Clover Crew is listed as new in 2026. Programs differ from county to county. The pages do not give a fee or the dates for the teen events.

name: North Carolina Envirothon
org: North Carolina Envirothon with local Soil and Water Conservation Districts
pay_detail: Wake County's district pays registration for Wake teams. Fees for other counties are not stated on the program page.
duration: Area contest plus 2 day state event
deadline_text: Wake County sign-up form due Nov 20, 2026. Area 4 registration due Feb 1, 2027. Area 4 contest Mar 18, 2027. State contest April 23 to 24, 2027.
who_can_apply: Teams of 3 to 5 students from a school, non-traditional school or youth group such as 4-H or FFA. High school teams need five members to place at state. Each team needs an adult advisor.
how_to_apply: Sign up with your county Soil and Water Conservation District. In Wake County, fill out the Wake Envirothon sign-up form. The official form is emailed to advisors later in fall 2026.
notes: The dates above come from Wake County's page. Other areas of the state have their own area dates and deadlines, so call your county district. Wake contact: Leah Purvis, 919-250-1065.

name: North Carolina FFA
org: North Carolina FFA Association (NC State University Agricultural Education)
grades: Middle and high school (the page says national FFA has members in grades 5 to 12)
pay_detail: 2026-27 dues: $12 for high school students ($7 national plus $5 state) and $8 for middle school students ($7 national plus $1 state). Many chapters collect these through the school.
duration: Membership year runs Aug 1 to July 31
deadline_text: The membership year runs Aug 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027. The state membership deadline is March 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who belong to a school FFA chapter, which runs through a school agricultural education program. Homeschool students can join if they take an agriculture course and have an SAE project (for example through the NCSU Agriscience Academy chapter).
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher if your school has an FFA chapter. Take an agriculture class. The chapter advisor sends in the roster and dues. Homeschool families use the Homeschool FFA Membership Application on the page.
notes: The state office is at 4111 Beryl Road, Raleigh, NC 27606, 919-515-4206. The site says North Carolina has over 47,000 FFA members. If your school has no ag program, the page explains how a school can start one.

name: North Carolina Governor's Page Program
org: North Carolina Office of the Governor, hosted by VolunteerNC
grades: High school students or recent high school graduates
pay_detail: $200 stipend per week to help with travel and lodging costs. A limited number of host families provide meals and rides for a $100 fee paid by the page.
duration: One page week of four days (Monday afternoon, then Tuesday to Thursday)
deadline_text: The application for 2026 is closed. The page says applications are taken on a rolling basis until spots are filled, so apply as soon as the next application opens. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students or recent high school graduates in good academic standing. Seniors may apply to take part the summer before college. College students are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Governor's Page application and send the online recommendation form to two people: a non-relative school staff or faculty member (unless homeschooled) and a non-relative adult who can speak to your fit. Applications without both recommendations are not processed.
notes: Founded in 1973. The work location is the Albemarle building, 325 N Salisbury St, Raleigh. Business clothes are required. Pages and their guardians arrange where to stay and eat in Raleigh. Office of the Governor phone: (919) 814-2000. The page does not list dates for page weeks. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: North Carolina Governor's School
city: Raleigh and Greensboro, NC (Meredith College and Greensboro College)
grades: 11 when nominated (grades 10 and 11 for dance, choral music and instrumental music)
pay_detail: $600 tuition per student, collected through the school or district. Need-based scholarships are offered by the NC Governor's School Foundation. Families pay for travel.
duration: Four weeks (June 20 to July 17, 2027)
deadline_text: Application forms were released in Sept 2026. Local school deadlines vary and come in fall 2026. Selection news goes out in early to mid March 2027.
who_can_apply: North Carolina residents in public or non-public schools. You must meet one of the GPA or course rules in the family overview, for example a 3.25 unweighted GPA. You cannot apply on your own. Your school or district must nominate you first.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or local Governor's School coordinator. Turn in the student application at your school, not to the state office. It has one essay or audition and a personal readiness form. Turn in two recommendation forms too.
notes: Competitive. The family overview says about 1,800 students are nominated and about 800 are picked in a typical year. Students must stay the whole session and may attend only once. The overview says you may not use AI on the application.

name: North Carolina House Page Program
org: North Carolina General Assembly, House of Representatives
grades: Current sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12)
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.
duration: One week, Monday to Thursday, while the legislature is in session
deadline_text: Information on the 2027 House Page Program will be posted late this fall (2026). Applications are taken on a first-come basis until all spots for the session are full.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors in good school standing. A North Carolina House member must sponsor you. You must not have been a House Page before. School principal approval is needed if you serve during the school year.
how_to_apply: Ask your own House member to sponsor you (find yours with the Find Your Legislators tool). Then fill out the online application, which goes to that member. You can ask the House Page office, Room 1329, 16 W. Jones Street, Raleigh, for a paper copy.
notes: Very competitive and you can apply with only one member. The Speaker of the House makes the final appointments. Housing in Raleigh is up to your parent or guardian. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: Job Corps in North Carolina (Schenck, Kittrell, Oconaluftee)
org: U.S. Department of Labor, Job Corps
city: Pisgah Forest, Kittrell and Cherokee, NC
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The process usually takes about two months.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Centers: Schenck, 98 Schenck Dr, Pisgah Forest, NC 28768. Kittrell, 1096 U.S. Highway 1 South, Kittrell, NC 27544. Oconaluftee, 502 Oconaluftee Job Corps Rd, Cherokee, NC 28719. No closure notice showed on the pages on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Lady Cardinal Mentorship Program
org: NC Department of Administration, Division for Women and Youth
pay_detail: $1,700 stipend, paid on the second to last day of the program. No housing is provided.

how_to_apply: Apply when the application portal opens in early January 2027. The FAQ says to check the program website for current deadlines. Email your resume, cover letter and transcript to doa.youth.involvement@doa.nc.gov. Students who skip these documents are dropped from the process.
notes: Only 15 to 20 spots. You must get yourself to your job site every day; the program only gives rides to Wednesday and Thursday events. Contact named on the page: Jean McBride. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: Cafe Coordinators

notes: Volunteer role, and it costs a yearly fee. Contact Lynn Cross (listed on the page) about scholarships.

notes: The page did not describe how students are picked.

how_to_apply: Show up at the Daily Planet Cafe at the museum or watch live on YouTube. No sign up is listed on the page.
notes: A good first step before applying to Cafe Coordinators.

notes: Niche: for serious young players. Entry fee and rounds' dates are not stated on the page.

notes: Delegates must attend the full week. The FAQ page says graduates get an automatic $20,000 scholarship to Chowan University, spread over 4 years. The girls' program is a separate American Legion Auxiliary program (Tar Heel Girls State) and is not covered here.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, North Carolina Wing

city: Statewide, North Carolina (squadrons in many towns)

notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. NC Wing office: 3520 Alamance Road, Burlington, NC 27215, 336-290-7473, info@ncwgcap.org. The NC Wing site lists a 2027 summer encampment page.

name: North Carolina Youth Apprenticeship
city: Statewide, North Carolina (employers and community college partners)

duration: Varies by apprenticeship
deadline_text: No single deadline. Each employer or program sets its own hiring.
who_can_apply: Start as early as age 16. You must be enrolled in high school or be a high school graduate, interested in a high-demand career field, and ready to do both on-the-job learning and classroom instruction.
how_to_apply: Find a Registered Apprenticeship opportunity on the ApprenticeshipNC site and contact the program sponsor or employer to apply. Questions: apprenticeshipnc@nccommunitycolleges.edu or 919-807-6988. The page also mentions youth apprenticeship consortia that serve high school students.
notes: The NC Department of Labor says youth under 18 who work in North Carolina must have a Youth Employment Certificate, started by the employer once you have a job offer. Some jobs are off limits to people under 18 unless a supervised practice agreement is approved. Specific openings and employers change, so use the Find Apprenticeship Opportunities tool.

notes: The page does not say where the application is, what it costs or when it is due. Check the page again or call the coordinator before you plan.

For the Junior Wildlife Assistant role you must be in 10th or 11th grade when you apply, live within 90 miles of the zoo, and be able to lift 50 lbs and stand for 30 minutes. Other roles have their own rules on their pages.

name: Nevada Youth Legislature

name: Soup Kitchen Volunteering, Elijah's Promise

name: Teen Volunteering (Teen Action Group and Kindness Club)

notes: Board meetings in fall 2026 are listed for Oct 20 and Nov 17 on the page.

notes: This is a school program, not a job. Students from outside the county are admitted only if there is space.

name: BOLD Summer Camp (BioCONECT Oncology Leadership Development), Rutgers Cancer Institute

The $500 deposit is non-refundable. No 2027 cost is posted.

notes: Selective program. Email the coordinator listed on the page if you need help getting a laptop.

name: Rutgers Summer Scholars Program
org: Rutgers University-New Brunswick Pre-College Summer Programs

duration: Summer Session I (started May 26, 2026) or Session II (started July 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened February 2; last day to apply May 17 (Session I) and June 28 (Session II). 2027 dates not posted.

notes: Some courses need extra technology or prerequisite courses. Withdrawing after the add/drop period puts a W on a Rutgers transcript. Questions: summerscholars@rutgers.edu.

name: Toxicology, Health and Environmental Disease (THED) High School Summer Program
org: Rutgers Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences Institute (EOHSI)

name: Rutgers Upward Bound Math-Science (RUBMS)

name: Rutgers Young Scholars Program in Discrete Mathematics
pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.

notes: Residential; students go home on weekends. The page was the Summer 2026 listing.

name: Teen / High School Volunteers, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
org: RWJBarnabas Health, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital

name: Youth Recreation Advisory Board, Woodbridge Township
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a civic board.
duration: One year term, August 1 to July 31
deadline_text: Terms start each August. The page gives no application dates.
who_can_apply: 15 high school students. High school principals suggest them, one member and one backup per school. The Mayor then names them for one year starting in August. Members can apply again until they graduate.
how_to_apply: Ask your high school principal to recommend you. The Mayor then appoints members for a one-year term starting in August.
notes: Very small: about 15 seats. The page lives on a township website that uses the woodbridgelibrary.org address.

name: New Jersey 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Ongoing clubs and programs; camp is a week in summer
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs and programs run through the year.

how_to_apply: Use the Join 4-H form on the New Jersey 4-H site, or find your county 4-H office on the Rutgers 4-H page.
notes: Not a job. It is a youth group. The Rutgers homepage has a Join 4-H form and a link to the New Jersey 4-H Camp. The pages did not give fees, so ask your county 4-H office.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Jersey Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of New Jersey
city: New Jersey (2026 session at Centenary University)
grades: Junior in high school when applying
pay_detail: No pay. Sponsors (units, posts or other groups) enroll and sponsor delegates; the site does not list a fee to the student.
duration: About 5 days (2026: Sunday June 21 to Thursday June 25)
deadline_text: 2026 sponsorships were filled and no applicants were being accepted. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Juniors who live or go to school in New Jersey and are legal U.S. residents. You must be fluent in English and able to attend the whole session. You must be willing to take part in nondenominational prayer, patriotic ceremonies, the Pledge and the National Anthem. An Auxiliary unit must sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact a local American Legion Auxiliary unit or a county chairperson to ask for sponsorship. The site lists contacts. You cannot apply without a sponsor.
notes: Girls only. Start asking local Auxiliary units in the winter. The 2026 site says sponsorships were already filled. A matching program for boys (Jersey Boys State) is run by the American Legion.

name: American Legion Jersey Boys State
org: American Legion Department of New Jersey
grades: 11th grade (junior) with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Post-sponsored: parents pay a $50 non-refundable fee and the post pays the rest. Self-sponsored: $50 non-refundable application fee plus $325 tuition if accepted (food, housing and supplies included). Scholarships may be available.
duration: One week; delegates arrive on Father's Day (the 80th session began June 21, 2026)
deadline_text: For the 2026 session (began June 21, 2026) the home page said applications were open through June 7. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors with at least one semester left. Posts pick students with school help, or you can apply on your own as self-sponsored.
how_to_apply: If a post sponsors you, your school staff recommend you. The local American Legion post interviews you. If you sponsor yourself, make an account on the ALJBS CampSite portal. Fill out the questionnaire. Add a 300 to 500 word essay, or a video or a counselor reference. Pay the $50 fee.
notes: Boys only (Jersey Girls State is a separate program). Post-sponsored and self-sponsored costs are in pay_detail.

name: Junior Volunteer Program
org: Capital Health (hospitals in Trenton and Hopewell area, NJ)

how_to_apply: Online application only, then orientation and on-site training. Questions: Volunteer Services, 609-303-4023, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday.
notes: Does not offer internships or shadowing. Year-round track runs Sept 14, 2026 to June 30, 2027 when open. Check the page for when applications reopen.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, New Jersey Wing
org: Civil Air Patrol, New Jersey Wing
city: New Jersey (local squadrons across the state)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: Governor's School of New Jersey in Engineering and Technology
org: Rutgers School of Engineering / State of New Jersey
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
deadline_text: 2027 application not posted on the program pages. The state page (updated 11/13/25) said 2026 applications were open; decisions are emailed in early April. Ask your school counselor about the school nomination deadline.
who_can_apply: New Jersey residents who have finished their junior year at a public, private or home school. Applicants must be nominated by their high school (one nominee per 325 juniors). It is competitive. Fewer than 25% of nominees get offers.
how_to_apply: Get nominated by your high school, then submit the online application with essays (admission is based heavily on essays). Contact: njgset@soe.rutgers.edu or 848-445-4753.
notes: Residential at Rutgers School of Engineering, 98 Brett Road, Piscataway. The Application Instructions page on the program site still mentions the Summer 2023 application, so rely on the state page and director for 2027 dates.

name: Career Prep at Mercer County Community College
pay_detail: Free. No tuition for the college classes.
duration: Senior year, follows the college calendar
deadline_text: The career prep page links to an application but does not say whether it is open and gives no dates. Ask admissions@mcts.edu for the 2027-2028 dates.
who_can_apply: Rising seniors with at least a 3.2 GPA and 95 percent attendance. Students in the MCTS Academy or Shared-Time programs cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Create an account in the MCTS online application portal and apply. Your counselor then uploads transcripts and attendance. Email admissions@mcts.edu with questions.
notes: You become a regular college student with a MyMercer account. Most classes are on the West Windsor campus. Mercer County residency is not spelled out on the page, so ask admissions. The Aviation section says that by continuing this program, costs could range from $24,000 to $36,000. The page does not say what that covers.

name: Shared-Time Career Programs (grades 11 and 12)
grades: Apply in 10th grade; programs run grades 11 and 12
pay_detail: Part of your regular school day. No cost stated.
duration: 2 years (grades 11 and 12), half day
deadline_text: The 2027-2028 application is open now. No closing date is posted on the page. Info sessions: Oct 29, Nov 19, Dec 9 and Dec 16, 2026 and Jan 11, 2027.
who_can_apply: 10th graders. The page gives no acceptance criteria for shared-time programs and refers to a separate admissions procedures page. The page says no RSVP is required for the information sessions. Your home district provides transportation.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the online application portal and fill in the form. Your school counselor then sends your grades and attendance. Email admissions@mcts.edu with questions.
notes: Students in a shared-time program cannot also do Career Prep. Ask your counselor for the deadline. Programs are at the Assunpink Center (Trenton) and the Sypek Center (Pennington).

name: Career and Technical Programs 2027-28 Application
org: Somerset County Vocational and Technical High Schools
grades: Not stated on the page. See the Application and Admission FAQ.

duration: 2027-28 school year start
