who_can_apply: Students applying for the 2027-28 school year. Some programs (biomedical, finance, HVACR, global business) are shared-time only.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the admissions page. An admissions test may be required (see the CTE Admissions Testing page). Call Pupil Services at 908-526-8900 ext. 7250 or 7243.
notes: The health sciences academy has its own admission page and phone, 908-526-8900 ext. 7148. Enrolled students can join a paid co-op job. Outside teens cannot.

name: Watershed Academy for High School Students
pay_detail: $525 to $575 per week in 2026. Limited full scholarships based on financial need.
duration: 1 to 4 weeks, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions ran July 6 to 31, 2026 with full payment due March 18, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. Ages and grades are not listed on the page. Scholarships are first come, first served, with priority to Greater Trenton Area students who attend all four weeks.
how_to_apply: Register through CampDoc and pay a 50 percent deposit. For a scholarship, fill out the separate online Financial Aid form for each child.
notes: The scholarship wording on the page still says 2025, so confirm it. Bus rides from several Trenton stops are mentioned. Contact 609-737-3735.

name: Volunteer Roles for Teens
duration: Varies: Sundays March to November, Tuesday mornings mid June to August, one year for animal care
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page shows the 2026 volunteer application. Next stream cleanups: April 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages differ by role: 14 for Critter Care (and stream sampling with an adult), 15 for Sunday Stewardship on your own, 16 for the Welcome Desk and Butterfly House Crew.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application through the Apply Here link on the page. You get a link to log your hours after you apply. Questions: 609-737-3735.
notes: Some roles need your own ride. The page says one stream monitoring role is not a good fit for 12th graders.

name: New Jersey Youth Corps
org: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development
city: New Jersey (local sites across the state)
pay_detail: Corpsmembers get a stipend while enrolled. The amount is not stated on the state page.
duration: Full time, year-round program; length of each cohort is not stated on the state page
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The program is described as year-round.
who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 25 who do not have a high school diploma.
how_to_apply: Send the online services request form on the NJ Department of Labor page for general questions. The state page does not list sign-up steps, so ask for the site that serves your county.
notes: For teens 16 and up who left school without a diploma. Not for students still working toward a diploma in a regular school. It includes help getting a high school equivalency diploma or an adult high school diploma. It includes counseling and help moving on to college or jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.

name: New Jersey Youth Institute (World Food Prize)
org: Rutgers School of Environmental and Biological Sciences, with the World Food Prize Foundation
pay_detail: Free to take part (no registration cost). For students invited to the Global Youth Institute in Des Moines, most expenses are covered by the World Food Prize, but travel is not included.
duration: One day (2026 date: March 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: registration and paper due by February 6, 2026; the Institute was March 6, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 12. The page does not list an age rule or a residency rule; it describes students from New Jersey.
how_to_apply: Research a global issue and write a paper with a teacher or mentor, following the guidelines PDF on the page. Register and submit the paper through the World Food Prize website.
notes: The Rutgers page was read through a summarizing fetch tool because the site blocks plain page requests, so check the page itself for the 2027 date. It is listed on the New Jersey 4-H page as a program for high school students.

name: New Mexico 4-H
pay_detail: New Mexico 4-H generally has no statewide membership fee. Some counties, clubs or projects have costs for supplies, livestock, workshops or camps. Ask your County Extension Office.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: The 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30. Enrollment usually opens in October. Deadlines vary by county.
who_can_apply: Any New Mexico youth ages 5 to 18 can join. You do not need a farm or any skills. Cloverbuds are ages 5 to 8. Novice is 9 to 11. Junior is 12 to 13. Senior is 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office and talk with your 4-H agent. Then create a family account and enroll at 4h.zsuite.org. Returning members re-enroll each year, update projects and submit the required forms.
notes: State office phone on the page is 575-646-3026. Call it if you are not sure which county you are in.

name: New Mexico Agricultural Education and FFA Association
pay_detail: Leadership Camp fee was $225 per camper on a page that looks older (copyright 2022). Camp scholarships were offered.
duration: School year. Leadership Camp is a separate event.
deadline_text: Join through your school's ag program.
who_can_apply: Students in New Mexico ag education programs. The association says it serves over 5,300 members in over 85 schools. No age or grade rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The site lists FFA chapter lists, a 2026-2027 plan for events, scholarships and Jr. High contests.
notes: Some pages on this site carry a 2022 copyright, so camp fees and dates may be out of date. Confirm with your ag teacher or the state office. The homepage does not show the $225 camp fee, so confirm it before relying on it.

name: Forest Stewards Youth Corps (Summer)
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly rate is not stated on the program pages.
duration: Early June to early August (2026)
deadline_text: The page contradicts itself. Its menu says FSYC Summer Hiring (Closed), but the text says the program is hiring now. No 2027 hiring dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Young people from forest-dependent communities in New Mexico. The summer program is for high school age youth. The Guild says its work covers ages 16 to 25.
how_to_apply: Watch the Guild's FSYC page for position descriptions and application forms. Crew member information is posted on the project page later in the year.
notes: The New Mexico Youth Conservation Corps Commission and the Cibola and Santa Fe National Forests pay for part of it. Past crew members who log 640 hours may get a federal hiring status. Pay and crew sites could not be read on the pages checked.

name: Conservation Crew Corpsmember (Rocky Mountain Youth Corps of New Mexico)
org: Rocky Mountain Youth Corps of New Mexico
pay_detail: $700 per week for the 2027 Corpsmember job. Paid by stipend.
duration: Seasonal, full time (40 or more hours a week). The end date is not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The 2027 Corpsmember jobs list a start date of March 18, 2027. The apply page does not give a last day to apply.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 30, per the 2027 job list. No earlier experience is needed for crew member jobs.
how_to_apply: Open the apply page and find the 2027 Conservation Crew Corpsmember job in Albuquerque or Taos. Then use its Apply Now link.
notes: The work is outdoors. The program page says ages 17 to 25, and the job list says 17 to 30. Ask RMYC if you are close to the top age. Some crews camp for 8 days in a row, then have 6 days off. Corpsmembers who complete a full AmeriCorps season become eligible for a scholarship award. The FAQ lists UNM College Credit as a member benefit.

name: WIOA Youth Program, Central Region
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the program. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 16 to 24. You live in Bernalillo, Sandoval, Valencia or Torrance County. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Call 505-818-1428 (WIOA Youth inquiries) or 505-977-3216, or use the contact form on the program page.
notes: Ask YDI if you qualify.

how_to_apply: Contact YDI through the form on the program page or call 505-977-3216 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
notes: WIOA programs have federal rules on who qualifies. Ask YDI if you qualify.

name: New Mexico Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
org: New Mexico Youth Conservation Corps Commission, EMNRD
pay_detail: Pay not stated on this page. Returning corps members can earn a $500 cash benefit or a $1,500 education voucher.

deadline_text: Set by each sponsor. The state page lists funded projects by year.
who_can_apply: New Mexico youth ages 14 to 25. Local governments, tribes and nonprofits apply for state funding and then hire the corps members.
how_to_apply: Find a funded project near you on the YCC projects map. Then contact that sponsor about jobs. A sponsor can be a city, county, tribe or nonprofit.
notes: Teens do not apply to the state. The state funds sponsors, who do the hiring. Pay, dates and application steps vary by sponsor. The projects map on this page shows 2021 to 2023 projects, and older ones are on a separate Projects page.

name: Dual Enrollment (New River Community College)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Semester by semester

You need a note of support from a high school official and a signed form from a parent. Strong freshmen and sophomores may be able to join. They need the OK of the high school principal and the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor and use the dual enrollment forms on the NRCC page. The parent signature form is required.
notes: The NRCC page still showed an old campus closure banner, so confirm the details with the college. Cost to students is not stated on the page.

name: New York State 4-H
org: Cornell Cooperative Extension, New York State 4-H

who_can_apply: Youth from kindergarten up to age 19. A kindergartner must turn 5 by January 1 of the 4-H year. A teen cannot enroll or re-enroll if they will turn 19 before January 1 of the new club year (club year runs Oct 1 to Sept 30). Counties can set their own details.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Cornell Cooperative Extension office. Join a club. If you cannot join a club, you can enroll as an independent member. You work on projects at your own pace with an adult helping.
notes: Not a job. The rules are for New York State 4-H as described by two county Cornell Cooperative Extension pages (Jefferson and Erie). The listed URL is the Erie County page. Your own county office has the sign-up steps and costs.

name: NYS DEC Summer Camps (Colby, DeBruce, Pack Forest, Rushford)
org: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
city: New York State (camps in Franklin County, the Catskills, Allegany County and the southern Adirondacks)

deadline_text: Registration for 2026 opened Sunday March 22, 2026 at 1 PM and weeks fill quickly (waitlist available). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth 14 to 17 can go to the weeks set aside for that age. Campers must be the minimum age by December 1 of the calendar year. The pages do not state a residency rule.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Empire Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of New York
city: New York State (check-in at SUNY Brockport)

how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Auxiliary unit. Ask your guidance counselor or email egsregistrar@gmail.com with your hometown, county and school. Join the local selection. Then use the login the unit gives you. Register online and pay the fee.
notes: Girls only. The site says there is a virtual orientation on Zoom in May or June. The program says it is not a sports camp or a recreational camp.

name: New York State Parks Lifeguard
org: New York State Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP)
city: New York State (state parks, pools and beaches; Long Island has its own process)

Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Newport Beach Fire Cadet Program

name: Newport Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers

deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are first-come, first-served and accepted as needed.
who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.

name: Newport Beach Ocean Lifeguard Trainee

pay_detail: Paid training is $16.90 an hour. Lifeguard I pay is $25.50 to $31.02 an hour.

deadline_text: Applications close January 20, 2027 at 5:00 p.m. The tryout is planned for Saturday, January 30, 2027, with check-in at 8:30 a.m. An info night is Wednesday, January 6, 2027, 6:00 to 7:30 p.m.

The info night is at Lifeguard Headquarters, 70 Newport Pier, in person or on Zoom, and is not required. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.

name: Newport Beach Teen Leader Program
org: City of Newport Beach Recreation and Senior Services
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.

deadline_text: The page says 2026 applications closed Thursday, May 1, 2026 (that date is a Friday, so confirm on the page). Applications are now closed. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.

name: Youth Career Program
org: City of Newport News, Office of Workforce Development and Economic Mobility
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages
duration: About 25 hours a week, June to August (from the employer page)
deadline_text: The Summer 2026 enrollment is closed. Student applications reopen on February 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: Newport News residents ages 16 to 17 and young adults ages 18 to 24. Under 18 needs a signed parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth - Apply for the Youth Career Program link on the city page. Finish the application steps.
notes: Not open to 14 and 15 year olds. The city page does not state the wage.

name: Oregon Coast Aquarium Youth Volunteer (Exhibit Interpreter)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fees. Perks include a free aquarium membership after 50 hours and guest passes.
duration: School-year program: 20 hours of training and 48 hours of volunteering in 4-hour shifts (68 total). Summer first-year program: 66 hours total.
deadline_text: The page lists school-year info sessions on Thursday October 15 at 6:00pm (virtual) and Saturday October 17, 10:30 am to 11:30 am (in person), and school-year training on November 7, 14 and 21. The page gives no year for these. Summer training is in June 2027. Email volunteer@aquarium.org to be added to the interest list.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 by the program start date. You must be entering grades 9 to 12 (or home school at that level).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application. Go to an info session (online or in person). Chosen volunteers go to 3 days of training in person.
notes: The page does not state a set application window. Summer volunteers can also earn hours through trips and career activities. Contact: volunteer@aquarium.org.

name: World Series of Innovation (Impact League)
pay_detail: Free to enter. Cash prizes of $300 to $1,500 for winning entries.
duration: Entries due Dec 13, 2026. Winners announced in spring 2027.
deadline_text: Entries are due Dec 13, 2026. The 2026-2027 challenge launched Sept 9, 2026.
who_can_apply: The Impact League is for ages 13 to 24. Younger kids (5 to 12) enter the Imagination League. Single entries and teams are both allowed.
how_to_apply: Go to innovation.nfte.com and submit your entry before the deadline. The announcement page does not give step-by-step rules, so read the full rules on that site.
notes: Online, so it works from any city. The Impact League age range runs past 18, so you compete with college-age entrants too (page does not say whether groups are judged separately). NFTE also holds a Youth Entrepreneurship Showcase in New York City on Nov 18 to 19, 2026; the page did not say who can attend.

name: Marine Teens Internship
org: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (NHMLAC)
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the application link and deadline.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.

name: Critical Action Lab (Natural History Museum of Utah)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not stated.
duration: A yearly group (the 2026 to 2027 group is already chosen)
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026 to 2027 group are closed. The page says to check back later.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Join the email list on the page to hear when applications open.
notes: The first group of Fellows began in fall 2023.

name: Teen Explainers (Natural History Museum of Utah)
pay_detail: Hourly wage starting at $13.00. You can choose to volunteer instead. Staff can ride UTA transit free during the internship.
duration: School year group: October 7, 2026 to April 14, 2027, about 90 hours. A summer group runs June to August.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026 to 2027 school year group are closed. The summer group (June to August) is described on the page; the next dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 who can attend all required group meetings.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the next application opens. Email Erin Shupe or call 801-581-3774 with questions. Subscribe to quarterly updates on the page.
notes: Meetings are Wednesdays 6 to 8 PM, plus some Saturdays. Later you work 2 gallery shifts of 2.5 hours a month.

name: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
org: National Institutes of Health, Office of Intramural Training and Education
pay_detail: Stipend, set each year by education level. The page does not state the amount. Free parking. You need proof of health insurance, and NIH does not provide housing.
duration: Full time, between May 10 and August 31, 2027. Exact dates are set with your mentor. No vacations during the internship.
deadline_text: The 2027 application is open now and closes Tuesday, January 26, 2027 at 12 pm ET. Reference letters are due Tuesday, February 2, 2027 at 12 pm ET.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or green card holders who will be 18 by September 30, 2027. You must be a senior now who will finish high school before it starts, or a college student. If you are 17 on June 1, 2027, you must live within 40 miles of an NIH campus.
how_to_apply: Apply in the NIH Application Center. Send your grades, a resume, a short essay about your goals, and two references. Then email NIH scientists whose work you like and point them to your application. Each scientist picks their own interns by April 1.
notes: Very competitive, and mostly for college students. Only seniors who meet the age rule can apply; juniors cannot. Free online application webinars on Oct 20 and Nov 17, 2026. Questions: SIP@nih.gov.

name: NISRA Volunteers and Summer Camp Jobs (Elgin and 12 other member communities)
city: Elgin and 12 other member communities, northern Illinois
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Part-time jobs (1 to 20 hours a week) are paid, but pay is not on the program page.
duration: Program seasons are 6 to 8 weeks. Volunteers are asked to commit for the full season.
deadline_text: No deadline. NISRA says it hires summer camp staff each winter and spring. Postings are on the ADP Workforce Now site.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old. The page does not list a minimum age for the part-time and camp jobs, so check the posting.
how_to_apply: For jobs, apply on NISRA's ADP Workforce Now site from the Employment page. For volunteering, use the Volunteer Opportunities link on the same page. Call NISRA at 815-459-0737.
notes: The City of Elgin is a member of NISRA. The city says NISRA offers programs at Elgin sites. The 15 week internship is for therapeutic recreation college students. Jobs need a reliable ride. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit.

name: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP), Gaithersburg
org: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
grades: High school juniors and seniors when you apply
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a competitive volunteer program.
duration: Seven weeks, mid-June to early August (2027 dates to be decided)
deadline_text: Not open yet as of Oct 11. The page (updated Sept 14) says the 2027 job announcement is expected on USAJOBS in mid-October, with applications due at the end of January 2027. A lower line says applications generally open Nov 1, so the open date is not firm.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens who are a high school junior or senior at the time of application, with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must be able to do the full seven weeks and live within 50 miles of the host campus. Families must provide their own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Watch for the SHIP job announcement on USAJOBS and follow the application page linked from the SHIP page. The page says to read the application process page for the full steps.
notes: The page lists two NIST campuses (Boulder, CO and Gaithersburg, MD); this card is for Gaithersburg. The 2026 poster session was held in Gaithersburg on Aug 6, 2026. The exact application dates for 2027 were not final on the page, so check it again in late October.

name: Conservation Youth Team
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $100 registration fee for shirts, name tag and materials. A scholarship covers this fee for a few first-year applicants.
duration: About 150 hours in summer plus fall or spring sessions for first-year members
deadline_text: Applications open December 1. 2026 materials were due March 16, 2026, with interviews in late March and decisions in April.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 13 to 17. This includes teens going into 9th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Conservation Youth Team page. Info sessions were held in February and March. Teens who are picked have an interview.
notes: Dates are from the 2026 cycle. Applications open December 1, and the year is not stated. The page lists interest sessions in February and March.

name: North Dakota 4-H Ambassador Program
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications were due Oct 15, 2026. The next chance is the June election. Its May 15 deadline is from last year, since 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 22. The program page does not say if you must be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Get the form from Ambassador Resources on the NDSU 4-H leadership page. Send it to the ND 4-H Center for Youth Development.
notes: Selection is the Saturday before Thanksgiving at 4-H Camp in Washburn. Questions: ndsu.4hambassadors@ndsu.edu.

name: North Dakota Extension Youth Conference (EYC)
pay_detail: Teens pay. Early-bird price was $365 per person (Thanksgiving through December), then the price rises $10 a month. Payment is due June 1.
duration: 4 days. The 2026 conference was June 22 to 25 at NDSU in Fargo.
deadline_text: 2026: early-bird registration ran from Thanksgiving through December, and registration closed June 1. 2027 dates are not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Youth who have finished seventh grade. You do not need to be in 4-H.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the NDSU event page.
notes: Ask North Dakota 4-H about financial help. The page does not mention scholarships.

name: North Dakota 4-H Leadership Awareness Weekend (LAW)
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.
duration: Weekend, Feb 14 to 15, 2027. If weather cancels it, make-up dates are April 4 to 5, 2027.
deadline_text: Event Feb 14 to 15, 2027 in Bismarck. The registration deadline is not listed on the program page.
who_can_apply: Grades 7 to 12. The program page does not say whether you must be in 4-H.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the NDSU event page.
notes: Cost is not listed yet. Call North Dakota 4-H or your county Extension office to ask.

name: North Dakota Governor's School
org: NDSU Office of Teaching and Learning and University of North Dakota
city: Fargo or Grand Forks, ND (host switches between NDSU and UND)
pay_detail: The NDSU pages do not list a cost. A UND article says a North Dakota Department of Public Instruction grant covered tuition and on-campus housing for the 2025 session. Check that this still holds.
duration: Four weeks. 2026 dates were June 8 to July 2.
deadline_text: The NDSU page shows the NDGS 2026 timeline with no year on the later dates: portal opened October 13, 2025 and closed February 15, 2026; acceptance emails March 12 (year not shown); accept by April 10 (year not shown). The 2026 program ran June 8 to July 2. The next session's dates are not posted on the program pages.
who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders who live in North Dakota. You can attend a public or non-public school. You need a cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher. Selection uses a personal essay of 250 words or less. It also uses two recommendations (one teacher, one counselor or administrator) and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the NDSU Governor's School site (2026 cycle). You need a personal essay of 250 words or less. You also need one teacher recommendation. You need one counselor or administrator recommendation too. Questions? Email ndsu.otl@ndsu.edu.
notes: The NDSU page says the program runs every other summer. The next session's host, dates and portal are not posted on the program pages. Ask NDSU at ndsu.otl@ndsu.edu.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Registration for January 2027 opportunities opens Dec. 17 at 5 p.m., per the library's teen hub page (year inferred). Fall 2026 registration is closed.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 8 to 12. Volunteers who work with the public must pass a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Fill in the teen volunteer form on the library page when it opens.
notes: Questions: 604-998-3450. The Dec 17 date comes from the Teens' community hub page. Exact roles are not listed on the page.

name: Become a Lifeguard and Swim Instructor at NVRC
org: North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the program pages. Job pay not stated.
duration: Several courses
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13. First Aid is 15. National Lifeguard is 15. Swim Instructor is 15. Lifesaving Instructor is 16. To apply for a job, you must be a citizen, a permanent resident or have a valid work permit.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses online. After you are certified, apply on the NVRC job site. Email swim@nvrc.ca with questions.
notes: Courses need 100% attendance. Withdraw 8 or more days before the start for a full refund. The minimum age to be hired is not stated on the pages.

name: Volunteer with North Vancouver Recreation and Culture (NVRC)
org: North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies. Early years roles ask for 4 to 6 months.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Some roles need an older age or certificates (for example Aquatics needs age 15, Bronze Cross and Swim Instructor). Fitness volunteers must be 17 or over. Under 18 needs a parent signature.
how_to_apply: There are eight steps. Fill out the online form. Give two references. Sign the volunteer agreement. Get a police check at the RCMP where you live. Sign the photo release. Upload your forms. Go to orientation. Then email volunteer@nvrc.ca.
notes: Contact volunteer@nvrc.ca or 604-983-6345. The police check must be done where you live.

name: Youth Train in Trades (North Vancouver School District)
org: North Vancouver School District 44 with BCIT, VCC and SkilledTradesBC
pay_detail: Tuition covered by the school board
duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: Deadline is the end of February for programs the next school year. Year not stated.
who_can_apply: Domestic students in North Vancouver School District, mainly grade 12. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school Career Program teacher. If you missed the deadline, email jkinakin@sd44.ca.
notes: The page lists 16 programs.

name: Vancouver Coastal Health North Shore Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can get reference letters and recognition.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week for at least 6 months
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply online any time.
who_can_apply: The page says its volunteers are over 16 years old. You need to be grown up, on time and good at talking with people.
how_to_apply: Fill in the North Shore form online. It takes 4 to 8 weeks. VCH runs a record check. Then you have an interview, reference checks and training.
notes: North Shore Volunteer Resources: (604) 984-5929, nsvolunteer@vch.ca. VCH's Vancouver program (VGH, UBC Hospital, G.F. Strong) does not state a minimum age on its pages, so ask vanvolunteer@vch.ca before applying there.

name: Civic Leadership Institute (CTD Summer Camp)
org: Northwestern University Center for Talent Development
pay_detail: Summer 2026 tuition: $5,530 residential camp or $3,125 day camp. Financial aid for qualified students is given on a rolling basis while funds last.
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran June 28 to July 17, 2026. 2027 dates and prices are not posted yet. The program has said to apply early for aid.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. CTD uses levels based on test scores. Or it uses a school record and teacher recommendation. Check the course page and the CTD eligibility page.
how_to_apply: Apply online through MyCTD. For admission, you use test scores or a portfolio. The portfolio is your report card and a teacher recommendation. If you have questions, email ctd-admissions@northwestern.edu.
notes: Costs a lot and is for advanced learners. CTD also has many other summer and weekend courses for grades 6 to 12 that are not listed here.

name: Summer Volunteer Service for Students
org: Northwestern Medicine (Delnor in Geneva, Central DuPage in Winfield, Lake Forest and other suburban hospitals)
city: Geneva, Winfield, Lake Forest and other suburbs, IL
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: One day a week for 8 weeks between May and August
deadline_text: The 2026 summer application period is closed. The page says to check back for the 2027 Summer Service Period in early autumn. It gives no 2027 dates on this page.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 years old. For Northwestern Memorial Hospital the age is 18, and it has no summer program. You must pass a health screening and an interview. You must also go to a virtual orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during the window. Then do an interview. Onboarding includes a health screening and an orientation. Ages 18 and up also get a background check.
notes: Volunteer offices: Delnor, 630-938-2180. Central DuPage, 630-933-6207. Lake Forest, 847-535-6851. Call the one near you.

name: Medill Cherubs Journalism Institute
org: Northwestern University, Medill School of Journalism
grades: Current high school juniors (rising seniors), no exceptions
pay_detail: Tuition $5,000 including room and board. Up to $100,000 in financial aid and scholarships is available. $55 application fee.
duration: 4 weeks (June 27 to July 23, 2027)
deadline_text: No applications before December 1, 2026. All materials are due by noon Central on March 1, 2027. Decisions by March 24, 2027.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who will be seniors in fall 2027. The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form, write a 200 to 225 word essay, list your journalism activities and send up to three work samples. Pay the $55 fee. Your counselor emails your transcript, GPA and school profile to Prof. Roger Boye. Add the financial aid form and a parent tax return if you want aid.
notes: Questions: r-boye@northwestern.edu (email is best) or (847) 491-2069.

name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Policy Debate Institute
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: $3,500 for the 4 week institute, $5,000 for the 6 week institute. $60 application fee.
duration: 4 or 6 weeks
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application opens this winter. Rolling admission through April or until the labs are full. 2026 dates were June 28 to July 25 (4 weeks) and June 28 to August 8 (6 weeks).
who_can_apply: Students rising into grades 9 to 12 the summer they attend. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and experience or interest in policy debate.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials such as a debate record, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. You need a laptop with a webcam, a mic and Microsoft Word.
notes: The 2026 program was online only. Check whether 2027 is online or on campus. Financial aid and scholarship page exists on the NHSI site but was not read.

name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Film and Video Division
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.
duration: 5 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: early deadline January 9, 2026 and regular deadline March 13, 2026, with rolling late applications for some concentrations. 2027 dates are not posted yet. The home page says applications open in November.
who_can_apply: Students in their sophomore or junior year who will be rising juniors or seniors. The page asks for a class rank in or near the top 30 percent. It also asks for proof of special skill or strong interest in media arts.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials. These may include two essays, a resume, a letter of recommendation, test scores and your transcript.
notes: Competitive and costly. Travel is not included. Aid is need-based only. Not a paid program.

name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Theatre Arts Division
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.
duration: 5 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: early deadline January 2, 2026 and regular deadline February 27, 2026 (online form). 2027 dates are not posted yet. The home page says applications open in November.
who_can_apply: Students in 10th or 11th grade who will be rising juniors or seniors. Juniors get priority. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and some theatre experience or strong interest.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send a resume, two essays, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. Test scores are optional. The Musical Theatre track needs a third essay.
notes: Competitive and costs a lot, but the program says need-based aid is given and does not offer merit aid. Travel is not included. Not a paid program.

name: Waterpark seasonal jobs with free training
org: NOVA Parks (Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority)
city: Northern Virginia (Fairfax, Alexandria and Arlington waterparks)
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
deadline_text: Page says NOVA Parks is hiring; no deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Attendants must be at least 14, lifeguards at least 15, cooks at least 16.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Now' link under the position on the Waterpark Employment page (current listings: lifeguard at Atlantis and Pirate's Cove, water safety instructor at Great Waves and Ocean Dunes).
notes: Atlantis is at Bull Run and Pirate's Cove at Pohick Bay (Fairfax County); Great Waves is in Alexandria and Ocean Dunes is at Upton Hill in Arlington. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: NOVAworks Young Adult Services
city: Sunnyvale, CA (serves San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County)
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
deadline_text: Open enrollment. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or in Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale. High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income. They also need one of these: justice involvement, being unhoused or a runaway, or foster care (in it now or aged out).
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. In-school applicants need income under the program limits plus a barrier; the page's out-of-school barrier list is broader.

name: National Park Service Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
city: Participating national parks (see the NPS park list)
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 season open in late January or early February 2027. Closing dates are set by each park and are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.

name: ACE Mentor Program of Greater New York
org: ACE Mentor Program of Greater NY
city: Teams in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island, White Plains and Riverdale (and remote)
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned. Scholarship and internship chances are listed as benefits.
duration: Late October through May (about 2 hours after school per meeting). Some teams start in January.
deadline_text: The page says most teams begin meeting late October 2026, with a few starting in January 2027. Team selection emails start in September and teams fill first come, first served. The page gives no registration close date and does not say whether registration is open now.
who_can_apply: Any high school student in grades 9 to 12. No experience is needed. No grades, essays or recommendation letters are needed. A parent consent form is needed.
how_to_apply: Register on the ACE GNY website. Use the yellow button on the students page. Get a parent to sign a consent form. Pick a team from the map you get by email. Then wait for a confirmation email.
notes: Teams meet at host firms or universities. The page also links to a Summer Internship Program for alumni, which this card does not cover.

name: Science Alliance High School Program
pay_detail: Each fall, winter, or spring course costs $1,000. Half of the seats in each class are held for families who ask for free or reduced tuition, based on household income. These seats go first come, first served.
duration: Three sessions a year (fall, winter, spring). Classes meet Tuesdays and/or Thursdays, 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. Winter 2027 genetics: January 7 to March 4, Tuesdays and Thursdays.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 sales opened October 8, 2026. Winter 2027 genetics runs January 7 to March 4, 2027. The page does not say when winter sign up opens or closes.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Sign up for the class that matches your grade band.
how_to_apply: Buy a seat with the purchase button on the course listing, or call Central Reservations at 212-769-5200. For free or reduced tuition, do not pay online: fill out the Tuition Assistance application instead.
notes: Free tuition goes to a family of 4 with income of $124,240 or less (see the page for other sizes). Taking Science Alliance also counts toward the Museum's SCIP and SRMP rules. Questions: ScienceAlliance@amnh.org.

name: Science Communication Internship Program (SCIP)
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend when you finish the program requirements.
duration: Six weeks, July 6 to August 14 in 2026, Monday to Friday, 25 hours a week (10 a.m. to 3 p.m. or noon to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: New York City high school students in 10th grade who have passed all classes for at least the last 3 terms. You must also have done an AMNH youth program, or a program at a SciNetworkNYC place (such as the Bronx Zoo, New York Botanical Garden, New York Hall of Science, or Wave Hill), or go to a partner school or group on the list. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Apply with the online form linked from the SCIP page when the next round opens.
notes: The page lists the partner schools and groups by name; check it to see if yours is there. You also join career readiness events and Museum events.

name: Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP)
pay_detail: $2,500 stipend when you finish the research and program requirements. You can also earn 1 CUNY Lehman College credit at no cost.
duration: One year, August to June: a 4-week Summer Institute in August, then about 4 hours a week after school (Tuesdays and Thursdays) plus 1 or 2 Fridays a month.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Class of 2028 are expected to open in Winter 2027. Interviews are in April and decisions come by the end of May.
who_can_apply: You must live and go to school in New York City and be in 10th or 11th grade. You must have passed your classes for the last three or more terms. You also must have taken an AMNH course, or go to one of the partner schools or groups on the list. You do not need to be a U.S. citizen.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and answer short questions. They ask why you like science, how you work on a team, and how you will make time. No report card or letters are needed. Some people get an interview.
notes: The FAQ says you do not need working papers. SRMP is meant to be your main after-school activity for the year. Join the program's email list on the Join SRMP page to hear when the application opens. Questions: srmp@amnh.org.

name: Arts & Entertainment Production Internship (Apollo Theater Academy)
pay_detail: $17.00 per hour
duration: The 2026 internship ran Apr 21 to May 21, 2026, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 3 to 6 PM. The page calls it six weeks in one place and eight or ten weeks in others.
deadline_text: The spring 2026 application closed Friday, Mar 27, 2026. The next cycle is not posted. Check the Apollo page for the next cycle.
who_can_apply: High school seniors (12th grade) who live in one of the five boroughs. You must send a current transcript or report card that shows 12th grade.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)

name: Genesys Works New York City Young Professionals
city: New York, NY (office at 55 Exchange Place)

Use the main Apply Now button or email info.nyc@genesysworks.org. Many schools give credit for the training and internship.

name: Teen Intern Program

notes: Because there is a stipend, ask the museum about working papers for under 18. The page does not say. Check the museum site for the next call.

name: Upward Bound at John Jay College

how_to_apply: Ask the program for the forms by email. You need the application and the recommendation forms. The Eligibility and Selection page lists who to write to: the Program Director or the Curriculum Coordinator. The form asks about you and your money. It also asks for a personal statement.

name: Chemical Engineering Summer Program

notes: The page says to register early because the program has hit its limit in past years. Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it. The prices on the page are the 2026 prices.

Confirm the steps with the director.

name: The Met High School Internship Program in Museum Education (Spring)

pay_detail: $1,100 stipend when you finish, which the page says matches New York State minimum wage law.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and write short essays. Ask one adult who is not family for a letter. If they pick you, you go to a group interview in person.

grades: 10th or 11th grade, or working on a High School Equivalency
pay_detail: $1,100 stipend when you finish, which the page says matches New York State minimum wage law.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and write short essays. Ask one adult who is not family for a letter. If they pick you, you go to a group interview in person.
notes: You must come to every date on the list. A parent or guardian must come to the party in June. The Met also has a spring internship for New York City students. Connecticut is not a place on this site yet, but students there can apply.

name: Junior Volunteer Program, Northwell Manhattan Campus (Lenox Hill Hospital)

deadline_text: Four sessions a year. Applications are due Mar 1 (spring), Jun 1 (summer), Sep 1 (fall) and Dec 1 (winter). The page says applications are session-based, not rolling, and late applications are considered for the next session. The page gives the month and day but no year.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 at the Manhattan hospitals. Junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) hand in working papers and a parent consent form. All applicants are interviewed, then there is a six-month trial period.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Lenox Hill volunteer page. There is an interview. There is a required orientation. You also need a medical clearance. Questions? Write to manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page says junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) must submit working papers and a parental consent form. Orientation and medical clearance are required. Volunteers 18 and older must pass a background screening. The page asks for 100 hours a year. The page gives a minimum age of 16 and no maximum age.

pay_detail: Intern tier is unpaid volunteering (OMNY card help for transit can be provided). Later tiers (Advanced Explainer, Mentor, Senior) are paid part-time jobs; the page gives no hourly rate.

who_can_apply: Explainers are high school students. The page does not state a grade or age range. Interns work one weekend shift a week.

The orientation date printed on the page shows the wrong year, so confirm it with NYBG. Late applications roll to the next session.

name: Summer Only Volunteering

Med-career internships and research are handled separately through HRNTV@NYULangone.org. The Manhattan page and the volunteer page do not mention working papers, so the work permit answer is unknown.

grades: Current 10th graders in New York City
pay_detail: Fellows do paid summer internships or enrichment programs (five summers over the six years). The page does not state the pay.
duration: Six years. Starts with the OppNet Summer Institute (length not stated on the page), then weekly after-school workshops in 11th and 12th grade.
deadline_text: The page says the last application is closed and the next one re-opens in Fall 2026. The page lists the usual due date as early February for current NYC 10th graders. The 2027 date is not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade at a New York City high school. You show strong effort in school. Most Fellows apply with a GPA of 87 or above. You come from an under-resourced community. Your household income (AGI) is under $125,000. You should not already have similar college and career help. You must commit to the whole program.
how_to_apply: Sign the interest form on the Apply page to get an email when the application opens. The online application takes a couple of hours. It needs your transcript, family facts and two recommendation forms. One is from a teacher. One is from a counselor or advisor. Chosen applicants are invited to group interviews. The page puts these in late March.
notes: Admitted Fellows must come to all days of the Summer Institute. A family member must come to an orientation. The application asks for household income. The program uses it to check the income limit. The pages do not say if a work permit is needed.

name: College Access Program (CAP)
pay_detail: Free to join. The page does not say whether the internships are paid.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Register on PAL's website.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who attend PAL Teen Centers.
how_to_apply: Register through the link on PAL's Teen Programs page.
notes: CAP meets at PAL's Webster Center in the Bronx. It is built for teens who would be the first in their family to go to college. PAL Teen Centers, for teens 13 to 19, are free and open 3 to 5 evenings a week.

name: NYC Parks Lifeguard Program
org: NYC Department of Parks and Recreation
city: New York City (pools and beaches in all five boroughs, including Manhattan and the Bronx)
pay_detail: $22 per hour for lifeguards who finish training and get a post. Lifeguards also get a $908 training payment after the summer season.
duration: Training course of 16 sessions, then the summer season. Beaches open Memorial Day weekend and outdoor pools open in late June. Both close the Sunday after Labor Day. You work five or six days a week.
deadline_text: No test dates are open for registration right now. The page says qualifying tests run from late October through late February in all five boroughs. Sign up on the Parks site to get a notice when dates open.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older by the first day of work. The test page said 16 by July 18, 2026. You must swim 50 yards and meet the vision rule.
how_to_apply: Register for a qualifying test on the Parks page when dates open (or join the notice list). Pass the swim and vision test, then do the training. A letter from an eye doctor can replace the on-site vision exam.
notes: The two Parks pages disagree on the swim time. The main page says 50 yards in 50 seconds or less. The test page says 50 yards in 40 seconds or less with proper form. Plan for the faster one. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: NYC P-TECH Early College and Career High Schools
city: New York City (schools in Manhattan and the Bronx include Inwood Early College, MECA, EChem and H.E.R.O. High)
pay_detail: The degree is free: courses, materials and college textbooks cost nothing. Internships are listed as a possible part of work-based learning; pay is not stated.
duration: Six years or less (grades 9 to 14)
deadline_text: The page gives no application dates. You apply through the regular NYC high school admissions process (MySchools). Check the MySchools site for the dates.
who_can_apply: Students entering high school in New York City. The program starts with career exploration in 9th grade, and college courses can begin as early as 10th grade. The page does not list entry rules for each school.
how_to_apply: The page says admission is unscreened (Educational Option method). Attend an information session, open house or high school fair, then rank a P-TECH school as a top choice on your high school application. Check each school's process on its website or at MySchools.nyc.
notes: This is a school choice made before 9th grade, so it fits 8th graders and their families. The page names five schools in Manhattan and the Bronx. Examples are Inwood Early College for Health and Information Technologies and Urban Assembly New York Harbor School. Check each listing to see how students get in.

name: Borough and Chancellor's Student Advisory Councils
city: New York City (one council for each borough, including Manhattan and the Bronx)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is listed.
duration: Borough councils meet monthly. The Chancellor's council meets monthly from October through June at the central office.
deadline_text: The page says members are often elected at the borough council meetings. No election or application dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who are seen as leaders at school, often through student government. Members are voted in at the borough meetings. Each year, two student reps are voted onto the Panel for Educational Policy.
how_to_apply: There is no open form on the page. Ask your school counselor or student government adviser how students are chosen for the borough council. Elections for the Chancellor's council happen at the borough meetings.
notes: There are six borough councils: one in each borough, with two in Brooklyn. The page does not list contacts or meeting dates. It is a leadership role, not a job.

name: Field Biology Internship (FBI)
city: Douglaston, Queens, NY (Alley Pond Park and other Queens sites)
pay_detail: $200 fee after you are accepted. Financial aid is available on request and needs no paperwork.
duration: 6 sessions of 3 hours per season (9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.). Spring 2027: Saturdays Mar 27 to May 8. Summer 2027: Tuesdays or Wednesdays, July 6 to Aug 11. Fall 2027: Saturdays Sept 18 to Oct 23.
deadline_text: Deadlines: Fall by Aug 1, Spring by Jan 2, Summer by May 1. The next one is for Spring 2027, due Jan 2, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students at least 14 and now in high school. You can be outdoors for 2 hours. You have your own ride to the site. You pass an interview. You come to 5 of 6 classes.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the internship page, then do a virtual interview. Contact: Erica Chow (email on the page).
notes: This is a learning internship, not a job, and it costs $200 unless you get aid. You must find your own transportation. Supported by Con Edison and other funders per the page. The page says 5 of 6 classes in its eligibility section but 6 out of 7 dates for spring and fall, so ask which applies.

name: Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you can earn school credit or work experience.
duration: One of three semesters. Fall and spring: one day a week after school. Summer: up to 3 days a week for 6 weeks in July and August, plus a late June orientation.
deadline_text: Deadlines: Fall by Aug 1, Spring by Dec 1, Summer by May 1. The next one is for spring, due Dec 1.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17. You must attend an interview and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer form on the volunteer page. Return it to the volunteer coordinator before the deadline. Then you have an interview and an orientation.
notes: The page lists deadline months, not the year. Popular program, so apply early.

name: Certified Junior Gardener Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid and free. No admission fee. You earn a certificate if you attend at least 13 of 16 sessions.
duration: 9 months of select Sundays, 1 to 3 p.m. 2026-27 dates: Oct 11 through June 6, 2027. Certification ceremony June 20.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed Oct 3, 2026 (acceptances Oct 6, 2026). An open house was held Sept 27. The next call is not posted.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. Only the student should fill out the application, not a parent.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the form on the page. Applications only, no walk-ins.
notes: Popular program with an acceptance step and a waitlist. Mostly outdoors, weather permitting. The museum is the Queens County Farm Museum.

name: Junior Volunteer Program
org: Flushing Hospital Medical Center (MediSys Health Network)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: Commit to 125 hours of service. Onboarding usually takes several weeks.
deadline_text: The page does not say whether applications are rolling or have deadlines. Call to schedule an interview.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Junior volunteers cannot serve on weekends or late evenings.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 718-670-5952 to book an in-person interview. No walk-ins. Bring a valid ID (state, school or passport), a working permit and one professional letter of recommendation. Then you need medical clearance (doctor form, urine drug screen, flu shot). You also go to a 4-hour orientation.
notes: The hospital lists a "Working Permit" as a requirement for junior volunteers. This may mean New York working papers. Ask the Volunteer Services office which work permit paper they accept. The page says volunteering does not guarantee a job. Hospital address: 4500 Parsons Blvd, Flushing.

name: Queens Teens Institute for Art and Social Justice (QTI)
city: Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens, NY
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend for the 9-month commitment, plus extra money for travel. QTI teens can also be considered for other paid Queens Museum jobs like workshop assistant and camp counselor.
duration: 9 months of weekly hybrid sessions (in person and online). No more than 4 absences. Start and end dates are not stated.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are open. Deadline: Oct 25, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.
who_can_apply: Teens, with a focus on BIPOC and other under-served Queens youth. The page does not list exact ages, grades or home address rules, so ask the museum.
how_to_apply: Send in the QTI 2026-27 form through the Submittable link on the Queens Museum announcement. Phone 718-592-9700. Email info@queensmuseum.org.
notes: This is the fifth year of the program. Ages, grades and work-permit rules are not stated on the announcement, so ask the museum.

name: Explainer (Science Career Ladder)
pay_detail: The page calls it an education and youth employment program and says you "work" at NYSCI. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: One full year, including the summer. High school students work at least 5 hours a week (weekends). You must attend every day of orientation first.
deadline_text: Hiring rounds in spring, summer and fall. The page lists open application periods of April 1 to May 1 and December 1 to January 2, No year is given; the next window is expected Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 2, 2027. Fall 2026 hiring is closed.
who_can_apply: New York City residents who are currently in high school or college in New York City. You do not need to love science. NYSCI wants curious students who will try new things and practice public speaking.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the page). You can also fill out an interest form to get a reminder and an invite to an info session. Questions: ebautista@nysci.org (listed on the page).
notes: NYSCI is at 47-01 111th St., Corona, Queens. The youth page lists "Young Adults, Age 14-24" in the site menu; the Explainer page itself does not state a minimum age, so confirm. The apply form link on the page showed as closed when read. Pay rate not stated. Work permit not stated on the page.

name: Summer High School Scholars Program
city: Queens, NY (St. John's Queens campus, or online)
pay_detail: $1,000 per course, due July 1 (2026 price). Students who later enroll at St. John's get a $2,000 High School Scholars Grant, renewable for up to four years.
duration: About 5 weeks. In 2026, July 7 to August 10, classes Monday to Thursday for 2 hours.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed Friday, June 19, 2026. Dates for summer 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors with a cumulative average of 92 (no test scores needed), or an average of 90 plus an SAT of 1210 or an ACT of 25. An interview may be required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with a parent consent form and an unofficial transcript. A counselor recommendation form and the official transcript come next. Contact: 718-990-7533. The number is on the page.
notes: Costs money and is for strong students. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates and price.

name: Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
grades: Current high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: Free to apply and attend. An OMNY card covers NYC transit. Stipends are not guaranteed; need-based stipends may go to students with financial hardship who meet all attendance rules.
duration: 7 weeks, Mon Jun 21 to Thu Aug 5, 2027, full time (about 35 hours a week, roughly 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: Applications for SSRP 2027 are open. Deadline: Monday, January 4, 2027 at 5:00 p.m. Eastern. Late applications will not be considered.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors or seniors who are at least 16 when the program starts. Students from outside NYC and outside the Tri-State area may apply but get no help with housing or travel. No GPA minimum. Sophomores are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You also need a letter of recommendation and a transcript (to show you are in high school). Selected applicants get a Zoom interview.
notes: Very competitive (about 32 students a year). You must attend the entire program with no gaps. Minors cannot work with human patients. You may not use SSRP work in science competitions. Contact: program administrator listed on the page, 1230 York Ave.

name: Leadership Scholars
city: New York City (all five boroughs) and Newark, NJ
pay_detail: Up to $400 at the end of the semester, based on participation.
duration: Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., November to May, in person at the New York City or Newark office.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 to 2027 were due Oct 16, 2026. Next dates are not posted. Join the email list on the apply page.
who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in 10th or 11th grade who live in New York City or Newark and can come in person once a week. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online from the Leadership Scholars page. Questions: charlie@sadienash.org.
notes: Office: 247 W 37th St, Suite 705, New York, NY. Next round not posted.

name: Nash U Leadership Internship
city: New York City (all five boroughs) and Newark, NJ
pay_detail: Eligible for a $400 stipend at the end of the internship.
duration: Saturdays 10 a.m. to 12 noon, November 2026 to May 2027, plus some events.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 to 2027 were due Oct 16, 2026. Next dates are not posted. Join the email list on the apply page.
who_can_apply: High school seniors who are women or gender-expansive youth of color and live in New York City or Newark. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online from the Nash U page. Questions: charlie@sadienash.org.
notes: You must commit to the full internship. Next round not posted.

name: Siblinghood Academy
city: New York City (all five boroughs) and Newark, NJ
pay_detail: In-person: up to $400 at the end. Virtual: up to $150 (you must attend 9 of 10 sessions). Referral bonus of $25 per friend.
duration: In person: once a week, Tuesdays or Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., November to May. Virtual: 10 weeks, offered each fall and spring.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 to 2027 were due Oct 16, 2026. Next dates are not posted. Join the email list on the apply page.
who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in grades 9 to 12 who live in New York City or Newark. You commit for the whole program. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online from the program page. Questions: cielito@sadienash.org.
notes: No more than 5 absences in person. Next round not posted.

name: Summer Institute
city: New York City (all five boroughs) and Newark, NJ
pay_detail: Eligible for a $450 stipend at the end of the summer, based on participation.
duration: 6 weeks. In 2026: July 6 to Aug 13, Monday to Thursday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at sites in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Newark.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed. Its deadline was March 13, 2026, with group interviews April 7 to 11 in NYC. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth enrolled in high school who live in New York City or Newark and have not done Summer Institute before. No grade or skill rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Apply Now page when the cycle opens, then join a group interview. Sign up for the opportunities email list to hear when it opens. Questions: nashers@sadienash.org.
notes: For young women and gender-expansive youth. The Brooklyn, Queens and other borough sites are part of the same program.

name: Metro New York Urban Green
pay_detail: Paid. The page does not state the rate for teen crews.
duration: School year and summer programs. Length varies by crew.
deadline_text: No teen crew openings were posted when checked in October 2026. The only openings listed were 2026 Stamford crews for ages 18 and up.
who_can_apply: High school students and recent grads ages 14 to 19 in the New York City, New Jersey and Connecticut area. Not everyone gets in.
how_to_apply: Watch the Current Opportunities list on the program page and apply through its Learn More and Apply links. You can also contact the Metro NY Region office.
notes: Contact: Pablo Galesi, (347) 200-4709, pgalesi@thesca.org. In New York, teens 14 to 17 need working papers to work.

name: High School Apprenticeships (Open Village Season)
grades: 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders can start in the fall)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. The page calls it a service learning experience.
duration: July and August, up to 3 days a week, Wednesday to Sunday, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: The interest form opens each March. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 18 in grades 9 to 12. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Apprenticeships page when it opens each March.
notes: Pay is not stated, so ask whether it is paid and whether working papers are needed. The site says the program has run for decades.

name: Afterschool Medical Science Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.
duration: Six weeks, one day per week after school.
deadline_text: No session dates or deadline are posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Staten Island high school students in grades 11 and 12, per the program page.
how_to_apply: Download the application. It is a PDF on the program page. Email the finished form to the program email on the page: Medicalscienceprogram@rumcsi.org.
notes: Session dates, start month and cost are not stated, so call or email to confirm before you plan. The general volunteer page says its openings are filled right now. It states no age rule. The application email could not be read in this check, so confirm it.

name: Wagner College High School Internship Program
org: Wagner College, Department for Lifelong Learning
pay_detail: No pay or fee is mentioned. You get community service hours and a certificate of completion from Wagner College.
duration: The fall session runs Oct 2 to Dec 12 (year not stated), on Fridays 5:30 to 8 p.m. or Saturdays 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. (hours depend on class).
deadline_text: No application deadline is listed. The page gives the fall session as Oct 2 to Dec 12 (year not stated). Spring dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Send the application form, a one-page essay (500 words max) about your goals, and a parent or guardian signature. You can apply online, by mail or by email. Contact: lifelong-learning@wagner.edu, 718-390-3221.
notes: Ask the office whether spring 2027 spots are open and whether the internship is paid.

name: Junior Docent Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: 10-week training course, then ongoing docent shifts.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026 Docent Class closed Friday, Sept 18, 2026. The next class dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens 14 years old and older who are in high school. Adults over 18 join the regular Docent program.
how_to_apply: Use the Docent application form linked on the zoo volunteer and job page. Candidates must pass the 10-week course. Volunteers go through a background check.
notes: The 2026 class deadline had passed as of 2026-10-09. Check the page around late summer for the next class. Teens learn public speaking and animal presentation skills.

name: Teen Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.
duration: Minimum 3 months, can be extended. Regular availability needed.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Placement depends on availability.
who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 years old. You must be able to work on your own and on a team and be available on a regular basis. Some roles (like animal diet prep) are adults only.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer application form linked on the zoo volunteer page. All volunteers go through a background check. The zoo cannot give status updates. It only contacts qualified candidates.
notes: Limited spaces. Volunteers in animal care jobs must show a negative TB test and proof of COVID-19 vaccination, per the page.

name: Expanding the Walls
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend paid at the end of the program, a Canon DSLR camera, and transportation fare to and from the museum. The page says this is not a job or an internship.
duration: Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Tuesdays 4:00 to 6:30 PM and Saturdays 11 AM to 3 PM, then Tuesday to Thursday 11 AM to 3 PM in the summer.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 program are open. The deadline is Nov 6, 2026 at 11:59 PM.
who_can_apply: High school-aged youth. No photography experience needed. To get the stipend you must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or otherwise eligible to work in the U.S., and show valid working papers when accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link on the Expanding the Walls page) by Nov 6, 2026. Show valid working papers when you are accepted. Questions: use the contact email on the page.
notes: Meets at 144 W 125th Street. The FAQ on the page still shows the 2026 dates in one spot; the headline dates for 2027 are Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Public school holidays are observed. The page does not state an age range or whether you must live in NYC.

name: The Door free youth membership (jobs, school, health, housing help)
pay_detail: Joining is free. Pay is not stated on this page. A separate program, The CUT Culinary Training, lists a stipend (see its card).
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time.
who_can_apply: Anyone ages 12 to 24. No documents are needed. Some programs have their own age rules.
how_to_apply: Go to 555 Broome Street, Manhattan, Monday to Friday 2:00 to 5:30 pm (extra hours 10:00 am to 2:00 pm for urgent needs and for youth without stable housing). Or call 212-941-9090 or email membership@door.org.
notes: The Door also has a Bronx drop-in center for runaway and homeless youth. Ask staff for details, because ages for it are not stated. Some job training programs have their own age rules, so ask staff.

name: The CUT Culinary training at The Door (ages 17 to 24)
pay_detail: Stipend of up to $3,100 over 150 hours
duration: 12 weeks
deadline_text: Start dates are not posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. All Door job programs need free Door membership first.
how_to_apply: Become a Door member (free), then contact Latasha Stephens at Lstephens@door.org or 917-696-3758.
notes: Other Door job programs have other age rules, such as 18 to 24 for several of them. Call first to ask about the next start date.

name: Youth Activist Committee
city: New York City (citywide, meets in person and online)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer activism. No cost is listed.

notes: The page describes youth activism and does not mention a work permit. The page lists meetings on the last Friday of each month from 4:30 to 6 PM, and says meetings are hybrid. Confirm before you go.

name: NYC Votes Youth Ambassador Program
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. Ask the program.
duration: Weekly meetings, with weekly summer trips. The full length of the program is not stated.
deadline_text: The Youth page says applications for 2026 are now closed. No 2027 dates are posted.

how_to_apply: Check the NYC Votes Youth Ambassadors page for the next call for applications.
notes: Run by the City of New York Campaign Finance Board. Past ambassadors registered voters at public events and with other city agencies. The pages do not say whether the work is paid or needs a work permit.

name: Art, Community, Education and Science (ACES) Internship
pay_detail: $17 per hour
duration: 13 months, about 4 to 8 hours each weekend (14 at most), plus two Saturday workshops a month and July weekday training
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back next winter for 2027 internships. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, eligible to work in the United States. You must be free on weekends and for the full 13 months (June to June). The 2026 page said June 2026 to June 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen. Watch the ACES page for news. If you have questions, write to education@wavehill.org or youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Wave Hill House, where this program meets, is wheelchair accessible. Interns travel off site for some field trips.

name: Forest Project
pay_detail: About $2,275 for the summer, paid through the NYC Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP). You also get credit for one college course.
duration: One summer (exact weeks not stated on the page)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back next winter for 2027 internships. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 16 years old by May 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for May 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the Forest Project page). Pay runs through SYEP, so you also need a separate SYEP application; for 2026 that was due before March 1. Wave Hill tells interviewed teens which SYEP provider to pick. Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Fieldwork is hard physical work outdoors with heavy tools on unpaved ground. The Ecology Building has 28 stairs and is not wheelchair accessible. You must be ready to join all of the program.

name: Woodland Ecology Research Mentorship (WERM)
pay_detail: About $3,500 paid across the whole program, plus credit for three college courses.
duration: 14 months: first summer (July to August), school year (September to June), second summer (July to August)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back next winter for 2027 internships. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for July 1, 2026. You must be free for all 14 months.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the WERM page). Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Courses are taught at Wave Hill and the University of Mount Saint Vincent. Fieldwork is outdoors on rough ground with heavy tools. The Ecology Building is not open to wheelchairs. The page names partners such as the American Museum of Natural History.

name: Discovery Guide Youth Volunteer Program
org: Wildlife Conservation Society (Bronx Zoo, Central Park, Prospect Park and Queens Zoos, New York Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
deadline_text: Not accepting applications now. Applications for the next cycle open in late December 2026 for Spring 2027. No closing date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.

name: Youth Insights (YI Artists, Arts Careers, Introductions, Leaders)
grades: 9 to 12 (varies by program; YI Leaders is grades 11 and 12)
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.

org: NYC Council initiative, run by youth groups such as the Police Athletic League and Henry Street Settlement
pay_detail: Paid employment. The pages do not state a rate.
duration: Up to 25 weeks between October and April (PAL). Henry Street says its program runs November to March.

name: Ohio FFA membership through your school chapter
