pay_detail: $17 per member covers State and National FFA dues. The school is invoiced by Ohio FFA. Local chapter dues are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Next date: Nov 30, 2026, for all chapters. The September 30, 2026 date for students in Fall CDEs has passed. Membership opens each August through FFA.org.
who_can_apply: Students at schools with an Ohio FFA chapter. The membership page does not list grades or ages. Ask your chapter advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's FFA chapter advisor to add you. Chapters submit membership through FFA.org. Schools with no program can contact Ohio FFA about starting a chapter.
notes: Not a job. The homepage reports 30,880 members in 345 chapters. State office phone is (614) 387-7575. The September 30 and November 30 dates are chapter deadlines, so a student should ask the advisor early.

name: STEM Summer Camps (Ohio State Marion)
org: The Ohio State University at Marion
grades: Rising 9th to 12th graders (for the two high school camps)
pay_detail: $185 per camp, which includes lunch and lab costs (2026 price).
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 camps ran June 22 to 26, 2026 and registration closed May 31, 2026 or earlier if full. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders in any United States school can sign up for Science Adventurers or Horizons of Science. A third camp is for rising 5th to 8th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application and payment for each camp (separate forms on the page). Questions go to Tiffiny Rye-McCurdy at rye-mccurdy.1@osu.edu.
notes: This is at the Ohio State Marion campus, not in Columbus. The page mentions no housing or rides, so plan your own.

name: Ohio State Fair Junior Fair Board
org: Ohio Expo Center, Ohio State Fair
pay_detail: Flat-rate stipend, higher in the second year. The amount is not stated. Housing and meals are provided in dorms at the fair.
duration: About 2 weeks (arrive the Monday before the Wednesday opening)
deadline_text: The page says the online application portal opens January 1 and the application is due March 1 ((year inferred from the next cycle)). Notices come early to mid March, interviews mid to late March, selection early April. Confirm the 2027 dates in January.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 20 who are now in a youth or career tech group. Examples are 4-H, FFA, DECA, Girl Scouts, Scouting America and Key Club. You need strong leadership and a record of being involved. Members serve one two-year term.
how_to_apply: Send the official Junior Fair Board application in the online portal on the Ohio State Fair page. Do it between January 1 and March 1. Interviews come next. Send questions to the co-coordinators listed on the page.
notes: The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for minors. Ask the coordinators.

name: Teen Volunteer Program at The Wilds
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: At least 40 hours through the summer
deadline_text: No deadline or dates are posted on the volunteer page. The visitor season runs May through October for adult volunteers.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 through 17 who like animals and nature and enjoy talking with visitors. The page asks for at least 40 hours of volunteer service over the summer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button under Teen Volunteers on the volunteer page. It is an online form.
notes: The page says nothing about housing or rides.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Ohio Wing
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the page. Payment options are on the last page of the application.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the unit locator. Visit with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ohio Wing office: 6031 E Main Street, PO Box 301, Columbus, OH 43213, phone 614-338-8198.

name: Ohio Youth & Government (YMCA model government)
org: Ohio Alliance of YMCAs, Ohio Youth & Government
city: Columbus, OH (State Assembly), delegations across Ohio
pay_detail: Registration fee amount is not stated on the program pages. A $25 late fee applied last year. Financial aid pages exist for middle and high school.
duration: Fall prep, then a 3-day State Assembly in spring
deadline_text: Last cycle: State Assembly February 12 to 14, 2026 at the Hyatt Regency Columbus. Registration closed November 28, 2025, with late registration December 1 to 10, 2025. 2027 dates are not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Middle school (6th to 8th) and high school (9th to 12th) students. You join through a local delegation run by a school or YMCA.
how_to_apply: Join or start a delegation at your school or YMCA in the fall. New delegations can email yg@ohioymcas.org or call (614) 407-4819. Students and advisors register on the State Assembly registration page.
notes: Not a job. The registration page still showed the 2026 assembly dates, so check it for the 2027 dates.

name: GRuB Summer Youth Program
pay_detail: Up to $1,000 educational stipend award, plus fresh farm food most weeks.
duration: About 8 weeks, Tue and Thu 9 AM to 1 PM, Wed 11 AM to 5 PM (2026: July 7 to Aug 27)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are full and closed. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 19 during the program. You must be able to attend the whole season.
how_to_apply: Check the program page for the next application. Email dusty@goodgrub.org or call 360-753-5522.
notes: The farm is at 2016 Elliott Ave NW, Olympia. GRuB also runs other programs for teens and young adults, including GroundED for youth working on a GED.

name: Teen Connection Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. The application says services are donated and there is no payment.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: Application form is on the site now. No deadline stated. The hospital says the most need is Monday through Friday in business hours, with few evening or weekend spots.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 pick the Teen Connection type on the application. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application form. Choose Teen Connection. For questions call Children's Nebraska. Use the phone number on the volunteer page.
notes: The application form asks for a Social Security number, a date of birth and an emergency contact. The same page also lists KIDS Nebraska. It is for young people ages 13 to 18 in Nebraska and western Iowa. No prior medical experience is needed.

name: Haddix STEM Corridor Program
org: Creighton University College of Arts and Sciences
pay_detail: Students can earn up to $4,800 for the hours they work.
duration: 8 weeks
deadline_text: The Summer 2026 application is closed. The program page does not post next year's dates.
who_can_apply: Current juniors at Omaha North, Omaha Central or Omaha South high school. You must be 16 or older by the start of the program. There are no exceptions. You need your own place to stay and a ride each day. You must go to every activity.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. A STEM teacher and a school counselor must also send in a review by the deadline.
notes: Only three Omaha high schools can apply. The poster session is typically held in early August. Start and end dates are Not stated on the program page.

name: Douglas-Sarpy 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Enrollment fee is $10 per youth per year.
duration: The 4-H year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30.
deadline_text: Join any time. To show projects at the Sarpy County Fair or the Nebraska State Fair, enroll by June 15.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18. Age is counted on January 1 of the 4-H year. You must be 8 by then for competitive events, large animal, shooting sports or food preservation projects.
how_to_apply: Join an existing club or start a new one. Then enroll online in 4HOnline. Call 402-444-7804 if you need help finding a club.
notes: A new club needs one trained 4-H volunteer and five youth from three different families. The page says enrollment in 4HOnline begins October 17. Clubs must meet at least six times per year.

name: The Durham Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include a 25 percent museum shop discount and a 25 percent soda fountain discount on days you volunteer.
duration: You must meet a minimum number of hours each year (the number is not stated on the program page)
deadline_text: The page lists no deadline. Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form to start.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older, unless an adult comes with you. Some jobs need you to be 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form. Then you finish an application, an interview and training. This includes a background check.
notes: Quote from the page: Must be 16 years of age, unless accompanied by an adult. Check which roles are open to teens under 18.

name: Jr Crew (grades 7 and 8 volunteers)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page
duration: Summer season. Exact length not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 Jr Crew season open on January 5, 2027. Close date not stated.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 and 8.
how_to_apply: Come back to the page on January 5, 2027 for application details.
notes: The 2026 Jr Crew program has concluded. Zoo Crew is for grades 9 to 12.

name: Kent Bellows Mentoring Program (KBMP)
grades: Core program: mostly juniors and seniors. Foundations: freshmen and sophomores.
pay_detail: Pay-as-you-are-able tuition of $1 to $600 per trimester. Supplies are provided.
duration: Twice a week: 4 to 6 pm in the school year, 3 to 6 pm in summer
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round. Interviews are in March, and most new mentees start in the summer session.
who_can_apply: High school students who love art and are committed to their education. Priority goes to students from schools not yet in the program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the program page. Staff interview applicants (mostly in March).
notes: Core program meets at Kent Bellows Studio, 3303 Leavenworth Street. Foundations meets at the Joslyn. The page also lists a Teen Pop-Up Market hosted by teens and an open call for youth ages 13 to 19.

name: Methodist Volunteen
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free cafeteria meal on the day they volunteer.
duration: At least 1 year
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page. There may be a waiting list because many teens apply.
who_can_apply: Incoming and current high school students in the Omaha metro area. You must commit to at least 1 year of service.
how_to_apply: Print the Volunteen form from the page and fill it out. Send it to the Volunteer Office.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the program page. The free meal on the page is listed under VIP perks. The page does not say it applies to Volunteens. Methodist Hospital and Methodist Women's Hospital may both have waiting lists.

name: Nebraska Medicine Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Initial six-month commitment, 2 to 4 hours a week
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply online any time.
who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who can commit to six months and 2 to 4 hours a week and finish orientation.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Volunteer Services reviews it. They call you for a welcome meeting. You talk about what you like and when you can come. Then finish New Volunteer Orientation and onboarding.
notes: Quote from the page: Be at least 16 years old.

name: Omaha Public Library Volunteer (youth ages 11 to 18)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library says it can provide volunteer hours for court-related community service.
duration: Short-term or ongoing, depending on the task
deadline_text: Applications are accepted all year.
who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 or older. Youth ages 11 to 18 need a parent or legal guardian to approve. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. There is one form for Central Library and another for all other branches. Youth and summer reading volunteers need a parent or guardian signature before starting.
notes: The library says it may not be able to place each applicant. It has the right to reject any application without reason. It reserves the right to do a background check or check references. Quote from the volunteer policy: OPL accepts volunteers ages 11 and older. The Central Library has its own volunteer form. It is linked on the volunteer page.

name: OPS Career Center Pathways
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The application opens December 1 and closes March 1. Late additions are taken until April 30. The program page does not give a year.
who_can_apply: Omaha Public Schools sophomores, juniors and seniors who are on track to graduate. CNA students must be 16 by May of that year. EMT students must be seniors.
how_to_apply: Apply with your 6-digit student ID. The application is shared by QR code and email. Have your GPA, counselor name and email, top 2 pathways, and a list of activities and volunteer work ready.
notes: Only for OPS students. The page says the district provides bus transportation. The Career Center is at 3230 Burt Street, Omaha.

name: Step-Up Omaha
pay_detail: Interns can earn $1,800 to $3,000 or more during the summer (2026 news release).
duration: 2026 program ran June 2 through July 31
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed March 16, 2026 (extended from an earlier date). 2027 dates not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 21. The program page does not list city or school rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at StepUpOmaha.com. The news release says to apply there.
notes: This card uses the March 2026 news release on the organizer's site. Check StepUpOmaha.com for 2027 dates. The release says roughly 100 employers took part in 2025.

name: UNMC High School Alliance
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Students get three polo shirts and a jacket free and buy their own black pants, socks and closed-toe shoes.
duration: Whole school year, August to May
deadline_text: The application page is titled for the 2026-2027 year. An open or close date is not stated on the program pages.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors who are at least 16 at the start of the school year. Your school district must take part (districts around Omaha). You need grades of B or above in Algebra 1, Biology, a physical science and a third year of science. You also need parent permission and an interview.
how_to_apply: Check that you meet the criteria and that your school district takes part. Review the forms. Then apply online. Eligible students are scheduled for an interview. Then they are notified by email.
notes: The page says there are only 65 spots a year. Just one-third of applicants are accepted. Participating public school districts include Omaha, Millard, Bellevue, Elkhorn and Westside. They also include Council Bluffs Community Schools, Gretna, Bennington, Ralston and others. If you do not qualify, ask your teacher about uBEATS. It is an online alternative. Questions: 402-559-3027.

name: Munroe-Meyer Institute Recreational Therapy Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Opportunities are year-round. Camp Munroe runs in quarterly cycles: spring, summer, fall and winter.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Contact the volunteer coordinator for current openings.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 26 can help with Pediatric Programs. Students 16 and older can also help with Adult Programs.
how_to_apply: Email the volunteer coordinator. Their name is on the page. Then finish the required training.
notes: Training is on behavior and disability. It is on play and safety too. The institute also lists job shadowing for high school students.

name: UNO Summer Scholars
org: University of Nebraska Omaha, Student Leadership and Involvement
pay_detail: Free. Tuition, fees, books and parking permits are covered for selected students.
duration: The 2026 session ran May 26 to June 26, 2026.
deadline_text: The page does not give an application deadline or 2027 dates. The 2026 session ran May 26 to June 26, 2026.
who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors (when applying) with at least a 2.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must show you want to be a leader after you finish school.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Upload your unofficial high school transcript. Send one letter of recommendation. Write an essay of at least 300 words about two goals for the next five years.
notes: The same page also lists UNO Jumpstart. It is a 2 week program for graduating seniors who are already UNO students.

name: Teen Tutor and Session Lead Volunteers
city: Libraries in Texas and Pennsylvania (ask which one has a chapter)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers earn volunteer hours.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week. Commit to at least one session, preferably a year.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register to volunteer on the site.
who_can_apply: Tutors are ages 13 to 18, love working with young kids, have a B or higher in high school math, and bring a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up to volunteer on the OneInMath site. Use the register-volunteer page.
notes: The program pages do not list chapter locations. The tutor page's library news mentions North Texas libraries, so ask the group which library near you has a chapter. Re-check 2026-10-10: the tutor page does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.

name: Oneonta Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked. Re-check 2026-10-10: the campus page does not say it is enrolling, and the Job Corps student page does not say applications are accepted on an ongoing basis, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling. The campus page footer shows 2023.

name: Mi4 Summer Internship at CHOC
org: Rady Children's Health (CHOC) Medical Intelligence and Innovation Institute
pay_detail: No cost to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page. Meals, housing and travel are on you; help for low-income students may be available.
duration: About 8 weeks, June 15 to Aug 7 (2026 dates). Monday to Thursday plus Friday field trips.
deadline_text: The 2026 round is over. The page says next year's application opens in February 2027. For 2026 it opened Feb 1 and closed Feb 28, with rolling interviews.
who_can_apply: Students in high school, college, grad school or medical school who are interested in health care and innovation. You must be at least a high school freshman. You need to be on site 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CHOC website when the form opens. Interviews are rolling, so apply early. You are admitted by form and interview.
notes: The page links to a CHOC volunteer page but does not state its age rule here. Hospital and outpatient shadowing rotations are 18 and up. Business casual dress is expected.

name: Girls Meet the Workforce Externship
pay_detail: Free to join. The page does not say the externship is paid.
duration: Four-month program with a four-week externship (the 2026 externship was in July)
deadline_text: Student sign-up dates are not on the page. The newest date found is old: a March 26, 2026 deadline for host companies, not for students. Ask the Girls Inc. Programs Team how and when girls sign up.
who_can_apply: Girls in 9th to 12th grade. The four-week externship is for 11th grade girls.
how_to_apply: The page has a Contact Us link. Ask the Girls Inc. Programs Team how girls sign up.
notes: For girls only. Past host companies named on the page include PepsiCo, Edwards Lifesciences and Disneyland Resort. Confirm dates with Girls Inc. first. The 2026 host flyer says girls get a minimum of 50 hours of training; the page says up to 40, so ask Girls Inc. which is current.

name: Golden West College Dual and Concurrent Enrollment
org: Golden West College (Coast Community College District)
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Dual enrollment classes taught at a high school are free; concurrent students pay college fees and books unless their district covers them. A limited number of help grants are offered.
duration: By term: fall, winter/spring and summer
deadline_text: The page says it is accepting applications and consent forms for Fall 2026, and high school registration for Fall 2026 began June 4, 2026. It gives no Fall 2026 class start date or last day to register, so email dualenrollment@gwc.cccd.edu to ask if you can still join this term. Winter/Spring and Summer terms are also listed, with no 2027 dates posted yet.
who_can_apply: Current high school students. You need a parent consent form and one Dual Enrollment Release Form. Concurrent students also submit a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form from their high school every term. High school students cannot register for a college class without a valid release form on file.
how_to_apply: Apply to Golden West College (new students create an Open CCC account) and write down your CCCID number. Then turn in the consent forms and get your high school's approval. Dual enrollment classes are taught at your high school, so your counselor adds you to the roster. Concurrent students use a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form and register in MyGWC. Questions: dualenrollment@gwc.cccd.edu.
notes: The consent form also covers Coastline College and Orange Coast College in the same district. Only one parent consent form is needed for all high school years. The page says tuition is free, but students may still owe college fees and course costs. It offers a Foundation financial aid form and a possible fee waiver. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page says it is now accepting applications and consent forms for Fall 2026, with no closing date posted. Fetched by curl after a certificate error.

name: Orange County Young Curators (OCYC)
org: UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages
duration: One school year; the 2025-26 exhibition opens in June 2026
deadline_text: Application dates for the next group are not on the museum program pages.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors from anywhere in Orange County. The 2025-26 group came from 9 school districts and was chosen from over 100 applicants.
how_to_apply: Application steps are not listed on the pages. Email langsonteens@uci.edu to ask.
notes: The museum is named UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art on the page. Confirm dates and any stipend with the museum first.

name: Library volunteers, ages 14 and up (Orange County Public Library)
org: Orange County Public Library, Orange County NC
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 1 or 2 hour shifts, Monday to Friday 10am to 5pm, as spaces are available
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. You need a set schedule and must complete an application. Adults also complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out a volunteer application. Sign in with the Volunteer Coordinator for each shift. Training is given.
notes: The county document is titled 2024, so confirm shifts and openings with the library before you go. Main branch only: 137 W. Margaret Lane, Hillsborough. Re-check 2026-10-10: the county PDF matches the age, schedule, application and background check terms. It says nothing about ongoing intake or a 2026 date, so the status is unconfirmed, not rolling.

name: OC Parks Volunteer
city: Orange County, CA (regional parks, trails, beaches, nature centers)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Long term; at least 36 hours a year. The page also lists short term volunteer opportunities.
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page. The sign-up form is linked from the OC Parks volunteer page.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 18, or 16 with parent permission. You must pass a background check and give at least 36 hours a year. The page does not give a separate age rule for OC Zoo roles.
how_to_apply: Complete the brief interest form linked from the OC Parks Volunteers page and tell them the work that interests you. Pass a background check and attend training. For short term opportunities, search the activity listing. Questions: volunteer@ocparks.com.
notes: Volunteers 16 with parent permission (the page does not mention 17). The page lists historic docent, backcountry patrol and OC Zoo roles. It lists others too. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page gives no sign-up deadline and does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.

name: OC Pathways Student Ambassador Program
org: OC Pathways (Orange County Department of Education)
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: One school year, built around a year-long Impact Project
deadline_text: The page says students apply in spring. Exact dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who want to take their leadership to the next level. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Apply in spring. The page does not link a form, so email Nadia Khodadadi at OC Pathways (address on the page) to ask how to apply.
notes: Ask your school CTE teacher or counselor too. Confirm the spring dates with OC Pathways.

name: OCFA Fire Cadet Program
city: Orange County, CA (cadet posts at fire stations)
pay_detail: Not stated; described as a community-based youth program
duration: 10 week Fire Cadet Trainee Academy (9 weeks at cadet posts, final exam in week 10)
deadline_text: The trainee academy is held once a year. The page does not list the next start date.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with a 2.0 GPA or higher, no arrests or convictions, and fire-safe grooming. Anyone over 18 also does a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the OCFA site to join the interest list. Later, people on the list are asked to finish a longer form.
notes: OCFA serves many Orange County cities. Ask which cadet post is nearest to you.

name: Orangewood Foundation Independent Living Program (ILP)
pay_detail: Not a job. Workshops may earn gift card incentives. The page does not say whether the program is free.
duration: Nine months of case management
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 who live in Orange County. You must be in foster care, extended foster care or Kin-GAP. That means a current or past Orange County dependent. Young adults on probation may also qualify.
how_to_apply: Ask your social worker for an ILP referral. You can also call Orangewood at 714-619-0200 or visit the Orangewood Resource Center, 1575 E. 17th Street, Santa Ana.
notes: Orangewood's Lyon Workforce Academy is a separate program, so it is not listed here. The OC Social Services Agency pays for part of the program. Call to ask about cost.

name: Santa Ana College Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: The enrollment fee is waived for part-time special admit students (under 12 units, or 15 units or fewer from partner schools). Other costs are not stated on this page.

how_to_apply: Use the New Students page on the Dual Enrollment site. Contact the Dual Enrollment Office at dualenrollment@sac.edu or (714) 564-6931.
notes: If you go over the unit limit you pay the enrollment fee for all units, not only the extra ones. The office is closed on Fridays in summer. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page says the program is active. It gives no term dates, no deadline, and no word that applications are taken on an ongoing basis. So the status is unconfirmed, not rolling.

name: Teen Volunteer Work Experience Program (Social Services Agency)

pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work experience.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 19. The page says there are no exceptions to the age rule. A parent or guardian must consent if you are under 18.
how_to_apply: Check the County of Orange volunteer page in spring 2027 and apply there. Questions: SSATeenVolunteers@ssa.ocgov.com.
notes: You must dress in neat business clothes. There are several office sites. The addresses are on the application form. Volunteers sign a promise to keep client facts private.

name: Santiago Canyon College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
pay_detail: The page says free transferable college units. Fees for books or other costs are not listed on the page.
duration: By semester

how_to_apply: Apply to SCC. Make your dual enrollment profile in the portal with your SCC student email. Send a course request. Then confirm your enrollment. Phone (714) 628-4764 or earlycollege@sccollege.edu.
notes: SCC is phasing out the paper Special Admit Form for high school dual enrollment. It now goes through the portal.

name: Ignite by 4-H Conference (Oregon delegation)
pay_detail: Event page lists $300. A donor covers a large part of the conference cost and airfare.
deadline_text: Applications close October 13, 2026 at 11:45 pm (the deadline was extended from October 1).
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who were in 4-H in the 2025-26 year (member, camp, event or in-school program) and have not attended a national 4-H event before. Must be able to travel to DC in March 2027 and to Portland airport. Oregon youth join a chaperoned group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form and upload a 2 to 4 minute video at beav.es/ignite2027 answering the prompt on the page. Do not use the national 4-h.org site.
notes: Requests for disability help are due Oct 31, 2026. This is a 4-H event named Ignite. It is not the same as the Ignition youth conference.

name: Oregon 4-H Ambassador Program
org: OSU Extension Service, Oregon State University
pay_detail: Unpaid leadership role
duration: One 4-H year
deadline_text: Applications were due May 1, 2026. Finalists interview at Summer Conference in late June (2026: June 24 to 27).
who_can_apply: County Ambassadors: contact your local 4-H office for rules. State Ambassadors: 4-H youth in the Senior age division who have been in 4-H at least one year. The page does not give the Senior division ages.

name: Oregon 4-H Summer Conference
org: OSU Extension Service, Oregon State University

notes: 2026 dates were June 24 to 27 and registration opened May 15, 2026 at 3:00 pm. Buses leave from several Oregon towns for an added fee. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Oregon 4-H Youth Development

pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county 4-H office about enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: Oregon youth. Check with your local 4-H program coordinator to find a club and project that fit your area.

notes: The page was written for the 2025-2026 4-H year. Not every project is offered in every county, since it depends on volunteers. To join in another county, you need an Out of County Participation Form.

name: Youth Tractor Safety Certification
city: Linn, Marion, Clackamas, Jefferson and other Oregon counties
pay_detail: $75 in most counties and $95 in Clackamas County (2026 prices).
duration: 22 hours over 2 to 3 dates

how_to_apply: Pick a county class on the page and use its register link. Or contact Andrea Leao or your local Extension office.
notes: The page says Oregon requires farmers and ranchers who hire minors under 18 to be sure those minors passed tractor safety training. That is the page's own statement. Ask your boss. 2026 sites included Linn, Marion, Clackamas and Jefferson counties.

name: Empowered Professionals of Tomorrow (UVU)
pay_detail: No pay. Tuition is free for admitted students. You pay for your own rides, lunches and personal costs.
duration: 7 weeks. Tuesdays to Thursdays, 9:00 AM to 3:15 PM (June 24 to Aug 7 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 program was full and had a waitlist. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Utah high school students in grades 9 to 11. The page says it is especially for first-generation college learners.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Share your interests, your goals and why you want to join. The application asks for short written responses, which carry strong weight. The team picks students by readiness, interest and fit. Applications can also go on the waitlist.
notes: You must go in person. Classes also have homework outside class time. Track choice is not guaranteed. Questions: text 801-928-7615. The page says you may be added to a contact list for future openings.

name: Otis College Summer of Art
org: Otis College of Art and Design
pay_detail: 2026 prices as posted: $4,390 full program (3 college credits) or $2,690 per individual class; $7,315 or $5,615 with housing. A $150 health center fee applies. 2027 prices are not posted.
duration: 4 weeks in July 2027. The main page says July 7 to 30; the dates page says orientation July 6, classes July 8 to July 30.
deadline_text: Registration begins Nov 16, 2026. The scholarship application deadline is April 16, 2027 (no exceptions). The registration deadline is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students and young creatives ages 14.5 to 19. No grade level is listed.
how_to_apply: Use Register Now on the Summer of Art page. Questions: soa@otis.edu or 310-665-6850. Scholarships have their own application.
notes: The page says ages 14.5 to 19; min_age is entered as 14 because the field takes whole years. Costs money. Prices shown are the 2026 numbers. In 2026 the early discount deadline was April 25. The April 16, 2027 date is the scholarship deadline, not the registration deadline.

name: OUSD Linked Learning Internships
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
fields: any; health; tech-cs; arts-media; engineering; business-finance
pay_detail: Summer internships are paid; amounts vary by employer (see the district list). The district's 2024 listing said Peralta Summer Institute students got a stipend; the current Peralta page only says classes are free.

notes: The OUSD page still shows Summer 2024 forms, so look for a new form in January 2027. Not every internship is open to every student.

name: OUSD Linked Learning: Pathways, Internships and Work Permits
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)

notes: The office handles work permits (needed for any paid job under 18). Check the pathways pages on the OUSD site to find work-based learning at your school.

name: Lifeguard I Outdoor (seasonal)
org: City of Overland Park Parks and Recreation

how_to_apply: The job description does not say how to apply. It requires Starguard certification from the City of Overland Park. The course is the Starguard Lifeguard Course.
notes: Quote from the job description: a minimum of 15 years of age. The job description does not state pay. Current postings and pay were not on the program page.

name: Pacific Marine Mammal Center Junior Docent and Junior Outreach Assistant

how_to_apply: Use Apply Now for the Junior Docent or Junior Outreach Assistant role. The center reviews forms and then gets back to you.
notes: The page says most volunteer roles are for ages 18 and up. Use the Contact Us button on the page for questions.

name: Pacoima Beautiful Agua University

notes: Pacoima Beautiful also lists Bee Wise, Agua Academy and YUTEP on its youth page. No details were posted for them.

notes: Classes run 8:00 AM to 2:30 PM and field days 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Dates may change each year.

notes: Service projects sign-up opens two weeks before each event.

name: Palo Alto Art Center Summer Camp Counselor in Training

notes: Same page lists the Ceramics Apprentice Program (16 and older, 2 years of Art Center ceramics or instructor approval, 2 hours a week, one training session). Spots may fill fast once registration opens.

name: Teen Library Advisory Board (Palo Alto City Library)

notes: Fingerprinting is required. Log your hours in Better Impact or the library cannot confirm them.

name: Teen Advisory Board (Mitchell Park Teen Services)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services

notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

name: Palo Alto Youth Council (PAYC)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services
deadline_text: The page says the application opens July 2027. No closing date stated.

how_to_apply: Online application, recommendation letter, intro video, then an interview with the nominating committee, once applications open.
notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

name: Pasadena City College Dual and Concurrent Enrollment for Middle and High School Students
pay_detail: Fees and fee waivers are not stated on the program pages. Ask outreach@pasadena.edu.
duration: By term. Fall 2026 runs 8/24/26 to 12/13/26.
deadline_text: The page shows applications opened 12/01/2025 for the Summer 2026 (6/22 to 8/14/26) and Fall 2026 (8/24 to 12/13/26) terms. No later application window is posted. Forms are processed in 2 to 3 weeks.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Dual enrollment is only at partner schools. These are in the Arcadia, El Monte Union (Rosemead High), La Canada, Pasadena, San Gabriel, San Marino, South Pasadena and Temple City districts. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Pick courses with your counselor. Then send the Recommendation form. A counselor and a parent sign it. If you are under 18, send the Medical Consent form too. Send your latest unofficial transcript as well. Then turn on your LancerPoint account and register. Questions: outreach@pasadena.edu.
notes: Do not email documents to the outreach address; upload them as the page says. Check with your counselor which classes your school offers.

name: Pasadena Humane Teen Volunteers (15 and up, Ambassador at 14 with a parent)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

deadline_text: The next virtual orientation is Tuesday, Nov 10, 5:00 to 6:15 p.m. Foster care and at-home service projects run year-round.
who_can_apply: Volunteer jobs are for ages 15 and over. Ambassador is open at 14 with a parent or guardian. Anyone under 15 must have a parent or guardian who also volunteers at all times.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a coming virtual orientation on the volunteer page. Then go to the training for each job you pick.
notes: The page does not say which roles are only for adults. Kids ages 6 to 14 have separate roles (Shelter Greeter, Boredom Busters). Those need a parent who volunteers too.

name: The Rose, Pasadena's Youth Literary Magazine
pay_detail: Unpaid. You are published, not paid.

how_to_apply: Send your writing or art to the teen librarian (email on the page). To help with the magazine, fill out the library's Teen Volunteer Application. Limits: poetry up to 40 lines, short fiction up to 1,000 words, book reviews 250 to 500 words.
notes: The library page does not say the age rule for the Teen Volunteer Application, so ask the teen librarian. Teen librarian contact is on the page. The page does not say whether contributors are paid.

name: Growing Strong summer internship
grades: Sophomore, junior or senior in fall 2026

how_to_apply: Fill out the application form. Have a recommendation form sent for you. Go to a Teen Summer Program Info Session.
notes: The page gives grades, not ages. 2027 applications open in early spring 2027. You must go to a Teen Summer Program Info Session to apply.

name: Volunteer with seniors at Peninsula Volunteers (PVI)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.
duration: Ongoing. Volunteer hours are usually Monday to Friday, and most in-person volunteering ends by 3 p.m.
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: The page does not give a minimum age for individual volunteers. It says people under 16 may take part on site but must have an adult with them the whole time.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application on the PVI website. Staff will contact you with open roles. Phone: 650-326-0665. Address: 800 Middle Avenue, Menlo Park.
notes: Weekday daytime hours make this hard during the school year, so summer or school breaks fit best. The under-16 rule appears in the group volunteering section of the page. Idealist listings for PVI say volunteers must be at least 16, but the PVI page itself does not say that, so ask PVI about the age rule before you apply.

name: Pennsylvania 4-H
pay_detail: Members pay a fee for educational materials. Extra fees vary by county and project area. Financial help is available. Amounts are not stated.
duration: Ongoing club membership
deadline_text: No deadline posted; join through your county 4-H office.
who_can_apply: Any child ages 5 to 18 who lives in Pennsylvania. Ages 8 to 18 (before January 1 of the current year) can join the program and take part in contests. Ages 5 to 7 are Cloverbuds. They do non-competitive activities.
how_to_apply: Look up your county 4-H program. Pick a club. Talk with your county educator. Then sign up in 4-H's ZSuite. If you cannot enroll online, ask the educator for help.
notes: A youth group, not a job. Ask your county educator what clubs and teen leader roles are near you.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Pennsylvania Wing
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: Pennsylvania FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
city: Pennsylvania (statewide, state office in Jersey Shore)
grades: High school grades 9 to 12 (middle school grades 5 to 8 has a separate group)
pay_detail: Yearly dues $18 for high school ($10 national and $8 state). Virtual Chapter dues are $16.
duration: School year; the 2027 State Leadership Conference is April 12 to 14, 2027 at the Hershey Lodge and Giant Center
deadline_text: Join through your chapter adviser any time. Next State Leadership Conference: April 12 to 14, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. If your school has no chapter, you can join the Virtual Chapter. It is open if you are homeschooled or in a cyber charter, private or charter school. It is also open if your school has no FBLA chapter. The Virtual Chapter page says members must take a business class. Students at schools with an active FBLA chapter cannot join it.
how_to_apply: Ask your chapter adviser at school. If you do not know who that is, contact Bruce Boncal, PA FBLA Executive Director, bboncal@pafbla.us. Virtual Chapter members fill out an online application signed by a parent.
notes: Virtual Chapter members pay their own travel costs. State office: (570) 398-4652, stateoffice@pafbla.us.

name: Pennsylvania FFA Association
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher.

how_to_apply: Sign up for agricultural education at a school that has an FFA chapter. Use the Chapter Locator on the Pennsylvania FFA site to find one near you.
notes: The state page says nearly 16,000 students are members, in four regions. Members compete at chapter, regional, state and national events. The National FFA Organization has its own listing in other cards. This one is the Pennsylvania state page.

name: Pennsylvania Junior Academy of Science (PJAS)

deadline_text: The 2026 State Meet was May 17 to 19, 2026 at Penn State University Park. Each region sets its own deadlines. The program pages do not list 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 in Pennsylvania: public, private, parochial or home schooled. You need an adult sponsor (a teacher, parent or scientist). You must do your own research and your own presentation.
how_to_apply: Pick a research category. Find a sponsor. Use the Find Your Region page for your region's deadlines, forms and location. Turn in any required SRC/IRB approval forms.
notes: A science fair, not a job. Your project may need extra approval forms depending on your research field, so ask your sponsor or Regional Director early. Regional pages list the exact deadlines.

name: Keystone Boys State

pay_detail: No pay. American Legion posts and the Department pay the fees, so little or no cost to the family.

notes: Girls only. The FAQ on the site is still from 2023, so confirm this year's dates, deadline and cost with the program before you plan. The national Auxiliary list shows June 21 to June 26, 2026 while the state site shows 20-25 June 2026.

name: Pennsylvania Outdoor Corps, Youth Summer Program

deadline_text: 2026 dates were June 29 to August 7, 2026. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 at the start of the program. High school students. Crews are based in cities across Pennsylvania.

notes: Crew locations change by year; check the SCA page for this year's list. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Pennsylvania School for Excellence in the Agricultural Sciences (PSEAS)
org: Penn State College of Agricultural Sciences

notes: No wage is paid. Page lists a contact email in two spellings, so confirm it.

name: Peralta Colleges Dual Enrollment (Laney, Merritt, Berkeley City, College of Alameda)

how_to_apply: Meet your counselor. Apply to a Peralta college. Turn in the High School Special Enrollment Form, a transcript and photo ID. Meet a college counselor. Then register.
notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers, including incoming 9th graders. The 2026 dates were June 22 to July 31. No application deadline is posted. The old OUSD page mentions a stipend. The Peralta page does not.

name: Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP)

name: Youth volunteers at Summer Playtime and Summer Day Camps

notes: Dates for the 2027 season are not posted on the page. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
