notes: The same page lists other teen programs (Teen Arts Council, Teen Vocal Showcase for ages 10 to 18, Teen Nights for ages 10 to 17). Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Library volunteering and VolunTEEN
org: Prince George's County Memorial Library System
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student service learning hours are available.
duration: Temporary (limited) or regular (at least 6 months) schedules
deadline_text: No deadline. Kids Achieve Club interviews: June for September programs, November for January programs.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 (library system rule). VolunTEEN is for grades 6 to 12. The Kids Achieve Club welcomes teens over 15. Volunteers cannot staff the Circulation or Information desks.
how_to_apply: Get a volunteer application from your local branch. Ask for the volunteer coordinator. For VolunTEEN, sign up through the Beanstack app.
notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Volunteer Program, Academy of Natural Sciences
org: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Regular time from half a day to several days a week, for at least one year
deadline_text: No deadline listed.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 14. The page lists no teen-specific roles; ask which positions accept teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.

name: Teen Sketch and Teen Podcast, Philadelphia Museum of Art
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.
duration: Fall 2026 programs. Teen Sketch length is not stated.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 programs are listed with Apply links. No closing date is posted on the page.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page describes Teen Podcast as a program for Philly teens. The page does not list ages or a school-district rule for Teen Sketch.
how_to_apply: Each program has its own Apply now link (a Google form) on the teens page. Questions: teens@philamuseum.org.
notes: The page does not say whether the programs are paid or free, or when the forms close. Email the teen team before you plan around it. The museum also ran A Future of Artists, a June to August 2026 exhibition of work by Philadelphia-area high school students.

name: Outdoor and Wilderness Leadership Skills (OWLS), Awbury Arboretum
pay_detail: Summer 2026 price was $675 ($641 for members) for the 2 week session. The camp page says scholarships (75% off) and sliding scale fees (30% to 60% off) are available to families in local zip codes.
duration: 2 weeks (June 15 to 26 in 2026)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 session ran June 15 to 26, 2026 and was sold out. The camp FAQ says Summer 2027 registration opens Monday, Feb. 1, 2027 at 9 am; OWLS 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Awbury Adventures Summer Camp page. Ask for financial aid BEFORE you sign up, because aid spots are few.
notes: This is training, not a paid job. The page does not say whether graduates get counselor jobs. A 2021 posting on the same site said 2 to 6 trainees were chosen as stipend-paid counselors in training; that is old, so ask.

name: Paid Youth Internships, Bartram's Garden
pay_detail: $11 to $12.50 per hour in 2025-26; 8.5 hours a week in the school year. Some interns can continue in summer at 20 hours a week.
duration: October to spring in the 2025-26 cycle; some interns continue in summer.
deadline_text: The 2025-26 cycle closed Sept 23, 2025 (program started Oct 6, 2025). The page says applications reopen in August for the 2026-27 school year, but still shows the 2025 dates.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors ages 14 to 18. You must live, go to school or have other ties in Southwest Philadelphia. Priority goes to 49th to 65th Streets between Chester Avenue and the river. You must have a work permit or be able to get one.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with short written answers. Then you have an in-person interview. If you are hired, you sign up for the city C2L-PHL program. It needs a Social Security card, an ID, proof of citizenship and Philadelphia home address, and a W-9.
notes: Competitive: about 50 students a year across all programs. The page still showed 2025-26 dates when read, so check it for the 2026-27 deadline. The Garden will never ask for birth dates or Social Security numbers by text message.

name: Bloomberg Arts Internship (BAI)
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support
duration: Eight weeks, up to 35 hours a week (2026: June 19 to August 14); select interns may continue in a school-year program up to 10 hours a week
deadline_text: The page posts no intern application dates. Its only application notice is for worksite hosts: Summer 2026 applications are officially closed.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in Philadelphia. The page does not state an age range or residency proof.
how_to_apply: The page gives no intern application steps. Contact info@philaculture.org or 215-557-7811.
notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the page.

name: Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L-PHL) Summer Program
org: City of Philadelphia Office of Children and Families, with JEVS Human Services
pay_detail: Stipend on a prepaid debit card, paid every other week; total $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program (hourly rate not listed).
duration: Summer program (plus school-year programming)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. FAQ: summer applications open between March and April each year.
who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. In-school youth get priority. You can apply to one program per cycle.
how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Northeast Philadelphia Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Northeast Philadelphia Composite Squadron (PA-214)
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Fridays from 7:00 to 9:15 p.m. at the Naval Support Activity Center, 700 Robbins St, Philadelphia, PA 19111.
deadline_text: The page posts no application deadline and does not say whether enrollment is ongoing. Contact the squadron.
who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Contact the squadron: cc214@pawg.cap.gov (squadron commander) or 215-531-2278. The wing's Join CAP page has the cadet steps.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists five other squadrons in the Philadelphia area. They are Willow Grove, Liberty, Griffin, Gen Carl A Spaatz and Chester County. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

name: Neuroscience Camp for High School Students, Drexel
org: Drexel University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies
grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a background in biology, chemistry or research
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)
deadline_text: The page says information about 2027 Summer Institutes will become available this winter. No 2026 or 2027 application dates are posted on this page.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.

name: Teen Lounge, Fleisher Art Memorial
pay_detail: Free. No attendance requirement. Snacks and bus passes provided.
duration: Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 4 to 6 pm, while Philadelphia schools are in session. Fall 2026 workshops start Sept 8.
deadline_text: Drop in during the school year, for Teen Lounge 2026-2027. Fall workshops started Tuesday, Sept 8, 2026, and that date has passed.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Drop in at 719 Catharine St, or email cy@fleisher.org.
notes: Not a job. Lead support from the William Penn Foundation and others is listed on the page.

name: Immersion Science Program (Fox Chase Cancer Center)
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
deadline_text: The application launches in mid to late October each year and stays open about 3.5 weeks. The exact 2026 dates are not posted on the program page. Interviews are in early to mid December and letters go out by email before December 31.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages.

name: PACTS (Partnership for Achieving Careers in Technology and Science), The Franklin Institute
pay_detail: Free program.
duration: School year, workshops meet twice a month on Saturday mornings
deadline_text: The page has an Apply link but no dates for the current year.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8 who live in the Philadelphia area.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to the PACTS Program online form on the page.
notes: For younger teens (grades 6 to 8). Older teens can join the Franklin Ambassador program through STEM Scholars, which has its own card.

name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are open and due November 16, 2026.
who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.

name: Young Volunteers at the Free Library of Philadelphia
duration: At least 1 to 3 hours a week for 2 to 3 months. Some seasonal and short-term roles are listed too.
deadline_text: Rolling. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12. The library says all volunteers must be at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Print the form and fill it out. Email it to volunteer@freelibrary.org or mail it to 1901 Vine Street. Then staff will set up a talk with you.
notes: The page asks for age 14 and up but also says grades 7 to 12, so younger 7th graders should call first. For a paid role, the library's LEAP after-school program hires Teen Leadership Assistants through Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L PHL). Questions: 215-686-5340.

name: Teen Ambassadors, Independence Seaport Museum
pay_detail: Described as a ten-week paid work and learning experience. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: June through August, plus select Saturdays in September
deadline_text: The page says apply by April 20 (priority interviews); its flyer link is dated March 2026. Next dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Philadelphia teens about to enter grades 10 to 12 who go to a high school in the city. You must be allowed to work in Philadelphia. If you are under 18, you must be able to get a work permit. You must be free for the whole program. It runs June through August, plus some Saturdays in September.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form linked from the page. Early applications get interviews first.
notes: Funded by The W.W. Smith Charitable Trust and The Hamilton Family Charitable Trust, both named on the page.

name: Teen and Adult Volunteer Program, Jefferson Abington Hospital
duration: Most assignments need at least 2 to 4 hours a week. Some late afternoon, evening or weekend shifts.
deadline_text: Rolling. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who has the shots and health checks Jefferson asks for.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the volunteer page. If they pick you, the hospital checks your record. You fill out some papers and show your shots: chicken pox, MMR, Tdap, a new TB blood test, and a flu shot in flu season.
notes: Volunteering here does not lead to a job, but it is health care experience for your resume. Shadowing is possible only if you find a staff member to supervise you yourself. Jefferson's Center City hospitals (TJUH and Methodist) take volunteers 18 and up only. Questions: 215-481-2492.

name: Summer Student Volunteer Program, Jefferson Health Northeast
org: Jefferson Health Northeast (Torresdale, Frankford and Bucks County hospitals)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get their own transportation.
duration: 8 weeks, 4 hours a day, one day a week
deadline_text: The program page gives no application dates and no year. The 2024 packet said applications are accepted from February until April.
who_can_apply: Students 16 or older who can keep a regular weekly shift. Needs two school references from teachers and proof of vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella and a TB test).
how_to_apply: Send the application, two letters of support from teachers and shot forms to the Volunteer Services Department. You can send by mail, scan, fax or email. Phone: 215-612-4170.
notes: Facts come from the 2024 application packet on the Jefferson site. The program web page shows only its title (checked 2026-10-09 with a normal fetch and with curl), so the age, time, pay and how-to-apply details are not confirmed on the page. Confirm the current dates, ages and form first. Spots are limited.

name: Philadelphia Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Philadelphia, PA (campus; page lists transportation and no dorms)
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists transportation to and from campus, breakfast and lunch, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: The pages show Apply and Get Started links but post no enrollment window and do not say applications are ongoing. Start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: the Philadelphia campus page lists transportation and no dorms. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program (MSAP)
grades: Currently enrolled in high school or an undergraduate school
pay_detail: Described as paid. The amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: The program page says eight weeks of paid full-time structured research. The 2026 program ran June 15 to July 31, 2026, which is shorter than eight weeks, so confirm the length. The page does not give the 2027 dates.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 program open Tuesday, October 27, 2026. The deadline is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students now in high school or college from the greater Philadelphia area, including Camden, NJ. You must be able to prove you can work in the United States. No age or grade is stated. The committee gives strong preference to students from groups underrepresented in science.
how_to_apply: Use the MSAP Applications page on monell.org when it opens. Sign up for Monell's newsletter for updates. Questions: AcademicAffairs@monell.org or 267-519-4700. About 200 applications come in each year. 18 to 24 students are usually enrolled.
notes: Minors do not need working papers to apply. They must get them after they are admitted. They come from the School District of Philadelphia, per the Monell FAQ. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. Monell does not provide housing or meals. Students must commit to the full program with no vacations.

name: Art Education high school programs (Mural Arts Philadelphia)
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program pages. The page says students can later apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.
duration: Twice a week. The fall session begins in late September 2026. The page gives no end date.
deadline_text: Rolling admission is open (page). The fall session begins in late September 2026.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 22 at the high school sites. Ages 10 to 13 are served at middle school sites. A parent or guardian must sign and provide extra information before a youth under 18 can be enrolled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Inquiry Form on the Mural Arts enroll page. It is not an application and does not confirm enrollment. An Art Education staff member follows up about classes near you. Contact: natalie.gearin@muralarts.org or (215) 685-0750.
notes: The pages say 3 high school sites and 6 middle school sites on the enroll page but 16 sites in total on the page, so ask which site is near you. Mural Arts also has paid summer work experience through Career Connected Learning (see the C2L PHL card). Ask whether classes are free. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Living History Youth Summer Institute, Museum of the American Revolution
pay_detail: The page says it is a paid six-week program. The pay amount is not stated. Public transportation help is offered.
duration: 6 weeks, weekdays (the 2023 session ran July 5 to August 11)
deadline_text: The page names a 2026 session but gives no application dates. The 2026 program is finished and no 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school and college students. You must be able to go on weekdays for the whole program. You must live close enough to the museum to travel there each day.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Contact the museum education team through the museum website.
notes: This is a small program. The 2023 press release said eight took part. It is part of the museum's African American Interpretive Program. Check the museum site for the next call for applications.

name: Youth Council, Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
org: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA)
pay_detail: Free to join. No pay or stipend is stated.
duration: Fall 2026: Wednesdays Oct 21 to Dec 9, 4 to 6 pm. Spring 2027: Wednesdays Jan 27 to Apr 14, 4 to 6 pm.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 starts Oct 21, 2026; Spring 2027 starts Jan 27, 2027. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the Youth Council page, which goes to pafa-museum.coursestorm.com. Each session has its own Register link.
notes: PAFA is on North Broad Street. The status is shown as open because the page lists a Register link for both sessions; the page gives no closing date.

name: Become a Lifeguard, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
deadline_text: Free training is offered year-round; reserve a slot on Eventbrite.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).

name: Parks and Rec Summer Youth Employment Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Summer
deadline_text: The page still says registration closed for the C2L-PHL Summer 2025 program. No 2026 or 2027 dates posted.
who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24. Residency is not stated on this page (the parent C2L-PHL program requires Philadelphia residency).
how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.

name: Provost's Summer Mentorship Program (Penn)
grades: Currently 9th or 10th grade (entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2027)
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the program pages, so ask the program before you plan around either.
duration: Four weeks, on campus. Exact summer 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: The page says the Summer Mentorship Program for 2027 will begin taking applications in January 2027. The deadline is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students who live in Philadelphia. You must go to a Philadelphia public, Catholic, private or charter high school. You need a minimum GPA of 3.0.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the program site when it opens in January 2027. You will need a high school transcript with fall 2026 grades. You need a 250 word essay about yourself and your interest in the program. You need an up to date vaccine record.
notes: The two pages word the grade rule differently (currently 9th or 10th on the apply page, entering 10th or 11th in fall 2027 on the main page); they describe the same group. Office: St. Leonard's Court, Suite 110, 3819 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104; contact form at https://vpse.upenn.edu/smp/contact-us/.

name: Penn Arts and Sciences High School Summer Programs
org: University of Pennsylvania, Penn LPS High School Programs
grades: Academies and Online Seminars: current 9th to 11th grade. Pre-College: current 10th to 11th grade.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: 2-week Academy $6,700; 3-week Academy $10,050; Pre-College Residential $15,192 to $23,604; Pre-College Online $8,692 or $14,300; Online Seminars $2,950. $1,500 deposit and $100 application fee (waived for School District of Philadelphia applicants).
duration: 2 to 6 weeks depending on program (2026 Academies: July 11 to August 1)
deadline_text: 2026: May 1 for Academies and Pre-College Residential/Online Session I; June 1 for Online Seminars and Pre-College Online Session II. Rolling admissions. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders (Pre-College: 10th to 11th).
how_to_apply: Online application from the student: essays (400 words each), transcript, recommendations. For the scholarship, say you attend a School District of Philadelphia school and fill in the scholarship section.
notes: There are no scholarships for the Pre-College programs. Contact hsprogs@sas.upenn.edu or 215-746-2309.

name: Junior Volunteer Program (Student Ambassador Program), Pennsylvania Hospital
deadline_text: The 2026 program closed early because of high demand. Applications for Summer 2027 open February 1, 2027. No closing date is posted, so apply early.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 17. The program targets high school students interested in health care, but all students are invited to apply.
how_to_apply: Starting February 1, 2027, create an account in the Penn Medicine volunteer portal and apply. More details will be posted closer to that date.
notes: It is only at the 800 Spruce Street site. Spots fill fast. Email PAHVolunteerServices@pennmedicine.upenn.edu or call 215-829-5187.

name: Police Explorer Cadet Program (Post 991)
org: Philadelphia Police Department, with Learning for Life
pay_detail: Pay, stipend or fees are not stated on the program pages.
duration: Every Saturday 10 am to 5 pm at the Philadelphia Police Academy, plus optional summer camps and a Washington DC trip.
deadline_text: The program site says applications are open for 2026-2027. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who want a law enforcement career. 14 year olds must be in high school. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent. Needs a passing behavior grade, good health for running and agility drills, and no arrests or convictions that would block a future police job.
how_to_apply: Use the online intake form on the program site. It is on the Apply and Forms page. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Most cadets are not paid, but the pages do not say. Cadets who want to be police officers are urged to join the police recruit testing later. Other Explorer camps include a Pennsylvania State Police week and a camp at Fort Indiantown Gap. The program site lists a $50 a year fee for insurance and registration, collected if you are accepted. It also lists about $350 for probation uniforms.

name: AIM Afterschool, Philadelphia Youth Network
pay_detail: Not stated; no cost is listed on the program page.
duration: School year (2026-27 sites are listed on the page)
deadline_text: The page says enrollment is open all year round.
who_can_apply: Middle school students in the School District of Philadelphia. They must go to one of the PYN school sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online forms in the PYN application portal. There are no paper applications. Send questions to afterschool@pyninc.org.
notes: For middle schoolers, so it suits younger teens. Pick a school site from the list on the page.

name: NextGen Career Clubs, Philadelphia Youth Network
pay_detail: Free career exposure program. The club itself is not described as paid.
duration: 3 days a week, 2 hours a session
deadline_text: Now recruiting at high schools across Philadelphia for Fall and Spring 2026/27. The page posts no closing date.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th or 12th graders enrolled at a PYN host high school, Martin Luther King High School or Simon Gratz High School. You must be able to come three days a week after school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Participant Interest Form on the PYN page. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: The page also lists a NextGen Career Club (Health Care).

name: PYNtern Program
grades: Rising 9th to 12th grade (Junior PYNtern rising 9th to 10th; Senior PYNtern rising 11th to 12th)
pay_detail: Up to $1,500 for a 6 to 8 week experience, depending on hours and milestones
duration: 6 to 8 weeks per cohort (page also says experiences last 6 to 12 weeks)
deadline_text: Now recruiting for Summer and Fall 2026 (page). Summer applications open early March, fall/winter cohort early August, winter/spring cohort November.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18, primarily rising 9th to 12th graders. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: City-Wide Philly Youth Opportunity Fair
pay_detail: Free to attend. The page says employers there have jobs and internships, but it does not say if they are paid.
duration: Friday Oct 23, 3 to 7 pm
deadline_text: Friday, October 23, 2026, 3:00 to 7:00 pm. Pre-registration deadline is Oct 15. The page says registration is not required to attend.
who_can_apply: The page says young people ages 16 to 24. Families and supporters can come too.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free pre-registration form on the event page (deadline Oct 15). Bring several copies of your resume.
notes: The page gives the day and month only; the year is taken from Oct 23 falling on a Friday in 2026. Under 16 is not listed as eligible.

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE), School District of Philadelphia
pay_detail: School program; the page does not say whether internships are paid.
duration: Typically 3 years, 1,080 hours of instruction; some programs 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: Follow the School Selection timeline for middle schoolers; high schoolers ask their counselor.
who_can_apply: District high school students starting in 10th grade. Middle schoolers choose a CTE program on their School Selection application; high schoolers can join if their school has the program and space allows.
how_to_apply: Middle school: pick schools that offer your CTE program on the School Selection application. High school: talk to your school counselor.
notes: The page notes that students ages 14 to 17 need working papers to work. Which schools offer which programs is in the CTE Programs List.

name: Counselor-in-Training Program, Camp Schuylkill
pay_detail: Volunteer program with no fee listed; hours can count as school or organization service hours.
duration: Two full weeks required; may be asked to work up to three weeks; one Saturday training in May
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026. Camp Schuylkill runs on a weekly schedule from June 21 to August 13, 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Positions are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.

name: Wildlife Clinic Support Volunteer, Schuylkill Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Minimum one 4-hour shift a week (about 20 hours a month)

name: Temple Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math & Science

notes: The page says that being accepted does not promise acceptance later at Villanova. It also does not give you an edge. A virtual info session is offered.

name: High School Program in Biomedical Research (Wistar Institute)
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend for finishing the program, plus SEPTA passes for travel
duration: Four weeks (the 2026 session ran July 6 to July 30). An optional three week extension in August depends on funding.

The program gives priority to students in the School District of Philadelphia. It strongly encourages Philadelphia high school students to apply. No grade level or residency rule is listed.

The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

notes: You must go to the required orientation, or you can apply next summer.

how_to_apply: Complete the Idea Submission questionnaire on the library volunteer site during a submission window. The Civic Engagement Team will contact you to get your idea library ready. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: A limited number of projects are accepted and a branch must agree to host. Other QPL pages list ages as 14-18 for this program, so check the age limit if you are 18.

name: Queens Public Library Teen Volunteering (ages 14-17)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours count as community service credit.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: Minors can apply year-round. Approval and placement can take up to 30 days, longer in summer and fall.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with a signed parent consent form. The page says some projects do not require NYS working papers, so check each project's description. Students at schools outside the country or the state may use a waiver.
how_to_apply: Get the parent consent form and NYS working papers (from your high school office), create a volunteer account, search projects and click Express Interest/Sign Up, then interview and get an offer letter. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: Library says some projects do not need working papers, so check each listing. Working papers take 1-3 weeks from your school, so start early. They are issued regardless of immigration status. Under-14s can only volunteer with a parent or guardian.

name: Raleigh Digital Connectors
org: City of Raleigh, Digital Impact Unit
pay_detail: A stipend, plus a free laptop when you finish. The page does not state the stipend amount.
duration: Several months of weekly meetings, with no more than four unexcused absences.
deadline_text: Applications for the Fall 2026 group are closed. The page says an interest form for the Fall 2027 group opens in January 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 who live in the City of Raleigh.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Digital Impact Programs page when it opens in January 2027. The form does not promise a spot.
notes: After Digital Connectors, you can join Raleigh Digital Ambassadors. It runs 10 months, with 45 hours of service and a stipend. You help people at events like Advice About Your Device.

name: Marbles Teen Play Corps
duration: One year. Minimum 30 service hours a year to stay active.
deadline_text: Apply December 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 (5 PM). You must first attend an information session with a parent or guardian: Nov 14, Dec 10, 2026, or Jan 16, 2027. Decisions by early March 2027.
who_can_apply: Rising 7th graders and older who are at least 12 years old by the first in-person training. The page lists no residency rule.
how_to_apply: Go to an info session with a parent or guardian. Then send the form, two letters from adults who are not family, and a short video. In the video, tell them your favorite way to play. Keep it under 2 minutes.
notes: Not everyone is accepted. If selected, you take a virtual Volunteer 101 and in-person Mission 101 and Play 101 trainings. Teens 16 and up can also volunteer on their own without Teen Play Corps. Questions: teenplaycorps@marbleskidsmuseum.org.

name: Raleigh Lifeguard and SAVE Free Lifeguard Training
org: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources, Aquatics
pay_detail: SAVE lifeguards work 155 hours at $14 an hour after the free class. The page does not list pay for certified lifeguards.
duration: SAVE: a lifeguard class, then 155 required work hours. Pools are open from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. at most sites.
deadline_text: The page says the city is accepting lifeguard applications now. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 and older. You must pass the city's drug test and background check. You must swim 150 yards without stopping, tread water for two minutes using only your legs, and pull a 10 pound object from the bottom of the pool in a timed test.
how_to_apply: Apply at governmentjobs.com. Search for "Lifeguard" if you are certified, or "Lifeguard - not certified" for SAVE, and pick Raleigh. The city then contacts you to set up an interview or a swim tryout.
notes: SAVE lifeguards also go to trainings each month and each season. Questions: Raleigh Aquatics, Aquatics@raleighnc.gov, 919-996-6852.

name: Raleigh Police Public Safety Cadets
org: Raleigh Police Department, Youth and Family Services
deadline_text: No dates or deadline are posted. Email the unit to ask how to join.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20. The page lists no other rule.
how_to_apply: Email Eric Hinton at Eric.Hinton@raleighnc.gov or call 984-222-4183.
notes: Cadets meet at the Raleigh Police Youth Services Center. It is at 4205 Spring Forest Rd, Raleigh, NC 27616.

name: Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program (RSYEP)
grades: High school student as of May 31, 2027
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The page does not state a pay rate.
duration: Eight weeks: June 14 to August 6, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 application and interviews run January 25 to March 15, 2027. Onboarding with a parent or guardian is April 3, 2027. The program runs June 14 to August 6, 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 and a high school student as of May 31, 2027. You must live inside Raleigh city limits. You cannot be in summer school or school sports during the program, and you cannot miss more than 5 days. Only one person per household is accepted.
how_to_apply: Apply online from January 25 to March 15, 2027, then interview. Bring proof of a Raleigh address to your interview (a school ID without an address does not count). If you get an offer, you need a government ID and must pass a background check, a drug test, and fingerprinting.
notes: You and a parent or guardian must go to onboarding on April 3, 2027 and to the parent orientation (the page lists both May 16 and May 22, 2027, so ask which). A free Skill Up job readiness training is on January 23, 2027. Questions: Rebekah Dixon, rebekah.dixon@raleighnc.gov, 919-996-5722.

name: UNC Health Rex VolunTEEN Program
grades: 10th to 12th grade (finished 9th grade before the program starts)
duration: 8 weeks, June 21 to August 13, 2027. One 4-hour morning or afternoon shift a week, Monday to Friday. Only one absence allowed.
deadline_text: The 2027 Summer application is online only from March 11, 2027 to March 12, 2027. Interviews March 22 to 25, orientation April 26 to 29, and you must volunteer the first week (June 21 to 25).
who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18 in 10th, 11th or 12th grade. You must be done with 9th grade before it starts.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form online. Two adults who know you, 21 or older and not family, email a reference form. This can be a teacher, a school counselor, or a boss. If they call you, go to an interview.
notes: There is also an Academic Year Program (one day a week, 3 to 5 PM, September to May), but it is closed for 2026 to 2027. If accepted, you need a health screening (TB, whooping cough, chicken pox, MMR). Questions: volsvcs1@unchealth.unc.edu or 919-784-3165.

name: Raleigh Youth Council
org: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources, Teen Programs
duration: Meetings every second and fourth Monday of the month, 7 to 8 p.m.
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join by coming to the next meeting.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page names Raleigh and Wake County and lists no other rule.
how_to_apply: Contact Nieya Garland at 984-338-6150, or register on RecLink and go to a meeting.
notes: The page says it is a good way to get school volunteer hours. Teen Programs: Teens@raleighnc.gov, 919-996-2139.

name: TWIG: Teens Working in the Garden (Red Butte Garden)
org: Red Butte Garden, University of Utah
pay_detail: Volunteer and intern roles. Pay is not stated.
duration: Dates not announced
deadline_text: The page says dates, schedules and the application will be announced. It says to check back in the spring.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12 who are ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 before your first shift.
how_to_apply: Check the page in spring for the application link. Email volunteer@redbutte.utah.edu.
notes: Garden work can mean kneeling, weeding and standing on uneven ground.

name: American Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care Training
pay_detail: Babysitting Basics Online costs $45 (4 hours, self-paced, certificate valid 2 years). In-person class prices vary by location.
duration: Online course: about 4 hours; in-person length varies
deadline_text: Ongoing.
who_can_apply: Red Cross says the in-person Babysitter's Training is for ages 11 to 16, and its online Babysitting Basics course is designed for youth 11 and older.
how_to_apply: Pick a class on the Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care page, or buy the online course there.
notes: The old take-a-class/babysitting-training link no longer works, so the page address was updated. Red Cross says these courses do not qualify you for state-licensed child care. Casual babysitting in a private home does not need a work permit per the California child labor guide (2013 edition).

name: American Red Cross Lifeguard and Water Safety Instructor courses
org: American Red Cross (taught by local pools, cities and YMCAs)
pay_detail: Course fees are set by each provider and are not listed on the program pages.
duration: Lifeguarding: about 27 hours in person, or about 6 hours online plus about 21.5 hours in person
deadline_text: Ongoing. Class dates depend on the provider.
who_can_apply: Lifeguarding: at least 15 years old by the last day of class, plus a swim test (swim, tread water, timed event). Water Safety Instructor and Basic Swim Instructor: at least 15 by the end of the course.
how_to_apply: Use Find a Class on the Red Cross lifeguarding page to pick a pool or YMCA class near you, and check the fee.
notes: Final test is a 50-question exam with an 80% pass mark. Certificate lasts 2 years. Before the update this file said Water Safety Instructor needs age 16; the Red Cross page says 15. For lifeguard jobs, check each employer's page for pay and work permit rules.

name: Red River Zoo Wildlife League
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay $125 per trimester for zoo members or $175 per trimester for non-members.
duration: Trimesters during the school year. Saturdays and Sundays, 9 am to 2 pm. At least two 4.5 hour shifts a month, up to four.
deadline_text: The page lists no deadline or trimester dates.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12, described on the page as 14 to 17 years old. Up to 25 teens are picked.
how_to_apply: Register online. Then do an interview. Bring a letter of recommendation. Or bring references from someone outside your family. Call 701.277.9240 to ask about the next trimester.
notes: Up to six teens work each shift.

name: Teen Volunteer Program (A.K. Smiley Public Library)
org: A.K. Smiley Public Library, City of Redlands
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours available.
duration: Fall, winter/spring and summer sessions; length not stated
deadline_text: No specific dates posted. Email to ask what is open now.
who_can_apply: In-person teen volunteers must be at least 16. You send a City of Redlands volunteer application and a liability waiver. If you are 18 or older you also need a LiveScan.
how_to_apply: Email yrr@akspl.org to ask what is open. They send details after you write. Youth Services phone: (909) 798-7674.
notes: The Youth Services volunteer rules say volunteers must commit at least one month and follow the City dress code. The Teens page also lists a Teen Makers and Helpers Lab for ages 13 to 18 with a sign-up form, but gives no details.

name: Junior (Student) Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: One-year commitment, 2-hour shift at least once a week
deadline_text: The page says junior recruitment opens from time to time during the year. No dates posted.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 with a reference from a teacher or school counselor. You must commit for one year.
how_to_apply: The page lists these steps for all volunteers: a volunteer application, an in-person interview, health requirements, a background screening, General Orientation and training. It shows no junior application link or contact, so ask the hospital volunteer office.
notes: Confirm first: no contact or junior application link on the page. The page says the commitment is one year and that junior recruitment opens periodically.

name: Red Rock Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Redwood City Leaders in Training (L.I.T.)
org: City of Redwood City Parks, Recreation and Community Services
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $88 for session 1, $98 for sessions 2 and 3, $49 for session 4
duration: 1 to 2 weeks per session
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened April 20 and were due May 8, 2026; interviews May 18 to 21; training June 13. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15; you must be 13 by the first training day. Written application, then an interview if selected. At most 20 L.I.T.s per session. Redwood City camps.
how_to_apply: Download the L.I.T. application and email it to tbrent@redwoodcity.org by the deadline. If chosen you interview, then get camp placement and payment instructions. Phone 650-780-5929.
notes: Teens pay a fee to take part (2026: $88, $98, $98 or $49 depending on session). The fee is due after a successful interview. Placement depends on camp needs. A mandatory Saturday training is required. 2027 dates are not posted, so expect a similar April to May window and watch the page.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the program pages; more than $7 million in awards and prizes
duration: May 2027
deadline_text: ISEF is in Los Angeles in May 2027 (exact dates not posted on the program pages). Affiliated fairs end by mid-April, and each fair sets its own deadline, so find yours now.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 or equivalent. You cannot enter ISEF directly; you must win at a Society-affiliated fair. Use the Find-a-Fair tool for California fairs.
how_to_apply: Use Find-a-Fair on the Society for Science site, then register with your school or regional fair.
notes: Projects can include no more than 12 months of continuous research. The 2027 ISEF is in California, which can lower travel costs for California finalists. The ISEF site says students from nearly every state in the U.S. and more than 60 countries, regions, and territories compete at affiliated fairs.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the program pages; $3.1 million in annual awards, $250,000 first place
duration: Application June 1 to November 5, 2026
deadline_text: Applications close Nov 5, 2026 at 8 p.m. ET (opened June 1, 2026). Top 300 announced Jan 7, 2027; Top 40 announced Jan 21, 2027; finals week Mar 11 to 17, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in their last year of high school who live and attend school in the US or its territories, any citizenship. You need your own original research with real data, plus essays, a paper of up to 20 pages, recommendations and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Society for Science application portal (sciencetalentsearch.smapply.org).
notes: Seniors only, so juniors should plan for next fall. Test scores are optional. Homeschooled students may apply.

name: Regional Medical Center Junior Volunteer Program
org: Santa Clara Valley Healthcare, Regional Medical Center
duration: At least 12 consecutive months and 144 hours
deadline_text: Closed now. The junior application window opens January 1, 2027 and closes January 7, 2027. Applications sent at other times are not considered.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. You must give at least one 3 to 4 hour shift each week, for at least 144 hours and 12 months in a row. No summer-only or school-break-only volunteering. Spanish and Vietnamese skills are a plus.
how_to_apply: Apply online between Jan 1 and Jan 7, 2027. Send the reference form to RMCVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org. If you are a good fit, you get a phone interview. Then you do an online orientation, a health check, a background check and training at the hospital.
notes: Read on the official Regional Medical Center page on 2026-10-16. You must be fully vaccinated and upload immunization records and a TB test for the health clearance. After 6 months and 100 hours you may qualify for shadowing. Have your reference form ready before Jan 1 since the window is only one week. Benefits include free parking and a free flu shot after one year.

name: City of Reno Junior Lifeguards
org: City of Reno Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
pay_detail: The class fee is $100.
duration: 4 days, 8:30am to 1:30pm each day
deadline_text: The 2026 sessions listed are Oct 5 to 8 and Dec 28 to 31. No registration deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 14 by the first session date. You must pass a swim test: 25 yards of front crawl, a step into deep water with a 10 foot underwater swim, and 1 minute of treading water.
how_to_apply: Pick a session on the program page. Each session links to a registration page, and the site has an Online Registration link. For questions, call Parks Administration at 775-334-2262.
notes: This is a good step toward the City of Reno lifeguard class, which starts at age 15. You must attend every day of a session to be certified.

name: City of Reno Red Cross Lifeguarding Class
org: City of Reno Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
pay_detail: The class costs $140. The page says the city will certify you for free if you are hired and onboarded by the class start date.
duration: In-person class days run 9am to 3:30pm. The class is blended, with online lecture and in-class training.
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated. The 2026 class dates run from Sept 19 to Dec 24, 2026.
who_can_apply: You must be 15 by the final scheduled session. You must also pass a swim test. Swim 150 yards, then tread water for 2 minutes using only your legs. Swim 50 yards. Then finish a timed event in 1 minute 40 seconds: a 20 yard swim, a dive to 10 feet for a 10 pound object, a swim back, and an exit without a ladder.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Online button for a class, or join the interest list by email. To get the free certificate, apply online for a city job. Be onboarded by the class start date.
notes: You must attend every day of the class to be certified. A shorter $124 renewal class is for people with a valid lifeguard certificate, or one that ended in the last 30 days. The program page does not say if a work permit is needed.

name: City of Reno Parks Volunteer Program
org: City of Reno Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Drop-in single days, or recurring scheduled tasks
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Under 16 can do drop-in single-day tasks with a parent-signed release form. 16 and older can do continuous volunteering after a background check. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Drop in: a parent signs the Volunteer Release of Liability Form and you sign a time sheet. Ongoing: send in a Volunteer Application, a Consent and Disclosure form and a Reno PD background form. Get a photo ID card. Call the Volunteer Coordinator at 775-334-2046.
notes: The listed roles on the page are mostly for seniors programs and fund raising. Ask the coordinator what fits a teen.

name: Camp Discovery Teen Assistant Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Earns over 80 community service hours.
duration: Camp breaks: fall, winter, spring and summer (Washoe County School District breaks)
deadline_text: No deadline or program dates listed.
who_can_apply: Open to grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Teen Assistant Application button on the page (online form). Then a 15-minute Zoom interview and an in-person training. Contact Kristen Kellogg, 775-398-5920, kkellogg@nvdm.org.
notes: You must be free during Washoe County School District breaks.

name: CBESS Student Researcher Program
org: University of Nevada, Reno Raggio Research Center
pay_detail: Free to attend. A stipend is not mentioned.
duration: One week on campus plus two or more weeks virtual, then monthly mentoring in senior year
deadline_text: No deadline or dates posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Bilingual English and Spanish high school juniors in Northern Nevada. Up to 30 are chosen for the summer program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CBESS Interest Form at nevada.formstack.com/forms/cbess. Questions: cbess@unr.edu or (775) 784-1110.
notes: Chosen students also do an outreach internship. Up to 64 more juniors get a certificate. They must first finish some questionnaires.

name: Engineering Summer Camps for Ages 14 to 17
org: University of Nevada, Reno College of Engineering
pay_detail: Fee not listed on the page. A $50 non-refundable deposit can hold a spot; full payment is due within a month of registering. Scholarships available.
duration: Camp dates not listed on the page
deadline_text: Summer 2027 registration opens February 1 (2027 inferred from the Summer 2027 label on the page).
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Sign up online when it opens on February 1. For a scholarship, add an essay on your interests and a teacher recommendation letter to the form. Questions: paigefroese@unr.edu.
notes: Camp prices and dates were not posted when this was checked. Check back before February.

name: UNR High School Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: $154 per credit for tuition plus an $18 per credit tech fee, plus any class fees.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline is stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Nevada high school students who meet each course's prerequisites. A counselor or vice principal must back you. That lets the classes count toward graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the UNR non-degree student application and the dual enrollment interest form. Send your shot records through the online portal (2 MMR doses and 1 Tdap). Upload your high school transcripts with the Transcript Upload form. Your counselor or vice principal fills out the school district contract form. They email it to DualEnrollment@unr.edu.
notes: Earlier college work can place you into classes. So can SAT or ACT scores, AP or IB scores, or placement tests.

name: Women in STEM High School Outreach Program
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program page.
duration: One school year
deadline_text: The program page lists the 2024 to 2025 application, which opened June 1, 2024 and stayed open until spots were full. No newer dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Nevada high school juniors and seniors. The program is aimed most at girls and young women who have faced barriers to STEM learning and research.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Join Women in STEM page. A paper form can be picked up at the Dean's Office, 4th floor of the Davidson Mathematics and Science Center on campus.
notes: The program page still shows the 2024 to 2025 year. Check with the program before you plan on it. It asks for four events in each of three event series, two advisor meetings and three mentor meetings during the year.

name: Volunteen
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a certificate at 20 hours.
duration: Self-paced, up to 20 hours
deadline_text: No start, end or deadline dates listed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Teen and a parent or guardian both sign the application.
how_to_apply: Online: make a Beanstack account and join the Volunteen Challenge. A coordinator emails the forms. Paper: fill out the online form or ask the volunteer coordinator at your branch.
notes: Paperwork and orientation come first. Both a teen and a parent or guardian must sign.

name: CampMed (free summer health camp)
org: Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science
pay_detail: Free
duration: 5 days, the last week of July
deadline_text: The page gives no application dates. The camp runs during the last week of July.
who_can_apply: Lake County high school students who like health care, science and research.
how_to_apply: Email campmed@rfums.org to ask how to apply.
notes: In person only. Ask when applications open.

name: INSPIRE: Summer research and mentoring for Lake County students
org: Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science
grades: High school and college students from Lake County
pay_detail: Pay or stipend is not stated on the program page. Ask the program.
duration: 8 weeks in summer
deadline_text: The INSPIRE 2026 application is closed. The page says the INSPIRE 2027 application will open in December 2026.
who_can_apply: Lake County students. High school students who live near the Rosalind Franklin University campus come first.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for INSPIRE link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026.
notes: Check whether it pays. Students can come back every summer until they finish a bachelor's degree. To reach the program, write to Rachael Lange at rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu or call 224-570-7325.

name: Nursing INSPIRE (paid summer program)
org: Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science
pay_detail: Described as a paid educational opportunity. The amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: 8 weeks, four days a week, June to August
deadline_text: The page still shows the last cycle it read: applications opened December 10, 2024 and closed January 23, 2025. Newer dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Juniors in good standing with a GPA of 2.0 out of 4.0 or higher and an interest in nursing. Applications are for juniors at Cristo Rey St. Martin College Prep, Highland Park, North Chicago, Round Lake and Waukegan High Schools.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More link on the Nursing INSPIRE page to find the form. To reach someone, write to Dr. Mosilda Asanji at mosilda.asanji@rosalindfranklin.edu.
notes: Only students at the five schools named can apply. The page looks about two cycles old (it shows 2024-25 dates), so ask the program for current dates. Parents join a session on financial planning for college.

name: Science Saturdays
org: Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science
pay_detail: Free. Lunch and transportation are provided.
duration: 9 Saturdays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., June to August
deadline_text: The Science Saturdays 2026 application is closed. For 2027 the application will open in December 2026.
who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a school list or grade rule beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Science Saturdays link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026. Contact: Rachael Lange, rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu, 224-570-7325.
notes: Only about 25 students are chosen each year.

name: Virtual Mentor Program
org: Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science
grades: Local high school and undergraduate students
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings, October to May
deadline_text: Registration closes November 30, 2026.
who_can_apply: Local high school and college students who like health care or science.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for the Virtual Mentor Program link on the pathway programs page. It opens a Google form (forms.gle). You must attend an orientation before being matched.
notes: Online, so you do not need to travel to North Chicago.

name: Richmond Fund for Children and Youth Oversight Board (youth seats)
org: City of Richmond Department of Children and Youth
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The application says members get training, childcare, meals and translation help at meetings.
duration: One-year term if you are under 24
deadline_text: The page lists 7 open seats as of 9/29/2026. It gives no closing date.
who_can_apply: People who live in Richmond or North Richmond and are 15 or older. If you are 15 to 17, a parent or guardian must approve. Some seats are set aside for youth who are 15 to 24 years old. You must be able to go to at least 6 meetings a year and give at least 50 hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Oversight Board Application, a PDF on the city page. A parent or guardian signs it if you are under 18. Email it to the City Clerk or mail it to the City Clerk's office at the address on the form.
notes: The board meets every first Monday at 6:00 PM in the Richmond City Council Chamber, 440 Civic Center Plaza. City Council members and the Mayor pick the members. The application says you can learn more at richmondyouth.org or by calling 510-620-6523. Having work or school experience is not required.

name: Junior Naturalist Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: One 4-hour training and at least 10 morning shifts (8:45 am to 12:15 pm) in the summer camp season (2026: June 1 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: No deadline listed on the page, which describes the 2026 camp season.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Add a one-page cover letter. Add one letter from a teacher, boss or volunteer leader. Email volunteer@maymont.org or call 804-525-9000.
notes: Ask the volunteer lead for the 2027 dates.

name: Mayor's Youth Academy Summer Program
org: City of Richmond, Office of Community Wealth Building
pay_detail: Paid by the employer or by the Academy. The youth pay rate is not stated on the FAQ page.
duration: Work experience about 6 weeks, early July to mid-August; mandatory training in May
deadline_text: Applications open each year on March 1. Work Experience notices go out by email in the second week of April.
who_can_apply: City of Richmond residents who are in school. Counselors in Training: ages 14 to 16 (14 by July 1). Summer Work Experience: ages 16 to 19 (16 by July 1, not 19 before the program ends).

name: Tween and Teen Volunteers and Book Buddies (summer)

name: Teen Advisory Boards (branch libraries)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated

name: Riverside County Youth Opportunity Centers (WIOA youth services)

Centers are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Phone numbers: Indio (760) 802-6059, Hemet (951) 765-0917, Moreno Valley (951) 653-1311, Perris (951) 657-7105, Rubidoux (951) 683-9622. Do not email your Social Security number. Paid work under 18 in California needs a work permit.

name: Riverside County Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Councils

Commission meetings are public, in the Board Chambers in Riverside. The paid Legislative Intern jobs that run the councils are for college students only.

name: Round Rock Lifeguard Training and Seasonal Aquatics Jobs
org: City of Round Rock Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Lifeguard pay shown as $15 to $19.50 per hour (from a graphic on the page; a separate rate sheet is the official source). Training costs $215 to $305, or $75 if you sign a full season work commitment. Scholarships are available.

deadline_text: No application deadline is listed. The 2026 classes ran Mar 16 to May 30, 2026. The program page links a 2027 class flyer.
who_can_apply: Must be 15 or older before the last class. Must pass a swim test: swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes, then swim 50 yards, and retrieve a 10 pound object from 7 to 10 feet.
how_to_apply: Sign up for training at roundrockrecreation.com. Then apply for jobs on the city job portal. To get the $75 rate, email the signed Commitment Letter to pardcustomerservice@roundrocktexas.gov. Call 512-218-5540 with questions.
notes: It is smart to apply early. If you pass the class, you get Lifeguard, CPR/AED and First Aid cards. They are good for 2 years. You must come to every class.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)

pay_detail: Free to students. There is a $75 application fee that you cannot get back. Ask CEE for a fee waiver if you need one.

Fee waivers may be available for need.

name: Teen Volunteer Program at Rush Copley Medical Center

name: Teen volunteers at Sacramento Public Library

name: Sacramento Youth Commission

notes: Appointed by the Mayor and City Council, so not every applicant is picked. The FAQ says the $50 stipend applies to the 1st and 3rd monthly meetings. No experience needed. Seats open at different times; check the Become a Commissioner page. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Zoo Teens

deadline_text: Applications opened online Oct 10, 2026 for Zoo Teens 2027 (Jan to April). Closing date not stated.

Cosumnes Fire Explorers are ages 15 to 18 (juniors and seniors), 2.0 GPA, and applications for next school year open in spring 2027.

name: Sacramento SPCA Youth Service Projects

name: High School Summer Research Internship (University of Utah Engineering)
