pay_detail: Youth fee is $25 if you enroll by October 31 and $30 from November 1 through the end of the 4-H year.
duration: One 4-H year. Every membership resets to inactive on August 15, so you re-enroll each year.
deadline_text: Enroll by October 31 for the lower fee ($25). After that the fee is $30 until the end of the 4-H year. Memberships reset every August 15.
who_can_apply: Youth in 3rd through 12th grade, ages 8 to 18. Each county sets up its own program.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office. Find a club. It needs at least five youth from three families. Choose at least one project. Then enroll online in 4HOnline.
notes: The October 31 date is the price cutoff, not a closing date. Counties customize their programs, so call your county Extension office first. This is a club and leadership program, not a paid job.

name: Texas 4-H Ambassador Teams
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: Each team posts its own dates. Examples on the page: Fashion and Interior Design March 1 to 31, 2026. STEM July 1 to 31. Shooting Sports opens June 1. Photography opens in spring.
who_can_apply: Texas 4-H members in high school. STEM Ambassadors must be 15 or older. Photo Ambassadors must first finish training as a Junior Master Photographer.
how_to_apply: Pick a team on the Texas 4-H Ambassadors page, then use that team application or contact. Some teams post their details on their own sites.
notes: You need to be an enrolled 4-H member. The Water Ambassadors dates on the page looked out of date, so check that team's own site.

name: Texas 4-H Council
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: 2026 Council training was July 27 to 30, 2026 in College Station. Ask your District 4-H Specialist for the district application deadline. The page does not list an At-Large deadline.
who_can_apply: Older Texas 4-H members. Peers vote for district delegates. Six At-Large Delegates are voted in across the state.
how_to_apply: Send in the 2026-2027 At-Large Delegate application and the 2026-2027 Council Membership Contract. Or run in your district. Ask your District 4-H Specialist for the district due date.
notes: All delegates must sign the council contract for 2026-2027. Both kinds of delegate sign it.

name: Texas Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of Texas
grades: Just finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: American Legion Posts or other community groups often pay the fee, so the cost to the boy is often little to nothing. The fee amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: One week. The 2026 session ran Sunday June 7 to Friday June 12, 2026.
deadline_text: 2027 dates and the application deadline are not posted on the program pages. The 2026 session ran June 7 to 12, 2026. The site shows an Applications Now Open banner, but it posts no deadline or 2027 dates, so ask your school and local Post.
who_can_apply: Male high school students who finished their junior year. You need at least one semester left. You must never have been to Boys State. School officials must recommend you. You need a parent or guardian's permission. The sponsoring American Legion Post must certify you. You must sign the Texas Boys State Pledge.
how_to_apply: A school official nominates you. That can be a principal, teacher, coach or counselor. A local American Legion Post certifies and sponsors you. Ask your counselor or contact your local Post. The program's site is texasboysstate.com.
notes: Boys State is for boys. Girls State is a separate program. The site says the program asks for one or more boys nominated from each accredited public or private high school. Top delegates may be picked for Boys Nation. Confirm the 2027 dates and fee with your local Post.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Texas Bluebonnet Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Texas
grades: Junior year (11th grade) of high school
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per delegate, not including travel to Seguin. Rules say a unit, school or community group pays it, never the student or her family.
duration: One week. The 2026 session was Sunday June 14 to Saturday June 20, 2026.
deadline_text: 2027 dates are not posted. In 2026, units could reserve spots Feb 1 to May 1 and schools Feb 15 to May 1. The page says spots fill fast, so act quickly.
who_can_apply: Female students now in their junior year at any Texas public or private high school. An ALA Unit may sponsor a home school student who meets the rules. You can attend only once. A student whose religion does not allow her to pledge allegiance to the U.S. flag is not eligible. You must be able to take part in all activities.
how_to_apply: You do not apply on your own. A school nominates you through faculty and a school official, and a local ALA Unit, the school or a community group reserves the spot. Ask your counselor or a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit early in the spring. Questions: GirlsState@alatexas.org or 214-733-7945.
notes: Girls State is for girls. Texas Boys State is a separate program run by the American Legion. Students chosen must attend the whole session to earn the certificate and pin.

name: Texas Brigades Camps (Cadet)
city: Camps across Texas (Rising Star, La Pryor, McCoy, Freer, Santa Anna, Garwood, Anahuac)
pay_detail: Camp price not stated on the program pages. The site says tuition help is available. Email camps@texasbrigades.org.
duration: 5 days
deadline_text: 2027 applications open Nov 1, 2026 and close March 15, 2027. The 2026 camps ran June 7 to Aug 1, 2026.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, from incoming 8th graders to incoming seniors. Apply as a Cadet. Past camp graduates can later apply as Assistant Leaders.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with two essay questions and a list of achievements. Rank your top three camp choices.
notes: Camp phone 210-556-1391. Assistant Leaders can earn college scholarships. Camps listed for 2026 include Bobwhite, Buckskin, Ranch, Bass, Waterfowl and Coastal Brigades.

name: Texas ChalleNGe Academy
pay_detail: Free. The page says the program is tuition free to the families it serves.
duration: The page lists a tuition-free 22-week residential program. It also lists a 20-week Residential Phase and a 5 and a half month on-campus phase, then a 12-month Post-Residential Phase. The page says the program requires a 17 and a half month commitment. Confirm with a recruiter.
deadline_text: Recruitment is open now for the January 2027 cohort. Classes start in January and July. The application cutoff is normally no later than 30 days before class starts (so about early December 2026 for January 2027).
who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 and a half to 18 who are U.S. citizens and Texas residents and are physically and mentally able to take part fully. The program is for youth who are currently disengaged from school.
how_to_apply: Go to an information briefing with a recruiter. Send the application packet and documents. Do a virtual interview with a case manager. Have a mentor fill out a mentor packet. Then a review board decides. Main line: 877-822-0050.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 600 HWY 3013 West, Eagle Lake, TX 77434.

name: Summer Junior Volunteer Program (North Austin)
grades: Enrolled in high school for the following school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: About 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (June 1 to June 25 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 application opened Monday Feb 9 and closed Friday Feb 13, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 by June 1 of the program year and enrolled in high school for the next school year. The flyer describes the program as ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, upload two recommendation letters from two different references, and upload your most recent report card. Accepted volunteers must show vaccine records (MMR, varicella, Tdap) and a negative TB test, and attend mandatory orientation on the first two days.
notes: The flyer calls the program prestigious and highly sought-after, so expect competition. Up to two absences are allowed. There are no weekend or make-up shifts. Questions: ATXNCVolunteerServices@texaschildrens.org or 737-229-3388. Check the Texas Children's volunteer pages for the 2027 flyer.

name: Texas DECA (high school)
org: Texas DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
pay_detail: Student membership is $16 total: $8 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local costs.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership deadlines come from your chapter advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 25 to 27, 2027 at the George R. Brown Convention Center in Houston.
who_can_apply: Students at a Texas high school with a DECA chapter. Texas DECA members must take part in a career and technical education (CTE) program. Chapters must offer business or marketing courses. The official pages list no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Josh Shankle, shankle@texasdeca.org. State office phone: 817-900-8037.
notes: DECA's page lists 352 Texas high school chapters. The state website does not explain joining step by step, so start with your school's advisor.

name: Texas Envirothon
org: Environmental Institute of Houston, University of Houston-Clear Lake
city: Statewide, TX (state event in Nacogdoches in 2026)
pay_detail: A non-refundable team registration fee is required each year. The amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: 3 day state event
deadline_text: 2026 state event: March 28 to 30, 2026 in Nacogdoches. Page says registration opens in 2026 with the deadline to be announced.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12, or the home school match. You join a team of five from the same school or group. The team has an adult advisor.
how_to_apply: Contact the Texas Envirothon office at 281-283-3045 or reistle@uhcl.edu. Then send in the sign-up packet and the fee. You must show proof of health insurance.
notes: Teams need an adult advisor plus chaperones of each gender. The school or group pays for travel, meals and lodging. Teams with fewer than five can play but may lose points on the oral part.

name: Texas FFA Association
grades: Agricultural science classes start no earlier than 7th grade. Junior FFA starts at 3rd grade.
pay_detail: National dues $7 plus Texas dues $9 is $16 a year, not counting area, district or local dues. Junior FFA is $9 a year (state only).
duration: School year, tied to your agricultural science class
deadline_text: No application deadline. You join through your school's agriculture program.
who_can_apply: Students who sign up for an agricultural science class at a school with an FFA chapter. The FAQ says the grade depends on the district and that home-schooled students are not covered by the program. Junior FFA needs age 8 and 3rd grade.
how_to_apply: Your first contact is your local agricultural science teacher. Sign up for an agricultural science class.
notes: Junior FFA is a state-only membership at $9 a year, says the membership page.

name: Texas HOSA Future Health Professionals
grades: Middle school grades 6 to 8, and high school (secondary) students
pay_detail: There are membership fees, but the amounts are not on the program pages. The site links to a 2026 to 2027 fee schedule.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No membership deadlines or conference dates are on the program pages. Ask your advisor for dates.
who_can_apply: Secondary students in a state-approved Health Science program, or who plan a career in the health professions. Middle school students in grades 6 to 8 who like a health career path can also join. Membership goes through affiliated school chapters.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's health science teacher or chapter advisor about joining the chapter. State office: texashosa@texashosa.org or 1-877-728-0150.
notes: State office: 201 W. Hillside Road Suite 26, Laredo, TX 78041. Ask your advisor for the fee amount and conference dates.

name: Texas State Parks Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ mentions no volunteer fees or costs.
duration: Varies by opening
deadline_text: Apply any time. Openings are listed in the online portal.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 16 must come with a parent or guardian. Everyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's signed permission, and a parent signs the liability waiver. Each opening can add its own requirements. Minors cannot do some kinds of work.
how_to_apply: Search openings in the TPWD volunteer portal and apply online. Or contact a park's volunteer coordinator. TPWD checks your application and matches you to an opening. Questions: Volunteer@TPWD.Texas.gov or 512-389-8674.
notes: Park host jobs are long RV-based stays and are not a fit for most teens. The page lists Buffalo Soldiers, State Park Ambassadors and Texas Outdoor Family as special programs, but this card does not cover their age rules. Volunteers 18 and older in ongoing roles must pass a yearly background check.

name: REACT @ TAMU Chemistry (summer research training)
org: Texas A&M University, Department of Chemistry
grades: High school students (the 2026 page says as of Fall 2026)
pay_detail: Applying is free. The registration fee is $250, due after you are accepted (2026 page). Lunch is provided.
duration: The 2026 header lists July 13 to 24, 2026 and also calls it a 6-day in-person program. The 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: The 2027 application opens Jan 19, 2027. No closing date is posted. In 2026, students were notified April 24, 2026.
who_can_apply: High school students who finished at least one high school chemistry course before the summer. The pages give no grade, age or residency rule. You need a recommendation from a high school chemistry teacher. Selection is merit based and space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, which includes a short chemistry research statement. The form sends a request to your chemistry teacher for the recommendation. Questions: tamu_react@tamu.edu.
notes: The program ran for the first time in 2025 (July 14 to 25). The fee and rules above come from the 2026 pages, so check them again when the 2027 application opens. The program site is a Google Sites page run by the department.

name: Summer Earn and Learn (SEAL) for students with disabilities
org: Texas Workforce Commission, Vocational Rehabilitation, with local workforce boards
pay_detail: Wages for hours worked. Each local board sets one hourly wage for its program. The amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: At least five weeks of paid work, with at least four hours in a week to count as a week. No more than 40 hours a week.
deadline_text: No dates for summer 2027 are posted on the program pages. It is a summer program. Ask your local office in the fall or winter.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 22 (and under 22 as of September 1 of the previous year) who get special education services under IDEA or have a disability under Section 504, and who are in an educational program. That includes secondary school, home school and other recognized programs.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions Vocational Rehabilitation Services office. Counselors refer current VR participants. Students who have not applied for VR but meet the disability rule may also be candidates. Statewide contact: 512-936-6400 or vr.office.locator@twc.texas.gov.
notes: Only for students with disabilities. Texas child labor hour limits for 14 and 15 year olds still apply. The pages do not give a posted 2027 timeline.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Texas Wing
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Year-round program with squadron meetings, plus encampments and other events
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend three squadron meetings first.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18. You must be in school or a graduate with a satisfactory record. You must be unmarried (except marriage under 18) and not on active duty. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive). You must be of good moral character. Cadets who join before age 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Pick a local squadron from the Texas Wing unit listing. Go to three squadron meetings as a trial. The squadron and higher headquarters must accept you. Call Wing headquarters at 936-205-9013 with questions.
notes: Meeting times differ by squadron. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

name: Texas Youth Range Workshop
org: Texas Section, Society for Range Management
pay_detail: Program fee not stated on the page. Organizers say they can help applicants find sponsors.
duration: 1 week
deadline_text: 2026 workshop was June 21 to 26, 2026. The 2026 deadline and 2027 dates were not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 from across Texas.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked from the workshop website. Questions: tssrmyrw@gmail.com.
notes: Check the site for the 2027 application. Sponsor contacts: Dorian Damerau 830-387-8429 or Jr. Tompkins 979-541-3411.

name: Growing Leaders (Thanksgiving Point)
pay_detail: Volunteer. Teens earn incentives. The page does not name them.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page.
notes: The volunteer page lists the program for events, summer camps and more.

name: SheTech Internship (Thanksgiving Point)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. Interns in some roles get a Thanksgiving Point Team Member Membership.
duration: 40 hours per semester for the district credit; some roles need more
deadline_text: Dates and deadlines are not posted on the page.
who_can_apply: High school girls. The page does not list grades. The program is accredited through Alpine School District for the fall and spring semesters only.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page. Questions: Stacie Wilding, swilding@thanksgivingpoint.org, 801-768-7426.
notes: The page says the credit is for fall and spring semesters only.

name: The Trade Collective (skilled trades student sign-up)
grades: High school students and recent graduates
pay_detail: Not stated. The student page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask the group.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Students or recent high school graduates who want to learn about skilled trades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student intake form on the Student page. Parents can email info@thetradecollective.org.
notes: The page does not list specific internships or pay. It says the group is forming partnerships with high schools, colleges and universities. Address on the site: 1910 Greenwood Street, Evanston.

name: Library Volunteer and Teen Volunteer
org: Topeka and Shawnee County Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The library keeps an application on file for 30 days; apply again if you have not heard back.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 13 years old or accompanied by an adult while on duty.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the library website. You may be interviewed. Volunteers are chosen by their qualifications. The library's needs at the time also count. Call or email the volunteer contact listed on the page with questions.
notes: Quote from the volunteer policy: Volunteers must be at least 13 years old or accompanied by an adult while on duty. The page links to a separate Teen Volunteer path. This card does not cover it in detail.

name: EcoClub (grades 5 to 12)
pay_detail: $125 per student for the whole school year (includes a t-shirt). A scholarship fund application is linked on the page.
duration: 1st and 3rd Tuesday of the month, 5:15 to 6:45 pm, during the school year
deadline_text: You may join at any time during the year. The 2026-27 meeting dates are linked on the page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12. Please RSVP before attending.
how_to_apply: RSVP, then pay online from the zoo page. A scholarship form is there too.
notes: This is a club, not a job. Meets at the Gary K. Clarke Education Center at the zoo, entering through the front admission gate.

name: Individual Volunteer (Tracy Aviary)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a free annual family membership after 20 volunteer hours.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Individual volunteers must be at least 15. Younger teens can volunteer with an adult. They fill out the Family Volunteer form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Individual Volunteer form on the page.
notes: Group service projects for 5 to 25 people are also offered. Court ordered service is for 18 and older only.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: Travis County Health and Human Services with Austin Public Health
pay_detail: Paid work experience; hourly rate not stated on the program page
duration: 5 to 7 weeks
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. The county says applications for Summer 2027 open in January 2027 (exact date not posted). Fill out the 2027 interest form to be told when they open.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 18 (14 by April 1) and in middle or high school, and must live and/or attend school in Travis County. Teens with disabilities can apply up to age 22. Other factors such as household income may also be considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (Jotform) and upload a Social Security card and a school ID or recent report card. Eligible applicants are invited to a mandatory job readiness training, then matched to a host site if space allows. Applying does not guarantee a placement.
notes: Phone 512-854-4590, syep@traviscountytx.gov. Up to 750 paid spots each year. Pay rate and hours are not stated on the page. The page does not mention a work permit. Texas rules for 14 and 15 year olds limit hours (see Texas Workforce Commission child labor page). The SAFE Alliance Summer Youth Leadership Academy also hires through this program.

name: TreePeople Volunteer Events (all ages with parent consent)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Single events; calendar posted at least a month ahead
deadline_text: Sign up for each event on the Events Calendar. No program deadline.
who_can_apply: No age limit. Minors need a signed parental consent form. Volunteers 15 and under (the FAQ says under 15) need an adult chaperone age 21 or older, one adult per 10 young volunteers.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the TreePeople events calendar. The confirmation email has the waiver and parent consent forms. Groups can email volunteer@treepeople.org to ask if there is room.
notes: TreePeople's jobs page lists only an 18+ fellowship, so this is the way in for teens. The page gives two versions of the chaperone age rule (15 and under vs under 15), so confirm by email.

name: Youth Tree Team
grades: Currently in high school or about to start high school
pay_detail: Starting at $12 per hour
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 12:30 pm
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: opened Nov 15, 2025, closed Feb 2, 2026, job ran June 1 to July 17, 2026. The page says 2027 details are coming later.
who_can_apply: Teens who are in high school or about to start, and at least 14 as of May 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link is posted. You must finish every step. These are a required Challenge Day, a required volunteer tree planting and an interview.
notes: Competitive. Not everyone who applies gets a job. Returning members can apply for outside study spots with partner groups. 2026 dates are shown. Watch the page for the 2027 schedule. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit (employment certificate) is required for minors under 16, so 14 and 15 year olds need one. A school issuing officer or the county school superintendent gives it.

name: Tri-Valley ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
fields: trades; health; tech-cs; engineering; education; law-government
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026-2027 school year is closed. Talk to your school's College and Career Specialist or counselor.
who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.

name: Tri-Valley Teen Job and Career Fair
org: City of Dublin, with San Ramon, Pleasanton, Danville and the Dublin/San Ramon Women's Club
city: San Ramon, CA (Alcosta Senior and Community Center)
pay_detail: Free to attend. This is a fair, not a job.
duration: One afternoon, 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.
deadline_text: Saturday, February 27, 2027, 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. The program page does not describe registration.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 in the Tri-Valley area.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say whether you must register. It says to bring several copies of your resume and to dress professionally.
notes: Location: 9300 Alcosta Blvd, San Ramon. The program page does not list which employers will come. Questions: Dublin City Hall, 100 Civic Plaza, 925-833-6650.

name: Trybe Summer Jobs and Paid Internships (East Oakland)
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).
duration: About 100 hours
deadline_text: The Trybe page shows only a 2022 Youth Summer Internship, marked closed (applications were due May 31, 2022). No 2026 or 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Current rules are not posted. The 2022 posting said youth 16 and over with valid photo ID and a valid SSN or ITIN were paid; younger youth got a stipend. Confirm with the program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 985-9915 or email info@oaklandtrybe.org. Trybe also has a Jobs/Internships page on its site.
notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.

name: Summer Medical Camp
org: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso, Foster School of Medicine
grades: Current or rising high school student
pay_detail: Snacks and learning materials are free. Camp cost is not stated on the program page.
duration: Two weeks per session
deadline_text: The 2026 camps ran June 8 to 18 and June 22 to July 2. Dates for the next camp will be announced closer to next summer.
who_can_apply: Current or rising high school students who are interested in a medical career and can attend in person from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. every day.
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe an application. It says students hear about the camp when staff visit high schools in the El Paso region. Call René André at 915-215-4408.
notes: The program page has a link named Summer Med Camp Mentor. The page gives no details about that role.

name: Tucker Youth Council
pay_detail: Unpaid civic role
duration: One-year term. Meetings on the third Wednesday, September to April.
deadline_text: The 2026 council application closed Aug 19, 2026. Meetings: 9/16, 10/21, 11/18, 1/20, 2/24, 3/17, 4/21, with optional dinner 4/26 and celebration 5/7. The next application is not posted.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors who live in the City of Tucker.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the city's Youth Council page. Members may reapply at the end of their term.
notes: The page lists no direct phone or email; it links to the city's Contacting the City page. The page does not post the next application date. Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Teen Volunteer (ages 15 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Can count for school service hours.
duration: You choose hours on the application (daily, weekly, monthly or one time).
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Tell them your due date if you need service hours.
who_can_apply: Teens 15 and older. A guardian enters their name to consent for a minor.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the volunteer page. You give contact info, free times, hours wanted, consent from a guardian and photo permission. Call (520) 792-9985 with questions.
notes: The museum hours listed on the page disagree, so confirm shift times.

name: Junior Staff in Training
org: City of Tucson Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Registration fee $25 for City residents, $30 for non-residents. The page does not say participants are paid. A discount program exists for low-income families.
duration: Up to 30 hours per week. Program dates not listed.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Teens and parents must attend an orientation. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Call Class Registration at 520-791-4877 or use the Register for Classes link on the page. Orientation details are emailed after you sign up. A Discount Program is there for people who need low income help.
notes: Aims at recreation careers. Contact 520-791-4873 for the schedule.

name: City Lifeguard Jobs and Starguard Classes
org: City of Tucson Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Starts at $16.75 per hour
duration: Starguard class days listed on the page, then June and July work
deadline_text: Swim tests Nov 1 and Nov 29, 2026, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Sign up for a swim test at the link. Starguard class days on the page (no years printed; the page footer reads 2026): Oct 4, 10, 11 (already passed as of 2026-10-13); Nov 14, 15, 21, 22; Dec 12, 13, 19, 20.
who_can_apply: Must be 15 when you apply. Must pass the swim test. Must be free to work all of June and July.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a swim test at tucsonparks.info/lifeguardfallswimtest. The page gives no other form. If you have questions, send an email to cotlifeguard@tucsonaz.gov or call 520-837-8119.
notes: The page shows 2026 in its footer, so the dates are likely fall 2026, but confirm. Swim test: 300 yard front crawl, 50 yard approach stroke with rescue tube, treading water, 50 yard side stroke with a dummy, 10 lb brick retrieval.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated. Teens track hours with a log.
deadline_text: No deadlines listed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form (PDF on the page) and give it to the library branch where you want to volunteer. The library contacts you if there is an opening.

name: Disadvantaged High School Student Summer Research Program

name: 4-H Healthy Living Ambassadors Club

name: Tustin Counselor in Training (C.I.T.) Program

name: Tustin Police Explorer Post 615
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

notes: You must finish an explorer academy in your first year. The page lists two phone numbers, 714-573-3197 and 714-573-3297. Confirm the number before you call.

name: Tustin Teens in Action

pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

name: Allina Health hospital and clinic volunteers (ages 15 and up)

name: Rooted in STEM

name: Walker Art Center Teen Arts Council (WACTAC)

name: COSMOS at UC Irvine (California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science)

name: UCI School of Medicine Summer Online Research Program
pay_detail: $2,350 for each 3-week session. Limited scholarships are for low-income families at underserved Southern California high schools.
duration: 3 weeks. In 2026 the sessions were June 22 to July 10 and July 13 to July 31.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. The page says the program typically closes to new applications by the end of January or the beginning of February. It reviews applications on a rolling basis.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 with a 3.3 unweighted GPA or higher. You should be interested in healthcare research.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Email your transcript to highschoolresearch@hs.uci.edu. An unofficial copy is fine. You then get a signed confirmation by email.
notes: For a scholarship you write an essay and give family tax information. Tax forms are due before acceptance. The page still mentions the 2025 program in its scholarship text, so ask the program to confirm the details.

name: UCI Summer Healthcare Experience
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,550. Ten full scholarships are based on financial need and merit.
duration: 5 days. In 2026 it ran July 27 to 31, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Breakfast and lunch are included.
deadline_text: In 2026, applications opened January 26 and closed February 27. No late applications were accepted. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page. Incomplete applications are not read. For a scholarship, check the scholarship box, send a transcript and answer the scholarship question.
notes: This is not an overnight program. Past students may reapply, but the page says preference goes to students who will benefit most. You get a certificate. Questions: Rachel Do, rkdo@hs.uci.edu.

name: UCLA Health Westwood High School Summer Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not free for student volunteers.
duration: At least 50 hours, finished by August 31
deadline_text: The page says the High School Summer Program is now closed. Information for Summer 2027 will be posted starting January 1, 2027. Hours must be done by August 31.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 by June 1. Grade and residency are not stated. A government photo ID and immunization proof are required.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a required Zoom info session. You get the form by email. Send it back with proof of shots (varicella, MMR, TB test). Then go to one required in-person orientation. Email studentvol@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Info sessions fill fast. Every slot showed FULL or CLOSED when read. The page also points to the Mattel Youth Ambassador program as another option. Santa Monica and West Valley campuses have their own student pages.

name: UCLA Summer Sessions for high school students
pay_detail: Fee-based. Ask UCLA Summer Sessions for current fees. Scholarship programs described on the page include BASE and Summer Scholars Support.
duration: Focus Series: 3 weeks; other formats vary (2026 sessions ran June 22 to July 31)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 enrollment is closed. Summer 2027 programs and dates are not posted yet; the site offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.
who_can_apply: High school students. The Summer Precollege Focus Series requires being at least 15 by the first day of Summer Sessions, and some programs set older ages. Regular summer courses must come from a pre-approved high school list.
how_to_apply: Apply or enroll through each page on summer.ucla.edu. California students in grades 9 to 11 can apply for Summer Scholars Support (need and merit scholarships), and 10th and 11th graders from under-resourced California communities can apply for BASE, a free 6-week online course with a UCLA mentor.
notes: Out-of-state and international students cannot receive UCLA Summer Sessions financial aid. Exact program prices were not found; use UCLA's fee calculator before applying.

name: UCR AI-Enabled Robotics Summer Camp
org: UC Riverside, Bourns College of Engineering
duration: 5 days, 9 AM to 4 PM (July 6 to 10 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was June 6, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. No specific grades or ages are listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Today form at engr.ucr.edu/form/ai-enabled-robotics-summer-camp. Email roboticssummercamp@ucr.edu.
notes: Held at Winston Chung Hall on the UCR campus. Dates and price are from the 2026 camp.

name: UCR STEM Summer Camp (wildfire science)
org: UC Riverside, College of Natural and Agricultural Sciences (XCITE Center)
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the camp page.
duration: 5 days, 9 AM to 4 PM (June 22 to 26 in 2026)
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The 2026 camp ran June 22 to 26, 2026.
who_can_apply: Current high school students in the Inland Empire. No grades or ages are listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Register Now form on the camp page. Email stemsummercamp@ucr.edu or call the XCITE Center at (951) 827-2612.
notes: The 2026 theme was The Science of Fighting Wildfires. Location in 2026: Tomas Rivera Library, 900 University Ave, Riverside. Confirm first: no cost is stated, and the page does not say whether the theme changes each year.

name: STRIDE Summer Stem Cell Research Training (UCR)
org: UC Riverside, Bourns College of Engineering
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.
duration: 5 weeks (June 22 to July 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: Recruitment starts in the fall before the program. No deadline is posted. The 2026 session ran June 22 to July 24, 2026.
who_can_apply: High school students in the Inland Empire (Riverside and San Bernardino counties) who are older than 16 by the program start date. Southern California permanent residents in Inland Empire school districts are encouraged, especially with a referral from a STEM teacher or a UCR outreach program.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the STRIDE page. Email stride@engr.ucr.edu or call (951) 827-5190.
notes: Confirm first: one Apply Now button on the page points to an older 2023 form. The page says applicants must be older than 16 by the program start date and states no maximum age. No stipend or cost is stated. Funded through a CIRM grant.

name: UCR TRIO Pre-College: Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search
pay_detail: Free to join. Only Upward Bound summer participants receive a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Year-round support; UB summer program is 6 weeks (5 weeks bused to campus, final week in residence halls)
deadline_text: The page posts no deadline and does not say applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Ask the TRIO office at (951) 827-4865 or trio@ucr.edu about current openings.
who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to get an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application. Give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu. You can also call the TRIO office at (951) 827-4865.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.

name: COSMOS at UC San Diego
org: UC San Diego (Jacobs School of Engineering) / California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $5,518 (housing, meals, field trips) plus a $46 application fee. Financial assistance form available for California residents. Amounts for 2027 not posted.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 5 to July 31)
deadline_text: 2027 applications open Jan 6, 2027 at 8 a.m. and close Feb 5, 2027. The statewide site gives 5:00 PM in one place and 11:59 pm in another, so confirm the closing time.
who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.

name: Sports Medicine Summer Academy (Research Scholars)
org: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies
pay_detail: $3,500 for the July 2026 session (commuter only; no housing or transportation). A hybrid fall session cost $2,000.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2026: July 6 to July 24)
deadline_text: 2026 summer enrollment closed June 26, 2026; fall 2026 enrollment closed Sept 21, 2026. Summer 2027 dates not posted; you can sign up for notifications on the program page.
who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page. Add the course to your cart. No application or essay is needed. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.

name: UCSF Health Volunteer Program (includes BCH Oakland campus)
org: UCSF Health / UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals
city: Oakland, CA (BCH Oakland) and San Francisco
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months
deadline_text: Registration filled on Oct 13, 2026. The page says to check back Tuesday, January 12, 2027 at 9:30 a.m.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: Volunteers serve at Parnassus, Mission Bay, Mt. Zion and BCH Oakland, on weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found.

name: AgriQuest Youth Summer Camp
org: University of Georgia College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
grades: Current 9th, 10th and 11th graders (rising sophomores, juniors, seniors)
pay_detail: $300 covers housing, meals, instruction, field trip transport and activities. Full scholarships for accepted students with financial need.
duration: 7 days
deadline_text: Applications open Nov 2, 2026 and close March 5, 2027. Decisions by March 19, 2027. Camp is June 6 to 12, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students who finished 9th or 10th grade. You should be truly curious about farming, food, nature science, math and tech.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add your unofficial transcript and two short essays. Add a recommendation form from one or two teachers or counselors.
notes: Questions: agriquest@uga.edu. Cancel 6 or more weeks ahead for a refund minus $50.

name: Young Scholars Program (UGA College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences)
org: University of Georgia, College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
city: Athens, Griffin or Tifton, GA (UGA campuses)
grades: Finished sophomore year of high school (first time in the program)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship, 30 hours a week. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages.
duration: Five weeks (June 1 to July 7 on the page, plus a three day conference July 8 to 10). The page does not show the year.
deadline_text: Last cycle: application opened Nov 3, 2025 and closed Jan 23, 2026. The program page now says the application is closed for this cycle. Next cycle dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who finished sophomore year and are 16 by the program start date. You must have taken one high school lab science course and one semester of algebra. You should be interested in ag, food and environmental science. First time participants only.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with short essays. Pick a campus (Athens, Griffin or Tifton). Add two recommendation letters from science or math teachers. Upload an official transcript.
notes: Not residential. You must arrange your own housing and transport, and travel to the campus daily. Contacts on the page: Athens 706-542-2713, Griffin 770-228-7264, Tifton 229-326-4663. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This program requires age 16.

name: Georgia Ready Summer Institute (UGA)
org: University of Georgia, Office of Academic and Community Engagement
grades: Rising high school seniors (going into senior year), Georgia students
pay_detail: Free to attend. The pages say there is no cost and that housing and meals are included.
duration: One week, residential
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed (the application page says the deadline passed). Dates for the next cycle are not posted. Contact oace@uga.edu for future application cycles.
who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students from across Georgia who are going into their senior year. No other rules are listed on the pages. In 2026 exactly 50 students were chosen from 664 applications.
how_to_apply: Apply through the UGA Admissions application portal when it opens. Ask the Office of Academic and Community Engagement (oace@uga.edu) about future cycles. Admissions phone on the application page: 762-400-8800.
notes: Very competitive: a UGA news story dated Sep 3, 2026 says the program got a record 664 applications for 50 spots. Exact 2026 dates and application requirements were not on the pages the reader could open. The ACE page says there is no cost to attend and describes residence hall living and dining, but does not explicitly say housing and meals are covered.

name: Summer Design Days
org: University of Idaho College of Art and Architecture
pay_detail: $450, or $425 for returning campers. It covers workshops, supplies, room and board. Local students who go home at night can email sdd@uidaho.edu for a different price.
duration: 4 days (June 24 to 27 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran June 24 to 27, 2026. Registration closed June 10, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. No grade or age rule is listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Email sdd@uidaho.edu or call 208-885-1186.
notes: Full refunds were offered only through June 11 in 2026. Check the page next spring for new dates and prices.

name: Mansfield Civics Institute
pay_detail: Free. A US Department of Education grant pays the cost.
duration: 2 weeks (July 5 to 16, 2027)
deadline_text: Applications open November 1, 2026 for the July 5 to 16, 2027 program. A closing date is not posted.
who_can_apply: Montana high school students. The page says sophomores and juniors during the 2025-2026 school year. That wording may be old, so ask the program contact about your grade.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply here form on the program page when it opens. Questions: Annie Zavitz at Annie.Zavitz@mso.umt.edu.
notes: Students live in residence halls and share meals. No closing date is posted, so apply as soon as the form opens.

name: ESTEEM/SER-Quest Summer Program
org: A. James Clark School of Engineering, University of Maryland (Center for Minorities in Science and Engineering)
pay_detail: No cost to students selected (stated on the page). No stipend is stated.
duration: 4 weeks (Jul 7 to Jul 31 in 2026), commuters only
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application deadline Mar 29, 2026; teacher recommendations due Apr 9, 2026; program Jul 7 to Jul 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 12th graders with at least a 3.2 GPA and no C's in math or science, who finished Trigonometry, Chemistry and Pre-Calculus with a B or better, want to study engineering at UMD, and can attend full time for all 4 weeks.
how_to_apply: Online application with an essay and resume, two teacher recommendations (one math, one science), and a virtual interview with the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: The page says taking part does not guarantee admission to UMD. No housing is offered. A free program, not a job, so no work permit.

name: Terp Young Scholars
org: University of Maryland, College Park (Extended Studies)
pay_detail: 2026 package fee: $1,791 campus option or $1,420 online option (3 credits, tuition and fees). Also a $75 application fee and a $275 program deposit that is credited to the bill. Partial scholarships, none above 30% of the package fee.
duration: 3 weeks (Jul 13 to Jul 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: Applications are closed now. The page says the window opens January 6 and closes June 1 (no year printed). The 2026 program ran July 13 to 31, 2026.
who_can_apply: Rising 10th grade through graduating 12th grade. The page does not state a minimum age or a GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and choose a campus or online. Then apply online. You need a transcript, a health insurance card and a card to pay the application fee and deposit. There are no essays or recommendations.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 prices; 2027 prices are not posted. Commuter program: no campus housing except the business course BMGT262. The grade posts to a UMD college transcript. Not a job, so no work permit.

name: Teen Counselor-in-Training (CIT) program
pay_detail: One-time $100 registration fee (orientation, training, t-shirt, certificate, supplies); financial aid available for students who qualify for free or reduced school lunch. CIT service is volunteer time.
duration: Flexible half or full days over the summer
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 are closed. The page says to check back in January 2027 for the next session; an info session is held each February and the 2026 orientation was June 12.
who_can_apply: The page title says ages 12 to 15 (the University youth programs list says 12 to 16). Applicants attend a February info session, interview, and a mandatory one-day orientation in June.
how_to_apply: Attend the free virtual info meeting in February, get the application, sign up for an interview, pay the fee if accepted, then attend orientation. Call 612-301-1210 for questions.
notes: Good first leadership experience for younger teens. Volunteer hours can be logged.

name: Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAV) Camp
org: University of Minnesota, Minnesota CAV program
pay_detail: Free to attend; lunch is provided
duration: One week, day camp
deadline_text: Information about the 2027 camp will be available in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 with an interest in automotive tech, manufacturing, engineering, planning or robotics. Space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Application steps for 2027 are posted early in 2027 on the camp page.
notes: Competitive: 20 spots. Day camp; the page does not mention transportation.

name: National Summer Transportation Institute (NSTI)
org: University of Minnesota Center for Transportation Studies
pay_detail: Free two-week day camp
duration: Two weeks, day camp
deadline_text: Dates and application instructions for the 2027 camp will be announced in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 9 with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, who have completed or can enroll in pre-algebra and are interested in engineering, science, transportation or technology.
how_to_apply: Application information for 2027 is posted early in 2027. Selection process details are on the camp's admission decisions page.
notes: For younger teens. The University's youth programs list shows ages 13 to 16 for this camp.

name: Explore@UNC
pay_detail: $625 per student per week (includes a $50 non-refundable registration and placement fee); some tracks may add a $25 activity fee; lunch and snacks included. Need-based aid for permanent NC residents who are rising seniors.
duration: 1 week. 2027 weeks: June 14-18, June 21-25, June 28-July 2, July 12-16. Commuter only, no residential option.
deadline_text: Not open yet. Pre-registration is planned for mid-December 2026 through mid-January 2027; the page gives no exact opening or closing day. Financial aid paperwork is due January 28, 2027. Placement notices come in early February 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2027, at a high school or homeschooled. Not open to 8th grade or below or to graduates.
how_to_apply: Pre-register online (interest form on the Explore@UNC pages). Pre-registering improves placement chances. Payment details come after placement.
notes: Families must have a local trusted contact. A temporary drop-off pass is $25 for the week and all-day parking is the family's cost. UNC also lists dual enrollment as a visiting student for rising seniors (see summer.unc.edu/dual-enrollment/); its cost was not read. Questions: explore@unc.edu.

name: UNC Summer School Visitor (rising high school seniors)
pay_detail: Summer School tuition applies. Amount is not on this page.
duration: Summer Session 2
deadline_text: The 2027 online application is not open yet and the page lists no opening date. Second Session deadlines: June 3 for rising high school seniors (all documents due), June 15 for other summer visitors. Decision letters begin March 2027.
who_can_apply: Honor roll students who have finished their junior year. International high school students cannot be considered. If you are under 17, you must say you will live with a parent or legal guardian during Summer School.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the Summer Visitor application. Send a transcript. Send a personal statement that names the course. Also send a letter of support from a teacher, principal or counselor.
notes: You can only take courses in Summer Session 2. High school seniors cannot audit courses. The 2027 application is not open yet, so no dates exist to confirm.

name: Union City Youth Commission
duration: August to May
deadline_text: The page lists applications from February 1 to April 1, interviews in April and appointments in May. It gives no year, so treat this as last year's pattern.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.

name: UnityPoint Health Iowa Lutheran Hospital Teen Volunteer (Volunteen)
org: UnityPoint Health - Des Moines, Iowa Lutheran Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers can earn silver cord hours for graduation.
duration: Set number of hours not stated for teens.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: The page says 'Be 14-18 years of age or older' and 'Currently enrolled in high school'.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then do a placement interview and orientation. Other steps are a handbook review, state and national background checks, a health screening, an annual flu shot and a TB test. Email DM_Volunteers@unitypoint.org or call (515) 263-5227.
notes: This card is for Iowa Lutheran Hospital only. Other UnityPoint hospitals in Des Moines have their own volunteer pages; teen rules for them were not read. The health screening, flu shot and TB test take time, so start early.

name: Schwanke Honors Institute
org: University of Montana Davidson Honors College
grades: Students entering their senior year (the 2026 program also allowed 2026 graduates)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $2,800 for tuition, course fees, housing, all meals and program costs. Scholarships are worth about 10 to 50 percent of the cost and need a separate application.
duration: About 10 days (2026 dates: June 10 to 19)
deadline_text: Check back in early 2027 for the 2027 application and dates. 2026 details are shown as an example only.
who_can_apply: In 2026: high school students entering their senior year and 2026 high school graduates. The page says the 2027 details will be updated later.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You fill out a separate scholarship application too. Got a question? Call 406-243-2537. Or send a note to bethany.applegate@umontana.edu.
notes: Students earn two college credits. The page says to check back in early 2027 for updated information and the application.

name: PATHS (University of Utah)
org: University of Utah, Continuing and Community Engagement
pay_detail: Free. Lunch and rides are provided. A one-time $15 registration fee is due if you are accepted (tell the team if that is a problem).
duration: 4 years. Two weeks of summer camp each year.
deadline_text: The page does not post the priority deadline yet. No dates are posted for the next group.
who_can_apply: Current 8th graders who will start high school in the fall and are first-generation college students (no parent finished college in the U.S.). No minimum GPA. Plan to join for all 4 years.
how_to_apply: Apply online with essay answers. A committee picks students.
notes: The page text looks old (it lists a May 30, 2022 deadline). Email or call before you plan around it. For 8th graders only, so it is for students about to start 9th grade.

name: Summer High School Institute (HSI)
pay_detail: Room, board and supplies are paid by funds from the Wyoming Legislature. There is a $325 activity fee. Travel and personal spending are on the student.
duration: Three weeks in June (the exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program pages)
deadline_text: Applications for HSI 2027 opened October 1, 2026. All pieces are due by February 7, 2027.
who_can_apply: Current 10th graders at a public or private high school in Wyoming or homeschooled, who live in Wyoming and plan to return to a Wyoming school. Must stay all three weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online student application. It needs a personal statement. This is an essay of at least 300 words or a video of no more than 4 minutes. It also needs an awards and achievements list and a recommendation letter. Your counselor uploads your transcript.
notes: The how-to-apply page says HSI 2027 applications open October 1 and all pieces are due February 7, 2027. Wyoming students only.

name: U.S. Senate Page Program
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
deadline_text: Padilla's office: opens Oct 13, 2026, closes Oct 26, 2026 for the Spring 2027 session.
who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or one who has completed the sophomore year (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent high school transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office. The page lists Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov as the contact for questions and does not say where to submit, so confirm the submission address with the office. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.

name: United States Senate Youth Program
org: Hearst Foundations, with the California Department of Education
grades: Juniors and seniors (rising juniors and seniors may apply)
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations
duration: Washington Week March 6 to 13, 2027
deadline_text: California's deadline for the 2027 program is October 7, 2026. That date has passed. The page does not give a date for the next cycle.
who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.

name: USC Summer Programs (pre-college)
org: University of Southern California, Summer Programs
pay_detail: 2026 total for domestic students: $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential. That adds tuition $7,401, course materials $300, program fee $325 and health center $104; residential adds $3,440 room and board. Also a $85 nonrefundable application fee and a $1,000 deposit that counts toward the total.
duration: Four weeks, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each class day (2026 classes began June 22)
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines were May 8 for domestic and March 13 for international applicants. 2027 dates and prices are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.

name: USC Viterbi Energy of STEM Summer Camp (free)
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed May 4, 2026 and applicants were told by the end of May. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 in 2026, rising grades 9 to 12. Active MESA, Mission Science and Engineering Transformer students come first. So do students at STEM Center schools. All students are considered.
how_to_apply: When it is open, send a student form and a teacher recommendation. You can use the online form or the PDF. Forms that are not complete are not considered. Contact k12summer@usc.edu.
notes: The page says in person at USC main campus. The USC Viterbi summer programs list calls it virtual. Confirm the format before you count on it.

name: Cyber-AI @ USD
org: University of San Diego, Center for Cyber Security Engineering and Technology
pay_detail: The page does not list a cost. Daily lunch is included.
duration: 5 days, in person
deadline_text: No dates are posted.
who_can_apply: College-bound 10th, 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: The page has no application link. Email cybercenter@sandiego.edu or call (619) 260-4564 to ask about the next session.
notes: Confirm first: the page lists no dates, cost or application. Its wording speaks to parents about investing in the program, so ask whether there is a fee and whether aid is offered.

name: TRIO Upward Bound
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the USD pages.
duration: School year services plus a summer program where students live on campus
deadline_text: Applications for Kearny and Hoover are reviewed on a rolling basis for the next school year. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Current 9th, 10th or 11th graders at Kearny High Educational Complex or Hoover High School. 8th graders who will go to Kearny or Hoover next year are encouraged to apply. Your family must meet federal income guidelines, or neither parent or guardian has a U.S. college degree.
how_to_apply: Check the rules on the Prospective Students page, then fill out the online application for your high school (Kearny or Hoover) on the Apply page. Staff follow up after you apply. Questions go to the Assistant Director for your school (emails on the Apply page).
notes: To stay in the program, go to a monthly meeting after school. Go to at least one workshop or event each fall and spring, and keep at least a 2.5 GPA. USD says it serves 120 students in the school year and 100 in summer.

name: USS Hornet Museum Volunteer (ages 16 and up)
org: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)
deadline_text: The page gives no deadline and does not say applications are rolling or ongoing. Apply through the volunteer form at volgistics.com or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.

name: SEES (STEM Enhancement in Earth Science) Summer High School Intern Program
org: UT Austin Center for Space Research with NASA and the Texas Space Grant Consortium
pay_detail: No stipend. Free for scholarship recipients and for virtual participation; paid participants pay $2,000 tuition (meals, housing, tours and local travel included, travel to Austin not included). Travel scholarships are available.
duration: Online work in June and July plus a 2-week on-site session in Austin (July 5-18 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline: February 22, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. PT, no late applications. 2027 dates are not posted; the page says future funding is not guaranteed.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores or juniors who are 16 by July 5 of the program year, interested in STEM, and U.S. citizens. Past SEES interns cannot repeat.
how_to_apply: Apply online at spacegrant.net/apps/sees: essays (maximum 250 words per response), a short intro video (submit the link), an unofficial transcript or report card, and a recommendation form. Travel scholarships are available and do not affect your selection.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applications and 215 accepted in 2024 (FAQ). It is an educational internship, not a paid job.

name: High School Summer Research Academy (HSRA)
org: College of Natural Sciences, The University of Texas at Austin
grades: Rising sophomore, junior or senior (preference for rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $4,500. Payment is due only after you accept a lab placement. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.
duration: 5 weeks, June 7 to July 14, 2027 (off June 18 and July 5)
deadline_text: The 2027 application opens mid January 2027. Deadline is listed as March 2027 (no day). Late applications may be accepted on a limited basis.
who_can_apply: Texas residents are prioritized. You must be 15 or older by June 1, 2027 and available all five weeks. In person only. You arrange your own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in mid January 2027. First round notices go out at the end of April and second round in early May, with a deposit due one week after you accept. Email hsra@utexas.edu.
notes: This costs a lot and is hard to get into. The page says a few need-based scholarships may be available. They give a stipend plus free tuition. There are no merit scholarships now. Your lab spot is based on your interests, your free time and space. Full tuition is due in mid May.

name: Summer Discovery at UT Austin
org: The University of Texas at Austin Office of Admissions with Summer Discovery
pay_detail: Costs $3,799 to $7,999 depending on the options chosen (the Summer Discovery page gives one range). Some courses add fees. Financial aid is not mentioned.
duration: 2 week or 3 week sessions (2026: June 14 to 26 and June 28 to July 17)
deadline_text: 2026 sessions were June 14 to 26 and June 28 to July 17. 2027 dates and deadlines are not posted on the program pages.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Participation does not guarantee admission to UT Austin.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button on the UT page. Summer Discovery, not UT, handles applications and sign-up. You can email summerdiscovery@utexas.edu. Or call 516-447-4907.
notes: Expensive. Students get a certificate of completion and a campus grade letter. The Summer Discovery page shows an early enrollment discount ending Oct 31 but does not say the year.

name: Longhorn Engineering Summer Camp (LESC)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: $75 commitment fee for Austin participants, collected only after acceptance (day camp, no lodging)
duration: 4 days (Austin sessions June 8-11 and July 6-9 in 2026; both were full)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026 closed March 12, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students entering 8th or 9th grade. A panel reviews applications (not first come, first served), and students who attend schools without engineering or STEM offerings are encouraged to apply. Houston and San Antonio sessions are by invitation only.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp page; you are notified by email by mid-May. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: For younger teens (about 13 to 15). Both 2026 Austin sessions are listed as full.

name: My Introduction to Engineering (MITE)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: $200, paid only after acceptance (students stay in a campus residence hall)
duration: 5 days (June 21-25 and July 12-16 in 2026)
deadline_text: Applications for MITE 2026 closed March 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 50 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $200 is a barrier.

name: DYNAMC (Discover Yourself In Accounting Majors and Careers)
org: McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin
grades: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.
duration: June 20 to 25, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
deadline_text: The page says applications are closed now. It lists a 2027 application deadline of Feb 1, 2027 (supplemental materials Feb 8, 2027) and does not state an opening date. Confirm with McCombs.
who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.

org: McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin

deadline_text: The page says applications are closed now. It lists a 2027 application deadline of Feb 1, 2027 (supplemental materials Feb 8, 2027) and does not state an opening date. Confirm with McCombs.
