notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.

name: Subiendo: The Academy for Rising Leaders
org: McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Travel is covered by the program.
duration: June 13 to 17, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
deadline_text: The page says applications are closed now. It lists a 2027 application deadline of Feb 1, 2027 (supplemental materials Feb 8, 2027) and does not state an opening date. Confirm with McCombs.
who_can_apply: Texas high school juniors only. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April. More info: https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/undergraduate/subiendo/

name: Utah 4-H Mock Legislature
city: Utah State Capitol, Salt Lake City, UT
pay_detail: $25 per person (includes t-shirt and lunch).
duration: 1 day (2026: April 22, 9 AM to 3 PM)
deadline_text: 2026 event was April 22, 2026. 2027 date not posted.
who_can_apply: 4-H youth in 9th to 12th grade. Adults also attend.
how_to_apply: Register on Zsuite (4h.zsuite.org). Questions: contact the Utah 4-H State Office at 435-797-4444 or your county 4-H office.
notes: Held with Rep. Joel Briscoe and the Office of Legislative Research.

name: Utah 4-H Teen Summit
pay_detail: Cost not posted yet.
duration: 3 days (July 12 to 14, 2027)
deadline_text: Registration opens summer 2027. Deadline not posted.
who_can_apply: All teens in grades 9 to 12 (those who have finished 8th grade).
how_to_apply: Sign-up for the 2027 Teen Summit will open in summer 2027. Contact Vernon Parent at vernon.parent@usu.edu or 385-468-4832.
notes: A youth waiver is needed. Check the page for the cost when registration opens.

name: Utah 4-H Teen Winter Retreat
pay_detail: $135 per person. Includes lodging, meals and activities.
duration: Friday 4 PM to Saturday 3 PM (Jan 22 to 23, 2027)
deadline_text: Registration Nov 1 to Jan 8, or until filled.
who_can_apply: Utah teens in grades 9 to 12. A waiver must be uploaded in Zsuite when you register.
how_to_apply: Sign up through Zsuite and upload the signed waiver. Teens in grades 10 to 12 can also apply to the Teen Winter Retreat Design Team, which has 8 spots. Apply by Oct 24 with a 4-H portfolio, which is a resume and cover letter, and short answers.
notes: Design Team applications are open Sept 1 to Oct 24 and let teens plan activities and teach workshops. Questions: Utah 4-H State Office, 435-797-4444.

name: Utah 4-H
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county office about fees.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: Join through your county 4-H office.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18 in any Utah county. Find your county office to sign up.
how_to_apply: Use the Find your County Office link on the Utah 4-H site, then ask that office how to join. Registration for state events is through Zsuite.
notes: State events include Teen Summit, Teen Winter Retreat and Mock Legislature. Fees and dates differ by county and event. Ask your county office.

name: Paid Work Experience for Ages 14 to 24 (Utah Workforce Services)
pay_detail: The page says paid internships. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: The program page does not list a deadline.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The apply page says the help is for youth who are out of school and struggling to connect to work or school, or who struggle at school or work. A counselor decides if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Apply online or at a local Employment Center. A counselor contacts you within three business days. You then send the papers they ask for within 45 days. Together you make a job plan.
notes: This is a state program with eligibility checks, so not every teen qualifies. You need a Utah ID account to apply online. The program page does not say which employers or pay rates are used.

name: Seasonal Jobs at Lagoon Amusement Park
pay_detail: Pay is called competitive. The rate is not stated on the program page.
duration: Seasonal. Dates are not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: No dates are listed on the program page. The page still says it is hiring for the 2024 season, so call to confirm the current year.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 when you finish the application. Some jobs have other age rules. You need a valid email address.
how_to_apply: Fill out one online application. List other jobs you would take as backups. Read the employee rules before you apply. You can call Employee Services at 801-451-8058 for help.
notes: Lagoon is in Farmington, Utah. Perks include free entry to Lagoon Family Days and park store discounts. The park uses E-Verify to check work eligibility. A separate job page covers the fall Frightmares season.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS)
org: Utah State Office of Rehabilitation, Vocational Rehabilitation
pay_detail: Instruction by community partners is free.
duration: Varies by student
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 through 21 (or age 22 while in special education services). You must be in a high school or after high school program. You must be eligible for IDEA services. Or you have a disability under section 504. You do not have to be a client of Vocational Rehabilitation.
how_to_apply: Contact your school Vocational Rehabilitation liaison or a local VR office. You can send an email to vrtransition@utah.gov. You can also call 801-887-9500.
notes: Every public high school and charter school has a VR counselor. Contractors check that a student fits before services start.

name: Utah Summer Agriculture Program (Supervised Agricultural Experience)
org: Utah State Board of Education, Career and Technical Education
pay_detail: The program itself is school based. Projects can be paid or unpaid, and your employer may pay you for SAE work. School credit may be offered.
duration: Starts the day after the school contract ends and runs to the day before the next one starts
deadline_text: Teachers send in their plan and roster April 15 to 30 each year. Ask your ag teacher when to sign up.
who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders enrolled in an approved agriculture class for the next school year, with an approved SAE plan. High school graduates are not eligible. Your school must run a Summer Ag Program.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school agriculture teacher. You need an approved SAE plan in the Agricultural Experience Tracker (AET). Use your boundary school's Summer Ag Program. If that is not available, you can work with a school in the same district with parent consent and approval.
notes: The guide is written for teachers and districts. Each program needs at least 35 students and a licensed ag teacher, so not every school has one. Ask your ag teacher.

name: UTEP Mining Engineering Summer Camp
org: Miguel A. Loya College of Engineering, UTEP
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.
duration: 3 days per session
deadline_text: The 2026 camps ran June 21 to 23, June 24 to 26 and June 28 to 30. Use the Get Notified button on the program page for future camps.
who_can_apply: High school students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade. You should like STEM jobs and mining engineering.
how_to_apply: The program page has a Get Notified for Future Camps option. Email miningengineering@utep.edu. Or call 915-747-7057.
notes: No 2027 dates are posted on the program page.

name: UTEP Upward Bound
org: University of Texas at El Paso
pay_detail: Free to students.
duration: Through high school graduation and the first summer semester at UTEP
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page. Email or call to ask about selection.
who_can_apply: High school students at schools in the program. Low-income students who could be the first in their family to go to college must qualify. Schools: Bel Air, Del Valle, Parkland, Riverside and Ysleta (YISD). Also Eastlake, El Dorado, Fabens, Pebble Hills, Socorro and Tornillo (SFT ISDs).
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Email upwardbound@utep.edu or call (915) 747-5062.
notes: Federally funded. Students must qualify to be selected. This is a college prep program, not a job.

name: UVA Advance Pre-College Program
org: University of Virginia Summer and Special Academic Programs
pay_detail: The FAQ says the maximum aid package covers full tuition and fees for Virginia residents, which is $7,097 for 2026. The cost for other students and the full breakdown were not read. Small number of need-based aid packages.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 11 to August 7), residential
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened December 1; deadline March 1, 2026; teacher recommendation March 4; decisions March 31; accept by April 15. No 2027 dates posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in good standing with a minimum 3.5 GPA in a college prep curriculum, age 15 or older on the first day and 18 or younger on the last day.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts, one teacher or administrator recommendation uploaded by the recommender, and a 350 to 500 word essay. Financial aid materials are due by March 1.
notes: Residents live in an air-conditioned residence hall with a 10 pm curfew. Travel, books, laundry and spending money are not included. Questions: UVaAdvance@virginia.edu, 434-243-2241. The Cost and Payment page was not read.

name: UVA Health Junior Volunteer Summer Program
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 8 to July 31); at least 50 hours, or one full weekday, with at least 6 weeks of service
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: interest form due February 20, 2026; info sessions February 25 and March 7, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school youth ages 14 to 18. Students must attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian and an all-day orientation on the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Submit the online interest form, attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian, then interview if selected. Two references must complete the online reference form before the interview.
notes: The page mentions a lottery. Cost and immunization rules for juniors were not stated on that page; UVA Health's general volunteer page lists a health assessment, vaccination requirements, background check and training for volunteers. Questions: 434-924-5251.

name: Virginia 4-H
org: Virginia Cooperative Extension (Virginia Tech and Virginia State University)
city: Statewide, Virginia (a local Extension office in each area)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Ask your local Extension office.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs, camps and events set their own dates.
who_can_apply: 4-H participants are youth ages 5 to 19. Community 4-H clubs are for ages 9 through 18. You join by contacting your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office and ask about the 4-H program.
notes: The page also lists a 4-H State Congress, camps, maker education, shooting education and youth leadership opportunities. Details such as dates and fees for those were not on the page.

name: Virginia Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of Virginia
city: Virginia (college campus; the 2026 session was the 83rd)
grades: Finished grade 11, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Free to the delegate. The $600 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as an American Legion post, business or school group. Parents and students may not pay it.
duration: One week (the 2026 session ran June 21 to 27, 2026)
deadline_text: 2027 session dates and sign-up dates are not posted yet. The 2026 session ran June 21 to 27, 2026. Local American Legion posts pick delegates earlier in the school year.
who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You and your parents must live in Virginia. Home-schooled boys can apply if they meet the home school rules on the site. You cannot attend Boys State twice.
how_to_apply: Your high school counselor suggests candidates. Local American Legion post members interview them. Find your district chairperson on the Apply page. Ask about how your district does it.
notes: Delegates stay in university dorms. A delegate who turns 18 before the last day must pass a background check. It costs about $16, and the program refunds it. Two delegates go to Boys Nation in Washington, DC. The site lists a 2027 page, but no 2027 dates were found on the pages. The apply page lists the fee as a $600.00 application fee per delegate. It says individual or parental sponsorships are not permitted. Registrar: registrar@vaboysstate.org.

name: Summer Youth Volunteer Program at VA El Paso
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: June through August
deadline_text: Applications open in May and spots fill up quickly. Expect it to reopen in May 2027.
who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Coordinator at elpcdce@va.gov. Ask about the summer youth program.
notes: The program page says applications open in May but gives no 2027 dates.

name: Virginia Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Virginia
grades: Finished grade 11, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: There is a delegate fee, but the amount is not stated on the program page. Fees are paid to the district registrar (the site lists April 15, 2027 for fees to reach registrars). Ask your district registrar about the cost and who may sponsor you.
duration: One week: Sunday June 20 to Friday June 25, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 25, 2027. The site lists April 15, 2027 for fees to reach district registrars, May 15, 2027 for all delegates registered, and June 1, 2027 for online forms. A date to apply to your local unit is not posted.
who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. Public, private and home school students can apply. Must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident of the United States (proof is needed).
how_to_apply: Delegates are selected by local American Legion Auxiliary units by interview, whenever possible. If your school has not been contacted, find your district on the map and email your district registrar for help. Online registration opens in spring 2027 for chosen delegates.
notes: The 2027 director listed is Cheryl Shine, director@vagirlsstate.org. Delegates must stay until 3:00 PM Friday to get program credit. The pages do not say the cost, so ask your district registrar.

name: Virginia House of Delegates Page Program
org: Virginia House of Delegates, Clerk's Office
pay_detail: Paid, about 40 hours a week: a weekly expense payment plus a wage every two weeks. Amounts are not stated.
duration: The 2027 session. The page says 7 weeks in odd-numbered years
deadline_text: The 2027 application closed Oct 16, 2026 at 3 p.m. Look for the 2028 application in late summer 2027.
who_can_apply: Virginia youth who will be 13 or 14 years old on January 13, 2027. You must be in good school standing. Your school must agree to the long absence.
how_to_apply: Apply on the portal linked from the Page Programs page. Finish every part. Talk to your school first, since you will miss weeks of class. Questions: HousePageInfo@house.virginia.gov or (804) 698-1502.
notes: Pages live together and have a study hall each night. Not the Senate Page Program. 2028 dates not posted.

name: Summer Youth Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to join; volunteers over 100 hours can be considered for scholarships through community partners (2024 flyer).
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2024: June 17 to July 26)
deadline_text: The VA page says applications for the 2026 program closed April 24, 2026. The 2024 deadline was April 30. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 (18-year-olds must be enrolled in high school). Based on the 2024 flyer; check the current year's rules.
how_to_apply: 2024 flyer: application with parent signature, a 1-page essay, an availability schedule, and a virtual orientation. Contact the VA Center for Development and Civic Engagement, vhalomyouthprogram@va.gov.
notes: Closed now. The age, hours and application steps come from the 2024 flyer because the current page only says 2026 applications are closed. The 2024 flyer also required COVID vaccination or an exemption; check the current policy.

name: Senate of Virginia Page Program
pay_detail: $340 a week before taxes plus a $225 a week non-taxed expense deposit (per diem). Rates can change. Families pay about $50 for an activity fee, uniform clothes and a binder, and get the student to Richmond.
duration: The whole legislative session: 46 calendar days in odd-numbered years and 60 calendar days (nine total weeks) in even-numbered years
deadline_text: The class of 2027 application closed Oct 1, 2026. The class of 2028 application opens July 1, 2027 and closes at 5 p.m. on Oct 1, 2027. Decisions usually come in mid-December.
who_can_apply: Virginia residents who are 13 or 14 on the first day of session (the second Wednesday in January), with no exceptions. You live with a parent or guardian. You go to an accredited school or a qualifying home school. You should have an A or B average.
how_to_apply: Use the Application for Admission page of the Prospective Senate Page Portal during the open window. Questions: pageinfo@senate.virginia.gov or (804) 698-7410.
notes: Pages stay at a designated hotel Sunday night to Friday noon each week, and the hotel room is billed to the Senate Clerk's Office. Admission counts as an excused school absence. Cell phones are turned in during work hours. Rates are listed as subject to change. The overview page lists a $50 activity fee in recent years and does not list uniform or binder costs.

name: Virginia State Parks Youth Conservation Corps
org: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation, State Parks
grades: Entering 9th grade (freshman year) at least; still in high school the next fall
pay_detail: $750 stipend after you finish the two-week program. You may also get community service hours.
duration: Two weeks. 2027 sessions: June 20 to July 3, or July 11 to 24
deadline_text: 2027 applications open Jan 1, 2027 and close Mar 19, 2027 at 5 p.m. Interviews Mar 30 to Apr 8, offers Apr 16, 2027.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 through 17. You must be at least 14 by June 1, 2027, must not turn 18 before the session ends, and must still be in high school the fall after the program. You need your own email, bank account and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Crew Member application on the page. Two professional or academic references must turn in their forms by the deadline. Chosen applicants join a group interview. They also go through a background check.
notes: Competitive. The page says it gets many more applications than spots. About ten crew members live at each host park with three to four adult crew leaders. Crews are split into male and female groups. Cell phones, laptops and other devices are not allowed during the program. Contact: vspycc@dcr.virginia.gov. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before working. Its page does not mention this program. Ask the program if one is needed.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Virginia Wing
city: Statewide, Virginia (squadrons from Winchester to Virginia Beach)
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.
duration: Weekly squadron meetings all year
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time through a local squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens).
how_to_apply: Use the unit locator to find a cadet or composite squadron. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Or apply online if your squadron says you can.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Virginia Wing HQ: 7401 Airfield Drive, Richmond, VA 23237, 804-454-7356. The wing site lists squadrons in Blacksburg, Charlottesville, Herndon, Springfield, Richmond and other towns.

name: Valley Humane Society Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. New volunteers buy a $30 Volunteer Starter Kit with a shirt, name badge and manuals.
duration: Most roles ask for one shift a week for six months to one year
deadline_text: The program page lists no deadline. You apply for an open shift.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. Some jobs need you to be 18. These are AniMeals, customer service and events. Parent and child volunteering is not offered.
how_to_apply: Look at the open shifts and apply for one you can work. A volunteer coordinator then contacts you to set up an orientation. You also take role workshops and shadow shifts.
notes: Students can earn community service hours with the same six month, weekly shift promise. Court ordered hours are not accepted. Volunteers must be fully vaccinated, according to the FAQ. Sunday dog care is the greatest need.

name: Valley Water Youth Commission
org: Valley Water (Santa Clara Valley Water District)
city: San Jose, CA (serves all Santa Clara County)
duration: 2-year term, up to 5 hours a month
deadline_text: The application is closed and will open again in Spring 2027. Fill out the interest form to be told.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.

name: Employee U
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Cost is not listed either.
duration: 8 weeks, flexible
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the program page. The page does not list the steps.
notes: You also get help with your resume and may be placed in a job at the Y. The page does not list locations, so ask your nearest Y.

name: Aquarium Educator Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.
duration: One shift a week for at least 3 months
deadline_text: Recruitment happens once a year in the spring. No 2027 date is posted. Sign up on the page to get an email when it opens.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 15 years old in the calendar year you apply and give one shift a week for at least 3 months.
how_to_apply: Join the email list on the volunteer page (it asks you to confirm you are 15 this year or older). Apply when spring recruitment opens. Questions: volunteer@vanaqua.org.
notes: The aquarium also has a Marine Mammal Rescue Centre volunteer role and practicums. Those are for ages 18 and up, so they are not on this card.

name: Art Exchange (Vancouver Art Gallery and Arts Umbrella)
org: Vancouver Art Gallery with Arts Umbrella
pay_detail: Free to students (full scholarship). Not a paid job.
duration: October 2026 to June 2027
deadline_text: Submissions for the 2026-27 program were due Tuesday, September 29, 2026 at 8 AM. Next cycle not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens aged 13 to 15. Applicants send a portfolio of 10 images in all. It has 5 to 7 finished works and 3 to 5 sketchbook images. They also send a letter of intent of 500 to 1,000 words.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY NOW link on the page to submit the portfolio and letter of intent. Questions: submissions@artsumbrella.com or 604-681-5268.
notes: Scholarship-funded learning program, not a paid job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: Teen Art Group (Vancouver Art Gallery and Emily Carr University)
org: Vancouver Art Gallery with Emily Carr University of Art + Design
grades: Aged 15 to 18 or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026
pay_detail: Registration fee $555.90 CAD. Four full-tuition scholarships are available for Indigenous students or students facing financial barriers.
duration: Thursdays 4 to 7 PM, October 15, 2026 to February 11, 2027
deadline_text: Registration for fall 2026 is open, per the page, with no closing date stated. The program starts Oct 15, 2026. The scholarship deadline was September 15, 2026.
who_can_apply: Students aged 15 to 18, or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Emily Carr University Continuing Studies site (use the Apply Now link on the page). Questions: teens@ecuad.ca.
notes: Paid-for arts program, not a job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: BC Children's and BC Women's Hospital Volunteer Program
org: BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital + Health Centre (Volunteer Resources)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.
duration: One year for every volunteer role
deadline_text: Apply any time. Recruitment info goes out in late October or November for a January start, in March for a May start, and in July for a September start.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older before you apply or go to an information session. Patient contact roles need age 18 or older. Child patient support roles need work or volunteer experience with children.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Staff will call you for an interview. If you get in, you do a record check, a reference check and training.
notes: The biggest need is Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm; evening and weekend spots usually go to current volunteers. Intake can take several months. If you are not placed within 6 months, the application is closed and you may apply again. Contact: volunteer@cw.bc.ca.

name: Mini Med School: Inside the Human Body (BC Children's Hospital Research Institute)
pay_detail: No cost is listed on the page. Attending all sessions makes you eligible to apply for a scholarship with $1,000 CAD toward post-secondary tuition.
duration: 4 Thursday evenings, 6:30 to 8:00 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions are Nov 5, 12, 19 and 26, 2026. Registration for 2026 is closed and the waitlist is full. A new round is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Grade 12 students in BC and the Yukon. From Fall 2026, Grade 11 students are not eligible even if they take Grade 12 level courses. Students in grades 8 to 11 can use the Self-Directed program instead, which offers recorded sessions.
how_to_apply: Register online. You give your contact details and a sponsor teacher's name and email. You give a signed Participant Agreement Form. You give three answers of 150 words or less. After the deadline, students are picked by random draw. Priority goes to First Nations, Inuit and Metis students and to students from different schools.
notes: Registration for the 2026 round is closed. Watch the page for the next round. In person sessions are at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them.

name: Pathways to Science (BC Children's Hospital Research Institute)
pay_detail: Free. You get a certificate of participation if you apply and attend 7 of the 10 sessions.
duration: 10 monthly online sessions, Sept 2026 to June 2027, about 1 hour each
deadline_text: Ten Monday sessions from Sept 2026 to June 2027 (Sept 21, 2026 is 6 to 7 p.m.; the others are 5 to 6 p.m.). No deadline is posted. You can sign up any time during the series until 1,000 students have applied.
who_can_apply: Grade 11 and 12 students in BC and the Yukon. No research experience needed. Limited to the first 1,000 students who apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for your name, contact details, grade and school. It asks for a parent or guardian's contact. It asks for one answer of 150 words or less. Say why you want to attend.
notes: Online talks only, not a job or hands-on lab work. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The institute says it does not offer any formal placements for students who want to volunteer, job shadow or gain work experience. The application form link is on the page.

name: Youth Employability Program (BGC South Coast BC)
pay_detail: Participants are paid to take part, with a completion bonus for finishing all 8 weeks. Amounts are not stated on the page. Free to join.
duration: 8 weeks per session
deadline_text: Sessions run every other month (the page gives Oct, Dec, Feb, Apr as examples) and recruiting starts one month before each start date. No events were listed when read.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 30 who need to find work. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Click an event under Upcoming Events on the page to apply. Central office: 604-879-6554 or info@bgcbc.ca. Seats are limited.
notes: Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet. The page did not say where the workshops are held.

name: Discovery Days in Health Sciences (BC Children's Hospital)
org: Canadian Medical Hall of Fame with BC Children's Hospital Research Institute
pay_detail: No registration fee. You or your school pay for transportation and any parking.
deadline_text: Friday, Nov 6, 2026. No student deadline is posted. Student sign-up opens about six weeks before event day (around late September 2026). School registration for fall events opens in Sept 2026, and student sign-up instructions are emailed to the contact teacher when registration opens.
who_can_apply: High school students in BC, grades 10 to 12 on the research institute page. A teacher must first register the school with the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame. The organizers encourage schools to consider students who are Indigenous, Black, a person of colour, or from rural or lower income backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to register your school on the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame website (cdnmedhall.ca/discoverydays). The teacher then gets the student sign-up steps. If you cannot find a teacher, email cmhf@cdnmedhall.ca. Give your city, high school and the event.
notes: One day event, not a job. The Medical Hall of Fame page does not name the city, but the research institute page says the event is at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Grades come from the institute page only.

name: Providence Health Care Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can ask for a reference after 30 hours at long-term care sites.
duration: 1 to 3 hours a week for at least 4 or 6 months in a row, depending on the program
deadline_text: No deadline. Each site takes online applications; if no one contacts you in 6 to 8 weeks, apply again.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older for long-term care sites; 18 or older for acute care (hospitals). You must complete a free criminal record check and get a free yearly flu shot or wear a mask.
how_to_apply: Pick a site on the volunteer page (for example Holy Family Hospital, Mount Saint Joseph long-term care or a St. Vincent's site) and fill out its online form. List references like teachers or coaches. If chosen, you will be called for an interview.
notes: At 16 or 17 you can only volunteer at the long-term care sites. There is no shadowing or direct patient care. Most shifts are weekdays during work or school hours. The FAQ also says Public Health requires two COVID-19 shots for volunteers.

name: ink Teen Advisory Group
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.
duration: February to December. Meetings every other Thursday during the school year (online or at Central Library), plus two-day summer workshops with mentors.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The ink page links an application form. Separately, writing and art for ink volume 10 can be sent in until April 23, 2027.
who_can_apply: Anyone 13 to 18 years old who lives or goes to school in Vancouver.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Click here to apply to ink TAG' form on the ink page. Questions: teens@vpl.ca or 604.331.3690.
notes: You can also send your own writing or art to ink (up to two pieces a year) without joining the group. The page says art or writing made with AI will not be published.

name: Reading Buddies for Teens
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. You earn community service hours, and the library can write a letter confirming them.
duration: One hour a week for about 8 weeks, plus a teen training session on the first date. Arrive 15 minutes early.
deadline_text: All five Fall 2026 sessions (Britannia, Fraserview, Kensington, South Hill, West Point Grey) were full on Oct 19, 2026. The Britannia session has a waitlist. Apply at least one week before a session starts. Next dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 who live in Vancouver. You need a signature from a coach, teacher, counsellor or community leader on your form, and you must come to every session.
how_to_apply: When new sessions are posted, fill in the online form at least one week before the start date. Get your reference person to sign it. Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: If you quit without a good reason, your spot goes to a teen on the waitlist. Sessions are loud and snacks are provided.

name: STEAM Buddies for Teens
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. You earn community service hours.
duration: One hour a week for about 4 weeks, plus a teen training session on the first date.
deadline_text: All four Fall 2026 sessions (Champlain Heights, Kitsilano, Mount Pleasant, Terry Salman) were full on Oct 19, 2026. Apply at least one week before a session starts. Next dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 who live in Vancouver. You must come to every session.
how_to_apply: When new sessions are posted, fill in the online form on the STEAM Buddies page at least one week before the start date. Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Like Reading Buddies, but with hands-on science and tech. Check the page each season for new branches and dates.

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Members earn community service hours.
duration: September to June. One hour every other week (4 to 5 p.m.), online on Teams or at a branch.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Fill in the online form any time. On Oct 19, 2026 the Kerrisdale and Kitsilano groups were full.
who_can_apply: Anyone 13 to 18 years old who lives in Vancouver.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked on the TAG page. Pick the online group or a branch group (Central Library, Kensington, Kerrisdale, Kitsilano or Renfrew). Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Some branch groups fill up, so the online Teams group may be the easiest to join. Event listings on the library calendar show exact dates and access details.

name: Teen DMs for Kids
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. You earn community service hours.
duration: Varies. Times and branches change, and some are one-time events.
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply at least one week before a program starts. Chances come up now and then, and the library contacts teens it picks.
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 who know some D&D. Teens who live or go to school in Vancouver get first pick. You need an adult reference who is not your parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill in the application form on the Teen DMs page and give the contact for an adult reference (a coach, teacher, counsellor or community leader). Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Some times of year are busier than others, so you may wait a while for your first game.

name: Teens Read it First
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get one community service hour for every 100 pages of the book, confirmed by letter.
duration: At your own pace, one book at a time
deadline_text: No deadline. Books go first come, first served.
who_can_apply: Teens who live in Vancouver. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Watch the teensatvpl Instagram for featured books. Ask for one by Instagram message or at teens@vpl.ca. Pick it up at your nearest branch, then email your rating and review to teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Share your opinion of the book, not a summary of the plot. Reviews of only one or two lines are sent back for more detail.

name: Science World Volunteer Program
grades: 11 and 12 for the High School Work Experience placement
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.
duration: 100 hours minimum, one 2 to 3 hour shift per week
deadline_text: The core volunteer intake is closed; intake and training sessions are scheduled each year. No dates posted.
who_can_apply: Core volunteer program: at least 16 years old, 100 hours minimum. High School Work Experience: Lower Mainland students in Grades 11 and 12; teachers sign students up.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page for the next intake. For the work experience placement, ask your teacher to sign you up.
notes: The Science World Teen Advisory Group (ages 16 to 18) is on hiatus and not taking applications (page checked 2026-10-09). Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: seed2STEM Summer Research Internship
org: ICORD, University of British Columbia (with SFU and Kelowna sites)
pay_detail: Minimum wage for 25 hours a week. Transit passes, loaner laptops, some meals and youth support workers are provided.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: The page says applications for Summer 2027 open in December 2026. Close date not posted.
who_can_apply: Indigenous (First Nations, Metis or Inuit) high school students in grades 9 to 12. You live in Metro Vancouver or Kelowna.
how_to_apply: Watch the seed2STEM page for the application. Email seed2STEM@icord.org or call 604-675-8830.
notes: Exact opening day not posted.

name: SFU Camps Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get volunteer hours, evaluations, confirmation letters and a reference request option.
duration: Minimum 2 weeks (at least 80 hours), consecutive or separate
deadline_text: 2026: online applications closed April 20, 2026 (Lead Volunteer deadline April 17, 2026); interviews mid-May (in person); training late June. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 years of age by June 29, 2026. If accepted, you submit a criminal record check and complete training.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application, attend one in-person interview, then complete in-person or online training. Returning volunteers can apply as Lead Volunteers by email.
notes: SFU Camps says it is not a registered non-profit; check with your teacher that your school accepts these hours for service or work experience credit. Top volunteers are encouraged to apply as paid instructors later (2026 instructor wage $27.05 to $28.50 per hour, CAD); the minimum age for instructors is not stated on the page. Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.

name: H.R. MacMillan Space Centre teen volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page lists education and skills training and mentions telescope viewing on some evening shifts as a volunteer benefit.
duration: Not stated. The summer Augmented Reality role is weekly support.

who_can_apply: Teens age 16 and older, and adults. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the "Volunteer with us" form linked on the Space Centre careers page. Questions can go to careers@spacecentre.ca.
notes: Age 16 and up, so 13 to 15 year olds cannot apply. The pages do not give shift length, hours or a start date, so ask before you plan. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Rechecked 2026-10-10: the volunteer page loads and confirms age 16 and up, the summer Augmented Reality role and the "Volunteer with us" form. It gives no year, dates or deadline.

name: Stanley Park Ecology Youth Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can request a reference letter after 25 hours.
duration: Varies by role; many are seasonal
deadline_text: Varies by role: DIRT and Nature House Host take applications year-round when there is room; EcoRangers apply in May; EcoCamp Assistant applications open in February and May; EcoStewards is listed as open.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17 can join EcoStewards, DIRT, Nature House Hosts, EcoRangers and EcoCamp Assistants. Ages 12 to 15 can join only EcoStewards, and only with adult supervision. A parent or guardian must sign the youth consent form.
how_to_apply: Register and sign up through Better Impact. If a role is closed, fill in the Volunteer Interest Form. Email vols@stanleyparkecology.ca with questions.
notes: Volunteer role in Canada. British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet, so work permit is marked unknown. Most other roles on the site are for volunteers 16 and older.

name: UBC Future Global Leaders (on campus)
org: UBC Extended Learning, University of British Columbia
pay_detail: 2026 fees listed in CAD: course $1,940 for Canadian students (including permanent residents) or $2,620 international; mini school $2,110 Canadian or $2,855 international. Optional residence add-on $2,650. A $500 deposit is due when you register. Fees can change. The President Bursary is for B.C. grade 11 students with financial need.
duration: 2 weeks per session
deadline_text: Summer 2027 sessions: July 5 to 16, July 19 to 30 and Aug 2 to 13, 2027. Residence registration deadlines (noon): May 21, June 4 and June 18, 2027. Commuter deadlines (noon): June 18, July 2 and July 16, 2027. Residence can close sooner if full. The page does not say when 2027 registration opens.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed grade 10 or equivalent. UBC recommends about a 78% average, 3.5 GPA, B average or IB 5. Students still learning English should have IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 80 or higher. Open to students from other countries.
how_to_apply: No application, transcripts or proof of English are needed. Check that you are eligible. Add a course or mini school to your cart. Have a parent or guardian create a Family Account. Pay the deposit at checkout. Then finish the information package within 48 hours.
notes: Costs money, and it is a camp-style university course, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The fee table is labeled 2026 and still shows a 'due May 1, 2026' date next to the 2027 sessions, so check the 2027 fees before you plan. An online version also exists (3 week courses); this card covers the on-campus version. Rechecked 2026-10-10: the on-campus page confirms the 2027 session dates and the residence and commuter deadlines on this card. It does not say when 2027 registration opens. It still labels the fee table 2026.

name: UBC Summer Science Program for Indigenous students
org: UBC Centre for Excellence in Indigenous Health, Faculty of Medicine
pay_detail: $200 program fee covers housing and meals. Workshops and Vancouver Aquarium admission are covered. Bursaries for students with financial need and travel bursaries are available. Travel to Vancouver is not included.
duration: 1 week
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was June 15, 2026. The program page for 2025 listed Week 1 as Aug 3 to 9 and Week 2 as Aug 10 to 16, with applications closing June 1. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: First Nations, Inuit or Metis students going into grades 9 to 12. Week 1 is for students going into grades 11 or 12. Week 2 is for students going into grades 9 or 10. The pages do not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Science application online (UBC form). Or send it by email to summer.science@ubc.ca, or by mail. A reference letter of about 200 words is recommended. It can come from a teacher, coach, mentor or community leader.
notes: Only for Indigenous students (First Nations, Inuit, Metis). It is a camp, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The page still shows 2025 dates, so check the newest page before you plan. The application page lists the 2026 deadline of June 15, 2026.

name: VPD Cadet Program
org: Vancouver Police Department, funded by the Vancouver Police Foundation
pay_detail: Free. The Vancouver Police Foundation pays for all program materials and fees.
duration: 28 weeks, September to May
deadline_text: Applications are closed for the 2026/2027 school year. The VPD page says to check back in the spring. Last pattern: the call for the class starting September 2025 was posted April 25, 2025.
who_can_apply: Teens going into Grade 10, 11 or 12 who live or go to school in Vancouver. You must want to finish school and not miss a lot of it. You cannot have serious arrests, a record of trouble with police, or gang ties.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Apply Now button on the VPD Cadet page when it reopens in spring 2027. Questions: cadets@vpd.ca.
notes: About 90 cadets a year. It is a leadership program, not police recruiting. The VPD Indigenous Cadet Program is a different summer job for ages 19 to 29. Unpaid, so BC child employment rules for paid work do not apply here.

name: Youth Explore Trades Sampler (Vancouver School Board)
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Semester 2 of grade 12
deadline_text: Dates not stated on the program page. Ask your counsellor.
who_can_apply: Vancouver School Board students. Apply in grade 11 for grade 12, semester 2, at John Oliver Secondary. Grade 12 students can apply if a space is left.
how_to_apply: Use the application on the page or ask your counsellor. Email careerprograms@vsb.bc.ca.
notes: Page says students should apply in grade 11, and that grade 12 students can apply if a space remains. Confirm with the school. Contact Mark Reid, Career Programs Teacher, mreid@vsb.bc.ca.

name: Youth WORK in Trades (Vancouver School Board)
org: Vancouver School Board Career Programs with SkilledTradesBC
pay_detail: Paid by the employer. Rate not stated.
duration: Credits earned over the school year or semester
deadline_text: The support form for finding a placement stays open until Dec 15 for semester 2 and May 15 for summer. Year not stated.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 at Vancouver School Board schools. You need an employer in a known trade. The employer, you, a parent and the district sign an agreement.
how_to_apply: Email careerprograms@vsb.bc.ca. For building trades, ask to join the SiteReady safety course.
notes: Contact Mark Reid at the program. Students who need only one or two classes can work four days a week and take self-paced classes at South Hill Education Centre.

name: Vancouver Youth Parliament (VYP)
pay_detail: $60 registration fee; financial help may be asked for by email
duration: One weekend session plus events during the year
deadline_text: The 39th session (Feb 6 to 8, 2026) closed applications Feb 1, 2026. The next one is expected around the same time.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 as of Dec 31, in the Vancouver region. This includes Vancouver, North Vancouver, West Vancouver, Burnaby and Richmond. A youth group, like a school or community group, must name you. Five members of that group must sign.
how_to_apply: Download the form. Find a sponsor group and five people to name you. Add a personal note if you did not take part last year. Fill out the online form and upload your files.
notes: Contact vyp@bcyp.org for session questions and registrar@bcyp.org for applying. The 40th session dates were not posted when read.

name: VCC Dual Credit (high school trades and culinary foundation programs)
org: Vancouver Community College with Lower Mainland school districts
pay_detail: VCC lists program tuition (for example $2,513 for Baking Foundation High School). Application and student fees are waived if accepted. School district may pay tuition for select courses.
duration: Varies by program (about 6 months to 40 weeks)
deadline_text: No single deadline. Your school district career office sets the date.
who_can_apply: High school students in partner school districts, including Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond and Langley. Process starts in grade 11 for courses in grade 12.
how_to_apply: Talk to the career staff at your school district. You need two references, a letter from a counselor or school leader, a letter from a parent, and the form.
notes: Recommended B or higher in English 11 and Math 11. Tuition amounts are from the VCC page and can change. Ask your district whether it pays.

name: Museum Teen Internship (Summer Service Program)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Interns get high school service credit, a letter of recommendation, training, free parking and museum passes to share.
duration: June to August; at least 25 service hours. Gallery shifts of 2-4 hours, 1-3 times a week; camp assistants commit to a full camp week (Mon-Fri, 8:45 a.m. to 1:45 p.m.)
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2026 are closed. The 2027 deadline is not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. Applicants must apply by the posted deadline, attend a short interview and orientation, and commit to at least 25 service hours.
how_to_apply: Apply by the posted deadline, then interview and attend orientation. Contact Anna Deater-Deckard, anna@vadm.org, 434-977-1025 x104.
notes: The museum is a small children's museum for infants to age 8, so the work is with young kids. Weekday and Saturday shifts are available.

name: Camp Woods and Wildlife
pay_detail: Selected students get a $300 scholarship and pay a $95 registration fee.
duration: 5 days (June 15 to 19 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 camp was June 15 to 19, 2026. The page says 2027 information and the application will be posted in February. Applicants are told starting in March.
who_can_apply: Virginia residents ages 13 to 16 on the first day of camp. You like nature, have good grades and have not been before. An adult who is not family must nominate you.
how_to_apply: Student fills in the first three sections of the application and nomination form. The nominating adult (teacher, forester, youth leader) fills in the fourth. Submit both together by mail, email or fax.
notes: Camp has run for more than 70 years. It was formerly called Holiday Lake Forestry Camp. Scholarships come from forest industry and conservation sponsors.

name: Virginia Envirothon
org: Virginia Association of Soil and Water Conservation Districts
pay_detail: No fee is mentioned on the program page.
duration: Spring contests
deadline_text: Page says to contact your local district by winter for spring local or regional contests. The state contest is held in mid to late May. The top three teams from each of six areas advance.
who_can_apply: High school students on a team of five with one adult coach or chaperone. The page says high school students but gives no grade range.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Soil and Water Conservation District. If you do not know it, email byron.minson@vaswcd.org.
notes: Exact 2027 dates were not posted on the program page. Check the Current Competition page on the same site.

name: Virginia Governor's School for Agriculture

pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

deadline_text: 2026 session ran June 20 to July 11, 2026. Deadlines vary by school division. 2027 dates were not posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors from Virginia public, private and home schools. Selection is by your school or county, not by Virginia Tech.
how_to_apply: Start with your school counselor. Or ask the gifted and talented lead. The Virginia Department of Education handles applications. They go through your school or county.
notes: Contact Dr. Brett Milliken, agschool@vt.edu, 540-231-6836 for cost and deadlines. Classes run 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with evening and weekend activities.

name: Summer Residential Governor's School for Medicine and Health Sciences

grades: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders)
pay_detail: $300 activity fee for outings and enrichment. Hardship waiver available. Tuition not stated on the program pages.
duration: About 3 weeks, late June to early July in 2026
deadline_text: 2027 dates and deadline not found on the program pages. Ask your school counselor.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders) enrolled in Virginia high schools who are interested in health careers. 20 students took part in 2026.
how_to_apply: The application starts at the local school district level. Forms are on the Virginia Department of Education Summer Residential Governor's School page. You can also email MHSgovschool@radford.edu.
notes: Held in Roanoke, not in Blacksburg. Email MHSgovschool@radford.edu. The Virginia Department of Education page blocked our reader, so check it for current dates.

grades: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders)
pay_detail: $300 activity fee for outings and enrichment. Hardship waiver available. Tuition not stated on the program pages.

deadline_text: Dates and deadline for the next session were not found on the program pages. Ask your school counselor.
